The kidneys may then have difficulty filtering waste and extra fluid from the blood and balancing salts, acids, and other body functions. Diabetes and high blood pressure are common causes. Early disease often causes no symptoms; advanced disease may cause swelling, tiredness, poor appetite, nausea, itching, anemia, mineral and bone problems, or kidney failure. Chronic kidney disease is differ

name: chronic leukemia
clinical_significance: A blood cancer that develops gradually as abnormal white blood cells multiply and remain in the blood or bone marrow. Some types progress slowly but still require regular medical monitoring.

name: chronic lymphocytic leukemia
clinical_significance: A usually slow-growing blood cancer in which abnormal B lymphocytes build up in the blood, bone marrow, and lymph nodes. It may cause enlarged lymph nodes, tiredness, repeated infections, anaemia, or no symptoms at first.

name: chronic myelogenous leukemia
clinical_significance: A blood cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many abnormal white blood cells, usually because of the BCR::ABL1 gene change. It may progress over time but is often controlled with targeted medicines.

name: chronic pain
clinical_significance: Pain that persists or recurs for longer than three months, beyond the usual healing period. It can affect sleep, movement, mood, and daily activity; causes and contributing factors vary, and treatment may combine physical, psychological, and medical approaches.

name: chronic periodontitis
clinical_significance: Long-term inflammation and infection of the tissues supporting the teeth, causing gum recession, loss of attachment, and damage to the jawbone. Without treatment it can loosen or destroy teeth and is associated with diabetes and other health conditions.

name: chronic rhinitis
clinical_significance: Long-lasting inflammation or irritation of the nose causing congestion, runny nose, sneezing, itching, or mucus draining into the throat. Causes include allergy, irritants, medicines, and structural problems; treatment is chosen after identifying the cause.

name: chronic sinusitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the sinuses lasting at least 12 weeks, usually with nasal blockage or discharge and sometimes reduced smell or facial pressure. Nasal polyps, allergy, infection, or structural factors may contribute; persistent symptoms warrant clinical assessment.

name: chronic villitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the placental chorionic villi, the small structures that exchange nutrients and oxygen between maternal and fetal blood. It may be caused by infection or have no identified cause; extensive disease has been associated with fetal growth restriction and preterm birth.

name: chronotherapy
clinical_significance: Scheduling a treatment or medicine to align with daily biological rhythms. Timing can affect benefit or side effects for some conditions, but the best schedule depends on the treatment and evidence for that use.

name: chrysenes
clinical_significance: A group of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons found in products of incomplete combustion, smoke, and some environmental pollutants. Some compounds in this group can damage DNA and are considered potential or established carcinogenic hazards.

name: chryseobacterium
clinical_significance: A genus of bacteria found in water and soil. Some species can cause opportunistic infections, including bloodstream, wound, or respiratory infection, especially in hospitalized or immunocompromised people; resistance can complicate treatment.

name: chrysosporium
clinical_significance: A genus of fungi found in soil and decaying plant material. Human infections are uncommon but can affect skin, lungs, or other tissues, particularly in people with weakened immunity.

name: chyle
clinical_significance: A milky fluid formed in intestinal lymph vessels after a meal. It contains lymph and absorbed dietary fat and normally travels through the thoracic duct into the bloodstream.

name: chylomicron
clinical_significance: A particle made by the intestine after eating fat. It carries dietary fat and cholesterol through the lymph and blood, then leaves remnants for the liver to remove.

name: chylomicron remnant
clinical_significance: A remnant particle left after a chylomicron delivers dietary fats to tissues. The liver normally removes it; elevated remnant particles can carry cholesterol and contribute to artery plaque.

name: chylothorax
clinical_significance: A buildup of chyle in the space around a lung, usually after injury or blockage of the thoracic duct. It can cause breathlessness and requires treatment of the leak, often with drainage and dietary or surgical measures.

name: chylous ascites
clinical_significance: Accumulation of lymphatic fluid rich in triglycerides within the abdominal cavity. It can result from lymphatic obstruction, malignancy, trauma, surgery, infection, or congenital disease and may cause abdominal distention, malnutrition, or immune-cell loss.

name: chymase
clinical_significance: An enzyme released mainly from mast cells that can promote inflammation and form angiotensin II in tissues. It is studied in allergy, cardiovascular disease, and fibrosis but is not a routine diagnostic test.

name: chymosin
clinical_significance: An enzyme that curdles milk by cutting a milk protein, important in digestion of milk by young mammals and in cheese-making. It is not a human diagnostic marker or treatment.

name: chymotrypsin
clinical_significance: Chymotrypsin is a pancreatic digestive enzyme that cleaves proteins in the small intestine; abnormal pancreatic release can contribute to tissue injury.

name: cicatrix
clinical_significance: A scar formed when tissue heals after injury, surgery, or inflammation. Scar tissue may be painless, but depending on its location it can restrict movement, distort an organ, or cause discomfort.

name: ciclopirox
clinical_significance: A topical antifungal medicine used for some skin and nail infections. Nail treatment can take months because the damaged nail must grow out; local irritation or rash may occur.

name: cidofovir
clinical_significance: Cidofovir is an antiviral nucleotide analogue used for selected serious DNA-virus infections; kidney toxicity requires careful dosing and monitoring.

name: cigar smoker
clinical_significance: A person who smokes cigars and is exposed to tobacco smoke and nicotine. Cigar smoking increases risks of cancers of the mouth, throat, oesophagus, and lung, as well as heart and lung disease; it is not a safe alternative to cigarettes.

name: cilengitide
clinical_significance: An investigational medicine that blocks integrins, proteins involved in cell attachment and blood-vessel formation. It was studied for cancer treatment but is not an established routine therapy.

name: ciliary body
clinical_significance: A ring-shaped part of the eye between the iris and choroid. Its muscle changes the lens shape for focusing, and its processes make the fluid that fills the front of the eye.

name: ciliary dyskinesia
clinical_significance: Abnormal movement of cilia that impairs clearance of mucus from the airways and can cause recurrent respiratory infections.

name: ciliophora
clinical_significance: A group of single-celled organisms with hair-like cilia used for movement or feeding. Most live in water; Balantioides coli, formerly called Balantidium coli, is a rare intestinal parasite of humans.

name: cilium
clinical_significance: A microscopic hair-like projection on a cell surface. Motile cilia move mucus or fluid, while primary cilia sense signals; inherited ciliary defects can cause respiratory, fertility, kidney, or developmental disorders.

name: cilostazol
clinical_significance: A medicine that widens leg arteries and reduces platelet clumping to improve walking distance in selected people with peripheral artery disease. It is not used in heart failure and may cause headache, palpitations, or diarrhoea.

name: cimetidine
clinical_significance: Cimetidine is an H2-receptor antagonist that reduces gastric acid secretion; it has numerous drug interactions and is used less often than newer agents.

name: cinacalcet hydrochloride
clinical_significance: A medicine that lowers parathyroid hormone and blood calcium by increasing calcium-sensing receptor activity. It is used for selected parathyroid disorders and can cause dangerously low calcium, requiring blood-test monitoring.

name: cineangiography
clinical_significance: Motion-picture X-ray imaging of the heart or blood vessels while contrast material passes through them, used to show blood flow and moving cardiac structures.

name: cingulate cortex
clinical_significance: A brain region involved in emotion, attention, pain processing, decision-making, and regulation of autonomic responses. Injury or disease affecting it may alter these functions, but symptoms depend on the broader brain network involved.

name: cingulate gyrus
clinical_significance: A curved brain structure forming part of the limbic system. It contributes to emotion, attention, memory, pain processing, and autonomic regulation; clinical effects of injury depend on location and extent.

name: ciprofloxacin
clinical_significance: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used for selected bacterial infections; tendon injury, nerve effects, QT effects, and resistance limit indiscriminate use.

name: circadian rhythm
clinical_significance: An internal cycle of about 24 hours that helps regulate sleep, alertness, hormones, body temperature, and metabolism. Light and darkness reset the cycle each day through signals from the eyes to the brain.

name: circular dichroism
clinical_significance: A laboratory method that measures how a molecule absorbs circularly polarized light to infer its shape or folding. It is used in biochemical and drug research rather than routine patient testing.

name: circulating microRNA
clinical_significance: A small RNA molecule measured in blood or other body fluids as a possible indicator of disease or treatment response. These tests remain largely investigational because levels can vary and clinical standards are not established for most uses.

name: circulating neoplastic cell
clinical_significance: A cancer cell that has entered the bloodstream after leaving a primary or metastatic tumour. Specialized tests may help study cancer spread or treatment response, but they are not suitable as general cancer screening tests.

name: cirrhosis
clinical_significance: Severe scarring of the liver caused by long-term liver damage. Scar tissue replaces healthy liver tissue and can reduce liver function and blood flow. It may cause no symptoms at first, but later may cause tiredness, poor appetite, weight loss, itching, jaundice, swelling of the abdomen or legs, easy bruising or bleeding, or confusion. Severe cirrhosis may cause internal bleeding, liver failure, or liver cancer.

name: cisapride
clinical_significance: A medicine formerly used to improve movement in the stomach and intestines. It was withdrawn or severely restricted in many countries because it can prolong the heart’s electrical interval and cause dangerous arrhythmias.

name: cisplatin
clinical_significance: A platinum-based chemotherapy drug that forms DNA cross-links and is used to treat several cancers; important toxicities include kidney injury, hearing loss, neuropathy, and nausea.

name: citalopram
clinical_significance: Citalopram is a selective serotonin-reuptake inhibitor used to treat depression and some anxiety disorders; nausea, sexual effects, and QT prolongation are important considerations.

name: citicoline
clinical_significance: A substance involved in making cell-membrane phospholipids and acetylcholine. It is sold as a supplement and studied for neurologic uses, but evidence does not establish it as a general treatment for memory loss or stroke.

name: citrates
clinical_significance: Salts of citric acid used in medicines and body fluids. Depending on the formulation, citrate may bind calcium, help prevent some kidney stones, alkalinize urine, or prevent clotting in stored blood or dialysis circuits.

name: citrobacter
clinical_significance: A genus of gut-associated bacteria that can cause opportunistic urinary, bloodstream, wound, or respiratory infections. Some species have important antibiotic resistance, so culture and susceptibility results help guide treatment.

name: citrobacter amalonaticus
clinical_significance: A species of Citrobacter found in the environment and sometimes in human clinical specimens. It can rarely cause opportunistic urinary, bloodstream, or wound infection; the sample source and symptoms determine whether it represents disease.

name: citrobacter braakii
clinical_significance: A species of Citrobacter that can rarely cause opportunistic urinary, bloodstream, or wound infections, especially in people with serious underlying illness. Antibiotic susceptibility should guide treatment when infection is confirmed.

name: citrobacter farmeri
clinical_significance: A species of Citrobacter occasionally isolated from clinical specimens and rarely associated with human infection. Its clinical importance depends on the specimen source and evidence of illness; laboratory identification and susceptibility testing can guide care.

name: citrobacter freundii
clinical_significance: A species of Citrobacter that can cause urinary, bloodstream, respiratory, or abdominal infection, especially in hospitalized or medically vulnerable people. It may carry inducible antibiotic-resistance mechanisms, so susceptibility testing is important.

name: citrobacter koseri
clinical_significance: A species of Citrobacter that can cause urinary or bloodstream infection and is a notable cause of brain abscess and meningitis in newborns. Treatment depends on the infection site and antibiotic susceptibility.

name: citrobacter youngae
clinical_significance: A species of Citrobacter found in the environment and occasionally in clinical samples. Human infection is uncommon; significance depends on the specimen source and evidence of illness.

name: citrulline
clinical_significance: An amino acid made during protein metabolism and the urea cycle. Blood citrulline is measured in selected metabolic and intestinal disorders; abnormal levels require interpretation with other tests and the clinical context.

name: citrullinemia
clinical_significance: An inherited disorder in which the body cannot properly remove nitrogen through the urea cycle. Citrulline and ammonia build up, causing vomiting, poor feeding, sleepiness, confusion, seizures, coma, or death without urgent treatment.

name: cixutumumab
clinical_significance: An investigational antibody against the insulin-like growth-factor-1 receptor studied as a cancer treatment. It is not an established routine therapy.

name: cladosporium
clinical_significance: A widespread genus of dark-pigmented moulds found on plants, soil, and indoor surfaces. It can trigger allergy or asthma and rarely causes skin, sinus, eye, or invasive infection, especially in people with weakened immunity.

name: cladosporium werneckii
clinical_significance: An older name for Hortaea werneckii, a salt-tolerant fungus that causes tinea nigra, usually a painless brown or black patch on the palm or sole. The superficial infection is generally treatable with topical antifungal medicine.

name: clamp
clinical_significance: A surgical instrument used to grasp, compress, occlude, or hold tissue, blood vessels, tubing, or other structures.

name: clarithromycin
clinical_significance: Clarithromycin is a macrolide antibiotic used for selected bacterial and mycobacterial infections; interactions and QT prolongation are important risks.

name: class bivalvia
clinical_significance: A class of aquatic molluscs that includes clams, oysters, mussels, and scallops. Shellfish allergy can cause hives, swelling, breathing difficulty, or anaphylaxis, and contaminated shellfish can transmit foodborne illness.

name: classical lissencephaly
clinical_significance: A rare brain-development disorder in which the cerebral cortex is unusually smooth because neurons did not migrate normally before birth. It can cause severe developmental disability, seizures, feeding problems, and shortened life expectancy.

name: classification
clinical_significance: Grouping clinical findings, diseases, organisms, or treatments into defined categories. Standardized classification supports communication, research, coding, and clinical decisions, but the chosen system and purpose matter.

name: clathrin
clinical_significance: A major polymeric coat protein composed of three heavy and three light chains forming a three-legged triskelion, which self-assembles into a polyhedral basket-like lattice that coats and internalizes endocytic vesicles during receptor-mediated endocytosis.

name: claustral
clinical_significance: Relating to the claustrum, a thin deep-brain structure connected with several cortical regions. Its role in human awareness and cognition is still being studied; the term alone is not a clinical diagnosis.

name: claustrophobia
clinical_significance: An intense fear of enclosed or confined spaces that may cause anxiety, panic, or avoidance.

name: clavicle
clinical_significance: The collarbone, a curved bone running from the breastbone to the shoulder blade. It supports the shoulder and commonly breaks after a fall or direct blow, causing pain, swelling, or visible deformity.

name: clavispora lusitaniae
clinical_significance: A yeast species, also called Candida lusitaniae, that can rarely cause bloodstream or other opportunistic infections. Some isolates resist amphotericin B, so antifungal susceptibility testing can guide treatment.

name: clavulanic acid
clinical_significance: A beta-lactamase inhibitor combined with certain penicillin antibiotics, such as amoxicillin, to protect them from bacterial enzymes that would otherwise break them down. Clavulanic acid alone is not an antibiotic.

name: clear cell
clinical_significance: A description of cells that look clear under a microscope because they contain little visible stain or have lost material during processing. It occurs in several unrelated tumours and conditions, so tissue origin and additional tests determine its meaning.

name: cleaved
clinical_significance: Describes a molecule or structure that has been cut into smaller parts, often by an enzyme. In clinical testing, the significance depends on which protein or molecule was cleaved and the assay being used.

name: cleft lip
clinical_significance: A birth defect in which the upper lip does not join completely before birth. The opening may be small or extend toward the nose and may occur alone or with a cleft palate, affecting feeding, teeth, or speech.

name: cleft mandible
clinical_significance: A rare birth defect in which a gap or split affects the lower jaw. It may interfere with feeding, breathing, or tooth alignment and can occur with other craniofacial differences.

name: cleft palate
clinical_significance: A birth defect in which the roof of the mouth does not close completely before birth, leaving an opening between the mouth and nose. It can affect feeding, speech, hearing, and dental development and is usually repaired by a specialist team.

name: cleidocranial dysplasia
clinical_significance: An inherited disorder of bone development affecting the collarbones and skull. It can cause delayed closure of skull joints, unusual teeth, short stature, and other skeletal differences.

name: clenbuterol
clinical_significance: A long-acting beta-2 agonist used as a bronchodilator in some countries and also misused for weight loss or athletic performance. It can cause tremor, rapid heartbeat, low potassium, dangerous arrhythmias, or cardiac injury and is not approved for human use in the United States.

name: clindamycin
clinical_significance: Clindamycin is a lincosamide antibiotic used for selected infections; diarrhea and Clostridioides difficile colitis are important adverse effects.

name: clinic
clinical_significance: A healthcare setting where people receive assessment, diagnosis, treatment, or follow-up, often without an overnight hospital stay. Clinics vary in specialty, staffing, services, and access.

name: clinical
clinical_significance: Relating to direct observation, examination, diagnosis, or treatment of a patient, rather than solely to laboratory or basic research findings.

name: clinical chemistry
clinical_significance: Laboratory testing of blood, urine, and other specimens to measure chemicals, proteins, hormones, enzymes, and metabolites. Results help assess organ function, diagnose illness, monitor treatment, and screen for some conditions.

name: clinical medicine
clinical_significance: The practice of diagnosing, treating, and preventing illness through direct care of patients. It integrates examination, tests, clinical evidence, treatment choices, and patient preferences.

name: clinical research
clinical_significance: Research involving people or their health data or samples to improve prevention, diagnosis, or treatment. It includes observational studies and clinical trials and requires ethical review, informed consent when applicable, and protections for participants.

name: clinical response
clinical_significance: A measurable change in a person’s health, symptoms, function, or test results after an illness or treatment. Its meaning depends on how it was assessed, when it occurred, and whether the change matters to the patient.

name: clinical trial
clinical_significance: A planned study in which people receive or are observed for an intervention to assess safety, effectiveness, or other health outcomes. Trials have defined protocols and oversight; phases and design determine what questions they can answer.

name: clinical trials
clinical_significance: Studies involving people that assess medical interventions, prevention, diagnosis, or health outcomes. They include clinical trials and observational research; ethical review and safeguards protect participants.

name: clinician
clinical_significance: A healthcare professional who assesses or treats patients, such as a physician, nurse practitioner, or other licensed provider. Training and scope of practice depend on the profession and jurisdiction.

name: clioquinol
clinical_significance: A quinoline-related antimicrobial used mainly in topical products in some countries. Oral use has been linked to serious nerve and vision injury, so it is not used systemically in many places.

name: clip
clinical_significance: A device used to hold tissue or structures together; surgical clips can close blood vessels, mark tissue, or occlude structures such as the vas deferens.

name: clitoral gland
clinical_significance: A small glandular structure described in some anatomical sources near the clitoris or urethral opening. The term is uncommon in routine care; symptoms or lesions in the area should be assessed according to their exact location.

name: clitoris
clinical_significance: A highly sensitive erectile organ at the front of the vulva, composed largely of erectile tissue and rich in sensory nerves. It contributes to sexual sensation; pain, injury, or persistent swelling may need clinical assessment.

name: cloaca chamber
clinical_significance: A chamber in the cloaca of birds and some other animals where the digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts open. It is important in veterinary anatomy and embryology but has no adult human counterpart.

name: clobazam
clinical_significance: A benzodiazepine medicine used with other treatments for seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. It can cause sleepiness, dependence, and dangerous breathing suppression, especially with opioids or other sedatives.

name: clobetasol propionate
clinical_significance: A super-high-potency corticosteroid applied to the skin for selected inflammatory skin diseases. Prolonged or extensive use can thin the skin or suppress the body’s steroid production, so treatment is limited and monitored.

name: clodronic acid
clinical_significance: A bisphosphonate medicine used in some countries for conditions involving abnormal bone breakdown, including cancer-related bone disease. Risks can include low calcium, kidney effects, and jawbone injury; availability and indications vary.

name: clofarabine
clinical_significance: A chemotherapy medicine used for some children and young adults with acute lymphoblastic leukemia that has returned or resisted prior treatment. It can cause severe low blood counts, infection, liver injury, and other serious effects.

name: clofazimine
clinical_significance: Clofazimine is a riminophenazine antimicrobial used mainly in multidrug treatment of leprosy and selected mycobacterial infections; skin discoloration is common.

name: clofibrate
clinical_significance: An older fibrate medicine formerly used to lower blood triglycerides and cholesterol. It is rarely used now because of adverse effects and the availability of safer, more effective lipid-lowering treatments.

name: clomiphene
clinical_significance: A medicine that stimulates ovulation and is used for selected causes of infertility. It can cause ovarian enlargement, visual symptoms, or multiple pregnancy, so treatment and ultrasound monitoring are individualized.

name: clomipramine
clinical_significance: Clomipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant particularly effective for obsessive-compulsive disorder; anticholinergic, cardiac, and overdose toxicity are important.

name: clonal anergy
clinical_significance: A state in which an immune cell remains alive but becomes unable to respond to a particular antigen. Clonal anergy helps prevent autoimmunity but can also weaken immune responses to infection or cancer.

name: clonal deletion
clinical_significance: A process in which developing immune cells that strongly recognize the body’s own tissues are eliminated. It helps establish immune tolerance; failure of this process can contribute to autoimmune disease.

name: clonal evolution
clinical_significance: The gradual change of a cancer as groups of tumor cells acquire different genetic changes. Groups that grow faster, spread more easily, or resist treatment can become dominant and make the cancer progress or recur.

name: clonal expansion
clinical_significance: Multiplication of cells descended from one original cell. It may occur when immune cells respond to a trigger or when an abnormal cell population grows in cancer or another disorder.

name: clonazepam
clinical_significance: Clonazepam is a benzodiazepine anticonvulsant and anxiolytic that enhances GABA activity; sedation, dependence, and respiratory depression can occur.

name: clone
clinical_significance: A group of cells descended from one original cell and sharing its genetic features. Cell clones are used in laboratory research and cell therapies; an abnormal clone can expand in cancers or blood disorders.

name: clone cell
clinical_significance: A cell grown from one original cell or cell line and sharing its genetic makeup. Clonal cells are used in research, diagnostics, and biotechnology, but laboratory findings may not fully predict behaviour in the human body.

name: clonic seizures
clinical_significance: A seizure pattern with repeated rhythmic jerking of muscles. It may involve one body region or both sides and can occur with loss of awareness; a prolonged seizure or repeated seizures without recovery require emergency care.

name: clonidine
clinical_significance: Clonidine stimulates central alpha-2 receptors to reduce sympathetic outflow and is used for hypertension and selected other conditions; abrupt withdrawal can cause rebound hypertension.

name: clonidine hydrochloride
clinical_significance: The hydrochloride salt form of clonidine, a centrally acting medicine that reduces sympathetic nerve signals. It is used for selected blood-pressure and other conditions; abrupt discontinuation can cause rebound high blood pressure.

name: cloning
clinical_significance: Production of genetically similar copies of a DNA segment, cell, or organism. In medicine, molecular and cell cloning support research and biomanufacturing; reproductive cloning of humans is not an accepted clinical practice.

name: clonorchis sinensis
clinical_significance: A liver fluke acquired by eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish. It can live in the bile ducts, cause inflammation or obstruction, and chronic infection increases the risk of bile-duct cancer.

name: clonus
clinical_significance: Repeated, rhythmic muscle jerks triggered by suddenly stretching a muscle, often at the ankle. It commonly indicates overactive reflexes from a problem affecting the brain or spinal cord.

name: clopamide
clinical_significance: A thiazide-like diuretic used in some countries for high blood pressure or fluid retention. It increases salt and water loss in urine and can cause low potassium or sodium, gout, or dehydration.

name: clopidogrel
clinical_significance: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet drug that irreversibly blocks the platelet P2Y12 receptor, reducing arterial thrombosis risk after selected cardiovascular events or procedures.

name: clorazepate dipotassium
clinical_significance: A benzodiazepine medicine used for short-term treatment of anxiety or alcohol withdrawal in some settings. It can cause sedation, impaired coordination, dependence, and dangerous breathing suppression with opioids or alcohol.

name: clostridiaceae
clinical_significance: A family of anaerobic, often spore-forming bacteria that includes Clostridium and related genera. Some produce potent toxins or cause wound, intestinal, or bloodstream infections; significance depends on the species and sample site.

name: clostridium
clinical_significance: A genus of anaerobic, often spore-forming bacteria found in soil and the gut. Some species cause serious disease through toxins or tissue invasion, including botulism, tetanus, gas gangrene, and food poisoning; names for some species have changed as taxonomy is updated.

name: clostridium acetobutylicum
clinical_significance: A soil bacterium used in industrial fermentation to produce acetone and butanol. It is not a usual cause of human disease.

name: clostridium aldenense
clinical_significance: A rare Clostridium species occasionally found in clinical specimens. Its role in human disease is not well established; a finding should be interpreted with the body site, symptoms, and specimen quality.

name: clostridium baratii
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species that can produce botulinum neurotoxin type F and has rarely caused human botulism. Suspected botulism is a medical emergency because paralysis can affect breathing.

name: clostridium beijerinckii
clinical_significance: A soil bacterium used in fermentation and production of solvents and other chemicals. It is not a common human pathogen.

name: clostridium bifermentans
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species occasionally isolated from human infections, including wounds or blood, but clinical disease is uncommon. Significance depends on specimen source and evidence of tissue infection.

name: clostridium bolteae
clinical_significance: A gut-associated Clostridium species that has been reported in occasional bloodstream, abdominal, or other infections. It is an uncommon opportunistic pathogen, and culture findings need clinical interpretation.

name: clostridium botulinum
clinical_significance: A bacterium that produces botulinum toxin, which blocks nerve signals to muscles and causes weakness or paralysis. Food, wounds, or swallowed spores can cause botulism, a medical emergency affecting breathing and swallowing.

name: clostridium butyricum
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species found in soil and sometimes in the human gut. Rare toxin-producing strains can cause botulism, so identification of a toxin-producing isolate requires public-health and clinical evaluation.

name: clostridium cadaveris
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium found in the human intestine and environment. It rarely causes opportunistic infection, such as bloodstream or wound infection, usually in people with serious underlying illness.

name: clostridium celatum
clinical_significance: An uncommon anaerobic bacterium occasionally recovered from clinical specimens. It is not a frequent human pathogen; the site of isolation and evidence of infection determine its importance.

name: clostridium citroniae
clinical_significance: A species of anaerobic bacteria found in the gut and occasionally in infections such as appendicitis or bloodstream infection. Its clinical importance depends on specimen source and the patient’s condition.

name: clostridium cochlearium
clinical_significance: A rare anaerobic bacterium reported in human infections, including abscesses. When isolated, clinicians consider whether it is a true pathogen or part of mixed growth from a nonsterile site.

name: clostridium cocleatum
clinical_significance: A rare anaerobic bacterium occasionally reported in clinical specimens. Its clinical significance is uncertain and depends on whether it is recovered from a normally sterile site with compatible signs of infection.

name: clostridium difficile
clinical_significance: Clostridioides difficile can cause antibiotic-associated diarrhea and life-threatening colitis; appropriate testing, infection-control precautions, and recurrence monitoring are important.

name: clostridium fallax
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species that is rarely reported from human clinical samples. A positive result should be interpreted with the specimen source, symptoms, and other microbiology findings.

name: clostridium glycolicum
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium found in soil and other environments that has occasionally been isolated from human infections. Its role is uncommon and should be assessed in the context of the clinical specimen.

name: clostridium haemolyticum
clinical_significance: A toxin-producing Clostridium species that primarily causes haemolytic disease in animals. Human infection is very rare; laboratory identification warrants specialist interpretation.

name: clostridium hathewayi
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium found in the intestine and occasionally associated with human bloodstream or abdominal infections. It is an uncommon opportunistic pathogen; antibiotic susceptibility can guide treatment.

name: clostridium histolyticum
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium that produces enzymes capable of breaking down tissue proteins. It is used in laboratory and industrial settings and has rarely been associated with wound or soft-tissue infection.

name: clostridium infection
clinical_significance: Infection caused by a Clostridium species. Illness ranges from food poisoning to wound infection, botulism, tetanus, or toxin-mediated tissue damage; treatment depends on the species, toxin, and site.

name: clostridium innocuum
clinical_significance: A gut-associated Clostridium species that can occasionally cause bloodstream, wound, or other opportunistic infection. Some isolates resist vancomycin, so species identification and susceptibility results can be important.

name: clostridium limosum
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium rarely isolated in human infection. Its significance depends on whether it is recovered from a sterile site and fits the patient’s clinical picture.

name: clostridium novyi
clinical_significance: A soil bacterium whose toxin can cause severe wound infection and tissue destruction, including gas gangrene. Human infection is uncommon but requires urgent surgical and antimicrobial treatment.

name: clostridium oceanicum
clinical_significance: A marine-associated anaerobic bacterium occasionally recovered from clinical samples. Human disease is rare, and an isolate requires interpretation with the sample source and evidence of infection.

name: clostridium oroticum
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species rarely reported in human clinical samples. Its clinical role is not well established and should be interpreted alongside symptoms and culture quality.

name: clostridium perfringens
clinical_significance: A bacterium that can cause rapidly destructive muscle infection with gas in tissues or food poisoning with sudden diarrhea and abdominal cramps. Severe wound infection requires emergency surgery and antibiotics.

name: clostridium ramosum
clinical_significance: A gut-associated anaerobic bacterium, now commonly classified as Erysipelatoclostridium ramosum. It can rarely cause opportunistic bloodstream or tissue infection, particularly in people with underlying illness.

name: clostridium rectum
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium associated with the intestinal tract and rarely reported in human infections. Clinical relevance depends on whether it is isolated from a normally sterile site with compatible illness.

name: clostridium sartagoforme
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species associated mainly with animals and the environment. Human infection is rare; identification from a clinical specimen should be interpreted in context.

name: clostridium septicum
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species that can cause spontaneous gas gangrene, sometimes without an obvious wound, and is associated with underlying colorectal or blood cancers. Rapidly progressive pain, swelling, or systemic illness requires emergency care.

name: clostridium sordellii
clinical_significance: A toxin-producing Clostridium species that can rarely cause severe soft-tissue infection and toxic shock, including after pregnancy-related procedures or wounds. Illness may progress rapidly and requires emergency treatment.

name: clostridium spiroforme
clinical_significance: A bacterium that primarily causes enteritis in rabbits. Human infection is rare; if isolated from a person, clinical significance depends on the specimen and evidence that it is causing disease.

name: clostridium sporogenes
clinical_significance: A spore-forming anaerobic bacterium found in soil and the environment and used in laboratory research. Human infection is uncommon, but occasional opportunistic isolates should be interpreted with clinical findings.

name: clostridium subterminale
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium occasionally isolated from human infections, including wounds or blood, but disease is rare. Its significance depends on specimen source, symptoms, and whether it is recovered with other organisms.

name: clostridium symbiosum
clinical_significance: A Clostridium species that normally occurs in the intestine and has occasionally been associated with bloodstream or abdominal infection. It is an uncommon opportunistic pathogen and requires clinical interpretation when isolated.

name: clostridium tertium
clinical_significance: An anaerobic bacterium that can cause bloodstream infection, especially in people with blood cancers, low white-cell counts, or recent chemotherapy. It may tolerate oxygen better than many Clostridium species and can show antibiotic resistance.

name: clostridium tetani
clinical_significance: A soil bacterium whose toxin causes tetanus after entering a wound. It produces painful muscle stiffness and spasms, often beginning in the jaw, and can interfere with swallowing and breathing; vaccination prevents it.

name: clostridium tyrobutyricum
clinical_significance: A bacterium used in dairy and food research because it can produce butyric acid and spoil some cheeses. It is not a common human pathogen.

name: clostridium ventriculi
clinical_significance: A bacterium now generally called Sarcina ventriculi, occasionally found in the stomach. Detection has been associated with delayed gastric emptying, gastritis, and rare serious complications, but its role should be interpreted with the patient’s symptoms and pathology.

name: clotrimazole
clinical_significance: Clotrimazole is an azole antifungal used topically or orally in selected formulations for fungal infections of skin, mouth, or vagina.

name: clotting factor
clinical_significance: A protein in the blood that participates in forming a clot. Deficiency or dysfunction can cause excessive bleeding, while excess activity or abnormal regulation may contribute to thrombosis; tests identify specific factors.

name: clove oil
clinical_significance: Clove oil contains eugenol and is used in some dental and topical products; concentrated ingestion or exposure can cause irritation, liver injury, or seizures.

name: cloxacillin
clinical_significance: A penicillin-family antibiotic used in some countries for infections caused by susceptible staphylococci, including selected skin, bone, or bloodstream infections. Allergy and antibiotic-associated diarrhoea are possible.

name: clozapine
clinical_significance: Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and selected suicidality risk; neutropenia, myocarditis, seizures, constipation, and metabolic effects require monitoring.

name: clubbed finger
clinical_significance: A rounded enlargement of the ends of the fingers, often with curved nails, that may signal long-term lung, heart, liver, bowel, or other disease. New or unexplained clubbing should be evaluated for an underlying cause.

name: clubbing
clinical_significance: Enlargement and rounding of the fingertips or toes with more curved nails and loss of the normal nail angle. It may accompany long-term lung, heart, bowel, liver, or other disease and should be medically assessed.

name: cluster headache
clinical_significance: Repeated attacks of extremely severe pain around or behind one eye, lasting about 15 minutes to three hours. The same side may tear, redden, swell, or feel congested, and the person often becomes restless.

name: clusterin
clinical_significance: A protein involved in cell stress responses, protein handling, and regulation of cell survival. It is studied as a possible biomarker in cancer and inflammatory disease, but it is not specific enough to diagnose a condition alone.

name: cmax
clinical_significance: The highest concentration of a medicine measured in blood after a dose. It helps describe absorption and exposure and can guide dose studies, but its meaning depends on the drug, timing, and therapeutic range.

name: cnidaria
clinical_significance: A group of aquatic animals that includes jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones. Some produce venom that can cause painful skin injury, systemic poisoning, or allergic reactions after a sting.

name: cns metastases
clinical_significance: Cancer that has spread to the brain, spinal cord, or their coverings from another site. It can cause headache, seizures, weakness, confusion, or other neurologic problems; treatment depends on the cancer type, number and location of lesions, and overall health.

name: coagulating gland
clinical_significance: A glandular structure in the male reproductive tract of some mammals, especially rodents, that adds proteins to seminal fluid and helps it coagulate. It has no direct human anatomical counterpart.

name: coal
clinical_significance: A combustible rock containing carbon and mineral matter. Mining and burning coal can expose people to dust, smoke, and pollutants that contribute to lung disease, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.

name: coal tar
clinical_significance: A thick by-product of coal processing used in some topical medicines for psoriasis and eczema. It can irritate skin and increase sensitivity to sunlight; long-term occupational exposure has different cancer risks from controlled topical use.

name: coated pit
clinical_significance: A membrane pit coated with clathrin proteins that helps cells take up receptors, nutrients, and other molecules. It is important in cell biology and is not a routine clinical finding.

name: coated vesicle
clinical_significance: A small membrane-bound compartment coated with proteins such as clathrin that transports substances within or into a cell. It supports receptor recycling and cellular trafficking and is mainly a research term.

name: cobalamin
clinical_significance: Vitamin B12, a nutrient needed for DNA production, healthy red blood cells, nerve function, and normal processing of certain fats and proteins.

name: cobalt
clinical_significance: Cobalt is a metal present in vitamin B12 and some industrial materials; excess exposure can injure the heart, thyroid, lungs, or skin.

name: Cobb syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare congenital disorder in which vascular malformations occur in a segmental pattern across the skin and deeper tissues, often including the spinal cord. Spinal lesions can cause pain, weakness, sensory loss, or bowel and bladder problems.

name: cobblestone lissencephaly
clinical_significance: A severe brain-development disorder in which abnormal neuronal migration produces a cobblestone-like brain surface. It is often associated with muscular dystrophy and eye abnormalities and can cause profound developmental disability and seizures.

name: cobicistat
clinical_significance: A medicine used with certain HIV drugs to slow their breakdown and increase their blood levels. It has no HIV-fighting activity by itself and can interact with many medicines, so the full regimen must be reviewed for interactions.

name: cocaine
clinical_significance: A stimulant drug that blocks monoamine reuptake and can also act as a local anesthetic; use can cause dependence, cardiovascular complications, seizures, stroke, and overdose.

name: coccidia
clinical_significance: A broad group of microscopic parasites that infect animals and sometimes people. Human intestinal disease is caused by selected coccidia, such as Cystoisospora, and is often more severe in people with weakened immunity.

name: coccidioides immitis
clinical_significance: A dimorphic soil fungus and a principal cause of coccidioidomycosis, or Valley fever, acquired by inhaling airborne arthroconidia. Infection is usually pulmonary but can disseminate, especially in people with impaired cellular immunity.

name: coccidioidomycosis
clinical_significance: A fungal infection caused by Coccidioides fungi, usually acquired by breathing spores from disturbed soil. It most often affects the lungs and causes cough, fever, tiredness, or chest pain; rarely, it spreads to the skin, bones, joints, or brain.

name: coccidiosis
clinical_significance: Infection caused by microscopic parasites called coccidia. It usually affects the intestine and may cause watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, vomiting, dehydration, or weight loss; severe or widespread disease is more likely when immunity is weakened.

name: coccyx
clinical_significance: The small pointed bone at the bottom of the spine, commonly called the tailbone. It connects to the sacrum, supports pelvic-floor tissues, and may become painful after a fall, childbirth, or prolonged sitting.

name: cochlea
clinical_significance: The spiral-shaped part of the inner ear that changes sound vibrations into nerve signals. Fluid movement inside it stimulates sensory hair cells, allowing the brain to recognize pitch and loudness.

name: cochlear duct
clinical_significance: The coiled, endolymph-filled membranous tube of the inner ear, situated between the scala vestibuli and scala tympani, housing the organ of Corti along its basilar membrane for auditory sensory transduction.

name: cochlear implant
clinical_significance: An electronic device for severe hearing loss that bypasses damaged inner-ear hair cells and stimulates the hearing nerve. It can provide useful sound perception but does not restore normal hearing and requires training.

name: cochlear nerve
clinical_significance: The nerve carrying sound signals from the inner ear to the brainstem. Damage can cause sensorineural hearing loss and may affect eligibility or outcomes for a cochlear implant.

name: cochlear nucleus
clinical_significance: A group of brainstem nerve cells that receives sound signals from the cochlea and relays them to higher auditory centres. Damage can disrupt hearing pathways and sound localization.

name: Cockayne syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited disorder in which cells cannot repair some types of DNA damage normally. It causes poor growth, developmental delay, worsening nerve problems, sensitivity to sunlight, hearing or vision loss, and an appearance of premature aging.

name: coconut oil
clinical_significance: A plant oil high in saturated fat, used in foods and skin products. Frequent dietary use may raise LDL cholesterol compared with unsaturated oils; topical products can cause irritation or allergy in some people.

name: codeine
clinical_significance: An opioid medicine used for some pain and cough indications. It can cause sleepiness, constipation, dependence, and life-threatening breathing suppression; metabolism varies, and extra caution is needed with children and other sedatives.

name: codeine phosphate
clinical_significance: The phosphate salt form of codeine, an opioid used for selected pain or cough indications. It can cause dependence and dangerous breathing suppression, especially with other sedatives or in people who metabolize it rapidly.

name: codon
clinical_significance: A group of three genetic building blocks in messenger RNA that specifies one amino acid or signals the end of protein production. Several different codons can specify the same amino acid.

name: coenzyme
clinical_significance: A small organic molecule that helps an enzyme carry out a chemical reaction. Many coenzymes come from vitamins and temporarily carry chemical groups or electrons.

name: coenzyme A
clinical_significance: A coenzyme required for many reactions in energy production and metabolism of fats, carbohydrates, and proteins. It is present in cells throughout the body and has no routine clinical test role by itself.

name: cognition
clinical_significance: The mental processes involved in acquiring, storing, retrieving, and using information, including attention, memory, language, reasoning, and judgment.

name: cognition disorder
clinical_significance: A decline or difficulty in one or more thinking abilities, such as memory, attention, language, or planning. Causes include neurologic disease, mental-health conditions, medicines, delirium, and systemic illness; assessment looks for treatable causes and impact on daily life.

name: cognitive behavior therapy
clinical_significance: A talking treatment that helps a person notice unhelpful thoughts and behaviors and develop more useful ways to respond. It is used for problems such as anxiety, depression, pain, insomnia, and some eating disorders.

name: cognitive impairment
clinical_significance: A decline in thinking abilities such as memory, attention, language, judgment, or problem solving. It may be mild with independence preserved or severe enough to interfere with everyday activities.

name: cognitive reserve
clinical_significance: The brain's ability to use alternative strategies or networks to maintain function despite injury or disease.

name: cohort
clinical_significance: A group of people who share a defined characteristic or experience during a specified period and are studied over time or compared with another group.

name: cohort study
clinical_significance: An observational study that identifies groups based on an exposure or other characteristic and compares the incidence of disease or other outcomes between them over time. It may be prospective or retrospective and commonly estimates relative risk.

name: coil device
clinical_significance: A medical coil, often a small metal device placed through a catheter to block blood flow in an aneurysm or abnormal vessel. It can prevent rupture or reduce bleeding, but carries risks such as clot, vessel injury, or incomplete closure.

name: coiled body
clinical_significance: A coiled structure in the cell nucleus, often referring to a Cajal body involved in processing RNA and assembling components used in gene expression. It is mainly a cell-biology research term.

name: coinfection
clinical_significance: Two or more infections present in the same person at the same time, such as HIV with tuberculosis or a viral and bacterial respiratory infection. Coinfection can alter symptoms, test interpretation, treatment, and disease severity.

name: coitus
clinical_significance: Sexual intercourse, traditionally meaning penile-vaginal penetration; the term does not include every form of sexual activity or intimate contact.

name: coitus interruptus
clinical_significance: The withdrawal method of contraception, in which the penis is removed from the vagina before ejaculation; it is less reliable than many other contraceptive methods.

name: colchicine
clinical_significance: A medicine used to treat gout flares and prevent attacks, and for familial Mediterranean fever. It reduces inflammation but has a narrow safety margin; overdose and interactions can cause severe muscle, nerve, blood-cell, or organ toxicity.

name: cold injury
clinical_significance: Harm caused by low temperature, including hypothermia, frostbite, chilblains, and nonfreezing tissue injury. Risk increases with prolonged exposure, wetness, wind, or poor circulation and may affect the whole body or a local area.

name: cold ischemia
clinical_significance: Reduced blood flow and oxygen to tissue while it is outside the body or before it is cooled or transplanted. Longer cold-ischemia time can damage organs and reduce the likelihood of successful transplantation.

name: colectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part or all of the colon. It may treat cancer, severe inflammatory bowel disease, diverticular complications, blocked bowel, or inherited high cancer risk; the amount removed depends on the disease.

name: colectomy partial
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove a section of the colon while leaving the rest in place. It may be performed for cancer, diverticular disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or blockage; effects on bowel function depend on the location and amount removed.

name: colesevelam hydrochloride
clinical_significance: A bile-acid-binding medicine used with diet and exercise to lower LDL cholesterol. It can also help some cases of bile-acid diarrhea; constipation, bloating, and reduced absorption of other medicines or vitamins may occur.

name: colestipol
clinical_significance: A bile-acid-binding medicine used to lower LDL cholesterol and sometimes relieve bile-acid diarrhea or itching from cholestasis. It can cause constipation and interfere with absorption of other medicines and fat-soluble vitamins.

name: colforsin
clinical_significance: A synthetic activator of adenylate cyclase studied or used in selected settings as an intravenous medicine to increase heart contraction and relax blood vessels. It can lower blood pressure or cause abnormal heart rhythms and requires monitoring.

name: colicin
clinical_significance: A protein toxin produced by some strains of Escherichia coli that kills or inhibits competing bacteria. It is studied in microbiology and is not a routine human treatment.

name: coliform bacteria
clinical_significance: Bacteria used as indicators of possible faecal contamination in water or food. Many coliforms are harmless, so detection signals a need to assess sanitation but does not prove that a disease-causing organism is present.

name: coliphage
clinical_significance: A virus that infects Escherichia coli bacteria. Coliphages are used in research and as indicators of faecal contamination; selected bacteriophages are being studied as alternatives or additions to antibiotics.

name: colitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the colon, which may cause diarrhea, abdominal pain, blood or mucus in stool, fever, or urgency. Causes include infection, inflammatory bowel disease, reduced blood flow, medicines, and radiation.

name: collagen
clinical_significance: A strong protein that forms much of the body's connective tissue. Different types support and strengthen skin, bone, cartilage, tendons, ligaments, blood vessels, and many internal structures.

name: collagen disease
clinical_significance: An older, broad term for diseases that affect connective tissues and often involve abnormal immune activity. Modern medical writing usually names the specific disease instead.

name: collagen fibril
clinical_significance: A bundle of collagen molecules that gives connective tissues tensile strength. Abnormal fibril formation or breakdown can weaken skin, tendons, bone, blood vessels, or other tissues.

name: collagenase
clinical_significance: An enzyme that breaks down collagen, a major structural protein in skin, bone, cartilage, and connective tissue. Natural collagenases help remodel tissue, while medicines or bacterial enzymes can be used in selected treatments or cause tissue damage.

name: collagenous sprue
clinical_significance: A rare small-intestinal disorder with collagen deposited beneath the lining, damaging absorptive villi and causing severe diarrhoea, weight loss, and malnutrition. It can resemble coeliac disease but may not improve with a gluten-free diet.

name: collateral circulation
clinical_significance: Alternate blood-vessel routes that develop or enlarge when a main artery becomes narrowed or blocked. They may partly maintain blood flow to tissue, but they may not prevent symptoms or injury if the blockage is severe.

name: colles fracture
clinical_significance: A break near the wrist end of the larger forearm bone, with the broken hand-side fragment displaced backward. It usually follows a fall onto an outstretched hand and causes wrist pain, swelling, and deformity.

name: collinsella
clinical_significance: A genus of bacteria commonly found in the human intestine and mouth. Some species are studied as part of the normal microbiota; a clinical isolate should be interpreted according to the specimen site and evidence of disease.

name: collinsella aerofaciens
clinical_significance: A species of Collinsella that commonly occurs in the human intestine. It is generally considered part of the gut microbiota; detection in stool alone does not indicate infection.

name: collinsella intestinalis
clinical_significance: A species of Collinsella associated with the human intestinal microbiota. It is not a common pathogen, and clinical significance depends on whether it is isolated from a normally sterile site with compatible illness.

name: collodion
clinical_significance: A thin, collodion-like membrane over a newborn’s skin that can occur in several inherited skin disorders. It may impair temperature control and fluid balance and requires careful neonatal skin care and evaluation.

name: colloid
clinical_significance: A gelatin-like material or mixture of molecules suspended in fluid. In medicine, the term may refer to thyroid colloid, a colloid solution used for volume support, or a laboratory substance; significance depends on context.

name: coloboma
clinical_significance: A birth defect caused by incomplete formation of part of the eye, leaving a notch or gap in the iris, retina, choroid, or optic nerve. Vision problems vary with the structure and amount affected.

name: colon
clinical_significance: The main part of the large intestine between the small intestine and rectum. It absorbs water and salts and stores and moves stool through its ascending, transverse, descending, and sigmoid sections.

name: colon carcinoma
clinical_significance: A cancer arising in the colon, most often from gland-forming cells. It may cause blood in stool, anaemia, abdominal pain, or altered bowel habits, but early disease can have no symptoms; screening and colonoscopy can detect precancerous polyps.

name: colon disease
clinical_significance: Any disorder affecting the colon, including infection, inflammation, poor blood supply, diverticular disease, polyps, cancer, or motility problems. Symptoms and treatment depend on the specific cause.

name: colon neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in the colon that may be benign, precancerous, or cancerous. Colonoscopy and tissue testing determine its type; removing precancerous polyps can reduce future colorectal-cancer risk.

name: colon perforation
clinical_significance: A tear or hole through the wall of the colon, caused by injury, inflammation, obstruction, a procedure, or weakened tissue. It can leak bowel contents into the abdomen and cause peritonitis or sepsis, requiring urgent treatment.

name: colon polyp
clinical_significance: A growth from the inner lining of the colon. Most are benign, but some adenomas and serrated polyps can develop into cancer over time; colonoscopy can detect and remove many polyps.

name: colonic diverticulosis
clinical_significance: Small pouches in the wall of the colon without active inflammation. They are common with age and often cause no symptoms, but can sometimes bleed or become inflamed or infected.

name: colonic fistula
clinical_significance: An abnormal connection between the colon and another organ, body cavity, or skin. It can cause stool or gas to pass through an unusual route, recurrent infection, or leakage and may require surgery.

name: colonic inertia
clinical_significance: Abnormally slow movement of stool through the colon, causing persistent constipation, bloating, abdominal discomfort, and infrequent bowel movements. It is diagnosed after other causes of constipation have been considered.

name: colonic stenosis
clinical_significance: Narrowing of part of the large intestine that makes it harder for stool and gas to pass. Causes include scar tissue, inflammation, cancer, or reduced blood supply; symptoms may include pain, bloating, constipation, vomiting, or bowel blockage.

name: colonoscope
clinical_significance: A flexible, lighted instrument with a camera that is inserted through the anus to examine the rectum and colon. It can contain channels for air, irrigation, biopsy tools, or devices used to remove polyps.

name: colonoscopy
clinical_significance: An examination of the rectum and colon using a flexible camera. It can find inflammation, bleeding, tumors, and polyps and allows tissue sampling or removal of some polyps during the same procedure.

name: colony-stimulating factor
clinical_significance: A protein signal that prompts bone marrow to make particular blood cells, especially neutrophils or platelets. Medicines that mimic these signals can prevent or treat low blood counts during cancer therapy or marrow disease.

name: color
clinical_significance: A visual property used to describe the appearance of skin, eyes, tissue, or a sample. A color change can reflect bruising, jaundice, poor oxygenation, pigment, infection, or lighting and must be interpreted with other findings.

name: color assessment
clinical_significance: A structured evaluation of colour discrimination or colour appearance, often using standardized plates or instruments. It can identify colour-vision deficiency and may be used in occupational, eye, or neurologic assessment.

name: color blindness
clinical_significance: An inherited or acquired difficulty distinguishing some colours, most often red from green. It is usually harmless but can affect reading charts, certain occupations, or recognition of colour-coded signals; acquired changes may indicate eye or nerve disease.

name: color vision
clinical_significance: The ability to detect and distinguish colours through the retina and brain. Testing can identify inherited colour-vision deficiency or changes caused by eye disease, optic-nerve damage, medicines, or brain injury.

name: colorectal
clinical_significance: Colorectal conditions affect the colon or rectum and range from benign disorders to cancer. Colorectal cancer is common but often preventable or more treatable when detected through recommended screening.

name: colorectal adenoma
clinical_significance: A usually noncancerous gland-forming growth in the colon or rectum that may gradually develop into colorectal cancer.

name: colorectal carcinoma
clinical_significance: Colorectal carcinoma is a major cause of cancer illness and death. Screening can detect cancer early and remove precancerous lesions; stage and tumor features guide treatment and prognosis.

name: colorectal neoplasm
clinical_significance: A colorectal neoplasm may be benign, precancerous, or malignant. Tissue diagnosis and appropriate evaluation distinguish these categories because some lesions can progress to cancer.

name: colorectal polyposis
clinical_significance: Multiple colorectal polyps can signal an inherited polyposis syndrome, which may confer a high lifetime risk of colorectal cancer and warrant genetic evaluation, intensified surveillance, and sometimes preventive surgery.

name: colorimetry
clinical_significance: Colorimetry provides objective color measurements used in some laboratory, imaging, and vision assessments; results can help quantify changes that are difficult to judge by eye.

name: colostomy
clinical_significance: Surgery that brings part of the large intestine through an opening in the abdomen, called a stoma. Stool and gas leave through the stoma into a pouch. A colostomy may be temporary or permanent and may be needed for cancer, bowel blockage, severe infection, injury, or other bowel disease. Stoma nurses can teach people how to care for it and return to usual activities.

name: colostrum
clinical_significance: The thick yellowish breast fluid made during late pregnancy and the first days after birth. It provides concentrated nutrition and immune protection, especially through antibodies, to the newborn.

name: colposcope
clinical_significance: A lighted magnifying instrument used to examine the cervix, vagina, or vulva closely and guide biopsy of suspicious areas.

name: colposcopy
clinical_significance: An examination using a magnifying instrument to inspect the cervix, vagina, and vulva after a screening test shows an abnormality. The clinician may apply solutions and take tissue samples from suspicious areas.

name: columbinic acid
clinical_significance: Columbinic acid is a polyunsaturated fatty acid mainly encountered in biochemical and nutrition research. It has no established role as a diagnostic marker or treatment in routine clinical care.

name: coma
clinical_significance: A state of profound unresponsiveness in which a person cannot be awakened and does not show purposeful responses. Coma is a medical emergency that may result from brain injury, stroke, infection, poisoning, or metabolic disturbance and requires urgent evaluation.

name: comamonadaceae
clinical_significance: Comamonadaceae is a bacterial family that includes environmental organisms and occasional opportunistic human pathogens. Its clinical relevance depends on identifying a species from a meaningful patient specimen rather than environmental or contaminant growth.

name: comamonas
clinical_significance: Comamonas is a genus of mostly environmental bacteria that only rarely causes human infection. When isolated from blood or another normally sterile site, it may represent an opportunistic infection and should be interpreted with the clinical findings.

name: comamonas terrigena
clinical_significance: Comamonas terrigena is an environmental bacterium with rare reports of human infection. Its recovery from a clinical specimen should be assessed for true infection, especially when isolated from a normally sterile site.

name: comamonas testosteroni
clinical_significance: Comamonas testosteroni is an uncommon opportunistic cause of bloodstream, urinary, abdominal, and other infections. A clinically significant isolate warrants species identification and susceptibility-guided treatment because resistance can vary.

name: combination chemotherapy
clinical_significance: Combining chemotherapy drugs can improve cancer control by attacking tumor cells through different mechanisms, but can also increase toxicity. The regimen is selected for the cancer type, stage, and patient’s health.

name: combination therapy
clinical_significance: Using two or more treatments together may improve disease control or target different mechanisms, but can also increase adverse effects or interactions. The value and risks depend on the condition and specific treatments.

name: comedo
clinical_significance: A comedo is a plugged hair follicle that appears as an open blackhead or closed whitehead in acne. Persistent or inflamed lesions may contribute to acne scarring.

name: comet assay
clinical_significance: The comet assay measures DNA damage in cells and is used mainly in laboratory research and toxicology. It is not a routine diagnostic test for an individual patient.

name: common bile duct
clinical_significance: The tube formed when ducts from the liver and gallbladder join. It carries bile into the first part of the small intestine, where bile helps digest dietary fat.

name: common cold
clinical_significance: A common viral infection of the nose and throat that usually resolves without specific treatment. Antibiotics do not treat it; breathing difficulty, dehydration, or unusually severe or persistent symptoms may indicate another problem or a complication.

name: common migraine
clinical_significance: A migraine attack without a preceding aura. It usually causes moderate or severe throbbing pain lasting four to 72 hours, often with nausea or sensitivity to light or sound and worsening with routine activity.

name: common ventricle
clinical_significance: A rare congenital heart defect in which the heart has a single functional pumping chamber rather than two separate ventricles. It can cause low oxygen levels and heart failure and usually requires specialist care and staged surgery.

name: common wart
clinical_significance: A common wart is a benign skin growth caused by human papillomavirus. It often resolves on its own, but treatment may be used for discomfort, spread, or cosmetic concerns; genital warts are a separate condition.

name: community
clinical_significance: Community context can shape exposure to illness, access to care, and public-health prevention. Community-based services can support screening, vaccination, chronic disease care, and continuity outside hospitals.

name: comorbidity
clinical_significance: The presence of two or more health conditions in the same person. The conditions may affect one another and can make symptoms, medicine choices, and treatment planning more complicated.

name: comovirus
clinical_significance: Comovirus is a genus of plant viruses and is not known to cause human disease. Its significance is mainly agricultural and in plant-virus research.

name: compact bone
clinical_significance: Dense outer bone tissue arranged in strong cylindrical units called osteons. It provides most of the skeleton’s strength and protects inner marrow while supporting movement and weight-bearing.

name: comparative anatomy
clinical_significance: Comparative anatomy helps identify similarities and differences in body structures across species. In medicine and biomedical research, it informs interpretation of animal models and the limits of applying their findings to humans.

name: compartment syndrome
clinical_significance: Dangerous pressure buildup inside a confined muscle group that reduces blood flow and can permanently damage muscle and nerves. Severe pain, swelling, numbness, or weakness after injury requires emergency assessment and often surgery.

name: compensatory scoliosis
clinical_significance: Compensatory scoliosis is often a flexible spinal curve that develops in response to an imbalance such as unequal leg length. Identifying and addressing the underlying cause may reduce the curve; a fixed or progressive curve needs further assessment.

name: complement
clinical_significance: A group of blood proteins that strengthens immune defense. When activated, complement can mark germs for removal, attract immune cells, increase inflammation, or directly damage some microbes.

name: complement activation
clinical_significance: Complement activation helps defend against microbes but can also drive inflammation and tissue injury when excessive or misdirected, as in some autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.

name: complement C4
clinical_significance: Complement C4 is an immune protein measured when evaluating or monitoring conditions such as lupus and some complement deficiencies. A low level can reflect consumption or inherited deficiency and must be interpreted with symptoms and other tests.

name: complement deficiency
clinical_significance: Reduced or absent activity of one or more complement proteins, increasing susceptibility to some infections or autoimmune disease.

name: complement receptor
clinical_significance: Complement receptors help immune cells recognize complement-tagged microbes and debris. Their activity supports immune defense and clearance, while dysregulation can contribute to inflammatory or autoimmune disease.

name: complementary DNA
clinical_significance: Complementary DNA (cDNA) is DNA copied from RNA and is widely used to study gene expression and identify pathogens. It underlies methods such as reverse-transcription PCR and some genetic tests.

name: complementary RNA
clinical_significance: Complementary RNA is an RNA sequence paired with a target nucleic-acid sequence. It is used in molecular biology and diagnostic methods to detect or study specific genes and RNA transcripts.

name: complete cystectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove the entire urinary bladder, usually for invasive bladder cancer. Because urine can no longer leave through the bladder, the surgeon creates a urinary diversion such as an ileal conduit, a continent reservoir, or a new bladder from bowel.

name: complete excision
clinical_significance: Complete excision removes an entire lesion or affected tissue and may provide diagnosis or definitive treatment. For cancer, examination of the specimen and margins helps determine whether removal was adequate and whether further treatment is needed.

name: complication
clinical_significance: A new problem or harmful effect that develops during or after an illness, treatment, or procedure. Examples include infection, bleeding, organ damage, medicine reactions, and blood clots; seriousness depends on the problem and its effect.

name: composite lymphoma
clinical_significance: Composite lymphoma contains two distinct lymphoma types in the same tissue or patient. Accurate pathologic classification matters because prognosis and treatment may differ between the components.

name: composite resin
clinical_significance: A tooth-colored material used to repair cavities, chipped teeth, or other defects. It is bonded to the tooth and shaped to match it, but may wear or stain sooner than some harder restorations.

name: composition
clinical_significance: In clinical practice, composition describes what a specimen, medicine, solution, or body substance contains. Knowing its components and proportions can affect interpretation of test results, dosing, compatibility, and safety.

name: compound nevus
clinical_significance: A compound nevus is a usually benign mole involving melanocytes at both the epidermal junction and within the dermis. A lesion that changes, bleeds, or looks unlike a person’s other moles should be assessed for skin cancer.

name: comprehension
clinical_significance: Difficulty with comprehension can affect communication, learning, and a person’s ability to follow care instructions. It may arise from language, hearing, cognitive, or neurologic problems and can guide assessment and support.

name: comprehensive care
clinical_significance: Comprehensive care coordinates prevention, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and follow-up around a person’s needs. Coordination is especially important for people with multiple conditions or complex care plans.

name: compression
clinical_significance: Pressure applied to tissue or a structure, which may reduce swelling or bleeding but can also impair nerves, blood vessels, or organs when excessive.

name: compression bandage
clinical_significance: A bandage that applies controlled pressure to a limb or body part. It may reduce swelling, support injured tissue, or help manage venous disease, but improper use can impair circulation or damage skin.

name: compression fracture
clinical_significance: Collapse of a vertebra or other bone because of compression, often related to osteoporosis or trauma.

name: compression pump
clinical_significance: Intermittent pneumatic compression pumps may help prevent blood clots in hospitalized or immobile people by promoting venous blood flow. They are not suitable for every patient, so fit and use depend on the clinical situation.

name: compression stocking
clinical_significance: Compression stockings can reduce venous pooling and swelling and may be used for selected venous disorders or clot prevention. They should be properly fitted, since excessive pressure can injure skin or impair circulation.

name: concanavalin A
clinical_significance: Concanavalin A is a plant lectin used in laboratory research to stimulate immune cells and study cell-surface sugars. It is not a routine clinical treatment or diagnostic marker.

name: concentration
clinical_significance: The amount of a substance in a given volume, such as the level of glucose or medicine in blood. It is reported in units such as milligrams per deciliter or millimoles per liter.

name: conception
clinical_significance: The joining of a sperm and egg, usually in a fallopian tube, to form the first cell of an embryo. The resulting cells divide as they travel toward the uterus, where implantation may occur several days later.

name: concern
clinical_significance: A patient’s concern may signal a symptom, treatment worry, or care need and should be explored during clinical assessment and shared decision-making.

name: concomitant agent
clinical_significance: A concomitant agent is another medicine or treatment used at the same time. It may change effectiveness, toxicity, or interaction risk, so the full medication list matters in treatment planning.

name: condition
clinical_significance: A health condition can affect symptoms, function, treatment choices, and prognosis. Clinicians consider its severity and interaction with other conditions when planning care.

name: conditional
clinical_significance: In medicine, a conditional finding, recommendation, or response applies only when a stated criterion is met. The condition should be clear to avoid misinterpretation of a test or care plan.

name: conditioning
clinical_significance: Learning in which repeated association or reinforcement changes a behavior or response; in medicine, conditioning can also mean preparing a patient or tissue for a treatment.

name: conduct disorder
clinical_significance: A persistent pattern of behavior that violates others’ rights or major age-appropriate rules and causes significant problems at home, school, or in relationships. It may coexist with other mental-health or learning needs; assessment helps guide behavioral and family support.

name: conduction anesthesia
clinical_significance: Conduction anesthesia blocks nerve signals along a nerve or nerve group to provide pain relief in a defined area. It can support surgery or procedures while avoiding general anesthesia, but carries risks such as bleeding, infection, or nerve injury.

name: conductive hearing loss
clinical_significance: Hearing loss caused by a problem in the outer or middle ear that prevents sound from reaching the inner ear normally. Earwax, fluid, a damaged eardrum, bone changes, or ear-bone disease may be responsible.

name: condyloma acuminatum
