clinical_significance: A soft, wart-like growth around the genitals or anus caused by certain human papillomavirus types. It spreads through intimate skin contact; treatment removes visible warts, but the virus may remain and recur.

name: cone dystrophy
clinical_significance: Cone dystrophy is an inherited retinal disorder that damages cone cells, causing reduced sharp central vision, impaired color vision, and light sensitivity; some forms worsen over time and can limit daily activities.

name: confidence interval
clinical_significance: A confidence interval expresses the uncertainty around an estimated result. In clinical studies, it helps show the range of effects compatible with the data and how precisely treatment benefits or risks were estimated.

name: confidentiality
clinical_significance: The duty of healthcare professionals and organizations to protect a person's health information from unauthorized access or disclosure. Information may be shared when the patient agrees or when law permits or requires it.

name: conformal radiotherapy
clinical_significance: Conformal radiotherapy shapes radiation to the target while limiting exposure to nearby healthy tissue. It can improve dose precision, though side effects still depend on the target’s location and dose.

name: conformation
clinical_significance: In biology and medicine, molecular conformation can affect how a protein or other molecule functions and binds to medicines. Changes in conformation may contribute to disease or influence test and drug design.

name: confusion
clinical_significance: Impaired ability to think clearly, orient, attend, remember, or respond appropriately; sudden confusion is delirium and may indicate infection, medication effect, metabolic illness, stroke, or another emergency.

name: confusional arousal
clinical_significance: A confusional arousal is an incomplete awakening from deep sleep with confusion and reduced responsiveness. Episodes can be mistaken for seizures or other altered states; injury risk and frequent episodes may warrant clinical review.

name: congenital abnormality
clinical_significance: A congenital abnormality can affect organ structure or function from birth and range from minor to life-threatening. Early detection may guide monitoring, treatment, and family counseling.

name: congenital anaemia
clinical_significance: Congenital anemia may impair oxygen delivery from birth and can reflect inherited blood disorders, infection, or other fetal and neonatal conditions. Cause and severity guide urgent treatment and longer-term follow-up.

name: congenital cataract
clinical_significance: Clouding of the eye lens present at birth or developing soon afterward. It can interfere with visual development and may require early eye assessment and treatment to prevent lasting reduced vision.

name: congenital hamartoma
clinical_significance: A congenital hamartoma is a benign, disorganized overgrowth of tissue native to the affected site. Its effects depend on location and size; some lesions can impair organ function or resemble a tumor on imaging.

name: congenital hemolytic anemia
clinical_significance: Congenital hemolytic anemia causes red blood cells to break down faster than they are replaced, sometimes leading to jaundice, anemia, gallstones, or severe newborn illness. Identifying the cause guides treatment and family testing.

name: congenital hydrocephalus
clinical_significance: Congenital hydrocephalus is excess cerebrospinal fluid in the brain from birth, which can raise pressure and harm brain development. Early recognition and specialist treatment, often with fluid diversion, can reduce complications.

name: congenital hyperinsulinism
clinical_significance: An inherited or developmental disorder in which a baby's pancreas releases too much insulin. This can cause dangerously low blood sugar, poor feeding, seizures, brain injury, or death unless recognized and treated promptly.

name: congenital hypoplastic anemia
clinical_significance: Congenital hypoplastic anemia involves reduced production of red blood cells from birth and may cause severe anemia, growth effects, or transfusion needs. The underlying cause determines monitoring and treatment.

name: congenital laryngocele
clinical_significance: A congenital laryngocele is an uncommon air-filled dilation connected to the larynx. If large or infected, it can cause a neck mass, voice changes, or airway obstruction and may require specialist treatment.

name: congenital macrodactylia
clinical_significance: Congenital macrodactyly is enlargement of one or more fingers or toes present from birth. Progressive growth can impair movement, footwear, or hand function and may require orthopedic or plastic-surgery care.

name: congenital megacolon
clinical_significance: A birth condition in which part of the intestine lacks the nerve cells needed to move stool. It causes blockage and enlargement of the bowel above it, with delayed first stool, swelling, vomiting, or severe constipation.

name: congenital microcephaly
clinical_significance: Congenital microcephaly is a smaller-than-expected head size present at birth, often reflecting altered brain growth. Developmental effects vary, so evaluation and ongoing developmental support may be needed.

name: congenital nephrotic
clinical_significance: Congenital nephrotic syndrome causes heavy protein loss in the urine, low blood protein, and swelling in early infancy. It can progress to kidney failure and requires prompt specialist care, nutritional support, and sometimes kidney replacement therapy.

name: congenital neutropenia
clinical_significance: Congenital neutropenia causes persistently low neutrophil counts from birth, increasing the risk of serious bacterial and fungal infections. Early diagnosis, infection prevention, and specialist-directed treatment can reduce complications.

name: congenital nystagmus
clinical_significance: Congenital nystagmus is involuntary eye movement beginning in infancy and may reduce visual clarity or depth perception. Eye assessment can identify associated conditions and guide vision support or treatment.

name: congenital phimosis
clinical_significance: Congenital phimosis is inability to retract the foreskin in a young child, which is commonly normal during early development. Pain, scarring, recurrent infection, or difficulty urinating needs clinical assessment; forceful retraction can cause injury.

name: congestive heart failure
clinical_significance: Heart failure can cause breathlessness, fatigue, and fluid retention and may worsen suddenly; early recognition and treatment reduce hospitalization and organ injury.

name: congo red
clinical_significance: Congo red is a laboratory dye used to detect amyloid deposits in tissue. A positive stain, interpreted with tissue appearance and other tests, can help diagnose amyloidosis and identify affected organs.

name: coniochaeta
clinical_significance: Coniochaeta is a fungus found in the environment that only rarely causes human infection. Identification from a patient specimen may matter in invasive disease, particularly in people with impaired immunity.

name: conization
clinical_significance: Conization removes a cone-shaped portion of the cervix for diagnosis or treatment of high-grade precancerous changes and selected early cancers. Pathology and margin findings guide follow-up; excision can rarely affect future pregnancy outcomes.

name: conjoined twins
clinical_significance: Identical twins who are physically joined because the early embryo did not completely separate. They may share organs or body structures, so detailed imaging and care by specialists are needed; the outlook depends on what is shared.

name: conjunctiva
clinical_significance: The thin, clear tissue lining the inside of the eyelids and covering the white part of the eye. It protects and lubricates the eye and helps the eyelids move smoothly across its surface.

name: conjunctival disease
clinical_significance: Conjunctival diseases can cause irritation, redness, discharge, or vision problems and may arise from infection, allergy, inflammation, or growths. Persistent pain, light sensitivity, or reduced vision warrants prompt eye assessment.

name: conjunctival neoplasm
clinical_significance: A conjunctival neoplasm may be benign or malignant; some lesions can threaten vision or spread locally. Examination and sometimes biopsy establish the diagnosis and guide treatment.

name: conjunctival sac
clinical_significance: The conjunctival sac is the space between the eyelid and eye surface where drops and ointments are placed. Correct placement helps topical eye medicines reach the ocular surface.

name: conjunctivitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the conjunctiva, the membrane lining the inside of the eyelids and covering the white of the eye. It can cause redness, itching or irritation, watering, and discharge, and may result from infection, allergy, or irritants.

name: Conn syndrome
clinical_significance: Primary aldosteronism caused by autonomous overproduction of aldosterone by one or both adrenal glands. It usually causes high blood pressure and may cause low blood potassium, although potassium can be normal.

name: connective tissue
clinical_significance: Connective tissue supports and links organs and structures throughout the body. Inherited or acquired connective-tissue disorders can affect joints, skin, blood vessels, lungs, or the heart, so findings may require evaluation across organ systems.

name: conotoxin
clinical_significance: Conotoxins are potent cone-snail peptides that affect nerve signaling. One synthetic conotoxin, ziconotide, is used in selected cases of severe chronic pain through intrathecal infusion; these toxins are also studied as drug leads.

name: consciousness
clinical_significance: Changes in consciousness can signal brain injury, stroke, infection, seizures, poisoning, or metabolic illness. Sudden reduced alertness or inability to awaken requires emergency assessment.

name: consent form
clinical_significance: A consent form documents that a person received information and agreed to a procedure, study, or treatment. Valid consent depends on understanding, capacity, and a voluntary choice; a signed form alone does not establish these.

name: consistency
clinical_significance: Consistency of a clinical finding or test result affects confidence in interpretation and comparison over time. In research and care, methods and measurements should be applied consistently to reduce error.

name: constipation
clinical_significance: A condition involving fewer than three bowel movements per week, hard or lumpy stools, difficult or painful passage, straining, or a feeling that the bowel has not emptied completely. Causes include diet, medicines, dehydration, functional bowel disorders, and structural or systemic disease.

name: constitutional symptom
clinical_significance: Constitutional symptoms such as fever, fatigue, weight loss, or night sweats affect the whole body rather than one organ system. They can occur with infection, inflammation, cancer, or other systemic illness and need context-specific evaluation.

name: constrictive pericarditis
clinical_significance: A chronic condition in which a thickened or scarred, noncompliant sac around the heart restricts diastolic filling. It can cause breathlessness, fatigue, leg or abdominal swelling, enlarged neck veins, and liver congestion; causes include infection, surgery, radiation, or unknown disease.

name: consultation
clinical_significance: A specialist consultation can clarify diagnosis or treatment options and may guide coordinated care. Timely consultation is important when a condition is complex, severe, or not responding as expected.

name: contact dermatitis
clinical_significance: Red, itchy, burning, or blistered skin caused by contact with an irritating or allergy-triggering substance. Common triggers include soaps, chemicals, metals, fragrances, plants, and medicines.

name: contact inhibition
clinical_significance: Contact inhibition normally limits cell growth when cells touch neighboring cells. Loss of this control is a feature of many cancer cells and is studied in cancer biology.

name: contact lens
clinical_significance: Contact lenses correct vision but can cause corneal infection or injury if worn, cleaned, or stored improperly. Eye pain, redness, light sensitivity, or blurred vision in a lens wearer needs prompt assessment.

name: contiguous disease
clinical_significance: Contiguous disease has spread directly into neighboring tissue or structures. This distinction can affect staging, surgical planning, and treatment, particularly in cancer and infection.

name: continent reservoir
clinical_significance: A continent urinary reservoir stores urine internally after bladder removal and is emptied through a catheterizable opening. It avoids an external collection bag but requires reliable emptying and long-term monitoring for complications.

name: continuous murmur
clinical_significance: A continuous heart murmur persists through systole and diastole and can reflect abnormal blood flow, such as a patent ductus arteriosus or an arteriovenous connection. Clinical assessment and echocardiography identify the cause.

name: contraception
clinical_significance: Any method used to prevent pregnancy, including intrauterine devices, implants, pills, injections, condoms, fertility-awareness methods, and sterilization. Methods differ in effectiveness, duration, side effects, cost, and protection against sexually transmitted infections. The best choice depends on health, preferences, reproductive plans, and access to care.

name: contraceptive agent
clinical_significance: Contraceptive agents prevent pregnancy through hormonal or other mechanisms. Choice depends on effectiveness, safety, interactions, preferences, and reproductive plans; most do not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

name: contraceptive device
clinical_significance: Contraceptive devices, including intrauterine devices and implants, provide highly effective pregnancy prevention for an extended period. Counseling helps match the method to health needs and preferences.

name: contract
clinical_significance: A contract in healthcare can define responsibilities, services, payment, or research participation. Its terms may affect access and obligations, so patients should understand relevant conditions before agreeing.

name: contractile proteins
clinical_significance: Proteins, especially actin and myosin, that interact inside muscle cells to generate force, shorten fibers, and produce body movement.

name: contracture
clinical_significance: A lasting inability to fully move a joint because nearby muscles, tendons, ligaments, skin, or other tissues have shortened or stiffened. It may follow injury, burns, paralysis, inflammation, or prolonged immobility.

name: contraindication
clinical_significance: A condition or circumstance in which a treatment, procedure, or medication should not be used because the potential harm outweighs the expected benefit.

name: contralateral
clinical_significance: On or affecting the side opposite a stated body part or injury. For example, a stroke on the left side of the brain may cause weakness on the right side of the body.

name: contrast bronchogram
clinical_significance: A contrast bronchogram outlines the airways during imaging and may help show structural narrowing or blockage. It is now rarely used because CT and bronchoscopy provide more practical evaluation.

name: contrast medium
clinical_significance: A substance administered or placed in the body to make tissues, organs, or body spaces more visible during imaging.

name: control groups
clinical_significance: A control group provides a comparison in a clinical study, helping researchers estimate whether an intervention caused an observed effect. Appropriate controls reduce bias and improve confidence in results.

name: controlled study
clinical_significance: A controlled study compares an intervention with a control condition to assess effects on health outcomes. Randomization and blinding, when feasible, reduce bias and strengthen conclusions.

name: contusion
clinical_significance: A bruise caused by a blunt blow that damages small blood vessels without breaking the skin. It may cause pain, swelling, and discoloration; severe injuries can damage muscle, organs, or deeper tissues.

name: convulsant
clinical_significance: A convulsant is a substance that can provoke seizures. Exposure may cause a medical emergency requiring airway support, seizure control, and treatment of the underlying toxin or cause.

name: Cooley's anemia
clinical_significance: Thalassemia causes inherited anemia of variable severity; carrier testing and genetic counseling can inform reproductive decisions, while severe disease may require transfusion and iron monitoring.

name: coombs test
clinical_significance: A blood test that detects antibodies affecting red blood cells. It helps investigate immune-related destruction of red cells and checks compatibility before some blood transfusions.

name: coping
clinical_significance: Coping strategies can help people manage stress, symptoms, and the practical effects of illness. Effective support may improve well-being and treatment engagement, while persistent distress may warrant professional help.

name: coping skill
clinical_significance: Coping skills are practical strategies for handling stress and illness-related challenges. Skills such as problem-solving, relaxation, and seeking support can complement medical treatment.

name: copolymer
clinical_significance: Medical copolymers are used in devices, drug delivery, and biomaterials; their properties influence stability, compatibility, and safety. Clinical relevance depends on the specific polymer and application.

name: copper
clinical_significance: Copper is an essential trace element needed for blood-cell formation, iron use, and nervous-system function. Deficiency or excess can cause anemia, neurologic problems, or organ injury, so abnormal levels need evaluation in context.

name: coprinellus radians
clinical_significance: Coprinellus radians is an environmental mushroom-forming fungus with no established role as a common human pathogen. Identification is mainly relevant to mycology or unusual clinical isolates.

name: coprolalia
clinical_significance: Involuntary utterance of obscene, taboo, or socially inappropriate words, most often described as a complex vocal tic in Tourette syndrome.

name: coprophagy
clinical_significance: Coprophagy can expose a person or animal to intestinal parasites and pathogens and may signal a behavioral, developmental, or nutritional concern. Persistent behavior merits assessment of its cause and associated health risks.

name: copulation
clinical_significance: Copulation can transmit sexually transmitted infections and may result in pregnancy. Sexual-health counseling can address consent, contraception, infection prevention, and fertility goals.

name: cor biloculare
clinical_significance: Cor biloculare is a rare congenital heart configuration with two chambers rather than the usual four. The resulting circulation can be severely abnormal and requires specialist cardiac assessment.

name: cor pulmonale
clinical_significance: Enlargement and weakening of the right side of the heart caused by high pressure in the lung arteries, usually from long-term lung disease. It may cause breathlessness, leg swelling, enlarged neck veins, or liver congestion.

name: cor triatriatum
clinical_significance: A rare birth defect in which a membrane divides the upper left heart chamber into two spaces. If the membrane blocks blood returning from the lungs, it can cause breathlessness, poor growth, or heart failure; some people have no symptoms.

name: cor triloculare
clinical_significance: Cor triloculare is a rare congenital heart defect with three cardiac chambers. Its effects depend on the anatomy and blood flow and can include cyanosis or heart failure, requiring specialist evaluation.

name: cord blood
clinical_significance: Umbilical cord blood contains blood-forming stem cells that can be used in transplants for selected blood cancers, blood disorders, and immune or metabolic diseases. Donation and private storage have different uses and limitations.

name: cordocentesis
clinical_significance: A prenatal procedure using ultrasound guidance to take a small blood sample from the umbilical cord. It can assess fetal anemia, infection, or selected genetic conditions but carries risks including bleeding and pregnancy loss.

name: cordotomy
clinical_significance: A procedure that cuts selected pain-sensing pathways in the spinal cord to relieve severe pain when other treatments have failed. It may cause numbness, weakness, breathing problems, or other lasting nerve complications.

name: cordycepin
clinical_significance: Cordycepin is a fungal-derived molecule studied for biological and potential anticancer effects. It remains investigational and is not an established treatment in routine clinical care.

name: corn oil
clinical_significance: Corn oil is a dietary source of fat and energy. Its health effects depend on overall diet and amount consumed; it is not a treatment for disease.

name: cornea
clinical_significance: The clear, curved front surface of the eye. It protects the eye and bends light so images focus on the retina; scratches, infection, swelling, or scarring can cause pain and blurred vision.

name: cornea disorder
clinical_significance: Corneal disorders can cause pain, light sensitivity, redness, and blurred vision, sometimes threatening sight. Prompt eye assessment is important for severe pain, sudden vision change, injury, or suspected infection.

name: cornea edema
clinical_significance: Corneal edema is swelling of the cornea that can blur vision and cause halos or discomfort. It may follow surgery, injury, raised eye pressure, or corneal disease; treatment targets the cause and protects vision.

name: cornea opacity
clinical_significance: Corneal opacity is clouding or scarring of the cornea that can blur or block vision, especially when central. Causes include injury, infection, inflammation, and inherited disease; treatment depends on cause and severity.

name: corneal burn
clinical_significance: A corneal burn from chemicals, heat, or radiation can rapidly damage the eye and threaten sight. Chemical exposure requires immediate, prolonged rinsing and urgent eye care.

name: corneal decompensation
clinical_significance: Corneal decompensation occurs when the cornea cannot maintain its clarity, often because its endothelial cells have failed. Swelling and blurred vision may progress and sometimes require corneal transplantation.

name: corneal endothelium
clinical_significance: The innermost layer of cells in the cornea. It moves extra fluid out of the cornea and helps keep it clear.

name: corneal epithelium
clinical_significance: The thin outer layer of the cornea that protects the eye and helps keep its surface smooth.

name: corneal infection
clinical_significance: Corneal infection can rapidly damage the clear front of the eye and cause scarring or vision loss. Contact lens wear is an important risk factor; pain, redness, light sensitivity, or blurred vision needs prompt eye assessment.

name: corneal perforation
clinical_significance: A corneal perforation is a full-thickness opening that threatens vision and can allow eye contents to leak or infection to spread. It is an ophthalmic emergency requiring immediate treatment.

name: corneal stroma
clinical_significance: The thick middle layer of the cornea. It gives the cornea much of its strength and helps keep it clear.

name: corneal ulcer
clinical_significance: A loss of tissue forming an open sore on the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. It is most often caused by infection with bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites, but may also follow an injury, severe dryness, poor eyelid closure, or contact-lens problems. It may cause eye pain, redness, tearing, discharge, sensitivity to light, or blurred vision. Healing can leave a corneal scar, and a deep or central ulcer can seriously damage vision or perforate the eye.

name: coronary
clinical_significance: Relating to the arteries and blood flow that supply the heart muscle. Narrowing or blockage of these arteries can reduce oxygen to the heart and cause chest pain or a heart attack.

name: coronary aneurysm
clinical_significance: An abnormal widening or ballooning of a coronary artery. It may result from atherosclerosis, inflammation, infection, injury, or a congenital condition and can cause clotting, blockage, or rarely rupture.

name: coronary angiography
clinical_significance: An X-ray examination of the heart arteries after contrast is injected through a thin catheter. It shows narrowed or blocked areas and can guide treatment, but the procedure can cause bleeding, stroke, kidney injury, or other complications.

name: coronary artery
clinical_significance: One of the arteries branching from the aorta that supplies oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle. Narrowing or blockage can cause angina or a heart attack.

name: coronary artery disease
clinical_significance: A condition in which fatty plaque builds up in the arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle, narrowing them and reducing blood flow. It may cause no symptoms, chest discomfort (angina), or a heart attack, and can lead to heart failure or abnormal heart rhythms.

name: coronary atherosclerosis
clinical_significance: Coronary atherosclerosis is plaque buildup in the heart’s arteries that can restrict blood flow, cause angina, and lead to heart attack. Risk-factor control and evidence-based treatment reduce cardiovascular risk.

name: coronary circulation
clinical_significance: The network of arteries and veins that supplies the heart muscle with oxygen and removes waste. Blood flow increases when the heart works harder and falls when an artery is narrowed or blocked.

name: coronary revascularisation
clinical_significance: Coronary revascularization restores blood flow to heart muscle, usually with angioplasty and stenting or bypass surgery. It can relieve symptoms and benefit selected patients; the choice depends on disease pattern, urgency, and overall risk.

name: coronary sinus
clinical_significance: A large vein on the back of the heart that collects deoxygenated blood from the heart

name: coronary stenosis
clinical_significance: Coronary stenosis is narrowing of a heart artery, commonly from atherosclerotic plaque. Its significance depends on whether it limits blood flow and causes ischemia; severe narrowing can cause angina or heart attack.

name: coronary vessel
clinical_significance: Coronary vessels supply and drain the heart muscle. Disease or blockage can impair heart function and cause ischemia, angina, or myocardial infarction.

name: coronaviridae
clinical_significance: Coronaviridae is the virus family that includes seasonal human coronaviruses and viruses causing SARS, MERS, and COVID-19. The illnesses range from mild respiratory infection to severe disease.

name: corpus callosum
clinical_significance: A broad band of nerve fibers connecting the brain's left and right halves. It allows the two sides to share information needed for movement, sensation, language, vision, and thinking.

name: corpus cavernosum
clinical_significance: One of two columns of erectile tissue in the penis that fill with blood during erection.

name: corpus luteum
clinical_significance: The temporary endocrine structure formed from an ovarian follicle after ovulation; it produces progesterone during the luteal phase and early pregnancy.

name: corpus spongiosum
clinical_significance: A column of erectile tissue surrounding the penile urethra and expanding distally to form the glans.

name: corpus striatum
clinical_significance: The corpus striatum is part of the brain’s basal ganglia, which help regulate movement and some aspects of learning and behavior. Damage or dysfunction can contribute to movement disorders.

name: cortical cataract
clinical_significance: A cataract that begins in the outer part of the eye's lens and forms spoke-like cloudy areas extending inward. It can cause glare, halos, and blurred vision, especially in bright light.

name: cortical dysplasia
clinical_significance: Cortical dysplasia is abnormal development of the brain’s cerebral cortex and is an important cause of drug-resistant focal epilepsy, particularly in children. Some cases require specialized imaging and epilepsy-surgery evaluation.

name: corticosteroid
clinical_significance: A steroid hormone from the adrenal cortex or a synthetic analogue; glucocorticoids reduce inflammation and immune activity, while mineralocorticoids regulate salt and water balance.

name: corticosterone
clinical_significance: Corticosterone is an adrenal steroid hormone involved in stress and metabolic responses and is a precursor in human steroid synthesis. It is not generally a routine clinical test.

name: corticotropin
clinical_significance: Corticotropin, also called ACTH, stimulates the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol. Blood testing helps assess pituitary-adrenal function and investigate disorders such as adrenal insufficiency or Cushing syndrome.

name: cortisol
clinical_significance: A hormone made by the adrenal glands that helps the body respond to stress, maintain blood pressure and blood sugar, regulate metabolism, and control inflammation. Too much or too little can cause serious illness.

name: cortisone
clinical_significance: A corticosteroid that is converted in the body to cortisol and can be used to reduce inflammation or replace glucocorticoid activity.

name: cortisone acetate
clinical_significance: Cortisone acetate is a corticosteroid used in selected settings for glucocorticoid replacement or anti-inflammatory treatment. Dose and duration matter because prolonged use can suppress adrenal function and cause systemic adverse effects.

name: cortodoxone
clinical_significance: Cortodoxone is a synthetic corticosteroid studied for glucocorticoid activity. It has no established routine clinical use.

name: corynebacterium
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium is a genus of bacteria that includes the diphtheria organism and species that can cause opportunistic infections. Species identification helps distinguish true pathogens from skin contaminants and guides infection control or treatment.

name: corynebacterium accolens
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium accolens is commonly found on skin and in the upper airway and may inhibit some nasal pathogens. It is rarely implicated in disease, so a clinical isolate is interpreted according to specimen and symptoms.

name: corynebacterium diphtheriae
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium diphtheriae can cause diphtheria, a potentially fatal toxin-mediated illness with airway obstruction, heart inflammation, and nerve injury. Vaccination prevents disease; suspected cases require urgent isolation and treatment.

name: corynebacterium jeikeium
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium jeikeium can cause bloodstream and device-associated infections, particularly in immunocompromised or hospitalized patients. It is often resistant to multiple antibiotics, making susceptibility testing important.

name: corynebacterium kutscheri
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium kutscheri primarily causes disease in rodents and is not a common human pathogen. A finding in a clinical sample should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed when relevant.

name: corynebacterium otitidis
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium otitidis has been isolated from the ear and may be associated with ear infection, though its clinical role can be uncertain. Interpretation depends on symptoms, specimen quality, and other findings.

name: corynebacterium pyogenes
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium pyogenes, now generally classified as Trueperella pyogenes, causes abscesses and other infections mainly in livestock. Human infection is rare and generally opportunistic.

name: corynebacterium renale
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium renale is primarily associated with urinary disease in cattle and is not a usual cause of human illness. Its importance is mainly veterinary.

name: corynebacterium xerosis
clinical_significance: Corynebacterium xerosis is a skin-associated bacterium that can occasionally cause opportunistic infection, including bloodstream or device-related infection. A positive culture should be assessed for contamination versus true disease.

name: cos cell
clinical_significance: COS cells are an engineered monkey-kidney cell line used in laboratory studies of gene expression and protein function. They are research tools, not a diagnostic test or treatment.

name: cosenzaea myxofaciens
clinical_significance: Cosenzaea myxofaciens is a rare bacterium formerly classified as Proteus myxofaciens. Its significance in human disease is poorly established; identification from a patient specimen requires clinical and microbiologic context.

name: cositecan
clinical_significance: Cositecan (karenitecin) is an investigational topoisomerase I inhibitor studied as an anticancer drug. It is not an approved routine cancer treatment.

name: cosmetics
clinical_significance: Cosmetics can cause irritant or allergic skin and eye reactions, and contaminated products can rarely cause infection. Product ingredients and exposure history can help identify the cause of a reaction.

name: cost control
clinical_significance: Cost control in healthcare can affect affordability, access, and choice of services or medicines. Clinical decisions should consider costs while preserving safe, evidence-based care.

name: Costello syndrome (disorder)
clinical_significance: Costello syndrome is a rare genetic condition affecting growth, development, skin, and the heart, with increased risk of certain tumors. Early multidisciplinary care and ongoing heart and cancer surveillance are important.

name: cosyntropin
clinical_significance: Cosyntropin is synthetic ACTH used in a stimulation test to assess whether the adrenal glands can produce cortisol. The test helps investigate adrenal insufficiency and some pituitary-adrenal disorders.

name: cotinine
clinical_significance: Cotinine is a nicotine breakdown product measured in blood, urine, or saliva to assess recent tobacco or nicotine exposure. It can support smoking-cessation care and research, but does not by itself identify the source of nicotine.

name: cottonseed oil
clinical_significance: Cottonseed oil is a dietary fat and may also be used as an ingredient in topical products. Clinical effects depend on amount and formulation; allergy or irritation is possible in sensitive individuals.

name: cough
clinical_significance: A protective reflex that clears mucus, irritants, or foreign material from the airways. Coughs may be short-lived or persistent and can result from infection, allergy, asthma, reflux, medicines, heart disease, or other conditions.

name: coulomb
clinical_significance: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge. It is used in physics and biomedical engineering, including describing charge delivered by some stimulation devices.

name: coumaphos
clinical_significance: Coumaphos is an organophosphate pesticide used mainly in veterinary and agricultural settings. Excess exposure can inhibit cholinesterase and cause a potentially life-threatening cholinergic poisoning.

name: coumarin
clinical_significance: Coumarin is a plant-derived chemical found in some foods and fragrances; it is not the anticoagulant warfarin. High exposure, including from some cassia cinnamon products, may harm the liver in susceptible people.

name: coumestan
clinical_significance: Coumestans are plant compounds with estrogen-like activity studied for possible hormonal effects. Evidence does not establish them as a treatment, and concentrated supplements may interact with hormone-sensitive conditions or medicines.

name: coumestrol
clinical_significance: Coumestrol is a plant-derived phytoestrogen studied for estrogen-like biological effects. Its clinical benefits and risks as a supplement are not established.

name: counseling
clinical_significance: Counseling can help people understand diagnoses, manage emotional or behavioral concerns, make informed health choices, and cope with illness. The appropriate approach depends on the person’s goals and needs.

name: count
clinical_significance: A count is a quantitative measure, such as a blood-cell or microbial count. Abnormal values can help detect disease or monitor treatment, but must be interpreted with the test method and clinical context.

name: country code
clinical_significance: A country code identifies a country in health records, surveillance, and international data exchange. Accurate coding supports reporting and coordination but does not itself indicate a clinical condition.

name: coxa magna
clinical_significance: Coxa magna is enlargement of the femoral head or neck, often following childhood hip disease or injury. It can alter hip mechanics, limit movement, and contribute to pain or early joint degeneration.

name: coxa valga
clinical_significance: Coxa valga is an increased angle between the femoral neck and shaft. It may occur with developmental or neuromuscular conditions and can affect hip stability, gait, and joint loading.

name: coxiella
clinical_significance: Coxiella is a bacterial genus best known for Coxiella burnetii, the cause of Q fever. Infection may be acute or persist as endocarditis or vascular infection, especially in people with relevant risk factors.

name: coxiella burnetii
clinical_significance: A bacterium that causes Q fever, usually spread by breathing dust contaminated by infected farm animals. It can cause fever, headache, hepatitis, or pneumonia and may persist as a serious infection of heart valves.

name: coxiellaceae
clinical_significance: Coxiellaceae is a bacterial family that includes Coxiella burnetii, the cause of Q fever. The family is chiefly relevant to infectious-disease diagnosis and zoonotic surveillance.

name: coxsackie virus
clinical_significance: Coxsackie viruses are enteroviruses that can cause hand-foot-and-mouth disease, herpangina, aseptic meningitis, and sometimes heart or muscle inflammation. Most infections are mild, but neurologic or cardiac complications can be serious.

name: coxsackieviruses b
clinical_significance: Coxsackievirus B infections can cause febrile illness, viral meningitis, myocarditis, or pericarditis. Severe disease is more likely in newborns and people with certain underlying conditions.

name: c-peptide
clinical_significance: A small protein fragment released when the pancreas makes insulin. Measuring it helps show how much insulin a person's body is making, rather than how much injected insulin is present. Kidney function and blood-glucose levels can affect the result.

name: C-peptide measurement
clinical_significance: C-peptide measurement helps distinguish the body’s own insulin production from injected insulin and can support evaluation of diabetes type, hypoglycemia, or pancreatic function. Kidney function and timing affect interpretation.

name: cpg island
clinical_significance: CpG islands are DNA regions rich in cytosine-guanine sequences that can regulate gene activity through methylation. Abnormal methylation patterns are studied in cancer and other diseases and are used in selected molecular tests.

name: crack cocaine
clinical_significance: Crack cocaine is an addictive stimulant that can cause heart attack, stroke, seizures, dangerous overheating, psychosis, and sudden death. Repeated use can cause dependence and substantial social and medical harm.

name: cranial
clinical_significance: Relating to the skull or toward the head, as opposed to caudal or toward the lower end of the body.

name: cranial cavity
clinical_significance: The hollow space inside the skull that contains and protects the brain, its coverings, blood vessels, and cerebrospinal fluid. A rise in pressure inside this space can compress the brain and become life-threatening.

name: cranial meningocele
clinical_significance: A cranial meningocele is a sac containing the brain’s coverings that protrudes through an opening in the skull. It may occur with other brain abnormalities and can require neurosurgical and developmental follow-up.

name: cranial nerve
clinical_significance: One of 12 pairs of nerves arising from the brain or brainstem. They control smell, vision, eye movement, facial sensation and movement, hearing, balance, swallowing, voice, and other head and neck functions.

name: cranial sinus
clinical_significance: A cranial sinus is a venous channel that drains blood from the brain. Thrombosis, infection, or injury involving these channels can obstruct drainage and cause neurologic complications.

name: craniocerebral trauma
clinical_significance: Craniocerebral trauma is injury to the skull and brain, ranging from concussion to bleeding or severe brain damage. Worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, seizure, or reduced consciousness after injury requires emergency evaluation.

name: craniocervical region
clinical_significance: The craniocervical region joins the skull and upper spine and contains critical neural and vascular structures. Congenital abnormalities, instability, or trauma here can compress the brainstem or spinal cord.

name: craniofacial dysostosis
clinical_significance: A birth disorder in which some skull bones join too early and the face develops unusually. It can change head shape, affect the eyes or airway, and sometimes increase pressure around the brain; severity varies.

name: craniolacunia
clinical_significance: Craniolacunia describes thin, irregular areas of skull bone, classically associated with severe neural-tube defects. It is a radiologic finding whose significance depends on the underlying congenital condition.

name: craniopharyngioma
clinical_significance: A usually slow-growing tumor near the pituitary gland and hypothalamus. It may cause headache, vision loss, excessive thirst or urination, hormone problems, growth changes, or increased pressure in the skull.

name: craniorachischisis
clinical_significance: Craniorachischisis is a severe neural-tube defect in which the brain and spinal cord remain exposed along an extensive opening. It is usually fatal before or shortly after birth.

name: cranioschisis
clinical_significance: Cranioschisis is a congenital failure of skull closure that may leave brain tissue exposed or herniating. It is a severe neural-tube defect requiring specialist prenatal counseling and perinatal care.

name: craniospinal irradiation
clinical_significance: Craniospinal irradiation treats tumors or other disease involving the brain and spinal fluid pathways by irradiating the brain and spinal axis. It can control disseminated disease but may affect growth, cognition, fertility, and bone marrow.

name: craniosynostosis
clinical_significance: Craniosynostosis is premature fusion of one or more skull sutures, altering head shape and sometimes increasing pressure on the developing brain.

name: craniotomy
clinical_significance: An operation in which a surgeon temporarily removes a piece of the skull to reach the brain or its coverings. It may be used to remove a tumor, stop bleeding, repair an aneurysm, or treat another brain problem. The bone is usually put back and secured at the end of the operation.

name: craving
clinical_significance: A strong, often difficult-to-control desire for a substance, behavior, or experience, commonly seen in substance-use disorders.

name: cream
clinical_significance: A spreadable semisolid preparation applied to the skin, often containing a medicine. Creams are usually less greasy than ointments and may be useful on moist or broad areas, but the correct product depends on the skin condition.

name: creatine
clinical_significance: A nitrogen-containing compound stored mainly in skeletal muscle that helps supply energy for short, high-intensity activity.

name: creatine kinase
clinical_significance: An enzyme found mainly in muscle and released into blood when muscle cells are damaged. Levels may rise after strenuous exercise, injury, seizures, muscle disease, or some medicines; other tests help identify the source.

name: creatinine
clinical_significance: Creatinine is a waste product filtered from the blood by the kidneys. Blood creatinine is used to estimate kidney function, but results also depend on muscle mass, age, diet, and other factors.

name: creatinine increased
clinical_significance: An increased creatinine level may indicate reduced kidney filtration, acute kidney injury, dehydration, or medication effects. Trends, urine findings, and estimated glomerular filtration rate help determine the cause and urgency.

name: creativity
clinical_significance: Creativity can be affected by neurologic, psychiatric, or developmental conditions and is sometimes studied as part of cognition and rehabilitation. It is not by itself a clinical diagnostic measure.

name: creosote
clinical_significance: Creosote exposure can irritate or burn the skin, eyes, and respiratory tract; substantial exposure can cause systemic poisoning. Prolonged occupational exposure to coal-tar creosote is associated with increased cancer risk.

name: crescentic glomerulonephritis
clinical_significance: A rapidly worsening inflammation of the kidney's filtering units. It can cause blood or protein in urine, swelling, high blood pressure, and kidney failure and usually requires urgent specialist treatment.

name: CREST syndrome
clinical_significance: A limited cutaneous form of systemic sclerosis named for Calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysfunction, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia. It may also affect the lungs, heart, kidneys, or digestive tract; monitoring for pulmonary hypertension and other organ involvement is important.

name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
clinical_significance: A rare, rapidly progressive brain disease caused by abnormal prion proteins that damage nerve cells. It causes worsening dementia and neurologic problems and is fatal; most cases arise spontaneously, while a smaller proportion are inherited or acquired through specific exposures.

name: cribriform
clinical_significance: Cribriform describes a sieve-like pattern seen in some tissues and tumors. In pathology, it can help characterize lesions, but its clinical meaning depends on the organ and the full microscopic diagnosis.

name: cribriform pattern
clinical_significance: A cribriform pattern is a sieve-like arrangement of cells or glands seen in some tumors. In pathology, it can help classify a lesion and assess its behavior, but significance depends on the organ and tumor type.

name: cricoid cartilage
clinical_significance: A complete ring of firm tissue at the lower part of the voice box, just above the windpipe. It supports the airway and connects with other structures involved in breathing and voice.

name: crisis intervention
clinical_significance: Crisis intervention provides immediate support to reduce danger and stabilize someone facing acute psychological distress, suicidality, violence, or another crisis. It may include safety planning, urgent treatment, and connection to ongoing care.

name: crisscross heart
clinical_significance: Crisscross heart is a rare congenital heart arrangement in which the ventricles and their inlet pathways are abnormally oriented. It is often associated with other major heart defects and requires detailed specialist assessment.

name: crithidia
clinical_significance: Crithidia are single-celled parasites; some species cause leishmaniasis-like disease in animals or people. Crithidia luciliae is also used in a laboratory test for anti–double-stranded DNA antibodies associated with lupus.

name: critical care
clinical_significance: Specialized care for people with life-threatening illness or injury who need close monitoring and support for failing organs.

name: crizotinib
clinical_significance: Crizotinib is a targeted cancer medicine used for selected tumors with ALK, ROS1, or other specific molecular changes. Tumor testing guides use; treatment can cause serious liver, lung, heart-rhythm, or vision-related adverse effects.

name: Crohn's disease
clinical_significance: Crohn’s disease is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the digestive tract and often causes flares of abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue, and weight loss. Complications include strictures, fistulas, malnutrition, and bowel obstruction; treatment aims to control inflammation and prevent damage.

name: cromolyn
clinical_significance: Cromolyn is a mast-cell stabilizing medicine used to prevent certain allergic symptoms and asthma in selected settings. It is not a rescue treatment for an acute asthma attack.

name: cromolyn sodium
clinical_significance: Cromolyn sodium can help prevent allergic or inflammatory symptoms, including selected asthma and eye or nasal allergy symptoms. It works best when used regularly as directed and does not replace emergency treatment for severe reactions.

name: croneton
clinical_significance: Croneton is a trade name for ethiofencarb, a carbamate insecticide. Exposure can inhibit acetylcholinesterase and cause sweating, salivation, vomiting, breathing difficulty, weakness, or seizures, requiring urgent poison-control or emergency care.

name: cronobacter
clinical_significance: Cronobacter is an environmental genus of bacteria that can contaminate powdered infant formula and feeding equipment. Infections are uncommon but can cause severe sepsis or meningitis in newborns and other vulnerable people.

name: cronobacter sakazakii
clinical_significance: Cronobacter sakazakii can cause rare but life-threatening bloodstream infection or meningitis in infants, especially newborns. Powdered formula and contaminated feeding equipment are recognized sources, so prompt evaluation of an ill infant is critical.

name: cross reaction
clinical_significance: A cross-reaction occurs when an antibody, immune cell, or test reacts to a similar but different target. It can cause allergy symptoms or misleading laboratory results and should be considered when interpreting testing.

name: crossbite
clinical_significance: A crossbite is a misalignment in which upper and lower teeth meet in the wrong side-to-side position. Persistent crossbite can affect chewing and jaw growth and may benefit from dental or orthodontic assessment.

name: cross-over study
clinical_significance: A cross-over study gives participants different treatments in sequence, with each participant serving as their own comparison. It can reduce between-person variability, but carryover effects and disease changes over time can bias results.

name: cross-sectional study
clinical_significance: A study that measures possible causes and health outcomes at one point in time. It can show how common a condition is and whether factors are linked, but it usually cannot show which came first or prove cause and effect.

name: croton oil
clinical_significance: Croton oil is a caustic plant-derived irritant that can cause severe skin and gastrointestinal inflammation. It has been used experimentally to provoke inflammation and is not a safe home remedy.

name: crotoxin
clinical_significance: Crotoxin is a potent neurotoxic component of some rattlesnake venoms that can impair nerve-muscle signaling and cause paralysis or respiratory failure. Envenomation is a medical emergency.

name: crotoxyphos
clinical_significance: Crotoxyphos is an organophosphate insecticide. Exposure can inhibit cholinesterase and cause a potentially life-threatening cholinergic syndrome requiring urgent toxicology care.

name: croup
clinical_significance: An acute viral infection causing inflammation and narrowing of the upper airway, typically producing a barking cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor in young children.

name: crown
clinical_significance: The visible part of a tooth above the gum line, or a dental restoration that covers and protects a damaged tooth.

name: crown-rump length
clinical_significance: The ultrasound measurement from the top of an embryo's head to its bottom. It is the most accurate way to estimate pregnancy age during early pregnancy and helps monitor early growth.

name: crushing injury
clinical_significance: Damage caused when a body part is compressed between heavy objects. It can cause fractures, muscle and nerve injury, internal bleeding, or crush syndrome with kidney failure and dangerous electrolyte changes; severe injuries require emergency care.

name: crutch
clinical_significance: Crutches help reduce weight-bearing or improve stability after injury, surgery, or weakness. Incorrect height or use can cause falls, nerve compression, or shoulder and hand strain.

name: crying
clinical_significance: Persistent or unusual crying in an infant may signal pain, illness, or feeding difficulty, while inconsolable crying with fever, lethargy, breathing trouble, or poor feeding needs prompt medical assessment. Crying patterns can also be relevant to developmental and mental-health evaluation.

name: cryobiology
clinical_significance: Cryobiology studies how cells and tissues respond to low temperatures and freezing. Its findings support preservation of blood, reproductive cells, and transplant tissues used in clinical care.

name: cryoelectron microscopy
clinical_significance: Cryo-electron microscopy determines the structures of biological molecules and viruses. It supports drug and vaccine research but is not a routine patient diagnostic test.

name: cryoglobulin
clinical_significance: Cryoglobulins are proteins that precipitate at low temperatures and may form immune complexes that inflame or block blood vessels. Their detection can help investigate vasculitis, kidney disease, or some blood cancers.

name: cryoglobulinemia
clinical_significance: A condition in which abnormal blood proteins thicken or clump when cold. They can inflame small blood vessels and cause purplish skin spots, joint pain, nerve problems, kidney injury, or poor circulation.

name: cryopreservation
clinical_significance: Preserving cells, tissues, sperm, eggs, or embryos by cooling them to very low temperatures with protective chemicals. The material can later be thawed for treatment, research, or reproduction.

name: cryoprotective agent
clinical_significance: Cryoprotective agents reduce damage to cells and tissues during freezing and thawing. They are used in fertility care, transfusion medicine, and tissue preservation; toxicity and removal depend on the agent and application.

name: cryoscopy
clinical_significance: Cryoscopy measures changes in a solution’s freezing point and can estimate solute concentration. It has laboratory and research uses, including analysis of body fluids, but is not a common standalone clinical test.

name: cryostat
clinical_significance: An instrument that maintains very low temperatures and cuts thin frozen sections of tissue for rapid microscopic examination.

name: cryosurgery
clinical_significance: Cryosurgery destroys selected abnormal tissue by freezing it. It is used for some skin lesions, cervical precancers, and other specific conditions; pain, blistering, scarring, or injury to nearby tissue can occur.

name: cryotherapy
clinical_significance: Treatment using controlled cold to destroy or reduce abnormal tissue. It may treat selected skin lesions, tumors, eye problems, or prostate disease; pain, blistering, scarring, and damage to nearby tissue are possible.

name: cryoultramicrotomy
clinical_significance: Cryoultramicrotomy cuts ultrathin frozen tissue sections for electron microscopy and research. It helps examine cellular structures but is a laboratory preparation method rather than a patient treatment.

name: cryptococcosis
clinical_significance: Cryptococcosis is fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus, often affecting the lungs or brain in people with immune suppression.

name: cryptococcus
clinical_significance: Cryptococcus is a genus of environmental yeasts that can cause lung infection or meningitis, particularly in people with weakened immunity. Species identification and antigen testing can guide diagnosis and prolonged antifungal treatment.

name: cryptococcus gattii
clinical_significance: Cryptococcus gattii can cause lung or brain infection, including in otherwise healthy people, and occurs in tropical regions as well as some temperate areas. Severe disease may require prolonged antifungal treatment and sometimes surgery.

name: cryptococcus neoformans
clinical_significance: A yeast found in soil and bird droppings that can cause lung or brain infection after it is inhaled. Serious disease is most likely in people with weakened immunity and may require prolonged antifungal treatment.

name: cryptococcus terreus
clinical_significance: Cryptococcus terreus is a rare environmental yeast with occasional reports of human infection. Its clinical importance depends on confirming that an isolate is causing disease and determining antifungal susceptibility.

name: cryptophthalmos
clinical_significance: Cryptophthalmos is a rare congenital condition in which eyelid development is abnormal and skin may cover part or all of the eye. It can impair vision and may occur with other facial or genitourinary abnormalities.

name: Cryptophthalmos syndrome
clinical_significance: Cryptophthalmos syndrome is a rare inherited disorder involving abnormal eyelid and eye development, often with other congenital abnormalities. Early ophthalmic and multidisciplinary assessment helps address vision and associated health needs.

name: cryptorchidism
clinical_significance: A condition in which one or both testicles have not moved into the scrotum by birth. Some descend during the first months of life; a testicle that remains undescended or later moves back up needs medical assessment. Persistent undescended testicles increase the risk of reduced fertility, twisting, injury, and testicular cancer.

name: cryptosporidiosis
clinical_significance: An intestinal infection caused by microscopic Cryptosporidium parasites. It spreads when contaminated water, food, surfaces, or material from infected people or animals is swallowed. It may cause watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, and loss of fluids. Some people have no symptoms, while illness may be prolonged or severe in people with weakened immune systems.

name: cryptosporidium
clinical_significance: Cryptosporidium is a parasite that causes watery diarrhea and can spread through contaminated water, food, or contact. Disease may be severe or prolonged in people with weakened immunity.

name: cryptosporidium parvum
clinical_significance: Cryptosporidium parvum is a common cause of cryptosporidiosis, a diarrheal infection spread through contaminated water, food, or animal contact. Dehydration can be serious, especially in young children and immunocompromised people.

name: crystal
clinical_significance: Crystals in urine or tissue can indicate stones, crystal-related kidney injury, or metabolic disease, depending on their type and location. Laboratory identification can help determine the cause and guide prevention.

name: crystallin
clinical_significance: Crystallins are proteins that help keep the eye lens transparent. Changes or aggregation of these proteins contribute to some inherited cataracts and are studied in lens disease.

name: crystalline lens
clinical_significance: The clear, flexible structure inside the eye that focuses light onto the retina. It changes shape for near vision and becomes cloudy in cataracts, causing blurred or reduced vision.

name: crystals
clinical_significance: Crystals found in urine or tissue may indicate kidney or gallbladder stones, medication precipitation, or a metabolic disorder. Their type, location, and symptoms determine whether further testing or treatment is needed.

name: cubic millimeter
clinical_significance: A cubic millimeter is a unit of volume used in laboratory reporting, including some blood-cell counts. Unit conversions matter when comparing results reported in different formats.

name: cue
clinical_significance: In clinical practice, a cue is a sign, word, or prompt that helps guide recognition, communication, or a behavior. Cues can support assessment and care but should be interpreted in context.

name: culdoscopes
clinical_significance: Culdoscopes were instruments used to view pelvic organs through the vagina; the approach is now largely obsolete. Modern imaging and minimally invasive surgery have replaced most diagnostic uses.

name: culdoscopy
clinical_significance: Culdoscopy was an older procedure for examining pelvic organs through the vaginal wall. It has largely been replaced by ultrasound, laparoscopy, and other methods with different diagnostic and procedural risks.

name: culex (genus)
clinical_significance: Culex mosquitoes can transmit pathogens including West Nile virus and lymphatic filariasis, depending on species and region. Their control is relevant to prevention of mosquito-borne disease.

name: culicidae
clinical_significance: Culicidae is the mosquito family, which includes vectors of malaria, dengue, West Nile virus, and other infections. Identification and control of vector species support public-health prevention.

name: cultural competency
clinical_significance: Cultural competency in healthcare can improve communication, trust, and understanding of a patient’s beliefs and needs. Culturally responsive care can reduce misunderstandings and support equitable treatment.

name: culture media
clinical_significance: Nutrient materials prepared to grow microorganisms in a laboratory, with different formulas chosen for specific organisms, tests, or identification purposes.

name: cultured cell
clinical_significance: Cultured cells are used to study disease, test medicines, and produce some biologic products. Results may not fully predict effects in the human body, so they require confirmation in clinical research.

name: cupriavidus
clinical_significance: Cupriavidus is a genus of environmental bacteria that can occasionally cause opportunistic human infection, particularly in people with underlying illness or devices. Species identification helps interpret unusual isolates.

name: cupriavidus pauculus
clinical_significance: Cupriavidus pauculus is an uncommon environmental bacterium that can cause opportunistic bloodstream or respiratory infection, especially in medically vulnerable patients. A clinically significant isolate may require susceptibility-guided treatment.

name: curare
clinical_significance: Curare-like drugs block neuromuscular transmission and can cause profound paralysis, including paralysis of breathing muscles. Related medicines are used during anesthesia only with airway and ventilatory support.

name: curcumin
clinical_significance: A yellow compound in turmeric that has anti-inflammatory effects in laboratory studies. Evidence that supplements treat disease is limited or variable, and concentrated products can interact with medicines or cause stomach or liver problems.

name: cure
clinical_significance: Complete elimination or permanent resolution of a disease. The meaning of cure varies by condition; remission or no detectable disease does not always mean that a disease has been cured.

name: cure study
clinical_significance: A cure study evaluates whether treatment eliminates disease or prevents recurrence over a defined follow-up period. Long-term monitoring is important because apparent remission may not equal permanent cure.

name: curette
clinical_significance: A spoon-shaped or ring-shaped surgical instrument used to scrape, remove, or clean tissue from a cavity, bone, skin lesion, or tooth-supporting area. Its use and risks depend on the procedure and body site.

name: curie
clinical_significance: A unit of radioactivity equal to 3.7 billion nuclear disintegrations per second; the SI unit is the becquerel.

name: current therapy
clinical_significance: Current therapy refers to the treatment a patient is receiving at a given time. Reviewing it helps assess response, adherence, adverse effects, interactions, and whether changes are needed.

name: curvularia
clinical_significance: Curvularia is an environmental mold that can cause allergic disease and, rarely, invasive infection, particularly in immunocompromised people. Specimen source and clinical findings help distinguish disease from contamination.

name: cushingoid
clinical_significance: Resembling the physical features of excess glucocorticoid exposure, such as a round face, central weight gain, thin skin, easy bruising, and muscle weakness.

name: cushingoid facies
clinical_significance: Cushingoid facial changes, such as facial rounding and redness, can result from prolonged glucocorticoid exposure or excess cortisol. They can prompt review for medication effects or Cushing syndrome.

name: Cushing's syndrome
clinical_significance: Cushing syndrome results from prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, often from corticosteroid medicines or a hormone-producing tumor. It can cause diabetes, hypertension, infection risk, muscle weakness, and bone loss; finding the cause guides treatment.

name: cusp device
clinical_significance: A cusp device is a device associated with a valve or cusp structure; clinical significance depends on the specific device and its intended use. Device function and complications are assessed in the relevant specialty context.

name: cusp tear
clinical_significance: A cusp tear can disrupt a valve leaflet or another cusp structure and may impair function. If it involves a heart valve, it can cause acute regurgitation and heart failure and requires urgent cardiac assessment.

name: cuspid
clinical_significance: A cuspid, or canine tooth, helps guide the bite and chewing. Impaction, decay, or misalignment can affect oral function and may need dental treatment.

name: custirsen sodium
clinical_significance: Custirsen sodium is an investigational antisense cancer medicine studied with chemotherapy. It has not become an established standard treatment.

name: cutaneotrichosporon mucoides
clinical_significance: Cutaneotrichosporon mucoides is an environmental yeast that can rarely cause invasive infection, especially in people with weakened immunity. Accurate identification and antifungal susceptibility testing can be important.

name: cutaneous fistula
clinical_significance: A cutaneous fistula is an abnormal channel from an internal organ or space to the skin, often draining fluid or pus. It may result from surgery, infection, or inflammatory disease and can require treatment of the underlying cause.

name: cutaneous leiomyoma
clinical_significance: A usually benign smooth-muscle tumour of the skin, often presenting as firm, painful papules or nodules that may be triggered by cold or pressure. Multiple lesions can be associated with hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal-cell cancer, so extensive or familial disease needs genetic and renal-risk assessment.

name: cutaneous leiomyosarcoma
clinical_significance: Cutaneous leiomyosarcoma is a rare malignant smooth-muscle tumor of the skin. Complete removal and assessment for recurrence or spread are important; deeper tumors may behave more aggressively.

name: cutaneous mastocytosis
clinical_significance: Cutaneous mastocytosis is an abnormal accumulation of mast cells in the skin, causing lesions and sometimes flushing, itching, or systemic mediator symptoms. Extensive disease can increase anaphylaxis risk and may require specialist assessment.

name: cutaneous myxoma
clinical_significance: A cutaneous myxoma is a usually benign skin tumor, but multiple lesions can occur in genetic syndromes such as Carney complex. Associated heart tumors and endocrine disease make syndromic recognition clinically important.

name: cutaneous photosensitivity
clinical_significance: Cutaneous photosensitivity is an exaggerated skin reaction to sunlight or ultraviolet exposure. It can result from medicines, autoimmune disease, or inherited disorders and may require trigger review and sun protection.

name: cutaneous plaque
clinical_significance: A cutaneous plaque is a raised or thickened skin lesion that can occur in inflammatory, infectious, or neoplastic conditions. Appearance, distribution, and sometimes biopsy help identify its cause.

name: cutaneous t-cell lymphoma
clinical_significance: A cancer of immune cells that mainly affects the skin. It may begin as itchy, scaly patches or thicker plaques and later form lumps or widespread redness; some types also involve the blood, lymph nodes, or other organs.

name: cutibacterium avidum
clinical_significance: Cutibacterium avidum is a skin bacterium that can occasionally cause deep infection, particularly around prosthetic hip joints. It may be dismissed as contamination unless specimen findings and symptoms support true infection.

name: cutis laxa
clinical_significance: A group of inherited or acquired connective-tissue disorders characterized by loose, inelastic skin caused by abnormal elastic fibers. Some forms also affect the lungs, blood vessels, heart, gastrointestinal tract, or skeleton.

name: cutis marmorata
clinical_significance: A transient or persistent physiological mottling of the skin presenting as a reticular, bluish-purple, or erythematous marble-like vascular network, triggered by cold exposure due to vasomotor constriction of deep cutaneous arterioles and dilatation of superficial capillary venules.

name: cxc chemokine
clinical_significance: CXC chemokines attract immune cells and regulate inflammation. Their signaling is involved in infection defense and diseases such as cancer and chronic inflammation and is a target of biomedical research.

name: cyanates
clinical_significance: Cyanates are chemical compounds that can irritate or harm the body depending on the specific substance and exposure. Identification of the compound and route helps determine toxicity and appropriate management.

name: cyanides
clinical_significance: Cyanides prevent cells from using oxygen and can cause rapid, potentially fatal poisoning. Suspected exposure requires immediate emergency response and antidote treatment.

name: cyanobacteria
clinical_significance: Cyanobacteria can produce toxins in contaminated water that cause skin, gastrointestinal, liver, or neurologic illness. Harmful algal blooms are a public-health concern, especially for people and animals exposed to affected water.

name: cyanogen bromide
clinical_significance: Cyanogen bromide is a highly toxic chemical that can release cyanide and cause severe respiratory and systemic poisoning. Exposure is an emergency requiring specialized hazardous-materials and medical response.

name: cyanogen chloride
clinical_significance: Cyanogen chloride is a rapidly acting toxic gas that injures the eyes and airways and can disrupt cellular oxygen use. Exposure requires immediate evacuation, decontamination, and emergency care.

name: cyanogenic glucoside
clinical_significance: Cyanogenic glycosides can release cyanide when certain plants or seeds are crushed, chewed, or metabolized. Large exposures can cause life-threatening poisoning.

name: cyanophos
clinical_significance: Cyanophos is an organophosphate insecticide that can inhibit cholinesterase. Significant exposure may cause excessive secretions, breathing difficulty, muscle weakness, seizures, or death.

name: cyanosis
clinical_significance: A blue or gray-blue color of the skin, lips, or moist linings caused by too little oxygen in blood or abnormal blood flow. Sudden cyanosis, especially with breathing difficulty, requires emergency care.

name: cyclacillin
clinical_significance: Cyclacillin is a penicillin-class antibiotic used for susceptible bacterial infections. As with other antibiotics, unnecessary use can cause adverse effects and contribute to antimicrobial resistance.

name: cyclazocine
clinical_significance: Cyclazocine is an opioid-receptor–acting drug that was studied for analgesia and opioid dependence but is not in routine use. It can cause dysphoria and other central nervous system effects.

name: cyclic AMP
clinical_significance: Cyclic AMP is an intracellular signaling molecule that relays signals from hormones and receptors. Abnormal signaling is involved in several diseases and is a target of some medicines.

name: cyclic GMP
clinical_significance: Cyclic GMP is an intracellular signaling molecule involved in blood-vessel relaxation, vision, and other processes. Medicines that alter cGMP signaling are used for conditions including pulmonary hypertension and erectile dysfunction.

name: cyclic neutropenia
clinical_significance: Repeated episodes of low neutrophils, the white blood cells that fight many infections. Episodes often recur at regular intervals and may cause fever, mouth ulcers, sore throat, or infections.

name: cyclic peptide
clinical_significance: Cyclic peptides are found in some medicines and natural toxins, and their structure can improve stability or target binding. Their clinical significance depends on the specific peptide and its approved or investigational use.

name: cyclin
clinical_significance: Cyclins regulate the cell cycle and control when cells grow and divide. Abnormal cyclin activity can contribute to cancer and may be measured or targeted in some research and treatments.

name: cyclin b
clinical_significance: Cyclin B controls progression into mitosis, the stage when a cell divides. Abnormal regulation can promote uncontrolled cell growth and is studied in cancer biology.

name: cyclin c
clinical_significance: Cyclin C helps regulate cell-cycle entry and gene activity. Changes in cyclin C signaling are studied in cancer and other disorders of cell growth.

name: cyclin d
clinical_significance: Cyclin D promotes progression through a key cell-cycle checkpoint. Overactivity is common in some cancers and can help guide research into targeted treatment.

name: cyclin E
clinical_significance: Cyclin E helps cells move from growth into DNA replication. Overexpression or dysregulation occurs in some cancers and may be associated with aggressive tumor behavior.

name: cyclin h
clinical_significance: Cyclin H is part of a protein complex involved in cell-cycle control and gene transcription. Its clinical relevance is mainly in molecular research on cell growth and cancer.

name: cyclocephaly
clinical_significance: Cyclocephaly is a rare, severe congenital brain and skull abnormality involving a single eye socket or closely associated midline structures. It is typically incompatible with long-term survival.

name: cyclodextrin
clinical_significance: Cyclodextrins can improve the solubility or delivery of some medicines and are used as formulation ingredients. Their safety depends on the specific cyclodextrin, dose, and route.

name: cyclohexane
clinical_significance: Cyclohexane is an industrial solvent that can cause dizziness, headache, and nervous-system depression after substantial inhalation exposure. Workplace exposure controls reduce risk.

name: cycloheximide
clinical_significance: Cycloheximide blocks protein synthesis in laboratory experiments and is used as a research reagent. It is toxic and not a human treatment.

name: cycloleucine
clinical_significance: Cycloleucine is an amino-acid analogue used mainly in biochemical research to study methylation and cell metabolism. It has no established routine therapeutic use.

name: cyclooxygenase inhibitor
clinical_significance: Cyclooxygenase inhibitors reduce prostaglandin production and include many nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. They relieve pain and inflammation but can cause gastrointestinal bleeding, kidney injury, fluid retention, or cardiovascular events.

name: cyclopentanes
clinical_significance: Cyclopentane-containing compounds appear in medicines and biologically active molecules. Their clinical relevance depends on the specific compound rather than the chemical ring alone.

name: cyclopenthiazide
clinical_significance: Cyclopenthiazide is a thiazide diuretic used to treat high blood pressure and fluid retention. Monitoring may be needed for electrolyte changes, kidney effects, and interactions.

name: cyclophosphamide
clinical_significance: Cyclophosphamide is chemotherapy and an immunosuppressant used for selected cancers and severe autoimmune diseases. It can cause low blood counts, infection, infertility, and bladder injury, so monitoring and protective measures are important.

name: cycloserine
clinical_significance: Cycloserine is an antibiotic used as part of combination treatment for selected drug-resistant tuberculosis infections. It can cause serious neurologic or psychiatric adverse effects, requiring careful dosing and monitoring.

name: cyclospora
clinical_significance: Cyclospora is a parasite that causes prolonged or relapsing watery diarrhea, often after contaminated food or water. Diagnosis may require a specific stool test, and selected infections are treated with antibiotics.

name: cyclospora cayetanensis
clinical_significance: Cyclospora cayetanensis causes cyclosporiasis, a food- or waterborne intestinal infection that can lead to weeks of watery diarrhea and weight loss. It can be more severe in people with weakened immunity.

name: cyclosporiasis
clinical_significance: An intestinal infection caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis. It is usually spread through contaminated food or water and may cause prolonged or repeated watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, tiredness, loss of appetite, and weight loss.

name: cyclosporine
clinical_significance: Cyclosporine suppresses immune activity to prevent organ-transplant rejection and treat selected autoimmune diseases. It can damage the kidneys, raise blood pressure, and interact with many medicines, so levels and organ function are monitored.

name: cyclothymic disorder
clinical_significance: A chronic mood disorder involving repeated periods of hypomanic symptoms and depressive symptoms that do not meet full criteria for mania, hypomania, or a major depressive episode. Symptoms persist for at least two years in adults or one year in children and adolescents and cause clinically significant distress or impairment.

name: cyclotron
clinical_significance: A cyclotron accelerates charged particles and can produce short-lived radioisotopes used in PET imaging. Reliable production supports timely diagnostic scans.

name: cyproheptadine
clinical_significance: Cyproheptadine is an antihistamine used for allergic symptoms and selected other conditions. It can cause marked drowsiness and anticholinergic effects and should be used cautiously with other sedating medicines.

name: cyproterone
clinical_significance: Cyproterone is an antiandrogen used in some countries for selected hormone-related conditions. Safety depends on the formulation and dose; liver injury, mood effects, and other serious harms are possible.

name: cyproterone acetate
clinical_significance: Cyproterone acetate is an antiandrogen used in selected settings, including prostate cancer or androgen-related disorders, depending on local approval. High cumulative doses have been linked to meningioma, and liver and other adverse effects require consideration.

name: cyst
clinical_significance: A closed sac containing fluid, air, cells, or semisolid material. Cysts can occur in the skin, organs, glands, or other tissues and may be harmless, infected, or related to another disease.

name: cyst formation
