clinical_significance: Cyst formation can occur in many organs and may be incidental, benign, infected, or related to a tumor or inherited disease. Symptoms, imaging features, and growth determine whether monitoring or treatment is needed.

name: cystadenocarcinoma
clinical_significance: A cystadenocarcinoma is a malignant cyst-forming glandular tumor. Organ of origin, stage, and pathology determine treatment and prognosis.

name: cystadenofibroma
clinical_significance: A cystadenofibroma is usually a benign ovarian tumor containing glandular and fibrous tissue. It can resemble ovarian cancer on imaging, so pathologic assessment may be needed to confirm the diagnosis.

name: cystadenoma
clinical_significance: A usually noncancerous gland-forming tumor containing fluid-filled spaces or cyst-like structures. It can occur in several organs, may enlarge or cause symptoms, and sometimes requires removal or monitoring.

name: cystathionine
clinical_significance: Cystathionine is an intermediate in sulfur-amino-acid metabolism. Abnormal blood or urine levels can help evaluate rare metabolic disorders, including homocystinuria.

name: cystathioninuria
clinical_significance: Cystathioninuria is a rare metabolic finding in which cystathionine is increased in urine, often without symptoms. Markedly abnormal results may prompt evaluation for an underlying metabolic or liver disorder.

name: cysteamine
clinical_significance: Cysteamine is used to reduce cystine buildup in people with cystinosis, helping delay kidney damage and other complications. Lifelong adherence and monitoring are important.

name: cystectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part or all of the urinary bladder. Partial cystectomy is used for selected localized disease; complete or radical cystectomy removes the bladder and requires another route for urine to leave the body.

name: cysteine
clinical_significance: Cysteine is an amino acid used to build proteins and support antioxidant defenses. Abnormal metabolism can contribute to inherited disorders, while supplementation is not a substitute for disease-specific care.

name: cysteine protease
clinical_significance: Cysteine proteases are enzymes that break down proteins and are involved in normal cell function, infection, inflammation, and cancer. They are studied as biomarkers and potential drug targets.

name: cystic change
clinical_significance: Cystic change on imaging describes a fluid-filled or cavity-like appearance within tissue. It may reflect benign degeneration, inflammation, or a tumor, so interpretation depends on location and imaging features.

name: cystic duct
clinical_significance: The cystic duct carries bile between the gallbladder and common bile duct. A stone blocking it can cause biliary colic or gallbladder inflammation.

name: cystic fibrosis
clinical_significance: Cystic fibrosis is an inherited disorder caused by harmful changes in both copies of the CFTR gene. Thick mucus can cause chronic lung infection and damage, pancreatic insufficiency, poor growth, infertility in many males, and other complications; lifelong multidisciplinary treatment improves health and survival.

name: cystic kidney
clinical_significance: Cystic kidney disease includes disorders that produce fluid-filled spaces in the kidneys. Some are harmless, while inherited forms can cause high blood pressure, kidney enlargement, pain, infection, or progressive kidney failure.

name: cysticercosis
clinical_significance: Infection caused by the larval form of the pork tapeworm, \textit{Taenia solium}, after a person swallows its eggs from contaminated food, water, or hands. Cysts may form in muscle, skin, the eyes, or the brain. Brain infection, called neurocysticercosis, may cause seizures, headaches, or other nervous-system problems. Cysticercosis is different from intestinal taeniasis and is not caused by eating undercooked pork.

name: cystine
clinical_significance: Cystine is formed from two cysteine molecules and can accumulate in cells in cystinosis or crystallize in urine in cystinuria. The cause and location determine whether treatment is needed.

name: cystinosis
clinical_significance: A rare inherited disorder in which cystine, a building block of proteins, builds up inside cells and damages organs. It often affects the kidneys and eyes and may also impair growth, the thyroid, muscles, or other tissues.

name: cystinuria
clinical_significance: An inherited disorder in which the kidneys release too much cystine into urine, allowing recurrent cystine kidney stones to form. It requires long-term fluid intake, monitoring, and sometimes medicines to prevent stones.

name: cystitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the bladder that may be caused by infection, irritation, medicines, radiation, or other conditions. It can cause burning or discomfort with urination, frequent or urgent urination, lower-abdominal pressure, or blood in the urine; some forms cause bladder or pelvic pain without infection.

name: cystography
clinical_significance: X-ray or other imaging of the urinary bladder after contrast is placed in it. It can show bladder injury, leaks, fistulas, structural abnormalities, or urine flowing backward toward the kidneys.

name: cystoscope
clinical_significance: A thin, lighted instrument used to examine the urethra and bladder and, when needed, perform procedures.

name: cystoscopy
clinical_significance: Cystoscopy uses a camera passed through the urethra to inspect the bladder and urethra and may allow biopsy or treatment.

name: cystostomy
clinical_significance: A procedure that creates an opening from the bladder to the skin or another passage so urine can drain when it cannot leave normally through the urethra. It may be temporary or long term.

name: cytarabine liposome
clinical_significance: Liposomal cytarabine is a long-acting chemotherapy formulation given into the cerebrospinal fluid for selected cancers involving the meninges. It can cause neurologic toxicity and requires specialist dosing and monitoring.

name: cytidine
clinical_significance: Cytidine is a nucleoside used in RNA synthesis and cellular metabolism. Its clinical relevance is mainly through related medicines and metabolic pathways rather than routine supplementation.

name: cytidine deaminase
clinical_significance: Cytidine deaminase breaks down cytidine and related medicines, including some chemotherapy drugs. Differences in its activity can affect drug exposure and are studied in pharmacology and cancer treatment.

name: cytidine triphosphate
clinical_significance: Cytidine triphosphate is a nucleotide used by cells to build RNA and support lipid metabolism. Abnormal nucleotide pathways are relevant to some inherited disorders and cancer research.

name: cytochalasins
clinical_significance: Cytochalasins disrupt actin filaments and cell movement and are used as research chemicals. They are not established human medicines.

name: cytochlor
clinical_significance: Cytochlor is a laboratory compound used in studies of cell growth and metabolism. It has no established routine clinical use.

name: cytochrome
clinical_significance: Cytochromes are proteins involved in electron transport and cellular energy production; some also metabolize medicines and toxins. Their activity can influence drug effects and interactions.

name: cytochrome oxidase
clinical_significance: Cytochrome oxidase is the terminal enzyme in mitochondrial oxygen use and energy production. Cyanide poisoning blocks this enzyme, preventing cells from using oxygen and causing rapid systemic toxicity.

name: cytochrome P450
clinical_significance: A family of enzymes, found mainly in liver cells, that chemically changes many medicines, toxins, and hormones so the body can remove them. Genetic differences and drug interactions can alter their activity.

name: cytochromes b
clinical_significance: Cytochromes b are components of electron-transport systems in mitochondria and some microbes. Alterations can affect energy production and may contribute to inherited mitochondrial disease.

name: cytochromes c
clinical_significance: Cytochrome c transfers electrons in mitochondrial energy production and helps initiate programmed cell death. Its measurement is mainly relevant to laboratory research on cell injury and apoptosis.

name: cytodiagnosis
clinical_significance: Cytodiagnosis examines cells from fluids or tissue samples to help detect cancer, infection, or other disease. Results can guide further testing but depend on sample quality and clinical context.

name: cytogenetic analysis
clinical_significance: Cytogenetic analysis examines chromosome number and structure. It can diagnose inherited conditions and identify changes in cancers that influence prognosis or treatment.

name: cytogenetic response
clinical_significance: A cytogenetic response measures how abnormal chromosome-bearing cells change during treatment, especially in some leukemias. It helps assess treatment effectiveness and may guide care.

name: cytogenetics
clinical_significance: The study of chromosomes, including their number, structure, and arrangement. Laboratory tests can help identify inherited conditions, developmental differences, some pregnancy problems, leukemia, and other cancers.

name: cytokine
clinical_significance: A small protein messenger that allows cells to communicate during immunity, inflammation, infection, healing, and blood-cell production. Cytokines can protect tissues, but excessive or poorly controlled activity can cause disease.

name: cytokine receptor
clinical_significance: Cytokine receptors allow cells to respond to immune signaling proteins. Abnormal receptor signaling can cause immune or blood disorders and is a target of some medicines.

name: cytokinesis
clinical_significance: Cytokinesis is the final separation of a dividing cell into two daughter cells. Errors can cause abnormal chromosome numbers and are studied in cancer and developmental biology.

name: cytological technique
clinical_significance: Cytological techniques prepare and examine cells to detect abnormal, infectious, or inflammatory changes. They support screening and diagnosis, but suspicious or inconclusive findings may require tissue biopsy.

name: cytology
clinical_significance: The study of individual cells under a microscope. Cells may come from a body fluid, scraping, brushing, or needle sample and can be examined for cancer, infection, inflammation, or other disease.

name: cytolysis
clinical_significance: Cytolysis is cell breakdown caused by immune attack, infection, toxins, or physical injury. It can release cell contents and contribute to inflammation or organ damage.

name: cytomegalovirus
clinical_significance: A common herpesvirus that often causes no symptoms or a mild illness in healthy people. It can cause serious disease in unborn babies and people with weakened immunity, affecting organs such as the lungs, eyes, brain, or digestive tract.

name: cytomegalovirus infections
clinical_significance: Cytomegalovirus infection is usually mild or silent in healthy people but can cause congenital hearing or developmental problems and severe organ disease in immunocompromised patients. Diagnosis and treatment depend on age, immune status, and affected organs.

name: cytomegalovirus retinitis
clinical_significance: Cytomegalovirus retinitis is a sight-threatening retinal infection, usually in people with advanced immune suppression or after transplantation. It can cause floaters and blurred vision and may progress rapidly; early antiviral treatment is essential to prevent permanent vision loss.

name: cytopenia
clinical_significance: A lower-than-normal number of one or more blood-cell types: red blood cells, white blood cells, or platelets. The effects depend on which cells are low and how severe the reduction is.

name: cytoplasm
clinical_significance: The jelly-like material inside a cell outside its nucleus. It contains the cell's working structures and is where many chemical reactions, transport processes, and energy-producing activities occur.

name: cytoplasmic granule
clinical_significance: Cytoplasmic granules store or release substances such as enzymes, hormones, or immune mediators. Abnormal granules can help identify blood-cell, immune, or metabolic disorders.

name: cytoplasmic organelle
clinical_significance: Cell organelles carry out specialized functions such as energy production, protein processing, and waste breakdown. Organelle dysfunction can cause inherited metabolic and multisystem diseases.

name: cytoplasmic streaming
clinical_significance: Cytoplasmic streaming moves fluid and materials within some cells. It is important in plant and cell biology research but has little direct routine clinical use.

name: cytoplasmic vesicle
clinical_significance: Cytoplasmic vesicles transport or store proteins and other substances inside cells. Defects in vesicle transport can contribute to neurologic, immune, and metabolic disorders.

name: cytoprotection
clinical_significance: Cytoprotection refers to measures that protect healthy cells from injury, such as reducing treatment-related damage to the bladder or stomach. The approach depends on the damaging exposure and must not compromise treatment effectiveness.

name: cytoreductive surgery
clinical_significance: Surgery that removes as much visible cancer as can be taken safely. It may not remove every cancer cell and is often combined with chemotherapy, radiation, or other treatment; its value depends on the cancer's type, site, and spread.

name: cytosine
clinical_significance: Cytosine is one of the bases in DNA and RNA. Changes involving cytosine, including chemical modification or mutation, can alter gene function and contribute to disease.

name: cytosine arabinoside
clinical_significance: Cytosine arabinoside, or cytarabine, is chemotherapy used for selected leukemias and other cancers. It can suppress bone marrow and cause infection, bleeding, or neurologic toxicity, so blood counts and symptoms need monitoring.

name: cytosine nucleotides
clinical_significance: Cytosine nucleotides are building blocks for DNA and RNA and participate in cellular metabolism. Altered nucleotide synthesis or breakdown is relevant to inherited metabolic disease and cancer therapy.

name: cytoskeletal protein
clinical_significance: Cytoskeletal proteins maintain cell shape and enable movement, division, and intracellular transport. Defects can cause inherited blood, muscle, skin, or neurologic disorders.

name: cytoskeleton
clinical_significance: A network of protein fibers inside a cell that maintains its shape, moves materials, enables movement, and helps the cell divide. It constantly changes in response to the cell's needs.

name: cytotoxic T lymphocyte
clinical_significance: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes kill infected or cancerous cells. Their activity is central to antiviral immunity and cancer immunotherapy, but excessive activity can also damage healthy tissue.

name: cytotoxicity
clinical_significance: The ability of a substance or cell to damage or kill another cell. This may be part of normal immune defense or may result from medicines, toxins, radiation, or other harmful exposures.

name: dacarbazine
clinical_significance: A chemotherapy medicine used for Hodgkin lymphoma, melanoma, and some other cancers. It may cause severe nausea, low blood counts, or liver injury.

name: dacetuzumab
clinical_significance: Dacetuzumab is an investigational antibody targeting CD40 that was studied as a cancer immunotherapy. It is not an approved standard treatment.

name: daclizumab
clinical_significance: A monoclonal antibody that blocks the interleukin-2 receptor on activated immune cells. It was used for selected immune conditions but was withdrawn or restricted in many settings because of serious liver and other risks.

name: dacomitinib
clinical_significance: A targeted medicine that blocks several members of the epidermal-growth-factor receptor family and is used for selected EGFR-mutated lung cancers. Diarrhea, skin reactions, mouth sores, and lung or liver problems may occur.

name: dacryocystitis
clinical_significance: Infection or inflammation of the tear sac near the inner corner of the eye, usually because the tear-drainage passage is blocked. It can cause pain, redness, swelling, and pus and may need prompt treatment.

name: dacryocystocele
clinical_significance: A fluid-filled swelling near the inner corner of the eye caused by blockage and widening of the tear-drainage system. In a newborn it may interfere with breathing if it extends into the nose and needs prompt assessment.

name: dacryocyte analysis
clinical_significance: Examination or counting of teardrop-shaped red blood cells on a blood smear; numerous dacryocytes may occur with marrow fibrosis, infiltration, severe anemia, or splenic disease.

name: dactinomycin
clinical_significance: An anticancer medicine that binds DNA and interferes with gene activity and cell growth. It is used for selected cancers and can cause bone-marrow suppression, mouth sores, nausea, and tissue injury if it leaks outside a vein.

name: daidzein
clinical_significance: A naturally occurring isoflavone found in soy and other legumes that can be converted by intestinal bacteria into related compounds.

name: dalotuzumab
clinical_significance: Dalotuzumab is an investigational antibody targeting the insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor, studied in clinical trials for cancer. It is not an approved standard treatment.

name: dalteparin
clinical_significance: An injectable blood thinner used to prevent or treat clots in veins and the lungs. It reduces clotting through the body’s natural anticoagulant system; bleeding is the main risk, and kidney disease may require dose adjustment.

name: dalteparin sodium
clinical_significance: The sodium salt of dalteparin, a low-molecular-weight heparin used to prevent or treat venous thromboembolism; bleeding is the principal serious adverse effect.

name: danazol
clinical_significance: A synthetic androgen with antigonadotropic effects, used selectively for endometriosis, hereditary angioedema, or other conditions; androgenic, lipid, liver, and thrombotic adverse effects limit use.

name: dance therapy
clinical_significance: Dance therapy can support movement, expression, and psychosocial well-being in rehabilitation or mental-health care. It may complement, but does not replace, condition-specific medical treatment.

name: Dandy-Walker syndrome
clinical_significance: A birth difference in the cerebellum and nearby fluid spaces of the brain. It may cause enlarged head size from fluid buildup, delayed development, balance problems, seizures, or no symptoms.

name: dantrolene
clinical_significance: A muscle relaxant that reduces the release of calcium inside muscle cells. It is the main treatment for malignant hyperthermia and may cause weakness or liver injury.

name: danusertib
clinical_significance: Danusertib is an investigational kinase inhibitor studied in early clinical trials for advanced cancers. It is not an approved standard treatment.

name: dapsone
clinical_significance: A sulfone antimicrobial used for leprosy, selected dermatitis, and other infections; haemolysis, especially with G6PD deficiency, methaemoglobinaemia, agranulocytosis, and severe skin reactions are important risks.

name: daptomycin
clinical_significance: An antibiotic used for selected serious infections caused by gram-positive bacteria, including resistant strains. It can damage muscles and kidneys, so treatment requires appropriate testing and monitoring.

name: darbepoetin alfa
clinical_significance: A long-acting medicine that stimulates the bone marrow to make more red blood cells. It is used for selected anemia related to kidney disease or cancer treatment, but can raise blood pressure and the risk of blood clots.

name: dark adaptation
clinical_significance: The gradual adjustment that allows the eyes to see better after moving from bright light into darkness. Poor dark adaptation may result from retinal disease, vitamin A deficiency, aging, or some medicines.

name: darunavir
clinical_significance: An antiretroviral medicine that blocks HIV protease, an enzyme needed to make new viruses. It is used with other HIV medicines and has important interactions and possible liver or skin reactions.

name: dasatinib
clinical_significance: A targeted cancer medicine that blocks abnormal tyrosine-kinase signals, especially those caused by BCR::ABL1. It treats selected blood cancers and may cause low blood counts, fluid around the lungs, bleeding, or abnormal heart rhythms.

name: data collection
clinical_significance: Clinical data collection gathers information on symptoms, tests, treatment, and outcomes. Accurate and complete data support diagnosis, safety monitoring, research, and quality improvement.

name: data management
clinical_significance: Clinical data management protects and organizes health or research information so it remains accurate, secure, and usable. Poor data handling can compromise care decisions, privacy, or study results.

name: data traceability
clinical_significance: Data traceability records where data came from, how they were changed, and who handled them. It supports reproducibility, audit, patient safety, and reliable clinical research.

name: daunorubicin
clinical_significance: A chemotherapy medicine that damages cancer-cell DNA and is used mainly for selected blood cancers. It can lower blood counts and, especially after repeated doses, weaken or damage the heart.

name: daunorubicin hydrochloride
clinical_significance: The hydrochloride salt of daunorubicin, an anthracycline chemotherapy drug that interferes with DNA and is used mainly for acute leukemias. Important risks include bone-marrow suppression and heart damage.

name: dav regimen
clinical_significance: An abbreviation used for more than one cancer-treatment combination. In older leukemia reports, DAV meant daunorubicin, cytarabine, and etoposide; in newer reports, it may mean daunorubicin, cytarabine, and venetoclax. The source must identify the drugs and cancer before the regimen is used.

name: dcc gene
clinical_significance: A gene that helps guide developing nerve fibers and may also help control cell growth. Harmful changes in this gene can cause some developmental nerve disorders and may contribute to certain cancers.

name: dcmp deaminase
clinical_significance: dCMP deaminase is an enzyme in pyrimidine metabolism that converts deoxycytidine monophosphate to deoxyuridine monophosphate. Its activity is studied in nucleotide balance and cancer-drug response.

name: de novo
clinical_significance: Newly arising in an individual rather than inherited from either parent; the term is commonly used for genetic variants or disease presentations.

name: deafness
clinical_significance: Complete or severe loss of hearing in one or both ears. The problem may involve sound passing through the outer or middle ear, the inner ear or hearing nerve, or more than one of these areas.

name: death
clinical_significance: The permanent end of life. It may be confirmed when the heart and breathing stop permanently or when all brain function has permanently stopped, according to medical and legal standards.

name: debridement
clinical_significance: Removal of dead, damaged, infected, or contaminated tissue from a wound. It may be done with instruments, irrigation, or other methods to reduce infection, reveal healthy tissue, and support healing.

name: debrisoquin
clinical_significance: Debrisoquin is an older blood-pressure medicine that also serves as a probe for CYP2D6 enzyme activity. Differences in how people metabolize it helped establish pharmacogenetic variation relevant to some medicines.

name: decanoic acid
clinical_significance: A ten-carbon saturated fatty acid, also called capric acid, found in some fats and studied for antimicrobial, metabolic, and antiseizure effects.

name: decapitation
clinical_significance: Decapitation is catastrophic trauma causing immediate, unsurvivable injury. It is relevant in emergency medicine, forensic assessment, and trauma surveillance.

name: decenoic acid
clinical_significance: An unsaturated ten-carbon fatty acid; its biologic effects depend on the position and geometry of its double bond and on tissue and dietary context.

name: decerebrate state
clinical_significance: A severe neurologic posture marked by extension and inward rotation of the arms and extension of the legs, usually indicating serious injury to the brainstem or structures above it.

name: decibel
clinical_significance: A unit used to describe sound intensity. Higher values mean louder sound; repeated or very loud exposure can damage hearing, depending on the level and duration.

name: decidua
clinical_significance: The specialized lining of the uterus during pregnancy. It is shed after delivery and helps support the pregnancy and placenta.

name: deciduoma
clinical_significance: Deciduoma is an uncommon and historically variable term for a mass or tumor-like growth associated with decidual tissue. Because usage differs by source, the underlying pathology must be specified for clinical decisions.

name: deciduous tooth
clinical_significance: A primary or baby tooth that is eventually shed and replaced by a permanent tooth. Early decay or loss can affect chewing, speech, and the space needed for permanent teeth.

name: decision making
clinical_significance: The process of comparing information, options, benefits, risks, and preferences to choose an action or plan, including shared decision-making in healthcare.

name: decitabine
clinical_significance: A cancer medicine that changes abnormal gene activity and interferes with growth of blood-forming cancer cells. It is used for selected blood cancers and may cause low blood counts, infection, bleeding, or fatigue.

name: declopramide
clinical_significance: Declopramide is an experimental compound studied for effects on DNA repair and multidrug resistance. It is not an established treatment in routine care.

name: decontamination
clinical_significance: Steps that remove or reduce a harmful substance from the skin, eyes, clothing, or digestive tract and prevent further absorption. The correct method depends on the substance; some exposures require washing, irrigation, or specialist treatment.

name: decorin
clinical_significance: A small protein-sugar molecule found around cells. It helps organize collagen, influences tissue growth and repair, and may affect scar formation.

name: decreased concentration
clinical_significance: Reduced ability to sustain attention or mental focus; causes include sleep loss, stress, medications, mood disorders, substance use, and neurologic or medical illness.

name: decreased dentin
clinical_significance: Reduced thickness or formation of dentin, the mineralized tissue beneath tooth enamel; causes include developmental defects, wear, erosion, caries, or dental treatment.

name: decreased libido
clinical_significance: Reduced sexual desire that may be related to relationships, mood, stress, medications, hormones, chronic illness, pain, or other health factors.

name: deep venous thrombosis
clinical_significance: Deep venous thrombosis is a blood clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg. It can cause swelling and pain and may break off to cause a life-threatening pulmonary embolism, so suspected cases need prompt diagnostic evaluation.

name: defecation
clinical_significance: The process of passing stool from the rectum through the anus. It involves signals from a full rectum, contraction of the bowel, and relaxation of the anal muscles, followed by voluntary control of timing.

name: defective virus
clinical_significance: A virus missing genetic information needed to reproduce independently. It can multiply only with help from another virus or host system and may influence infection without always causing disease on its own.

name: defense mechanism
clinical_significance: A psychological process, often unconscious, that helps a person manage conflict, anxiety, or distress; its usefulness depends on context and flexibility.

name: defensin
clinical_significance: A small protective protein made by skin, lining tissues, and immune cells. It can damage microbes and is part of the body’s early defense against infection.

name: deferasirox
clinical_significance: An oral iron-chelating medicine used to reduce chronic iron overload when clinically indicated; kidney, liver, hearing, and gastrointestinal toxicity require monitoring.

name: deferiprone
clinical_significance: An oral iron chelator used for transfusional iron overload; neutropenia or agranulocytosis is an important adverse effect requiring blood-count monitoring.

name: deferoxamine
clinical_significance: A parenteral iron chelator used for severe or chronic iron overload and sometimes aluminum toxicity; treatment requires monitoring for ocular, auditory, renal, and infectious complications.

name: defibrillator
clinical_significance: A device that delivers an electrical shock to treat certain life-threatening abnormal heart rhythms. External defibrillators are used during cardiac arrest; implanted devices can detect and treat dangerous rhythms automatically.

name: defined observation
clinical_significance: A defined observation is a specified, reproducible finding or measurement used in clinical records or research. Clear criteria improve consistency, comparison, and interpretation of patient outcomes.

name: deformity
clinical_significance: An abnormal shape, alignment, or structure of a body part caused by development, injury, disease, pressure, or unusual growth. It may affect appearance, movement, comfort, or organ function.

name: degarelix
clinical_significance: An injected hormone-blocking medicine that rapidly lowers testosterone. It is used for advanced prostate cancer; injection-site reactions, hot flushes, bone loss, and other hormone-related effects may occur.

name: degenerative disorder
clinical_significance: A disease in which progressive cellular or tissue deterioration causes loss of structure or function, as in neurodegenerative, joint, retinal, or muscle disorders.

name: deglutition
clinical_significance: The coordinated process of moving food, liquid, or saliva from the mouth through the throat and esophagus into the stomach. Problems can cause choking, coughing, or food entering the airway.

name: degranulation
clinical_significance: Release of stored chemicals from cells such as mast cells, white blood cells, and platelets. The chemicals help respond to injury or infection but can also cause allergy, inflammation, blood-vessel changes, or clotting.

name: degrees fahrenheit
clinical_significance: A unit on the Fahrenheit temperature scale. In clinical care, body temperature may be reported in Fahrenheit; 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit is an approximate average normal oral temperature, not a universal threshold.

name: dehiscence
clinical_significance: Partial or complete separation of a healing wound or surgical closure. It may involve only the skin or deeper tissues; increasing pain, drainage, or exposed tissue requires prompt medical assessment.

name: dehydration
clinical_significance: Loss of more water and electrolytes than are replaced, often from vomiting, diarrhea, fever, sweating, or poor fluid intake. It can cause thirst, dry mouth, reduced urination, dizziness, fast heartbeat, abnormal electrolyte levels, or shock.

name: dehydroascorbic acid
clinical_significance: The oxidized form of vitamin C. Cells can take it up and convert it back to active vitamin C, allowing it to participate in antioxidant and other chemical reactions.

name: dehydroepiandrosterone
clinical_significance: A hormone made mainly by the adrenal glands that the body can convert into other sex hormones. Levels change with age and illness; supplements may cause acne, unwanted hair, mood changes, or medicine interactions.

name: deinstitutionalize
clinical_significance: To help a person leave long-term institutional care and live in the community with suitable housing, healthcare, and support. The plan should protect safety, treatment needs, and independence.

name: deja vu
clinical_significance: A brief feeling that a new situation has happened before. Occasional episodes are common, but frequent episodes with loss of awareness, unusual movements, or confusion may occur with seizures and need assessment.

name: delavirdine
clinical_significance: An older HIV medicine that blocks reverse transcriptase, an enzyme HIV needs to copy its genetic material. It was used with other HIV medicines, but resistance and drug interactions limit its use.

name: delayed hypersensitivity
clinical_significance: An immune reaction that develops hours or days after exposure rather than immediately. It can cause contact dermatitis, some medicine rashes, or a reaction to a tuberculosis skin test.

name: delayed orgasm
clinical_significance: Persistent difficulty or inability to reach orgasm despite adequate stimulation, causing distress. Medicines, illness, hormonal or nerve problems, anxiety, trauma, and relationship factors may contribute.

name: delayed puberty
clinical_significance: Puberty that has not begun or is not progressing at the expected age. Family pattern, poor nutrition, chronic illness, hormone disorders, or problems involving the ovaries, testes, brain, or pituitary may contribute.

name: deletion mutation
clinical_significance: A genetic change in which one or more DNA building blocks are missing. Its effect depends on the location and size of the deletion and whether it changes a gene or its control region.

name: delftia
clinical_significance: A group of oxygen-using bacteria found mainly in soil and water. Human infection is uncommon but can occur as an opportunistic infection, especially in people with weakened immunity or medical devices.

name: delftia acidovorans
clinical_significance: Delftia acidovorans is an environmental bacterium that rarely causes human infection but can cause bloodstream, respiratory, or device-associated disease, especially in medically vulnerable people. A credible isolate should be interpreted with symptoms and susceptibility results.

name: delirium
clinical_significance: A sudden change in attention, awareness, and thinking that fluctuates over hours or days. It usually results from illness, infection, medicines, substance use or withdrawal, dehydration, or another medical problem.

name: Delphi technique
clinical_significance: The Delphi technique gathers judgments from experts through repeated, usually anonymous surveys to build agreement. It is used in healthcare research to develop guidelines or prioritize outcomes when evidence is limited.

name: deltacoronavirus
clinical_significance: A group of coronaviruses identified by their genetic features. Some infect birds or mammals, and their ability to infect people or cause disease depends on the specific virus and host.

name: deltaretrovirus
clinical_significance: A group of viruses that includes human T-cell leukemia viruses. They copy their RNA into DNA inside infected cells; some can persist for years and cause blood-cell disorders or cancer.

name: delta-tocopherol
clinical_significance: One form of vitamin E found in foods and supplements. It has antioxidant activity, but alpha-tocopherol is the main form maintained in human blood and used to assess vitamin E status.

name: deltoid
clinical_significance: The large, triangular muscle covering the shoulder. It helps lift the arm and stabilize the shoulder joint; injury or nerve damage can cause pain and weakness.

name: delusion
clinical_significance: A firmly held false belief that remains despite clear evidence to the contrary and is not explained by the person’s cultural background. It may involve persecution, grandiosity, illness, or other themes.

name: delusional disorder
clinical_significance: A mental disorder with one or more persistent delusions lasting at least one month, while overall functioning is relatively preserved. Hallucinations, if present, relate closely to the delusional belief.

name: demeclocycline
clinical_significance: A tetracycline antibiotic that blocks bacterial protein production. It was also used to reduce excess water retention in some patients with inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion; adverse effects include sun sensitivity and kidney or liver problems.

name: demecolcine
clinical_significance: A colchicine-related substance that disrupts microtubules, structures needed for cell division. It has limited medical use and can be highly toxic, causing gastrointestinal, blood-cell, nerve, or organ injury.

name: dementia
clinical_significance: A lasting decline in memory, thinking, language, judgment, or other mental abilities that interferes with independent daily life. Causes include brain diseases, blood-vessel disease, infections, medicines, and some treatable medical problems.

name: demethylation
clinical_significance: Removal of a small chemical group called a methyl group from a molecule such as DNA or a protein. In DNA, this change can alter which genes are active and affect cell development or disease.

name: demographics domain
clinical_significance: Demographics describe population characteristics such as age, sex, and social context. They help interpret health risks and outcomes and identify disparities, but should not replace individual clinical assessment.

name: demulcent
clinical_significance: A substance that coats and soothes irritated moist body linings, temporarily reducing discomfort from dryness, inflammation, or minor injury.

name: demyelinating disease
clinical_significance: A disease in which the protective covering around nerve fibers is damaged. Nerve signals then slow or fail, causing problems such as weakness, numbness, vision changes, or poor coordination.

name: demyelination
clinical_significance: Loss or damage of myelin, the protective coating that helps nerve fibers send signals quickly. It can disrupt movement, sensation, vision, balance, or thinking and may result from immune, infectious, inherited, or toxic disorders.

name: denaturant
clinical_significance: A substance added to another product to change its taste, smell, or properties, often to make it unsuitable for drinking. Some denaturants are poisonous or irritating, so health effects depend on the product and amount swallowed or contacted.

name: dendrimer
clinical_significance: Dendrimers are branched nanoscale molecules studied for drug delivery and imaging; clinical use depends on biocompatibility, distribution, and toxicity testing.

name: dendrite
clinical_significance: A branching extension of a nerve cell that receives signals from other nerve cells or sensory receptors and carries those signals toward the cell body.

name: dendritic cell
clinical_significance: An immune cell that captures foreign material and shows pieces of it to other immune cells. This helps start a targeted immune response against infections and abnormal cells.

name: dendritic spine
clinical_significance: A tiny branch on a nerve cell that receives signals from other nerve cells. Its shape and number can change with learning, development, and some brain diseases.

name: denervation
clinical_significance: Denervation is loss of nerve supply to a muscle or tissue, causing weakness, atrophy, altered sensation, or autonomic dysfunction.

name: dengue
clinical_significance: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral illness that can cause fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint aches, nausea, and rash. Severe dengue can cause bleeding, shock, or organ injury; warning signs often appear as fever subsides and require urgent care.

name: dengue virus
clinical_significance: The virus that causes dengue fever and is spread mainly by infected Aedes mosquitoes. Four major types exist; protection after infection is strongest against the same type and does not reliably prevent later infection by other types.

name: denial
clinical_significance: A psychological response in which a person cannot or will not accept a distressing fact, diagnosis, or situation. It may briefly reduce distress but can delay needed decisions or treatment when persistent.

name: denileukin diftitox
clinical_significance: Denileukin diftitox-cxdl is a targeted biologic approved for adults with relapsed or refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphoma after at least one systemic treatment. It can cause capillary-leak syndrome, vision changes, and other serious adverse effects.

name: denominator
clinical_significance: The number below the line in a fraction. In a medical rate or proportion, it represents the total population or group being compared with the number above it.

name: denosumab
clinical_significance: A medicine that blocks a protein needed to activate bone-destroying cells. It is used for osteoporosis and some cancer-related bone problems; stopping it without follow-up can cause rapid bone loss and spine fractures.

name: densitometry
clinical_significance: Measurement of how dense a tissue is, most often the mineral content of bone. A bone-density scan helps diagnose osteoporosis, estimate fracture risk, and monitor treatment.

name: density
clinical_significance: The amount of mass in a given volume. In medicine, density measurements help describe bone mineral content, tissue composition, fluid collections, or findings on imaging.

name: Dent disease
clinical_significance: An inherited disorder of the kidney’s filtering tubes, usually affecting boys. It causes loss of small proteins in urine, excess urinary calcium, kidney stones or calcium deposits, and sometimes progressive kidney failure.

name: dental abscess
clinical_significance: A pocket of pus caused by infection in a tooth or surrounding gum. It may cause severe toothache, swelling, fever, or difficulty opening the mouth; spreading facial or neck swelling needs urgent care.

name: dental alloy
clinical_significance: A mixture of metals used to make dental fillings, crowns, bridges, dentures, orthodontic appliances, or other restorations. Its strength, appearance, corrosion resistance, and possible allergies depend on its composition.

name: dental alveolus
clinical_significance: The part of the upper or lower jawbone that forms a tooth socket and holds the tooth root. It can shrink after tooth loss or severe gum disease.

name: dental amalgam
clinical_significance: A durable filling material made by mixing liquid mercury with powdered metals, mainly silver, tin, and copper. It is strong but has a silver color and may be unsuitable in some situations.

name: dental anxiety
clinical_significance: Fear or distress about dental treatment that may cause avoidance, delayed care, or difficulty during appointments. Reassurance, communication, pain control, and behavioral or medicine-based support may help.

name: dental arch
clinical_significance: The curved arrangement of teeth and the bone supporting them in the upper or lower jaw. Its shape affects tooth alignment, bite, speech, chewing, and space for dental restorations.

name: dental articulator
clinical_significance: A device that holds models of the upper and lower teeth and imitates jaw movements. It helps dental professionals design and adjust crowns, bridges, dentures, and other restorations so they fit the bite.

name: dental calculus
clinical_significance: Hardened plaque formed when minerals in saliva or gum fluid collect on teeth. It cannot be removed reliably by brushing alone and can contribute to gum inflammation and disease.

name: dental caries
clinical_significance: Tooth decay caused when bacteria use sugars and produce acids that remove minerals from enamel and dentin. Untreated decay can cause sensitivity, pain, infection, and tooth loss.

name: dental cement
clinical_significance: A dental material used to attach crowns, bridges, or orthodontic bands, fill small spaces, or protect exposed tooth tissue. Its strength and use depend on the material and treatment.

name: dental clasp
clinical_significance: A part of a removable partial denture that rests against or around supporting teeth to help keep the denture in place. Poor fit or excessive pressure can irritate teeth or gums.

name: dental deposit
clinical_significance: Material that collects on a tooth, such as plaque, hardened tartar, food debris, or stain. Some deposits irritate the gums or support decay and may require professional cleaning.

name: dental disease
clinical_significance: A disorder of the teeth, gums, jaw, or supporting tissues, including decay, gum disease, infection, and tooth loss. Fluoride, daily cleaning, limited frequent sugar exposure, and dental visits reduce risk.

name: dental dysplasia
clinical_significance: Abnormal development of a tooth or its supporting tissue. It may change the tooth’s shape, color, strength, position, or eruption and can increase the risk of wear, decay, or infection.

name: dental fissure
clinical_significance: A narrow natural groove or developmental defect in a tooth, especially on a chewing surface. Food and bacteria can collect there, increasing the risk of decay.

name: dental hygiene
clinical_significance: Daily care of the teeth, gums, tongue, and mouth, including brushing with fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between teeth. It removes plaque and helps prevent decay, gum disease, and bad breath.

name: dental implant
clinical_significance: A small biocompatible fixture placed in the jawbone to support a replacement tooth, bridge, or denture. Bone may grow around it for stability; risks include infection, poor healing, nerve injury, and implant failure.

name: dental impression material
clinical_significance: A material placed in a tray to make an accurate mold of the teeth and mouth tissues. The mold helps make crowns, dentures, orthodontic appliances, restorations, or study models.

name: dental inlay
clinical_significance: A custom-made filling fitted inside the grooves of a damaged tooth and bonded in place. It restores areas too large for a simple filling but does not cover the tooth’s cusps like an onlay or crown.

name: dental material
clinical_significance: A substance used in dental care, such as composite, amalgam, ceramic, metal, cement, bonding material, impression material, or implant material. Choice depends on the treatment, location, strength, appearance, and patient factors.

name: dental occlusion
clinical_significance: The way the upper and lower teeth meet when the mouth closes or the jaw moves. An abnormal bite may contribute to difficulty chewing, tooth wear, jaw pain, or muscle strain.

name: dental overjet
clinical_significance: The horizontal distance between the upper and lower front teeth when the teeth are closed. A large overjet may increase the risk of trauma to the upper front teeth and affect biting.

name: dental papilla
clinical_significance: Soft embryonic tissue beneath a developing tooth. Its cells form the dentin and living pulp, which contains the tooth’s nerves and blood vessels.

name: dental pellicle
clinical_significance: A thin protective film of salivary proteins that forms on tooth enamel soon after cleaning. Bacteria can attach to it and build dental plaque.

name: dental plaque
clinical_significance: A sticky film of bacteria, saliva, and food material on teeth and along the gums. If not removed by brushing and cleaning between teeth, it can cause decay, gum inflammation, and gum disease.

name: dental porcelain
clinical_significance: A tooth-colored ceramic used for crowns, veneers, bridges, and other restorations. It provides a natural appearance but may chip or fracture under heavy force.

name: dental procedure
clinical_significance: An examination, preventive service, or treatment involving the teeth, gums, jaw, or mouth, such as cleaning, filling, extraction, root-canal treatment, or restoration. Benefits and risks depend on the procedure.

name: dental prosthesis
clinical_significance: An artificial replacement for one or more missing teeth or nearby mouth tissues, such as a denture, bridge, crown, or implant-supported restoration. It restores appearance, speech, and chewing.

name: dental pulp
clinical_significance: The living soft tissue at the center of a tooth. It contains nerves, blood vessels, and connective tissue and can become inflamed or infected when decay or injury reaches it.

name: dental sac
clinical_significance: A layer of tissue surrounding a developing tooth. It forms the tissues that support the tooth, including the periodontal ligament, cementum, and part of the surrounding jawbone.

name: dentate gyrus
clinical_significance: A curved part of the hippocampus that helps process incoming information and form memories. It also produces some new nerve cells during adulthood.

name: dentifrice
clinical_significance: A preparation, such as toothpaste or tooth powder, used to clean teeth. Fluoride dentifrice strengthens enamel and helps prevent tooth decay when used regularly.

name: dentigerous cyst
clinical_significance: A fluid-filled sac that forms around the crown of an unerupted tooth, usually in the jaw. It may cause swelling, move nearby teeth, or damage bone if it becomes large or infected.

name: dentin
clinical_significance: The hard tissue beneath tooth enamel that forms most of the tooth. Tiny channels within it can transmit sensitivity, especially when dentin is exposed by decay, wear, gum recession, or injury.

name: dentin sensitivity
clinical_significance: Brief, sharp tooth pain caused by cold, heat, sweet foods, touch, or air reaching exposed dentin. Decay, worn enamel, gum recession, cracks, or aggressive brushing can expose it.

name: dentinogenesis
clinical_significance: Formation of dentin by specialized cells during tooth development and repair. Abnormal dentin formation may produce weak, discolored, sensitive teeth that wear or fracture easily.

name: dentinogenesis imperfecta
clinical_significance: An inherited disorder in which dentin forms abnormally, causing teeth that may look blue-gray or amber and break, wear, or discolor easily. Some forms occur with fragile bones.

name: dentist
clinical_significance: A licensed healthcare professional who examines, prevents, diagnoses, and treats diseases and injuries of the teeth, gums, jaw, and mouth.

name: dentistry
clinical_significance: The healthcare field concerned with preventing, diagnosing, and treating disorders and injuries of the teeth, gums, jaw, and mouth, including restoration, replacement, and oral health education.

name: dentition
clinical_significance: The teeth present in the mouth, including their number, arrangement, development, and eruption. Children usually have primary teeth that are replaced by permanent teeth; disease, injury, or development can alter either set.

name: denture
clinical_significance: A removable replacement for some or all missing teeth and nearby mouth tissues. Partial dentures replace selected teeth; complete dentures replace all teeth in one jaw. Correct fit, cleaning, and review help prevent sores and infection.

name: denture base
clinical_significance: The part of a denture that rests on the gums and mouth tissues and supports the artificial teeth. Its shape and fit distribute chewing pressure and help prevent soreness.

name: denturist
clinical_significance: A dental professional authorized in some regions to make, fit, adjust, and repair removable dentures within the local scope of practice. Dentists may also assess oral disease and provide related treatment.

name: Denys-Drash syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare genetic disorder caused by changes in the \textit{WT1} gene. It can cause severe kidney disease, differences in sex development, and a high risk of Wilms kidney tumor in childhood.

name: deoxycoformycin
clinical_significance: An anticancer medicine that blocks an enzyme needed by some cells to make DNA. It was used for selected blood cancers and can suppress bone marrow, weaken immunity, and increase the risk of serious infections.

name: deoxycytidine
clinical_significance: A DNA building block made of the base cytosine joined to the sugar deoxyribose. Cells use it to make and repair DNA.

name: deoxycytidine kinase
clinical_significance: An enzyme that chemically activates deoxycytidine and some similar medicines. The activated medicines can interfere with the DNA of cancer cells or viruses and stop them from multiplying.

name: deoxyglucose
clinical_significance: A molecule resembling glucose that is used mainly in research and PET imaging. When labeled with a radioactive form of fluorine, it can show tissues using unusually large amounts of glucose, including many tumors and areas of inflammation.

name: deoxyguanosine
clinical_significance: A DNA building block made of the base guanine joined to the sugar deoxyribose. Cells use it to make and repair DNA.

name: deoxyribonuclease
clinical_significance: An enzyme that breaks DNA into smaller pieces. An inhaled laboratory-made form can thin thick mucus in some people with cystic fibrosis by breaking down DNA released from damaged cells.

name: deoxyribonucleic acid
clinical_significance: DNA, the molecule that stores hereditary information in cells. Its sequence helps instruct protein production and cell control; changes may be inherited or acquired during life and can affect health.

name: deoxyribonucleosides
clinical_significance: Molecules made of one of the four DNA bases joined to the sugar deoxyribose. Cells use them as starting materials when making or repairing DNA.

name: deoxyribonucleotides
clinical_significance: DNA building blocks made of a base, deoxyribose sugar, and phosphate groups. The four forms—dATP, dGTP, dCTP, and dTTP—are assembled into DNA strands.

name: deoxyuridine
clinical_significance: Deoxyuridine is a DNA-related nucleoside used in laboratory studies and some metabolic evaluations. Abnormal handling may be relevant to rare nucleotide-metabolism disorders.

name: dependovirus
clinical_significance: A group of small viruses that usually need another virus, such as an adenovirus or herpesvirus, to reproduce. They are generally not known to cause serious disease in healthy people.

name: depersonalization
clinical_significance: A feeling of being detached from or observing one’s own body, thoughts, or emotions as if from outside. It can occur with anxiety, trauma, panic, substance use, or other mental health conditions.

name: dephosphorylation
clinical_significance: Removal of a phosphate group from a molecule. This can switch proteins and other cell components on or off and change how cells communicate, use energy, grow, or respond to signals.

name: depression
clinical_significance: Depression is a group of mental-health disorders marked by persistent low or irritable mood, loss of interest, or both, with possible changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, movement, or self-worth. Symptoms interfere with daily life and may include thoughts of death or suicide; effective treatments are available, and suicidal thoughts require immediate support.

name: depressive disorder
clinical_significance: A mood disorder involving persistent low mood, loss of interest, or both, with possible changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, movement, or self-worth. Diagnosis depends on the pattern, duration, severity, and functional impact of symptoms.

name: depth perception
clinical_significance: The ability to judge how far away objects are and where they are in three-dimensional space. It depends mainly on using both eyes together and also on movement, size, shading, and perspective cues.

name: depurination
clinical_significance: Loss of the DNA bases adenine or guanine, leaving a gap in the DNA strand. If the gap is not repaired correctly, it can cause a genetic mutation.

name: derealization
clinical_significance: A feeling that the outside world is unreal, distant, dreamlike, or visually changed, while the person knows it is not literally unreal. It may occur with anxiety, panic, trauma, dissociation, or substance use.

name: dermabacter
clinical_significance: Dermabacter is a genus of bacteria found on human skin and in the environment. It rarely causes disease, but may cause opportunistic infection in vulnerable patients; culture results require clinical interpretation.

name: dermabacter hominis
clinical_significance: Dermabacter hominis is a skin-associated bacterium that can occasionally cause opportunistic infection, including bloodstream infection in medically vulnerable people. A positive culture should be assessed for contamination versus true disease.

name: dermabrasion
clinical_significance: A procedure that uses a rapidly rotating instrument to remove outer skin layers. It may improve selected scars, wrinkles, sun damage, or lesions but can cause pain, pigment changes, infection, or scarring.

name: dermatan sulfate
clinical_significance: A long chain of sugar molecules found in skin, connective tissue, blood vessels, and heart valves. It helps organize tissues and can influence wound healing and blood clotting.

name: dermatitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the skin causing some combination of itching, redness, swelling, scaling, dryness, or blisters. It may result from irritation, allergy, infection, medicines, genetics, or another disease.

name: dermatitis herpetiformis
clinical_significance: A long-lasting, intensely itchy rash with groups of small bumps or blisters, commonly on the elbows, knees, buttocks, or scalp. It is strongly linked to celiac disease and usually improves with a strict gluten-free diet.

name: dermatographic urticaria
clinical_significance: A form of hives in which scratching, rubbing, or pressure causes raised, itchy lines on the skin within minutes. The reaction results from release of histamine by skin immune cells.

name: dermatologic disorder
clinical_significance: A disease affecting the skin, hair, nails, or skin glands. It may cause rash, scaling, pigment change, lumps, ulcers, pain, itching, hair loss, or abnormal nail growth.

name: dermatologist
clinical_significance: A physician who specializes in diagnosing and treating disorders of the skin, hair, nails, and related mucous membranes, including infections, inflammatory diseases, tumors, and cosmetic concerns.

name: dermatomycosis
clinical_significance: A fungal infection of the skin, hair, or nails. It may cause scaling, itching, discoloration, cracking, or hair loss; treatment depends on the site and may require a topical or oral antifungal medicine.

name: dermatomyositis
clinical_significance: An autoimmune disease that causes muscle inflammation and often weakness, especially in muscles near the hips and shoulders, along with skin changes such as a purple rash around the eyes or raised patches over the knuckles. It may affect swallowing or breathing muscles. In adults, it is associated with an increased risk of cancer, particularly around the time the disease begins.

name: dermis
clinical_significance: The strong, flexible skin layer beneath the epidermis. It contains collagen and elastic fibers, blood vessels, nerves, hair follicles, and sweat and oil glands that support and nourish the skin.

name: dermoid cyst
clinical_significance: Dermoid cysts are usually benign, but their effects depend on location; they can cause pressure, pain, infection, or torsion, and some can damage nearby structures. Ovarian dermoid cysts may twist or rupture, while orbital lesions can affect vision or bone.

name: dermoscopy
clinical_significance: Examination of a skin lesion with magnification and special lighting that reveals structures not visible to the unaided eye. It helps assess pigmented and other lesions but does not replace biopsy when cancer is suspected.

name: descending colon
clinical_significance: The left-sided part of the large intestine, extending downward from the transverse colon toward the sigmoid colon. It absorbs water and salts and helps compact stool before it moves toward the rectum.

name: desflurane
clinical_significance: An inhaled medicine used to maintain general anesthesia. It acts quickly but may irritate the airway, lower blood pressure, cause nausea, or rarely trigger malignant hyperthermia in susceptible people.

name: desipramine
clinical_significance: A tricyclic antidepressant that increases norepinephrine activity. It is used for selected mental health or pain conditions but may cause dry mouth, constipation, drowsiness, abnormal heart rhythms, or dangerous overdose.

name: deslorelin
clinical_significance: Deslorelin is a long-acting gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist used mainly in veterinary medicine to reversibly suppress reproductive hormone function. It is not a routine human therapy.

name: desmin
clinical_significance: A structural protein that links parts of muscle cells and helps maintain their alignment. Changes in the desmin gene or abnormal desmin buildup can cause muscle weakness and heart-muscle disease.

name: desmoid tumors
clinical_significance: Fibrous growths that usually do not spread to distant organs but can invade nearby tissues and recur. Some remain stable; observation, medicine, or surgery may be considered according to symptoms and location.

name: desmoplastic
clinical_significance: Describing the formation of dense, scar-like fibrous tissue, often around a tumor or in response to chronic inflammation or injury.

name: desmoplastic fibroma
clinical_significance: A rare noncancerous but locally aggressive fibrous growth in bone. It can cause pain, swelling, or fracture and may return after treatment.

name: desmopressin
clinical_significance: A medicine that mimics vasopressin, a hormone that reduces urine production and helps control bleeding. It is used for central diabetes insipidus, some bleeding disorders, and selected nighttime urination problems; excess fluid can dangerously lower blood sodium.

name: desmosine
clinical_significance: Desmosine is a cross-linking component of elastin, the protein that gives tissues stretch and recoil. It can be measured in research or specialized testing as a marker of elastin breakdown in lung or connective-tissue disease.

name: desmosome
clinical_significance: A strong junction that fastens neighboring cells together, especially in the skin and heart muscle. It links internal support fibers and helps tissues resist stretching and friction.

name: desogestrel
clinical_significance: A progestin used in some hormonal contraceptives. It prevents pregnancy mainly by suppressing ovulation and thickening cervical mucus; irregular bleeding, mood changes, breast tenderness, or other hormonal effects may occur.

name: desonide
clinical_significance: A low-strength corticosteroid applied to the skin to reduce redness, itching, and inflammation from conditions such as eczema or dermatitis. Excessive or prolonged use can thin the skin or cause other local effects.

name: desoximetasone
clinical_significance: A corticosteroid applied to the skin to reduce inflammation and itching in responsive rashes. Strength, body site, amount, and duration affect the risk of skin thinning and absorption into the body.

name: desoxycorticosterone
clinical_significance: A steroid hormone with mineralocorticoid effects. It makes the kidneys retain sodium and water and lose potassium, thereby influencing blood volume and blood pressure.

name: desulfovibrio
clinical_significance: A group of bacteria that can live without oxygen and use sulfate during metabolism. They occur in the environment and intestine; invasive human infection is uncommon and must fit the patient’s symptoms and specimen findings.

name: desulfovibrio desulfuricans
clinical_significance: Desulfovibrio desulfuricans is an anaerobic sulfate-reducing bacterium found in the environment and gut. It rarely causes human infection, including bacteremia or infected aneurysm, so its recovery from a sterile site can be clinically significant.

name: desulfovibrio piger
clinical_significance: Desulfovibrio piger is a sulfate-reducing bacterium found in the human intestine. It has been studied in relation to gut inflammation, but associations do not establish that it causes disease; it is not a routine diagnostic target.

name: desulfovibrionaceae
clinical_significance: Desulfovibrionaceae is a family of sulfate-reducing bacteria that includes organisms found in the environment and human gut. Rare species can cause opportunistic infection, but clinical significance depends on a credible isolate from an appropriate specimen.

name: desvenlafaxine succinate
clinical_significance: A form of desvenlafaxine, an antidepressant that increases serotonin and norepinephrine signaling. It is used for major depressive disorder and may cause nausea, insomnia, increased blood pressure, or withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly.

name: detached
clinical_significance: Separated or no longer connected. In medicine it may describe a retina, tissue, device, or feeling of emotional distance; the clinical meaning depends on the surrounding term and findings.

name: detergent
clinical_significance: A cleaning substance that helps remove oils and dirt from surfaces. Some detergents can irritate or burn the skin, eyes, airways, or digestive tract, especially when concentrated or swallowed.

name: deubiquitinating enzymes
clinical_significance: Enzymes that remove a small regulatory tag from other proteins. This can change whether a protein is broken down, where it works, and how cells control signals, repair DNA, and respond to infection.

name: deubiquitination
clinical_significance: Removal of the ubiquitin tag from a protein. This process can prevent the protein from being broken down or can change its activity, location, or role in cell signaling.

name: deuteranopia
clinical_significance: An inherited red-green color-vision deficiency caused by missing green-sensitive pigment in the retina. People may have difficulty distinguishing some shades of green, red, brown, and orange.

name: deuterium
clinical_significance: A naturally occurring form of hydrogen whose nucleus contains one proton and one neutron. Small amounts occur in water; very high exposure to heavy water can disrupt cell function.

name: deuterium oxide
clinical_significance: Deuterium oxide, or heavy water, is used in research and some specialized medical applications. Large amounts can disrupt normal cell division and metabolism, so exposure is hazardous.

name: developmental disabilities
clinical_significance: Lifelong conditions that begin during childhood and affect movement, learning, thinking, language, behavior, or ability to manage daily activities. Support needs vary and may include medical, educational, communication, and social services.

name: developmental process
clinical_significance: The physical, brain, emotional, social, and functional changes through which a person or organ grows and acquires abilities. Development is influenced by genes, health, nutrition, relationships, learning, and environment.

name: developmental psychology
clinical_significance: The study of how thinking, emotions, relationships, behavior, and abilities change from infancy through old age. It examines the effects of genes, health, learning, experience, relationships, and environment.

name: developmental regression
clinical_significance: Loss of skills a child previously acquired, such as speech, movement, social interaction, or self-care. Regression is a warning sign requiring prompt evaluation for neurologic, genetic, metabolic, infectious, or other causes.

name: developmental stage
clinical_significance: A period of growth characterized by typical physical, thinking, emotional, social, language, or self-care changes. Children vary, so stages describe broad patterns rather than exact deadlines.

name: device embolisation
clinical_significance: Movement of a medical device or broken piece of one through the bloodstream until it lodges in and blocks a blood vessel. It can reduce blood flow and may cause pain, organ injury, or an emergency requiring removal.

name: dexamethasone
clinical_significance: A strong, long-acting corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and immune activity. It is used for selected allergic, brain-swelling, cancer-related, endocrine, and other conditions; risks include infection, high blood sugar, mood changes, and adrenal suppression.

name: dexlansoprazole
clinical_significance: A proton-pump inhibitor that reduces stomach-acid production. It is used for acid reflux and related esophageal injury; prolonged use may contribute to infections, low magnesium or vitamin B12, fractures, or kidney inflammation.

name: dexmedetomidine
clinical_significance: A sedative that activates alpha-2 receptors and is given by injection during monitored care or intensive care. It usually depresses breathing less than many sedatives but can slow the heart or lower blood pressure.

name: dexmethylphenidate
clinical_significance: A stimulant used to treat attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. It increases dopamine and norepinephrine activity and may cause reduced appetite, insomnia, headache, increased heart rate or blood pressure, or misuse.

name: dexrazoxane
clinical_significance: A medicine used in selected cancer treatments to reduce heart damage from anthracyclines or tissue injury after leakage of an anthracycline from a vein. It can suppress bone marrow and increase infection risk.

name: dexrazoxane hydrochloride
clinical_significance: A salt form of dexrazoxane used in selected settings to reduce anthracycline-related heart damage or tissue injury after medicine leakage from a vein. Its use requires specialist dosing and monitoring.

name: dextroamphetamine
clinical_significance: A stimulant that increases dopamine and norepinephrine activity in the brain. It is used for selected attention or sleep disorders and may cause insomnia, reduced appetite, fast heartbeat, high blood pressure, or dependence.

name: dextrocardia
clinical_significance: A congenital condition in which the heart points or lies mainly on the right side of the chest. It may occur alone or with reversed organs and structural heart defects.

name: dextromethorphan
clinical_significance: A cough suppressant that reduces activity in brain pathways controlling the cough reflex. Excessive amounts can cause drowsiness, agitation, hallucinations, seizures, breathing depression, or serotonin toxicity.

name: dextrothyroxine
clinical_significance: Dextrothyroxine is an older thyroid-hormone isomer that was studied as a cholesterol-lowering drug. It is not used routinely because of heart-related safety concerns.

name: diabetes complications
clinical_significance: Problems caused by diabetes, including low or high glucose emergencies and long-term damage to the eyes, kidneys, nerves, heart, blood vessels, teeth, and feet. Regular monitoring and risk-factor control reduce risk.

name: diabetes insipidus
clinical_significance: A disorder causing large amounts of very dilute urine and intense thirst because vasopressin is lacking or the kidneys do not respond to it. It is unrelated to diabetes mellitus and can cause dehydration.

name: diabetes mellitus
clinical_significance: Diabetes mellitus is a group of diseases in which blood glucose remains too high because the body makes too little insulin, cannot use insulin effectively, or both. Over time it can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves, heart, and blood vessels; glucose control and regular screening reduce complications.

name: diabetic angiopathy
clinical_significance: Damage to small or large blood vessels caused by diabetes. It can reduce circulation, injure the eyes, kidneys, heart, brain, or feet, and increase the risk of wounds, heart attack, or stroke.

name: diabetic cardiomyopathies
clinical_significance: Heart-muscle disease associated with diabetes that is not fully explained by blocked heart arteries or high blood pressure. It can make the heart relax or pump poorly and may lead to heart failure.

name: diabetic foot
clinical_significance: Foot problems associated with diabetes, including loss of sensation, deformity, ulcers, infection, poor circulation, and slow healing. Daily inspection, proper footwear, glucose control, and early care help prevent serious injury.

name: diabetic ketoacidosis
clinical_significance: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a life-threatening emergency caused by insufficient effective insulin, leading to ketone buildup and metabolic acidosis. It can cause dehydration, vomiting, abdominal pain, deep rapid breathing, and altered alertness; urgent hospital treatment is required, and it can occur with only modest glucose elevation.

name: diabetic nephropathy
clinical_significance: Diabetic kidney disease is a common complication that can progress silently to chronic kidney disease and kidney failure. Urine albumin and blood filtration tests detect it early, and controlling glucose and blood pressure can slow progression.

name: diabetic neuropathy
clinical_significance: Nerve damage caused by diabetes. It may cause burning pain, tingling, numbness, weakness, loss of protective feeling in the feet, or problems with digestion, blood pressure, sweating, bladder control, or sexual function.

name: diabetic retinopathy
clinical_significance: Damage to retinal blood vessels caused by diabetes. It ranges from nonproliferative changes, such as microaneurysms and hemorrhages, to proliferative disease with abnormal new blood vessels. Leakage can cause macular edema, while bleeding or scar tissue can lead to vision loss or tractional retinal detachment. Early disease may have no symptoms.

name: diacetoxyscirpenol
clinical_significance: A toxin produced by some Fusarium molds that can contaminate food or animal feed. Exposure may irritate the digestive tract, suppress blood-cell production, and impair immune function.

name: diacylglycerol
clinical_significance: A fat-like molecule made from cell membranes that acts as an internal chemical signal. It helps control cell growth, movement, secretion, metabolism, and responses to hormones or other signals.

name: diagnosis
clinical_significance: Identification of a disease or health condition using symptoms, medical history, examination, and appropriate tests. A clinician may compare several possible causes before reaching the most likely diagnosis.

name: diagnostic procedure
clinical_significance: An examination or procedure used to identify, exclude, locate, or monitor a disease or injury. The purpose, preparation, risks, accuracy, and follow-up depend on the specific procedure and patient.

name: diagnostic service
clinical_significance: A healthcare service that collects or interprets information to detect, identify, characterize, or monitor a disease or health condition, such as laboratory testing, imaging, or specialist assessment.

name: diagnostic trial
clinical_significance: A clinical study that evaluates how accurately a test detects, rules out, or predicts a disease or important health outcome. Researchers may compare it with an established test or another accepted way of determining the diagnosis.

name: diakinesis
clinical_significance: The final stage before the first division that produces eggs or sperm. Paired chromosomes become tightly packed and remain connected at points where they exchanged genetic material.

name: dialister micraerophilus
clinical_significance: Dialister micraerophilus is a rare anaerobic bacterium found in the human microbiome that can occasionally cause abscesses or bloodstream infection. Its recovery from a sterile site may be meaningful, but requires clinical interpretation and reliable identification.

name: dialister pneumosintes
clinical_significance: A bacterium found in the mouth and respiratory tract that grows without oxygen. It may contribute to mixed infections, but a positive sample must be interpreted with symptoms and collection site.

name: dialysis solutions
clinical_significance: Specially prepared fluids used during hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. They allow waste and excess water to move out of the blood; their salt, glucose, and other contents are adjusted to the patient’s needs.

name: dialysis therapy
clinical_significance: Use of hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis to replace part of kidney function by removing waste and excess fluid and correcting some salt and acid imbalances. Treatment is individualized according to kidney function, symptoms, health, and goals.

name: diamine
clinical_significance: A molecule containing two amino groups. Diamines occur naturally in metabolism and are used in laboratory, pharmaceutical, and industrial chemistry; health effects depend on the specific compound and exposure.

name: dianhydrogalactitol
clinical_significance: Dianhydrogalactitol is an investigational DNA-alkylating anticancer drug studied for recurrent brain tumors and other cancers. Its safety and effectiveness are not established for routine care.

name: dianisidine
clinical_significance: An industrial chemical used in some dyes and laboratory reagents. Significant or repeated exposure can irritate tissues and may damage blood or increase cancer risk; workplace protection is important.

name: diapause
clinical_significance: Diapause is a temporary developmental or metabolic pause in some organisms; it is relevant to parasite and vector biology but is not a human clinical condition.

name: diapedesis
clinical_significance: Movement of blood cells, especially infection-fighting white cells, through the walls of tiny blood vessels into nearby tissue. This allows them to reach and respond to infection, injury, or inflammation.

name: diaper rash
clinical_significance: Inflammation of skin covered by a diaper, commonly caused by moisture, urine, stool, friction, or yeast infection. It causes redness and soreness; a persistent, severe, blistering, or spreading rash needs medical assessment.

name: diaphoretic
clinical_significance: Describing heavy sweating or something that causes sweating. Sudden cold sweating with chest pain, faintness, breathlessness, confusion, or weakness may signal a serious medical problem and needs urgent assessment.

name: diaphragm
clinical_significance: The dome-shaped muscle separating the chest from the abdomen and the main muscle used for breathing. When it contracts, it flattens and draws air into the lungs; when it relaxes, air leaves.

name: diaphragmatic eventration
clinical_significance: Abnormal thinning or weakness of part or all of the diaphragm, causing it to sit higher than usual. It may cause no symptoms or lead to breathlessness, especially if severe or present from birth.

name: diaphragmatic hernia
clinical_significance: Movement of abdominal organs through a hole or weak area in the diaphragm into the chest. It may be present from birth or follow injury and can impair breathing or cause bowel obstruction.

name: diaphysis
clinical_significance: The long central shaft of a bone such as the femur, humerus, or tibia. It contains a hollow marrow cavity and is surrounded by strong compact bone; fractures there may require prolonged healing.

name: diarrhea
clinical_significance: Passing loose or watery stools more often than usual. Causes include infections, medicines, food intolerance, inflammation, malabsorption, or other illnesses. Diarrhea can lead to dehydration and, when prolonged, malabsorption.

name: diastematomyelia
clinical_significance: A birth defect in which the spinal cord is divided into two parts, often by bone or fibrous tissue. It may occur with abnormal vertebrae, a skin mark, weakness, altered sensation, or bladder problems.

name: diastole
