name: lanugo
clinical_significance: Lanugo is the fine hair that covers a fetus and is usually shed before birth. It may persist in some premature newborns and can also appear with severe malnutrition or eating disorders in older people.

name: laparoscope
clinical_significance: A slender instrument with a light and camera used to view the abdominal or pelvic cavity through a small incision during minimally invasive surgery.

name: laparoscopic colectomy
clinical_significance: Laparoscopic colectomy is removal of part or all of the colon through small incisions using a camera and specialized instruments.

name: laparoscopy
clinical_significance: Keyhole surgery that uses a small camera and instruments through small cuts in the abdomen or pelvis. It can be used to look for a problem, take a sample, or treat conditions such as appendicitis, gallstones, endometriosis, or an ectopic pregnancy. Recovery is often easier than after open surgery, but risks and recovery time depend on the procedure.

name: laparotomy
clinical_significance: An operation that uses a larger cut in the abdomen to reach the abdominal or pelvic organs.

name: lapatinib
clinical_significance: Lapatinib is a targeted cancer medicine that blocks HER2 and epidermal-growth-factor receptors and is used for selected advanced breast cancers.

name: lapatinib ditosylate
clinical_significance: Lapatinib ditosylate is the salt form of lapatinib, a targeted medicine used for selected HER2-positive breast cancers.

name: large colon
clinical_significance: The large colon is the main portion of the large intestine that absorbs water, stores fecal material, and moves contents toward the rectum.

name: large intestine
clinical_significance: The final part of the digestive tract, extending from the small intestine to the rectum. It absorbs water and helps form and move stool.

name: laromustine
clinical_significance: Laromustine is an investigational alkylating chemotherapy drug studied mainly for acute myeloid leukemia. It can suppress bone marrow and cause serious infection or bleeding risk; it is not an established standard treatment.

name: Laron syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited growth disorder in which the body cannot respond properly to growth hormone. It causes severe short stature, characteristic facial features, and very low levels of the growth signal needed for normal bone development.

name: larotaxel
clinical_significance: Larotaxel is an investigational taxane chemotherapy drug studied for advanced cancers, including breast cancer. Like other taxanes it can cause low blood counts, nerve symptoms, and infusion reactions; it is not an established standard treatment.

name: larva
clinical_significance: A larva is an immature stage in the life cycle of some animals, including insects and parasitic worms. Identifying larvae in a specimen can help diagnose certain parasitic infections or determine a vector’s life stage.

name: laryngeal carcinoma
clinical_significance: Laryngeal carcinoma is cancer arising in the voice box and may cause hoarseness, swallowing difficulty, pain, or breathing problems.

name: laryngeal cartilage
clinical_significance: Laryngeal cartilage forms the structural framework of the voice box, maintains the airway, and supports vocal-fold movement.

name: laryngeal cleft
clinical_significance: A laryngeal cleft is a congenital opening between the airway and esophagus that can allow aspiration and cause feeding or breathing problems.

name: laryngeal edema
clinical_significance: Swelling of the tissues of the larynx that can narrow the upper airway and cause hoarseness, stridor, or respiratory distress. It may result from allergy, infection, trauma, or airway instrumentation.

name: laryngeal fistula
clinical_significance: An abnormal passage between the voice box and nearby tissue or the swallowing tract. It can allow food or saliva to enter the airway and cause coughing, repeated chest infections, or breathing problems.

name: laryngeal hemorrhage
clinical_significance: Bleeding within or around the larynx, which may result from trauma, instrumentation, vocal strain, vascular lesions, infection, or tumor and can threaten the airway.

name: laryngeal masks
clinical_significance: Laryngeal masks are supraglottic airway devices placed above the vocal cords to maintain ventilation during anesthesia or emergencies.

name: laryngeal mucositis
clinical_significance: Inflammation and open sores in the lining of the voice box, often after radiation, chemotherapy, infection, or irritation. It can cause hoarseness, throat pain, painful swallowing, or breathing difficulty.

name: laryngeal nerve
clinical_significance: A branch of the vagus nerve supplying the larynx; injury can cause hoarseness, swallowing difficulty, or breathing problems.

name: laryngeal obstruction
clinical_significance: Partial or complete blockage of the laryngeal airway caused by edema, foreign body, tumor, trauma, infection, vocal-cord dysfunction, or other structural disease.

name: laryngeal web
clinical_significance: A laryngeal web is a thin membrane across part of the airway, usually congenital or acquired after injury, causing hoarseness or airway narrowing.

name: laryngectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part or all of the larynx, usually for cancer or severe structural disease. After total removal, breathing occurs permanently through an opening in the neck; partial surgery may preserve some voice and swallowing.

name: laryngitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the voice box that causes hoarseness or temporary voice loss. Common causes include viral infection, voice overuse, smoke or other irritation, and reflux.

name: laryngomalacia
clinical_significance: A birth condition in which soft tissue above an infant’s vocal cords partly collapses during breathing in, causing noisy breathing. It often improves with growth, but feeding trouble, pauses in breathing, or poor growth may occur.

name: laryngoscope
clinical_significance: An instrument used to see the throat and vocal cords, especially while placing a breathing tube. Common blades are curved Macintosh and straight Miller types; use can injure teeth, lips, or throat.

name: laryngoscopy
clinical_significance: An examination of the voice box and nearby throat using a mirror or a thin camera passed through the mouth or nose. It helps investigate hoarseness, swallowing problems, airway narrowing, bleeding, or suspected tumors.

name: laryngospasm
clinical_significance: Sudden tightening of the vocal cords that partly or completely blocks breathing. It can be triggered by saliva, blood, reflux, airway procedures, or anesthesia and may cause noisy breathing, choking, or inability to breathe.

name: laryngostenosis
clinical_significance: Narrowing of the voice box, or larynx, that can restrict breathing. Causes include scarring after intubation, injury, inflammation, tumors, and congenital narrowing; noisy breathing or breathlessness may occur.

name: larynx
clinical_significance: The voice box in the front of the neck between the throat and windpipe. It contains the vocal cords, produces sound, helps keep food and liquid out of the lungs, and regulates airflow during breathing.

name: larynx disease
clinical_significance: Any disorder affecting the larynx, including inflammation, infection, structural lesions, vocal-cord dysfunction, neurologic disease, or cancer.

name: larynx muscle
clinical_significance: A muscle of the voice box that moves the vocal folds and helps protect the airway and produce sound.

name: larynx neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in the voice box. It may be noncancerous or cancerous and can cause hoarseness, swallowing difficulty, pain, breathing problems, or a neck lump.

name: laser
clinical_significance: A device that produces a concentrated beam of light. Depending on its wavelength and power, it can measure tissue, cut or seal tissue, remove abnormal growths, or treat selected eye and skin conditions.

name: laser ablation
clinical_significance: The use of focused laser energy to heat, destroy, or seal targeted tissue. The technique is used in selected vascular, ophthalmic, dermatologic, and other procedures.

name: laser capture microdissection
clinical_significance: Laser capture microdissection isolates selected cells from a tissue sample under microscopic guidance. It can support precise molecular or genetic testing of tumors and other diseases when mixed cell populations would obscure results.

name: laser surgery
clinical_significance: Laser surgery uses a focused beam of light to cut, remove, seal, or reshape tissue in selected procedures.

name: laser therapy
clinical_significance: Laser therapy uses controlled light energy to treat selected skin, eye, vascular, dental, or other medical conditions.

name: lassa fever
clinical_significance: A viral illness that can cause fever, weakness, vomiting, bleeding, and damage to several organs. It is usually spread by contact with urine or droppings of infected rodents in parts of West Africa and sometimes by contact with body fluids.

name: lassa virus
clinical_significance: An arenavirus that causes Lassa fever, a potentially severe hemorrhagic illness acquired mainly through contact with infected rodent excreta or body fluids.

name: lassitude
clinical_significance: A state of marked fatigue, weakness, or lack of energy that may occur with systemic illness, anemia, endocrine disease, infection, medication effects, or psychological conditions.

name: latanoprost
clinical_significance: Latanoprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue eye drop that increases uveoscleral outflow and lowers intraocular pressure in glaucoma or ocular hypertension; iris pigmentation and eyelash growth may occur.

name: late endosome
clinical_significance: A late endosome is a cell compartment that sorts internalized material for recycling or delivery to lysosomes for breakdown. Its function is relevant to intracellular trafficking, infection biology, and some inherited storage disorders.

name: latent infection
clinical_significance: A latent infection persists in the body without causing active disease symptoms at that time. Some infections can reactivate later, especially when immune defenses weaken; the organism and appropriate testing determine treatment and follow-up.

name: latent syphilis
clinical_significance: Latent syphilis is syphilis infection without current symptoms, identified by testing and classified by duration to guide treatment and follow-up.

name: latent tuberculosis
clinical_significance: Infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis in which the bacteria remain inactive and cause no symptoms but may later become active.

name: lateral
clinical_significance: Toward or located at the side, away from the body’s midline. For example, the ears are lateral to the nose; the opposite term is medial.

name: lateral meniscus
clinical_significance: The lateral meniscus is a crescent-shaped cartilage pad on the outer side of the knee that distributes load and stabilizes movement.

name: lateral sclerosis
clinical_significance: Damage affecting nerve pathways along the side of the spinal cord that carry movement signals. It may cause increasing stiffness and weakness, as in some motor-neuron diseases; the exact diagnosis requires the associated clinical findings.

name: lateral ventricle
clinical_significance: One of two fluid-filled spaces inside the brain that produce and contain cerebrospinal fluid, helping protect and support the brain.

name: latex allergy
clinical_significance: Latex allergy is an immune reaction to proteins in natural rubber latex. Contact can cause skin symptoms, while severe allergy may cause breathing difficulty or anaphylaxis; people with a confirmed allergy should avoid latex exposure in healthcare and daily life.

name: lathyrism
clinical_significance: A neurologic disorder caused by prolonged or excessive ingestion of certain Lathyrus legumes, especially grass pea, characterized primarily by progressive spastic weakness of the legs.

name: lauric acid
clinical_significance: Lauric acid is a saturated fatty acid found in coconut and palm-kernel oils and in some foods. Dietary effects depend on the overall food and diet pattern; it is not a treatment for disease.

name: lauroleic acid
clinical_significance: Laurooleic acid is a monounsaturated fatty acid found in some fats and studied in lipid metabolism. It has no established role as a stand-alone treatment or diagnostic marker.

name: lavage fluid
clinical_significance: Liquid used to wash a body space, wound, or organ during a medical procedure, or collected afterward for laboratory analysis. Its contents can help detect infection, bleeding, cancer cells, inflammation, or abnormal proteins.

name: laxative
clinical_significance: A laxative is a medicine or product used to relieve constipation by softening stool, adding bulk, or stimulating bowel movement. Choice depends on the cause; overuse can cause diarrhea, dehydration, or electrolyte problems.

name: lead
clinical_significance: A toxic heavy metal that can harm the nervous system, blood-forming system, kidneys, cardiovascular system, and reproductive system. Exposure may occur through contaminated paint dust or soil, drinking water, workplaces, hobbies, imported products, or other sources; children and fetuses are especially vulnerable to neurodevelopmental effects.

name: lead poisoning
clinical_significance: Harm caused by exposure to lead, which can damage the brain, nerves, blood, kidneys, and reproductive system. Children may develop learning, behavior, growth, or developmental problems. Sources include old paint and dust, contaminated soil or water, workplace or hobby materials, and some imported products. Diagnosis uses blood lead testing; treatment starts by stopping exposure, with chelation for selected severe cases.

name: leaf senescence
clinical_significance: Leaf senescence is the programmed aging and breakdown of leaves in plants. It has no direct human clinical significance but is studied in plant biology and crop science.

name: learning
clinical_significance: Learning is the process of acquiring or changing knowledge and skills through experience, practice, or instruction. Difficulty learning may arise from developmental, neurologic, sensory, emotional, or educational factors and is assessed in context.

name: learning disorder
clinical_significance: A neurodevelopmental disorder causing persistent difficulty acquiring or using academic skills such as reading, writing, or mathematics despite appropriate instruction.

name: lecithin
clinical_significance: Lecithin is a mixture of phospholipids, often including phosphatidylcholine, found in cell membranes and used as a food emulsifier or supplement. Evidence for treating health conditions with supplements is limited, and products may contain soy or egg allergens.

name: leclercia
clinical_significance: Leclercia is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria found in the environment and occasionally in human specimens. Some species can cause rare opportunistic infections, particularly in people with serious illness or weakened immunity; isolation alone does not prove disease.

name: leclercia adecarboxylata
clinical_significance: Leclercia adecarboxylata is an uncommon Gram-negative bacterium that can cause opportunistic wound, urinary, or bloodstream infection, especially in people with underlying illness or devices. It may also be found with other bacteria, so cultures are interpreted clinically.

name: lectin
clinical_significance: Lectins are proteins that bind specific sugars and occur in many plants and animals. They are used in laboratory research and some diagnostic methods; some raw foods contain lectins that can cause illness if not properly prepared.

name: LED therapy
clinical_significance: Light-emitting diode (LED) therapy uses selected wavelengths of light for purposes such as skin treatment or wound care. Benefits depend on the condition and device, and evidence varies; it is not a substitute for established treatment.

name: leech therapy
clinical_significance: Carefully controlled use of medicinal leeches to remove congested blood from selected tissue, especially after reconstructive surgery. Their saliva also prevents clotting. Bleeding, infection, anemia, and allergic reactions are possible, so clinical monitoring is essential.

name: leeche
clinical_significance: A leech is a blood-feeding worm. Medicinal leeches are used under supervision to relieve venous congestion in selected reconstructive procedures; risks include prolonged bleeding, anemia, and bacterial infection.

name: leflunomide
clinical_significance: Leflunomide is a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug that inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase and lymphocyte proliferation; it treats rheumatoid or psoriatic arthritis but can cause hepatotoxicity, cytopenias, hypertension, and fetal harm.

name: left atrium
clinical_significance: The upper-left chamber of the heart. It receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and passes it through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.

name: left kidney
clinical_significance: The left kidney filters blood, removes waste and excess water, and helps regulate blood pressure, electrolytes, and red-cell production. Its function is assessed with blood and urine tests and imaging when indicated.

name: left lung
clinical_significance: The left lung exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide and contains upper and lower lobes. Disease, injury, or removal of lung tissue on this side can affect breathing and oxygen levels.

name: left ventricle
clinical_significance: The lower-left chamber of the heart. It receives oxygen-rich blood from the left atrium and pumps it through the aortic valve into the aorta and throughout the body.

name: leg
clinical_significance: The lower limb, often meaning the region between the knee and ankle, although it may also refer broadly to the entire lower extremity.

name: leg ulcer
clinical_significance: An open sore on the lower leg that heals slowly or not at all. Causes include poor vein or artery circulation, diabetes-related nerve damage, pressure, and inflammation. Venous ulcers often occur near the ankle and may be accompanied by leg swelling or varicose veins; the cause should be assessed because treatment depends on it.

name: legal guardian
clinical_significance: A legal guardian is a person authorized by a court or applicable law to make specified decisions for someone who cannot make them independently, including some healthcare decisions. The guardian’s authority and the person’s own decision-making rights depend on local law and the circumstances.

name: legionella
clinical_significance: Legionella is a group of water-associated bacteria that can cause Legionnaires' disease, a severe pneumonia, or Pontiac fever, a milder illness.

name: legionella longbeachae
clinical_significance: Legionella longbeachae is a Legionella species associated particularly with exposure to contaminated potting mix and capable of causing pneumonia.

name: legionella pneumophila
clinical_significance: A bacterium found in water systems that can cause severe pneumonia after a person inhales contaminated water droplets. It may also cause a milder fever illness; older age, smoking, and weakened immunity increase risk.

name: legionellosis
clinical_significance: An infection caused by Legionella bacteria, ranging from a mild flu-like illness to Legionnaires’ disease with pneumonia.

name: Legionnaires' disease
clinical_significance: Legionnaires’ disease is a potentially severe pneumonia caused by Legionella bacteria, usually acquired by inhaling contaminated water droplets. It can progress rapidly, especially in older adults, smokers, or people with weakened immunity, and requires prompt medical evaluation and antibiotic treatment.

name: leifsonia
clinical_significance: Leifsonia is a genus of environmental, mostly water-associated bacteria. Rare species, particularly L. aquatica, have caused catheter-related bloodstream or other infections; a positive culture needs clinical correlation.

name: leifsonia aquatica
clinical_significance: Leifsonia aquatica is a water-associated Gram-positive bacterium that rarely causes human infection, including catheter-related bloodstream or surgical-site infection. It may be difficult to identify and should be interpreted with the culture source and clinical findings.

name: Leigh disease
clinical_significance: A progressive mitochondrial disorder of early life characterized by symmetric lesions of the brainstem and basal ganglia, developmental regression, movement abnormalities, and lactic acidosis.

name: leiomyomatosis
clinical_significance: Leiomyomatosis is development of multiple benign smooth-muscle tumors or proliferations, which may affect the uterus, skin, lungs, or other sites.

name: leiomyosarcoma
clinical_significance: Leiomyosarcoma is a rare cancer of smooth muscle that can arise in the uterus, digestive tract, blood vessels, or other soft tissues. Symptoms depend on its location; treatment and outlook depend on tumor site, extent, and grade.

name: leishmania
clinical_significance: A group of single-celled parasites transmitted mainly by infected sandflies. Different species cause skin, mucosal, or visceral leishmaniasis, ranging from localized ulcers to life-threatening illness.

name: leishmania chagasi
clinical_significance: Leishmania chagasi is a name historically used for the parasite now generally classified as Leishmania infantum in the Americas. It causes visceral leishmaniasis, a potentially fatal disease of internal organs if untreated.

name: leishmania donovani
clinical_significance: A parasite spread by infected sandflies that causes visceral leishmaniasis. It can infect organs such as the spleen, liver, and bone marrow, causing prolonged fever, weight loss, enlarged organs, and reduced blood-cell counts.

name: leishmania major
clinical_significance: A parasite commonly causing cutaneous leishmaniasis in parts of Africa, Asia, and the Middle East. Sandfly transmission produces one or more skin ulcers that may heal slowly and leave scars.

name: leishmania mexicana
clinical_significance: A parasite that causes mainly cutaneous leishmaniasis in the Americas. Infection after a sandfly bite may produce a persistent skin nodule or ulcer and, less commonly, involve mucous membranes.

name: leishmania tropica
clinical_significance: A sandfly-transmitted parasite that commonly causes localized cutaneous leishmaniasis. It produces chronic skin sores that may heal over months and leave permanent scars.

name: leishmaniasis
clinical_significance: An infection caused by Leishmania parasites transmitted by sandflies. It may produce skin ulcers, damage to the nose or mouth, or a life-threatening illness affecting organs such as the spleen, liver, and bone marrow.

name: lelliottia amnigena
clinical_significance: Lelliottia amnigena is a Gram-negative environmental and plant-associated bacterium that has occasionally been isolated in human infections. Its significance in urine, blood, or other specimens depends on symptoms, repeat cultures, and the patient’s risk factors.

name: leminorella grimontii
clinical_significance: Leminorella grimontii is a rare Gram-negative bacterium recovered from clinical specimens and occasionally implicated in healthcare-associated urinary, wound, or bloodstream infections. A culture result must be assessed with symptoms and susceptibility testing because evidence is limited.

name: leminorella richardii
clinical_significance: Leminorella richardii is a rare Gram-negative bacterium found in clinical specimens. Leminorella species have occasionally caused healthcare-associated infections, but isolation alone does not establish disease and antimicrobial susceptibility can vary.

name: lenalidomide
clinical_significance: Lenalidomide is an immunomodulatory anticancer drug used for multiple myeloma and selected myelodysplastic or lymphoma disorders; myelosuppression, thrombosis, infection, and severe teratogenicity are important risks.

name: lenograstim
clinical_significance: A recombinant granulocyte colony-stimulating factor that increases neutrophil production and is used to prevent or treat some forms of neutropenia.

name: lens
clinical_significance: A clear, flexible structure behind the iris and pupil that bends light onto the retina. Muscles change its shape for near or distant focus; clouding causes cataract, while displacement can blur vision or raise eye pressure.

name: lens coloboma
clinical_significance: A lens coloboma is a congenital segmental defect or notch in the eye lens caused by incomplete development.

name: lens disease
clinical_significance: A disorder of the eye lens, including cataract, dislocation, inflammation-related opacity, or developmental abnormality, that may impair focusing or vision.

name: lens dislocation
clinical_significance: Displacement of the crystalline lens from its normal position because of trauma, zonular weakness, surgery, or connective-tissue disease; it can cause blurred vision, glaucoma, or inflammation.

name: lens subluxation
clinical_significance: Partial displacement of the crystalline lens while some zonular attachments remain, potentially causing blurred or fluctuating vision, refractive change, or glaucoma.

name: lente insulin
clinical_significance: Lente insulin was a historical intermediate-acting zinc-suspension insulin. It has been discontinued in the United States and is not part of routine current diabetes treatment; patients require a clinician-guided alternative rather than substituting insulin formulations themselves.

name: lentiform nucleus
clinical_significance: A group of deep brain structures involved in controlling movement. It includes the putamen and globus pallidus and works with other brain regions to help start and regulate actions.

name: lentigo
clinical_significance: A lentigo is a sharply defined flat brown skin spot caused by increased melanocytes or pigment and may be benign or, rarely, atypical.

name: lentinan
clinical_significance: Lentinan is a mushroom-derived beta-glucan studied as an immune-modulating adjunct in cancer treatment and used in some countries. Evidence and availability vary by region; it is not a substitute for standard cancer therapy or a proven over-the-counter cancer treatment.

name: LEOPARD syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited disorder that can cause many dark skin spots, abnormal heart rhythms, widely spaced eyes, narrowing of the pulmonary valve, genital differences, slow growth, and hearing loss. The combination and severity vary between people.

name: lepidoptera
clinical_significance: The insect order containing butterflies and moths; contact with some caterpillars can cause skin, eye, or systemic reactions.

name: lepirudin
clinical_significance: Lepirudin is a direct thrombin inhibitor formerly used as an anticoagulant in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia; bleeding and kidney clearance are important considerations.

name: leprosy
clinical_significance: A long-term infection caused mainly by bacteria that affect the skin and cooler nerves in the arms, legs, and face. It can cause pale or reddish patches with reduced feeling, thickened nerves, weakness, and eye or nose problems. A skin sample or other tests may confirm it. Treatment uses several antibiotics, commonly rifampicin, dapsone, and clofazimine, to prevent lasting nerve damage and disability.

name: leptin
clinical_significance: A hormone produced mainly by adipose tissue that signals stored-energy status to the brain and influences appetite and energy balance.

name: leptin receptor
clinical_significance: A cell-surface protein that receives signals from leptin, a hormone made mainly by fat tissue. It helps the brain regulate appetite, energy use, growth, and reproductive function in response to stored body energy.

name: leptomeningeal sarcoma
clinical_significance: Leptomeningeal sarcoma is a rare malignant tumor involving the membranes and fluid spaces around the brain or spinal cord.

name: leptomeninges
clinical_significance: The arachnoid mater and pia mater, the two delicate inner membranes covering the brain and spinal cord.

name: leptospira
clinical_significance: A genus of spiral-shaped bacteria that includes the causes of leptospirosis, usually acquired through water or soil contaminated with infected animal urine.

name: leptospiraceae
clinical_significance: Leptospiraceae is a family of spiral-shaped bacteria that includes Leptospira species, the causes of leptospirosis. Identification of a pathogenic member can help explain exposure-related febrile illness and guide testing and treatment.

name: leptospirosis
clinical_significance: Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection usually acquired through skin or mucous-membrane contact with water or soil contaminated by infected animal urine. It can cause sudden fever, headache, muscle pain, and red eyes; severe disease may lead to kidney or liver failure, bleeding, or meningitis and needs urgent care.

name: leptotrichia
clinical_significance: Leptotrichia are anaerobic oral bacteria that can cause bacteremia, especially in people with neutropenia or mucosal injury; bloodstream isolates should be taken seriously and treated according to susceptibility.

name: Leriche syndrome
clinical_significance: Aortoiliac occlusive disease causing reduced blood flow to the pelvis and lower limbs.

name: leridistim
clinical_significance: Leridistim is an investigational blood-cell growth factor studied to help restore neutrophils after chemotherapy. It is not an established routine treatment.

name: lerisetron
clinical_significance: Lerisetron is an investigational serotonin 5-HT3 receptor blocker studied to prevent nausea and vomiting, including after chemotherapy. It is not an established marketed antiemetic.

name: lesion
clinical_significance: Any localized abnormal change in tissue caused by disease, injury, inflammation, infection, or a tumor. A lesion may be visible, felt, or found only on imaging or microscopic examination.

name: lesion identification
clinical_significance: The process of locating and describing an abnormal area in the body using examination, imaging, endoscopy, laboratory tests, or tissue sampling.

name: less than
clinical_significance: “Less than” is a mathematical comparison meaning that one value is lower than another. In clinical reports it may mark a result below a test’s detection or quantification limit; interpretation depends on the assay and units.

name: lestaurtinib
clinical_significance: Lestaurtinib is an investigational kinase inhibitor studied for acute myeloid leukemia and other cancers, including tumors with FLT3 or JAK pathway activity. It is not an established standard treatment.

name: lethal injection
clinical_significance: Lethal injection is a method of execution, not a medical treatment. Clinicians and professional organizations may face ethical and legal restrictions concerning participation, which vary by jurisdiction.

name: lethargy
clinical_significance: Lethargy is reduced energy, alertness, or responsiveness; it may result from sleep loss, infection, metabolic disease, medicines, depression, or neurologic illness. Sudden marked lethargy can occur with serious illness.

name: letrozole
clinical_significance: Letrozole is an aromatase inhibitor that lowers oestrogen production and is used mainly for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer and ovulation induction; hot flushes, arthralgia, bone loss, and fetal harm are important considerations.

name: leucine
clinical_significance: Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid needed for protein synthesis and muscle metabolism. Its breakdown is impaired in maple syrup urine disease, and excessive supplementation is not a substitute for balanced nutrition or treatment.

name: leucine zipper
clinical_significance: A leucine zipper is a protein structure that helps some transcription factors bind DNA or pair with other proteins. It is important in gene regulation and laboratory research but is not itself a clinical test or diagnosis.

name: leuconostoc
clinical_significance: Leuconostoc is a genus of lactic-acid bacteria used in food fermentation and found in the environment. It can rarely cause invasive infection, especially in hospitalized or immunocompromised people, and is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin.

name: leuconostoc citreum
clinical_significance: Leuconostoc citreum is a lactic-acid bacterium found in fermented foods and the environment. Human infection is uncommon; Leuconostoc can be intrinsically resistant to vancomycin, so accurate identification matters when it is recovered from a sterile site.

name: leuconostoc lactis
clinical_significance: Leuconostoc lactis is a bacterium associated with fermented foods that has rarely been reported in bloodstream or other opportunistic infections. It is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin, and clinical cultures require assessment for true infection.

name: leuconostoc mesenteroides
clinical_significance: Leuconostoc mesenteroides is used in food fermentation and has occasionally caused bloodstream or other opportunistic infections, especially in medically vulnerable people. It is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin.

name: leuconostocaceae
clinical_significance: Leuconostocaceae is a family of lactic-acid bacteria found in foods and the environment. Some members can rarely cause human infection and are intrinsically resistant to vancomycin, a fact relevant to laboratory identification and treatment selection.

name: leucovorin
clinical_significance: Leucovorin is a folate medicine used to reduce the toxicity of methotrexate, enhance some chemotherapy regimens, and treat certain folate-related problems.

name: leucovorin calcium
clinical_significance: Leucovorin calcium is the calcium salt of leucovorin, used as rescue therapy after methotrexate and in selected colorectal-cancer treatments.

name: leukapheresis
clinical_significance: A blood-filtering procedure that removes excess white blood cells and returns the remaining blood. It may rapidly reduce very high counts causing symptoms in leukemia, but it is temporary and does not replace treatment of the underlying disease.

name: leukemia
clinical_significance: Leukemia is a cancer of blood-forming tissues, usually the bone marrow, that produces abnormal blood cells and disrupts normal blood-cell production. It can cause fatigue, infections, bruising, or bleeding; the type, genetic findings, and extent of disease guide treatment.

name: leukemoid reaction
clinical_significance: A marked reactive increase in the white-cell count, usually with prominent neutrophilia

name: leukoaraiosis
clinical_significance: White-matter changes seen on brain scans, often related to aging and long-term small-vessel disease such as high blood pressure. Extensive changes may be associated with slower thinking, walking problems, or stroke risk.

name: leukocyte
clinical_significance: A white blood cell that helps defend the body against infection and other threats. Main types include neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils; unusually high or low numbers can reflect infection, inflammation, medicines, or bone-marrow disease.

name: leukocyte differentiation
clinical_significance: Leukocyte differentiation is the process by which developing white blood cells mature into specialized types such as neutrophils, lymphocytes, and monocytes. Abnormal maturation can contribute to immune deficiency or blood cancers and is assessed in blood and bone-marrow testing.

name: leukocyte disorder
clinical_significance: A disorder involving the number, function, or development of white blood cells, including leukopenia, leukocytosis, immune deficiency, and malignant leukocyte proliferation.

name: leukocyte elastase
clinical_significance: Leukocyte elastase is an enzyme released mainly by neutrophils that helps break down microbes and tissue proteins. Excess activity can damage tissue during inflammation; elastase measurements may be used in selected research or diagnostic tests.

name: leukocyte trafficking
clinical_significance: Leukocyte trafficking is the movement of white blood cells from blood into tissues and between immune compartments. It is essential for infection and inflammation responses and is targeted by some immune-modifying medicines.

name: leukocyte transfusion
clinical_significance: Transfusion of donated white blood cells in rare, carefully selected situations involving life-threatening infection and severe inability to produce neutrophils. Benefits are uncertain and risks include fever, lung injury, immune reactions, and infection transmission.

name: leukocytosis
clinical_significance: A higher-than-usual number of white blood cells. It may occur with infection, inflammation, stress, smoking, medicines, or blood and bone-marrow disorders; the specific cell type and symptoms help identify the cause.

name: leukodystrophy
clinical_significance: A group of inherited disorders that damage myelin, the protective covering around nerves in the brain and spinal cord. They can cause progressive problems with movement, thinking, vision, hearing, or other nervous-system functions.

name: leukoencephalopathy
clinical_significance: Leukoencephalopathy is disease of the brain’s white matter caused by inherited, infectious, toxic, vascular, metabolic, inflammatory, or other processes.

name: leukonychia
clinical_significance: White areas or bands in one or more nails. Causes include minor injury to the nail, inherited traits, infection, medicines, or illness; the pattern and whether it grows out with the nail help determine the cause.

name: leukopenia
clinical_significance: An abnormally low white-blood-cell count, which may increase susceptibility to infection depending on the cells affected and the severity of the reduction.

name: leukoplakia
clinical_significance: A persistent white patch or plaque in the mouth that cannot be rubbed off and cannot be characterized as another condition. It is a clinical description rather than a specific tissue diagnosis; some lesions contain precancerous changes or may progress to cancer, so assessment and often biopsy are needed.

name: leukopoiesis
clinical_significance: The process by which the bone marrow makes and develops white blood cells. Production increases or changes during infection, inflammation, immune disorders, and some blood diseases.

name: leukorrhea
clinical_significance: Whitish vaginal discharge that may be normal, especially during hormonal changes, or may result from infection or inflammation. Foul odor, itching, pain, bleeding, or a new change may suggest an underlying condition.

name: leukostasis
clinical_significance: A medical emergency in which very high numbers of abnormal leukocytes impair microvascular blood flow, potentially causing respiratory distress, neurologic symptoms, organ ischemia, or hemorrhage.

name: leukotriene
clinical_significance: A leukotriene is an inflammatory lipid mediator made from arachidonic acid that contributes to bronchoconstriction, mucus, vascular leak, and immune-cell recruitment.

name: leukotriene degradation
clinical_significance: Leukotriene degradation is the enzymatic breakdown of leukotrienes, inflammatory signaling molecules involved in asthma and allergy. Changes in this pathway are studied in airway and inflammatory disease research.

name: leukotriene receptor
clinical_significance: A cell-surface protein activated by leukotrienes, inflammatory chemicals that can narrow airways, increase mucus, and promote swelling. Blocking these receptors can help prevent selected asthma and allergy symptoms.

name: leuprolide
clinical_significance: Leuprolide is a gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist used to suppress sex-hormone production in conditions such as prostate cancer, endometriosis, and fibroids.

name: leuprolide acetate
clinical_significance: Leuprolide acetate is the salt form of leuprolide, used to suppress ovarian or testicular hormone production for selected medical conditions.

name: levalbuterol
clinical_significance: An inhaled short-acting bronchodilator that stimulates beta-2 receptors and relaxes airway muscle. It relieves wheezing and shortness of breath but may cause tremor, nervousness, headache, or a fast heartbeat.

name: levamisole
clinical_significance: Levamisole is an antiparasitic and immune-modulating drug used selectively; serious low white-cell counts and vasculitic reactions can occur.

name: levetiracetam
clinical_significance: Levetiracetam is a broad-spectrum antiseizure medicine that binds synaptic vesicle protein SV2A; it treats focal and generalized seizures and may cause somnolence, dizziness, or behavioral and mood changes.

name: levobunolol
clinical_significance: Levobunolol is a beta-blocker eye drop used to lower pressure inside the eye in glaucoma or ocular hypertension.

name: levocardia
clinical_significance: Levocardia is a normal left-sided position of the heart; it may occur with normal organ arrangement or with other congenital laterality abnormalities.

name: levocarnitine
clinical_significance: Levocarnitine is the biologically active form of carnitine used to treat selected carnitine deficiencies and help transport fatty acids into mitochondria.

name: levodopa
clinical_significance: Levodopa is a dopamine precursor that crosses the blood--brain barrier and is converted to dopamine, usually with carbidopa or benserazide, to treat Parkinson disease; dyskinesias, hallucinations, nausea, and motor fluctuations can develop.

name: levofloxacin
clinical_significance: Levofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; tendon injury, peripheral neuropathy, QT prolongation, dysglycaemia, and central-nervous-system effects are important class risks.

name: levoleucovorin
clinical_significance: Levoleucovorin is the active isomer of leucovorin, used as methotrexate rescue and with selected chemotherapy regimens.

name: levoleucovorin calcium
clinical_significance: Levoleucovorin calcium is the calcium salt of levoleucovorin, used to reduce methotrexate toxicity and support selected cancer treatments.

name: levonorgestrel
clinical_significance: A progestin hormone used in birth-control pills, hormonal intrauterine devices, and emergency contraception to prevent or delay ovulation and alter cervical mucus.

name: levorphanol
clinical_significance: Levorphanol is a potent opioid analgesic that can relieve severe pain but also cause sedation, dependence, and respiratory depression.

name: levothyroxine sodium
clinical_significance: A manufactured form of thyroid hormone used to replace hormone missing in hypothyroidism. The dose is adjusted using blood tests, and it is usually taken consistently on an empty stomach.

name: Lewy body
clinical_significance: A Lewy body is an abnormal neuronal inclusion containing alpha-synuclein, characteristic of Parkinson disease and Lewy-body dementia.

name: lexatumumab
clinical_significance: Lexatumumab is an investigational antibody that activates TRAIL receptor 2 to promote cancer-cell death. It was studied in early clinical trials for advanced cancers but is not an established treatment.

name: Leydig cell
clinical_significance: A cell between the testicular tubules that produces testosterone, mainly in response to luteinizing hormone.

name: liarozole
clinical_significance: Liarozole is an investigational retinoic-acid metabolism blocker studied for skin disorders such as ichthyosis and psoriasis and for cancer. It is not an established standard treatment; studies reported adverse effects including dry mouth, headache, and itching.

name: libido
clinical_significance: A person's sexual desire or interest. It can change with age, relationships, mood, stress, sleep, illness, pregnancy, menopause, hormone levels, and medicines; a change is important mainly when it causes distress or affects a person's wellbeing.

name: lice infestation
clinical_significance: Lice infestation causes itching and can lead to skin infection from scratching; treatment should target the affected site and avoid unnecessary pesticide exposure.

name: lichen planus
clinical_significance: Lichen planus is a noncontagious inflammatory condition that can affect the skin, mouth, genitals, nails, or scalp. It may cause itchy bumps, painful mouth or genital sores, nail changes, or scarring hair loss; persistent oral or genital lesions need clinical follow-up.

name: lichenification
clinical_significance: Thick, leathery skin with more visible skin lines caused by repeated scratching or rubbing. It often develops in long-lasting eczema, allergies, or other itchy skin conditions.

name: Liddle syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited cause of early high blood pressure in which the kidneys retain too much sodium and lose too much potassium. It may begin in childhood or young adulthood and usually requires specialist treatment.

name: lidocaine
clinical_significance: Lidocaine is a local anaesthetic that blocks voltage-gated sodium channels and, intravenously, can treat selected ventricular arrhythmias; excessive exposure may cause seizures, hypotension, arrhythmia, or cardiac arrest.

name: Li-Fraumeni syndrome
clinical_significance: An inherited condition that greatly increases the chance of developing several cancers, often at a young age. Cancers may include breast cancer, sarcoma, brain tumors, adrenal cancer, or leukemia; specialized screening is usually advised.

name: ligament
clinical_significance: A ligament is a strong band of connective tissue that connects bones and stabilizes joints. A sprain is a ligament injury; severe tears can cause pain, swelling, and joint instability.

name: ligand
clinical_significance: A ligand is a molecule that binds to a receptor or other target molecule. In medicine and biology, ligand binding can trigger or block cell signals and is central to many drug actions and laboratory tests.

name: ligase
clinical_significance: An enzyme that joins two molecules, often using energy from ATP. Ligases help repair DNA, copy genetic material, and build or maintain other important molecules.

name: ligation
clinical_significance: Ligation is the tying, clipping, or sealing of a blood vessel, duct, or other tubular structure during a procedure. It can stop bleeding or block flow, and risks depend on the structure and operation involved.

name: light coagulation
clinical_significance: Light coagulation uses intense focused light, usually a laser, to heat and seal tissue or blood vessels.

name: light cycle
clinical_significance: A light cycle is the recurring pattern of light and darkness that helps regulate circadian rhythms and biological activity.

name: light microscope
clinical_significance: An instrument that uses visible light and lenses to magnify cells, tissues, microorganisms, or other small structures. It is widely used in clinical laboratories, pathology, microbiology, and research.

name: light microscopy
clinical_significance: Examination of cells, tissues, microorganisms, or other specimens using visible light and a microscope. Different stains and preparation methods reveal structure, infection, inflammation, blood cells, or abnormal growth.

name: light scattering
clinical_significance: Deflection of light when it meets particles, cells, molecules, or irregular structures. Measuring the scattered light can help estimate particle size or concentration in laboratory tests and can affect the appearance of tissues on imaging.

name: lignan
clinical_significance: Lignans are plant compounds found in foods such as seeds, whole grains, and vegetables. Gut bacteria can convert some into hormone-like metabolites; their effects on health are still being studied, and supplements are not proven disease treatments.

name: lignin
clinical_significance: Lignin is a structural polymer in plant cell walls and a dietary fiber component. It has no direct human clinical use, though it is studied in nutrition and plant science.

name: lignoceric acid
clinical_significance: Lignoceric acid is a very-long-chain saturated fatty acid found in small amounts in some fats and cell lipids. Its breakdown is relevant to peroxisomal disorders such as adrenoleukodystrophy, in which very-long-chain fatty acids can accumulate.

name: limb
clinical_significance: An arm or leg, including its bones, joints, muscles, tendons, nerves, blood vessels, and skin. Limb problems may affect movement, sensation, strength, circulation, or function.

name: limb bud
clinical_significance: A limb bud is an embryonic outgrowth that develops into an arm or leg through coordinated signaling, growth, and tissue differentiation.

name: limb development
clinical_significance: Limb development is embryonic formation and growth of the bones, joints, muscles, nerves, vessels, and skin of the arms and legs.

name: limb fracture
clinical_significance: A break in a bone of an upper or lower limb, assessed according to location, displacement, open or closed status, joint involvement, and associated neurovascular injury.

name: limb girdle
clinical_significance: A limb girdle is the skeletal connection of a limb to the trunk, such as the shoulder or pelvic girdle.

name: limb injury
clinical_significance: Trauma affecting an arm or leg, including injury to bone, joint, muscle, tendon, ligament, nerve, blood vessel, or skin.

name: limb pain
clinical_significance: Pain arising from an arm or leg, with causes including trauma, nerve disease, vascular insufficiency, infection, inflammation, and musculoskeletal disorders.

name: limb prosthesis
clinical_significance: A limb prosthesis is an artificial device replacing part or all of an arm or leg to restore mobility, function, appearance, or independence.

name: limbic encephalitis
clinical_significance: Limbic encephalitis is inflammation affecting brain regions involved in memory and emotion. It can cause rapidly developing memory loss, confusion, seizures, or behavior changes and may be linked to autoimmune disease, cancer, or infection; prompt evaluation is important.

name: limbic system
clinical_significance: A group of connected brain structures involved in memory, emotion, motivation, learning, and some automatic body responses, such as changes in heart rate during stress.

name: limbus corneae
clinical_significance: The corneal limbus is the circular border where the transparent cornea meets the white sclera and conjunctiva, containing stem cells important for corneal repair.

name: linagliptin
clinical_significance: Linagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor used with diet and exercise to improve blood glucose control in type 2 diabetes.

name: lincomycin
clinical_significance: Lincomycin is a lincosamide antibiotic used for selected serious bacterial infections; it can cause antibiotic-associated diarrhea and colitis.

name: lindane
clinical_significance: Lindane is an organochlorine insecticide formerly used for lice or scabies; neurotoxicity and environmental persistence limit its use.

name: lined canister
clinical_significance: A container with a protective inner lining used to collect or store a medical substance, specimen, waste, or device component. The lining helps prevent leakage, contamination, chemical reaction, or damage to the container; its exact use depends on the equipment.

name: linezolid
clinical_significance: Linezolid is an oxazolidinone antibiotic that blocks formation of the bacterial 70S initiation complex and treats resistant Gram-positive infections; thrombocytopenia, neuropathy, lactic acidosis, and serotonin interactions require caution.

name: lingual thyroid
clinical_significance: A lingual thyroid is thyroid tissue at the base of the tongue caused by failure of normal thyroid descent and may obstruct swallowing or breathing or cause hypothyroidism.

name: lingual tonsil
clinical_significance: The lingual tonsil is lymphoid tissue at the base of the tongue that contributes to immune surveillance of the throat.

name: liniment
clinical_significance: A liquid or semiliquid preparation rubbed onto the skin, usually to provide temporary relief of muscle or joint discomfort. Some contain irritating or warming substances and should not be used on broken skin, near the eyes, or under tight coverings unless directed.

name: linitis plastica
clinical_significance: A form of stomach cancer that spreads widely through the stomach wall, making it thick and stiff. It may cause early fullness, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, or vague upper-abdominal discomfort.

name: linkage disequilibrium
clinical_significance: Linkage disequilibrium occurs when genetic variants near each other are inherited together more often than expected by chance. It helps genetic studies locate disease-associated regions but does not by itself show that a variant causes disease.

name: linoleic acid
clinical_significance: An essential omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid obtained from food. The body uses it to make cell membranes and signaling molecules.

name: linolenic acid
clinical_significance: A polyunsaturated fatty acid. Alpha-linolenic acid is an essential omega-3 nutrient from plant foods, while other forms occur in animal tissues and have different roles.

name: linseed oil
clinical_significance: Linseed oil, also called flaxseed oil, is rich in the plant omega-3 fatty acid alpha-linolenic acid. It is used as food or a supplement, but it is not equivalent to marine omega-3 medicines and can interact with medicines that affect bleeding.

name: linsitinib
clinical_significance: Linsitinib is an investigational inhibitor of insulin-like growth factor 1 and insulin receptors, studied as a targeted cancer drug. Trials have not established it as routine cancer treatment.

name: lintuzumab
clinical_significance: Lintuzumab is an investigational antibody targeting CD33, a protein on many acute myeloid leukemia cells. It has been tested with chemotherapy, but it is not an approved standard treatment.

name: liothyronine sodium
clinical_significance: A manufactured form of triiodothyronine, an active thyroid hormone, used in selected thyroid disorders. It acts quickly and can cause fast heartbeat, tremor, anxiety, bone loss, or heart strain if excessive.

name: lip
clinical_significance: The lips are mobile folds of skin and mucosa containing muscle, blood vessels, and sensory nerves; they form the oral seal and assist speech, facial expression, feeding, and swallowing.

name: lip disease
clinical_significance: A disorder of the lips, such as infection, inflammation, ulceration, trauma, pigmentation change, benign tumor, or malignancy.

name: lip infection
clinical_significance: Infection of the lip caused by bacteria, viruses, fungi, or an infected wound. It may cause pain, redness, swelling, blisters, cracks, pus, or fever; rapidly spreading swelling or breathing difficulty may occur in a serious infection.

name: lip neoplasm
clinical_significance: A lip neoplasm is an abnormal growth in the lip that may be benign or malignant; persistent sores or lumps require assessment.

name: lipase
clinical_significance: An enzyme that breaks down fats into smaller molecules. Blood lipase testing is commonly used when pancreatitis is suspected, although an abnormal result is not specific in every case.

name: lipedema
clinical_significance: A long-term disorder causing an unusual, usually symmetrical buildup of painful fat in the legs and sometimes arms. The feet and hands are usually spared, while easy bruising, tenderness, and swelling may occur.

name: lipemic index
clinical_significance: A laboratory estimate of how cloudy a blood sample is because of excess fats. Marked cloudiness can interfere with some test results and may prompt review of the sample or repeat testing.

name: lipid
clinical_significance: A fat or fat-like substance, including triglycerides, cholesterol, phospholipids, and fat-soluble vitamins. Lipids store energy, form cell membranes, help make hormones, and help the body absorb vitamins A, D, E, and K.

name: lipid bilayer
clinical_significance: The double layer of fat-like molecules forming the basic structure of cell membranes. It separates the cell from its surroundings and controls movement of substances.

name: lipid binding
clinical_significance: Lipid binding is the attachment of a molecule to fats or lipid-containing structures. It can affect how medicines and proteins travel through blood, enter cells, or interact with cell membranes.

name: lipid disorder
clinical_significance: An abnormal level or handling of fats in the blood or tissues, such as high LDL cholesterol, high triglycerides, or unusually low protective HDL cholesterol.

name: lipid droplet
clinical_significance: A lipid droplet is a cell structure that stores fat for energy and membrane production. Abnormal lipid-droplet handling is studied in fatty liver disease, obesity, and inherited metabolic disorders.

name: lipid metabolism
clinical_significance: The processes by which the body digests, transports, stores, makes, and breaks down fats for energy, cell membranes, and hormone production.

name: lipid peroxidation
clinical_significance: Lipid peroxidation is oxidative damage to fats in cell membranes and lipoproteins. Excess can injure cells and is studied in inflammation, vascular disease, and other conditions; markers are not diagnostic on their own.

name: lipid peroxide
clinical_significance: A lipid peroxide is a fat molecule chemically altered by oxidation. Accumulation can damage cell membranes and is studied as a marker of oxidative stress, but results require clinical context.

name: lipid transport
clinical_significance: Movement of fats through blood and tissues by lipoproteins, carrier proteins, or other mechanisms for energy use, storage, membrane formation, and hormone production.

name: lipidomics
clinical_significance: Lipidomics is the large-scale measurement of fats and related molecules in cells, tissues, or body fluids. It is used mainly in research to study metabolism and disease and is not yet a routine standalone diagnostic test.

name: lipoatrophy
clinical_significance: Loss of the layer of fat beneath the skin, causing dents or hollow areas. It can follow repeated injections, inflammation, autoimmune disease, HIV treatment, or inherited disorders and may alter medicine absorption at injection sites.

name: lipoblastoma
clinical_significance: A usually benign tumor of immature adipose tissue occurring mainly in infants and young children; it may be localized or diffuse and can recur if incompletely removed.

name: lipodystrophy
clinical_significance: Abnormal loss or distribution of body fat. It may be inherited or caused by medicines, metabolic disease, or repeated injections and can lead to insulin resistance, diabetes, high triglycerides, or changes in appearance.

name: lipofuscin
clinical_significance: Lipofuscin is a yellow-brown, non-degradable pigment made of oxidized lipid and protein residues that accumulates in long-lived cells with ageing and in some degenerative diseases.

name: lipogenesis
clinical_significance: Lipogenesis is the process of making fatty acids and triglycerides from smaller molecules, especially when energy intake exceeds immediate needs. Abnormal regulation is relevant to fatty liver disease and metabolic disorders.

name: lipogranulomatosis
clinical_significance: Inflammation in which fat accumulates and triggers organized collections of immune cells called granulomas. It may affect skin, soft tissue, or internal organs and can result from injury, leakage of oily material, or metabolic disease.

name: lipohypertrophy
clinical_significance: A firm or lumpy buildup of fat under the skin, often at repeated insulin-injection sites. Injecting into these areas can change how insulin is absorbed.

name: lipoid nephrosis
clinical_significance: An older name for a kidney disorder, most often in children, in which the kidney filters leak large amounts of protein into the urine. It can cause swelling around the eyes, legs, or abdomen.

name: lipoidosis
clinical_significance: Abnormal buildup of fats within cells or tissues, usually because a metabolic pathway cannot process or transport them normally. It may be inherited or acquired and can damage organs such as the liver, nerves, or kidneys.

name: lipolysis
clinical_significance: Breakdown of stored body fat into fatty acids and glycerol so they can be used for energy. Fasting and stress hormones increase this process, while insulin generally reduces it.

name: lipoma
clinical_significance: A common benign tumor made of mature fat cells. It is usually soft, movable, painless, and slow-growing beneath the skin of the trunk, neck, or limbs; a deep, firm, painful, or rapidly enlarging fatty lump needs assessment to distinguish it from other tumors.

name: lipomatous neoplasm
clinical_significance: A growth made partly or mainly of fat cells. It may be noncancerous, like a lipoma, or cancerous, like a liposarcoma; a deep, firm, painful, or rapidly enlarging lump needs specialist assessment.

name: lipophagy
clinical_significance: Lipophagy is the breakdown of lipid droplets through autophagy, a cell recycling process. It helps regulate fat stores and is studied in liver disease, obesity, and metabolic research.

name: lipophilicity
clinical_significance: Lipophilicity is the tendency of a substance to dissolve in fats or oils rather than water, influencing drug absorption and distribution.

name: lipopolysaccharide
clinical_significance: Lipopolysaccharide is the outer-membrane endotoxin of Gram-negative bacteria, consisting of lipid A, core polysaccharide, and O antigen; circulating lipid A can trigger cytokine release, fever, shock, and disseminated inflammation.

name: lipoprotein
clinical_significance: A particle made of fat and protein that carries cholesterol and other fats through the blood. Different types transport dietary fat, triglycerides, or cholesterol; high LDL levels can contribute to artery disease.

name: lipoprotein lipase
clinical_significance: An enzyme on capillary walls that breaks down triglycerides in chylomicrons and very-low-density lipoproteins so tissues can use or store the fatty acids. Its activity is regulated by nutritional and hormonal signals.

name: liposarcoma
clinical_significance: Liposarcoma is a cancer of fat-forming soft tissue, often arising deep in the thigh or abdomen. It may grow without early symptoms; diagnosis usually requires imaging and biopsy, and treatment depends on subtype, site, and spread.

name: liposome
clinical_significance: A liposome is a tiny vesicle made of a lipid bilayer that can carry medicines or other substances into or around the body.

name: liquid
clinical_significance: A liquid is a fluid state of matter. In healthcare, liquids include blood, urine, spinal fluid, and other specimens or medicines; their composition and test results depend on the specific fluid and clinical question.

name: liquid biopsy
clinical_significance: A non-invasive laboratory technique that analyzes tumor-derived biomarkers, including circulating tumor cells, cell-free circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and exosomes isolated from peripheral blood or other bodily fluids for cancer detection and genomic profiling.

name: liquid chromatography
clinical_significance: A laboratory method that separates dissolved substances as a liquid carries them through a material that interacts differently with each substance. It is used to identify or measure medicines, hormones, metabolites, proteins, and toxins.

name: liquid crystal
clinical_significance: Liquid crystals have properties between those of liquids and solid crystals and are used in optical sensors and some medical devices. Their clinical relevance depends on the specific imaging or measurement system.

name: liraglutide
clinical_significance: Liraglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist used to improve glucose control in type 2 diabetes and, at some doses, support weight management.

name: lisch nodule
clinical_significance: A Lisch nodule is a harmless pigmented hamartoma of the iris, commonly associated with neurofibromatosis type 1.

name: lisinopril
clinical_significance: Lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor used for hypertension, heart failure, and kidney protection in some diabetes; cough, hyperkalaemia, renal-function changes, angioedema, and fetal toxicity are important risks.

name: lissencephaly
clinical_significance: A birth condition in which the brain’s surface has few or no normal folds because nerve cells did not move to their usual positions during development. It can cause seizures, severe developmental impairment, feeding problems, and movement difficulties.

name: listeria
clinical_significance: Listeria is a genus of bacteria; L. monocytogenes can cause foodborne illness, bloodstream infection, and meningitis, especially in pregnancy, older adults, and people with weakened immunity.

name: listeria grayi
clinical_significance: Listeria grayi is an environmental Listeria species not usually associated with human disease. Its recovery from a clinical specimen should be interpreted with the specimen source and evidence for true infection.

name: listeria innocua
clinical_significance: Listeria innocua is generally considered nonpathogenic, although rare human infections have been reported. Because it can resemble L. monocytogenes, accurate laboratory identification is important when it is isolated from a patient.

name: listeria ivanovii
clinical_significance: Listeria ivanovii mainly causes disease in animals and only rarely infects humans. Its detection in a clinical specimen should be assessed for possible invasive infection and confirmed by the laboratory.

name: listeria monocytogenes
clinical_significance: Listeria monocytogenes is a foodborne bacterium that can cause gastroenteritis, bloodstream infection, or meningitis. Infection is especially dangerous during pregnancy, in newborns, older adults, and people with weakened immunity.

name: listeria seeligeri
clinical_significance: Listeria seeligeri is an environmental species that rarely causes human disease. Its significance in a clinical culture depends on the specimen and evidence of infection.

name: listeria welshimeri
clinical_significance: Listeria welshimeri is an environmental species not commonly linked to human illness. Recovery from a clinical sample is uncommon and requires interpretation in context.

name: listeriosis
clinical_significance: Infection with Listeria monocytogenes, usually acquired from contaminated food. It may cause fever and diarrhea or severe disease such as bloodstream infection or meningitis, especially in pregnancy, newborns, older adults, and people with weakened immunity.

name: liter
clinical_significance: A liter is a metric unit of volume equal to 1,000 milliliters. It is used to measure fluids such as urine output, intravenous fluids, and fluid intake.

name: literacy
clinical_significance: Literacy is the ability to read and use written information. Health literacy affects how people understand health instructions and navigate care, but it is not a diagnosis and should be considered when communicating with patients.

name: lithiasis
clinical_significance: The formation or presence of stones (calculi) in an organ or duct. The term is often named for the site, such as nephrolithiasis in the kidney, ureterolithiasis in the ureter, or cholelithiasis in the gallbladder.

name: lithium
clinical_significance: Lithium is a mood stabilizer used mainly for bipolar disorder and selected augmentation treatment; its narrow therapeutic range requires monitoring for tremor, thyroid or renal dysfunction, dehydration, drug interactions, and toxicity.

name: lithium carbonate
clinical_significance: A mood-stabilizing medicine used mainly to treat bipolar disorder and reduce the risk of manic or depressive episodes; serum levels, kidney function, thyroid function, and drug interactions require monitoring.

name: lithotripsy
clinical_significance: Lithotripsy breaks stones into smaller pieces so they can pass or be removed. Extracorporeal shock-wave lithotripsy treats selected urinary stones from outside the body; choice of procedure depends on stone size and location, and bleeding, pain, or tissue injury can occur.

name: Little's disease
clinical_significance: An older name for spastic cerebral palsy, a condition caused by early brain injury or abnormal development that produces stiff muscles and movement difficulties, mainly in the legs. It is not progressive, although needs change over time.

name: live birth
clinical_significance: A live birth is delivery of an infant showing signs of life such as breathing, heartbeat, or movement, regardless of gestational age.

name: livedo racemosa
clinical_significance: A persistent, irregular, branching net-like pattern of reddish-blue skin caused by disease of small or medium blood vessels. It may occur with autoimmune, clotting, inflammatory, or other systemic disorders and needs evaluation.

name: livedo reticularis
clinical_significance: A net-like, violaceous discoloration of the skin caused by altered blood flow in small cutaneous vessels.

name: liver
clinical_significance: The largest internal organ, beneath the right ribs. It processes nutrients, makes bile to help digest fats, stores energy, helps regulate blood chemicals, and breaks down medicines and harmful substances.

name: liver abscess
clinical_significance: A pocket of pus in the liver, usually caused by bacteria or an amoeba. It may cause fever, chills, or pain in the upper-right abdomen. Treatment depends on the cause and size and may include antimicrobial medicines and drainage.

name: liver circulation
clinical_significance: The liver receives oxygen-rich blood from the hepatic artery and nutrient-rich blood from the portal vein. Blood passes through liver tissue and leaves through the hepatic veins to the heart.

name: liver cirrhosis
clinical_significance: Liver cirrhosis is advanced scarring that can lead to portal hypertension, bleeding, fluid accumulation, confusion, and liver cancer; complication surveillance and cause-directed care are important.

name: liver damage
clinical_significance: Liver damage is injury or loss of liver-cell function caused by infection, alcohol, medicines, toxins, fatty disease, autoimmune disease, or other processes.

name: liver disorder
clinical_significance: Any disease affecting the liver, including fatty liver, viral hepatitis, autoimmune disease, scarring, blockage of bile flow, or cancer. Symptoms may be absent or include jaundice, fatigue, pain, swelling, or abnormal blood tests.

name: liver dysfunction
clinical_significance: Liver dysfunction is reduced ability of the liver to perform tasks such as processing nutrients, making proteins, clearing toxins, and producing bile.

name: liver failure
clinical_significance: A life-threatening loss of the liver's ability to make proteins, process nutrients, remove harmful substances, and regulate blood clotting. It can cause jaundice, bleeding, confusion, swelling, and multiple-organ failure.

name: liver fibrosis
clinical_significance: Excessive scar formation in the liver after ongoing injury or inflammation. It can progress to cirrhosis, reduce liver function, and result from viral hepatitis, alcohol, fatty liver, immune disease, or other causes.

name: liver function tests
clinical_significance: Liver function tests are blood tests that assess liver-cell injury, bile-flow problems, or the liver’s ability to make proteins and clear substances. Individual results are not diagnostic by themselves and are interpreted with symptoms, medications, and other tests.

name: liver infection
clinical_significance: Infection of liver tissue, such as a viral hepatitis infection or a bacterial liver abscess. Symptoms may include fever, tiredness, nausea, right-upper-abdominal pain, jaundice, or confusion and require medical evaluation.

name: liver neoplasm
clinical_significance: A liver neoplasm is an abnormal growth in the liver that may be benign or malignant and may arise from liver cells, bile ducts, or metastasis from another cancer.

name: liver pain
clinical_significance: Discomfort in the upper-right abdomen that may arise from the liver, gallbladder, bile ducts, stomach, muscles, or other organs. Persistent pain, jaundice, fever, vomiting, or confusion may indicate an underlying illness.

name: liver regeneration
clinical_significance: The liver's ability to restore lost tissue by growing and reorganizing remaining cells after injury or partial surgical removal.

name: liver transplantation
clinical_significance: Surgery to replace a severely diseased or failing liver with a healthy donor liver or part of one. It may be used for advanced liver disease, sudden liver failure, or selected liver cancers; lifelong medicines help prevent rejection.

name: loa loa
clinical_significance: Loa loa is a filarial worm transmitted by deer flies in parts of West and Central Africa. It can cause temporary swelling and visible migration across the eye; heavy infection can complicate treatment for other parasitic diseases.

name: lobaplatin
clinical_significance: Lobaplatin is a platinum-based antineoplastic drug used in some countries and studied for its ability to damage cancer-cell DNA.

name: lobe
clinical_significance: A lobe is a distinct subdivision of an organ or structure, such as a lung, liver, brain, thyroid, or gland.

name: lobectomy
clinical_significance: A lobectomy removes one lobe of an organ, most often part of a lung or liver. It may treat cancer or other localized disease; recovery and risks depend on the organ, remaining function, and reason for surgery.

name: lobeline
clinical_significance: Lobeline is a plant-derived alkaloid studied for effects on nicotine receptors and smoking cessation. Evidence has not established it as a safe, effective cessation medicine, and it can cause nausea, dizziness, or other toxicity.

name: lobstein disease
clinical_significance: Lobstein disease is an older name for osteogenesis imperfecta, an inherited disorder of fragile bones that fracture easily. Severity varies; dental, hearing, joint, and breathing problems may also occur.

name: lobucavir
clinical_significance: Lobucavir is an experimental antiviral medicine studied for hepatitis B and other viral infections. It was not approved for routine use, and its development was stopped after long-term animal studies raised safety concerns.

name: lobular carcinoma
clinical_significance: Lobular carcinoma is a cancer arising from cells of a breast lobule, the gland that produces milk; it may be invasive or confined to the lobule.

name: lobule
clinical_significance: A lobule is a small subdivision of an organ or tissue, such as a liver lobule, lung lobule, or breast lobule.

name: local
clinical_significance: Limited to a particular body site or region rather than involving the whole body. A local treatment or symptom affects the treated or affected area, although nearby or wider effects can sometimes occur.

name: local anesthesia
clinical_significance: Temporary loss of sensation, especially pain, in a small, specific body area caused by a local anesthetic applied to the surface or injected nearby. The person usually remains conscious, although sedation may be added; excessive dosing or accidental injection into a blood vessel can cause seizures, heart problems, or other toxicity.

name: local anesthetic
clinical_significance: A local anesthetic temporarily blocks nerve signals to prevent pain in a limited area. Excessive dose or accidental injection into a blood vessel can cause seizures, heart-rhythm problems, or cardiac arrest.

name: local therapy
clinical_significance: Local therapy treats a disease at or near the affected area rather than throughout the body, for example with a cream, injection, surgery, or focused radiation.

name: localized
clinical_significance: Limited to one particular area, organ, or body site without evidence of distant spread. A localized disease may still be serious, but treatment can sometimes focus on the affected area.

name: localized edema
clinical_significance: Swelling confined to a particular body region because of fluid accumulation, commonly caused by venous or lymphatic obstruction, inflammation, trauma, allergy, or local infection.

name: localized scleroderma
clinical_significance: An autoimmune skin disorder causing localized thickening and hardening of the skin, with or without involvement of deeper tissues; it differs from systemic sclerosis.

name: location
clinical_significance: Location describes the site of a finding, symptom, injury, or procedure. Precise location helps clinicians distinguish possible causes and plan examination, imaging, or treatment.

name: locomotion
clinical_significance: Movement of an organism or person from one place to another using coordinated muscles, bones, nerves, and balance systems.

name: locus
clinical_significance: The specific location of a gene or other DNA sequence on a chromosome. It is described using the chromosome number and a coded position on its short or long arm.

name: locus coeruleus
clinical_significance: The locus coeruleus is a brainstem nucleus whose noradrenaline-producing neurons influence arousal, attention, stress, sleep, and pain.

name: lod score
clinical_significance: A statistical measure used in genetic linkage analysis to compare how likely it is that two genetic markers are inherited together rather than independently. Higher positive scores provide stronger evidence of linkage in the studied family.

name: loiasis
clinical_significance: Loiasis is infection with the filarial worm Loa loa, transmitted by deerflies and sometimes causing transient eye-worm migration and localized swelling.

name: lometrexol
clinical_significance: Lometrexol is an investigational antifolate chemotherapy drug studied for solid tumors. It can affect rapidly dividing normal cells and cause serious toxicity; it is not an established standard cancer treatment.

name: lomustine
clinical_significance: Lomustine is an oral chemotherapy medicine used for selected brain tumors and other cancers; delayed low blood counts are an important risk.

name: lonafarnib
clinical_significance: A farnesyltransferase-inhibiting medicine used for selected progeroid syndromes, in which abnormal protein processing contributes to premature aging features. It can cause gastrointestinal symptoms, liver abnormalities, and drug interactions.

name: loneliness
clinical_significance: Loneliness is distress related to a gap between desired and actual social connection. Persistent loneliness is associated with worse mental and physical wellbeing but is not itself a psychiatric diagnosis.

name: Long QT syndrome
clinical_significance: A heart rhythm disorder in which the heart takes too long to reset between beats. It may be inherited or caused by medicines or abnormal body salts and can lead to fainting, dangerous rhythms, or sudden death.

name: longevity
clinical_significance: Longevity is length of life. In health research, it is considered alongside healthy life expectancy, disability, and quality of life; lifespan alone does not indicate an individual’s health.

name: longitudinal studies
clinical_significance: Longitudinal studies follow participants or measurements over time to examine change, incidence, exposures, outcomes, and temporal relationships.

name: long-term care
