clinical_significance: Ongoing help with daily activities, nursing, medical needs, or supervision for a person who cannot live fully independently. Care may be provided at home, in assisted living, or in a nursing facility and should match changing needs.

name: long-term memory
clinical_significance: Information retained for a long period, from hours or days to a lifetime. It includes explicit memories of facts and events and implicit skills or habits.

name: long-term potentiation
clinical_significance: Long-term potentiation is a lasting increase in the strength of communication between nerve cells after repeated stimulation and is important in learning and memory.

name: lontucirev
clinical_significance: Lontucirev, also called ONYX-015, is an experimental genetically modified adenovirus studied as an oncolytic cancer treatment. It was tested in clinical trials but is not an established or approved standard therapy.

name: loperamide
clinical_significance: Loperamide is a medicine that slows intestinal movement and reduces diarrhea. It may be unsafe in bloody or fever-related diarrhea, and excessive doses can cause severe abnormal heart rhythms.

name: loperamide hydrochloride
clinical_significance: Loperamide hydrochloride is an antidiarrheal medicine that slows movement through the intestine; excessive doses can cause dangerous heart rhythms.

name: lopinavir
clinical_significance: Lopinavir is an HIV protease inhibitor used with ritonavir in antiretroviral treatment; drug interactions are common.

name: loratadine
clinical_significance: An antihistamine used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and hives. It usually causes less drowsiness than older antihistamines, but sleepiness, headache, or dry mouth can still occur.

name: lorazepam
clinical_significance: Lorazepam is a benzodiazepine used short term for severe anxiety, seizures, or sedation; it can cause drowsiness, dependence, and breathing suppression.

name: Lorenzo's oil
clinical_significance: Lorenzo’s oil is a mixture of fatty acids studied in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy. It may lower very-long-chain fatty acids in some presymptomatic boys, but it does not reverse established brain disease and requires specialist monitoring.

name: losartan
clinical_significance: Losartan is an angiotensin-receptor blocker used for high blood pressure, some kidney disease, and heart failure; it can raise potassium levels.

name: losartan potassium
clinical_significance: Losartan potassium is the salt form of losartan, an angiotensin-receptor blocker used to lower blood pressure and protect selected patients with kidney or heart disease.

name: losoxantrone
clinical_significance: Losoxantrone is an investigational anticancer drug studied for leukemia and other cancers. It is not an established standard treatment; heart and bone-marrow toxicities are concerns with this drug class.

name: loss of heterozygosity
clinical_significance: Loss of heterozygosity is loss of one of two different versions of a gene in a cell, a change that can contribute to cancer when a tumor-suppressor gene is affected.

name: loteprednol etabonate
clinical_significance: Loteprednol etabonate is a corticosteroid eye medicine used for eye inflammation; prolonged use can raise eye pressure and increase infection risk.

name: lotion
clinical_significance: A lotion is a liquid or semiliquid product applied to the skin. Medicines in lotion form may treat inflammation, infection, or dryness; ingredients and directions matter because irritation or allergy can occur.

name: louse
clinical_significance: A louse infestation can cause itching and skin irritation and may spread among close contacts; diagnosis and appropriate treatment depend on whether head, body, or pubic lice are involved.

name: lovastatin
clinical_significance: Lovastatin is a statin medicine that lowers LDL cholesterol and reduces cardiovascular risk; muscle injury and liver effects are uncommon but important risks.

name: love
clinical_significance: Love is an emotional and social bond that can support wellbeing and relationships. It is not a medical diagnosis; relationship changes or distress may affect mental health and can be discussed in care when relevant.

name: low grade
clinical_significance: Describes a disease or tumor that appears less aggressive or more slowly developing than higher-grade forms. The exact meaning and outlook depend on the specific disease and test used.

name: low vision
clinical_significance: Low vision is lasting visual impairment that cannot be fully corrected with standard glasses, contact lenses, medicine, or surgery. It can affect reading, mobility, and daily tasks; rehabilitation and assistive devices may improve independence.

name: low-density lipoprotein
clinical_significance: A particle that carries cholesterol through the blood. Too much LDL cholesterol can collect in artery walls, forming fatty deposits that narrow arteries and increase the risk of heart attack and stroke.

name: lower extremity
clinical_significance: The lower extremity is the hip, thigh, knee, leg, ankle, and foot, including their bones, joints, muscles, nerves, vessels, and skin.

name: lubiprostone
clinical_significance: Lubiprostone activates intestinal chloride channels and is used for selected forms of chronic constipation and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation.

name: lubricant
clinical_significance: A substance that reduces friction between surfaces; medical lubricants are used on skin, mucosa, instruments, or devices and should be selected for tissue compatibility and intended use.

name: lucanthone
clinical_significance: Lucanthone is an older antischistosomal drug that was also studied as an anticancer agent. It is not a routine modern treatment and can cause serious adverse effects, including liver or nervous-system toxicity.

name: luciferase
clinical_significance: Luciferase is an enzyme that produces light in certain organisms. It is widely used as a laboratory reporter to measure gene activity, cell viability, or infection-related signals, but the enzyme itself is not a clinical diagnosis.

name: Lugol's solution
clinical_significance: Lugol's solution is a mixture of iodine and potassium iodide used in selected laboratory, diagnostic, and medical applications; it can irritate tissue and affect thyroid function.

name: lumbar plexus
clinical_significance: The lumbar plexus is a network of nerves from the upper lumbar spinal roots that supplies the lower abdomen, pelvis, and parts of the thigh and leg.

name: lumbar puncture
clinical_significance: A procedure that uses a needle in the lower back to collect cerebrospinal fluid, the liquid around the brain and spinal cord. The fluid can be tested for infection, bleeding, inflammation, or cancer; pressure can also be measured, and some medicines can be given. Clinicians check bleeding risk and possible increased pressure in the skull first. Headache, back pain, bleeding, and infection are possible complications.

name: Lumbar Region
clinical_significance: The lumbar region is the lower part of the back between the ribs and pelvis, containing the five lumbar vertebrae.

name: lumbar vertebrae
clinical_significance: The five large bones of the lower spine between the ribs and pelvis. They bear much of the body’s weight, allow bending, protect spinal nerves, and can be affected by fractures, arthritis, or disc problems.

name: lumbosacral region
clinical_significance: The lumbosacral region is the junction between the lower lumbar spine and the sacrum at the back of the pelvis.

name: luminescence
clinical_significance: Luminescence is emission of light from a substance through a process other than high-temperature incandescence, such as fluorescence or chemiluminescence.

name: luminescence type
clinical_significance: Luminescence type identifies the mechanism by which a material emits light, such as fluorescence, phosphorescence, bioluminescence, or chemiluminescence.

name: lung
clinical_significance: One of the two breathing organs in the chest. The lungs take oxygen into the blood and remove carbon dioxide. The right lung has three sections, and the left has two to leave room for the heart.

name: lung abscess
clinical_significance: A pocket of infection and pus that forms inside damaged lung tissue, often after inhaling stomach contents or because of bacteria. It may cause fever, cough, foul-smelling sputum, chest pain, and breathlessness.

name: lung cyst
clinical_significance: A lung cyst is a round air- or fluid-containing space in lung tissue, caused by developmental disease, infection, emphysema, inflammation, or another disorder.

name: lung development
clinical_significance: Lung development is embryonic and postnatal formation and maturation of airways, alveoli, blood vessels, and gas-exchange capacity.

name: lung disease
clinical_significance: Lung disease includes disorders affecting the breathing tubes, air sacs, lung tissue, covering, blood vessels, or chest wall. These conditions may cause cough, breathlessness, chest discomfort, wheezing, or low oxygen.

name: lung fibroma
clinical_significance: A usually noncancerous growth made of fibrous tissue in or near the lung. It often causes no symptoms and is found on imaging, but its appearance, growth, and location may require further imaging or biopsy.

name: lung injury
clinical_significance: Damage to lung tissue or the pulmonary circulation caused by trauma, infection, inhaled substances, inflammation, aspiration, oxygen toxicity, or other disease.

name: lung lavage
clinical_significance: A procedure in which doctors wash parts of the airways or lungs with sterile fluid and then remove it. It may clear certain material from the lungs or collect a sample for testing.

name: lung neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in the lung or airways that may be noncancerous or cancerous. It may cause cough, blood in sputum, chest pain, breathlessness, or no symptoms; imaging and sometimes tissue sampling determine its nature.

name: lung transplantation
clinical_significance: Lung transplantation replaces one or both severely diseased lungs with donor lungs. Recipients need lifelong medicines to prevent rejection and monitoring for infection, airway or blood-vessel problems, and complications from immunosuppression.

name: lupus erythematosus
clinical_significance: A long-term autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. It can cause tiredness, joint pain, rashes, and inflammation or damage in organs such as the kidneys, lungs, heart, brain, or blood vessels.

name: lupus nephritis
clinical_significance: Lupus nephritis is kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus. It may cause protein or blood in the urine, swelling, or high blood pressure and can progress to kidney failure; urine, blood, and sometimes kidney-biopsy findings guide treatment.

name: lurtotecan
clinical_significance: Lurtotecan is an experimental topoisomerase I inhibitor studied as chemotherapy, including in ovarian cancer. Trials did not establish a clear clinical advantage, and it is not a routine cancer treatment.

name: luteal cell
clinical_significance: A cell in the ovarian corpus luteum that produces progesterone after ovulation and supports the uterine lining.

name: lutein
clinical_significance: A yellow plant pigment found in leafy green vegetables and concentrated in the retina. Along with related pigments, it helps filter blue light and may protect eye tissues from oxidative damage.

name: luteinization
clinical_significance: Luteinization is the transformation of an ovarian follicle after ovulation into a corpus luteum that produces progesterone.

name: luteinizing hormone
clinical_significance: Lutein is a carotenoid found in leafy vegetables that accumulates in the retina. As part of the AREDS2 supplement formula, it may slow progression in people with intermediate age-related macular degeneration; supplements are not recommended to prevent AMD in people without it.

name: luteolin
clinical_significance: Luteolin is a plant flavonoid found in some fruits and vegetables and studied for antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Human evidence is limited, so supplements are not established treatments for disease.

name: luteolysis
clinical_significance: Luteolysis is the breakdown of the corpus luteum, causing progesterone levels to fall when pregnancy has not occurred.

name: luteoma
clinical_significance: A luteoma is a usually benign ovarian mass of hormone-producing lutein cells, sometimes associated with pregnancy and androgen excess.

name: lux unit
clinical_significance: A lux is a unit of illuminance, or light falling on a surface. It is used to specify lighting levels and measure exposure in research or light-based treatment settings.

name: lyase
clinical_significance: An enzyme that breaks or joins certain chemical bonds without adding water or using oxidation as the main step. Lyases participate in many processes that make or use energy in cells.

name: lycopene
clinical_significance: Lycopene is a dietary carotenoid found in tomatoes and other foods; evidence does not support using supplements as a substitute for cancer or cardiovascular prevention and treatment.

name: lyme disease
clinical_significance: A bacterial infection spread by infected ticks; blacklegged ticks transmit it in the United States. Early symptoms may include an expanding rash, fever, tiredness, headache, and muscle or joint aches; untreated infection can later affect nerves, joints, or the heart.

name: lymph
clinical_significance: A clear fluid collected from body tissues and carried through lymph vessels. It transports immune cells and excess fluid to lymph nodes and eventually returns it to the bloodstream.

name: lymph leakage
clinical_significance: Lymph leakage is escape of lymphatic fluid after injury, surgery, or obstruction and may cause swelling, fluid collections, or chylous drainage.

name: lymph node
clinical_significance: A lymph node is a small immune organ that filters lymph and helps activate immune responses to infection, inflammation, or abnormal cells.

name: lymphadenectomy
clinical_significance: Lymphadenectomy is surgical removal of lymph nodes for cancer staging or treatment. It can help assess spread but may cause lymphatic swelling, numbness, pain, or other site-specific complications.

name: lymphadenitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation or infection of one or more lymph nodes, causing swelling and sometimes tenderness, warmth, or pus. Causes include viruses, bacteria, cat-scratch disease, tuberculosis, and other disorders.

name: lymphadenopathy
clinical_significance: Enlargement of one or more lymph nodes. It may be localized or widespread and can result from infection, inflammation, immune disease, medicines, or cancer. Persistent, hard, or unexplained nodes can have an important underlying cause.

name: lymphangiectasis
clinical_significance: Abnormal widening of lymph vessels. It may be present from birth or develop later and can cause swelling, leakage of lymph, loss of protein through the intestine, or fluid around the lungs.

name: lymphangiogenesis
clinical_significance: Formation of new lymph vessels from existing vessels. This can help repair tissue and drain fluid, but it may also contribute to chronic swelling, inflammation, or the spread of cancer.

name: lymphangiography
clinical_significance: An imaging test that uses contrast dye to show lymphatic vessels and their flow. It can help find blocked vessels, leaks, or abnormal connections, although newer scans are often preferred.

name: lymphangioleiomyomatosis
clinical_significance: A rare lung disease in which unusual cells grow in the lungs and lymphatic vessels, causing many small cysts. It mainly affects women and can lead to breathlessness, collapsed lung, bleeding, or kidney tumors.

name: lymphangioma
clinical_significance: A noncancerous birth defect in which lymph vessels form abnormally and become enlarged. It usually appears in infancy or childhood as a soft swelling, often in the neck, armpit, or chest.

name: lymphangiomyoma
clinical_significance: A rare, usually noncancerous growth made of smooth-muscle-like cells around lymph vessels. It is most often associated with lymphangioleiomyomatosis and may contribute to cysts or blockage of lymph flow.

name: lymphangiosarcoma
clinical_significance: A rare, fast-growing cancer arising from the lining of lymph vessels. It may develop in tissue with long-standing lymph swelling and can appear as a bruise-like, purple, or ulcerated skin lesion.

name: lymphangitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation and infection of lymphatic vessels, usually spreading from an infected skin wound or cellulitis; tender red streaks, fever, and enlarged regional lymph nodes may occur.

name: lymphatic basin
clinical_significance: The group of lymph vessels and lymph nodes that drains a particular body area. Doctors use this drainage pattern to examine nearby nodes and assess possible spread of infection or cancer.

name: lymphatic disease
clinical_significance: Any disorder affecting lymph vessels, lymph nodes, or related organs. It may cause swelling, repeated infection, abnormal fluid collections, or cancer and may result from birth defects, injury, infection, inflammation, or tumor growth.

name: lymphatic mapping
clinical_significance: Imaging or tracer-guided identification of lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes that drain a body area. It helps plan surgery, locate a sentinel node, investigate lymphedema, or assess possible cancer spread.

name: lymphatic system
clinical_significance: A network of lymph, lymphatic vessels, lymph nodes, and lymphoid organs and tissues, including the spleen, thymus, tonsils, and bone marrow. It returns excess tissue fluid to the bloodstream, transports absorbed dietary fats and fat-soluble nutrients, and supports immune-cell development, surveillance, and responses to infection.

name: lymphatic tissue
clinical_significance: Lymphatic tissue contains immune cells and structures that filter lymph, trap antigens, and coordinate immune defense.

name: lymphatic vessel
clinical_significance: A lymphatic vessel transports lymph from tissues through lymph nodes and eventually returns fluid to the bloodstream.

name: lymphedema
clinical_significance: Lymphedema is persistent swelling caused by impaired lymph drainage, commonly in an arm or leg after lymph-node surgery, radiation, infection, or a congenital lymphatic disorder. It can cause heaviness, skin changes, restricted movement, and repeated skin infections; ongoing care can help control symptoms.

name: lymphoblast
clinical_significance: An immature cell that normally develops into a type of infection-fighting white blood cell. Large numbers of abnormal lymphoblasts can build up in the blood or bone marrow in acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

name: lymphoblast count
clinical_significance: A lymphoblast count measures immature lymphoid cells in blood or bone marrow and may help evaluate or monitor acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

name: lymphocele
clinical_significance: A lymphocele is a collection of lymphatic fluid caused by disruption or blockage of lymph vessels, often after surgery or transplantation.

name: lymphocyte
clinical_significance: A type of white blood cell that recognizes infections and abnormal cells and helps coordinate immune defense. The main types are B cells, which make antibodies, and T cells, which direct or carry out cellular immune responses.

name: lymphocyte activation
clinical_significance: The process by which a lymphocyte recognizes a target and begins responding. Activated lymphocytes multiply and help coordinate antibody or cellular immune defense.

name: lymphocyte count
clinical_significance: A lymphocyte count measures lymphocytes in the blood and can help assess infection, immune deficiency, inflammation, or blood disorders.

name: lymphocyte proliferation
clinical_significance: Rapid multiplication of lymphocytes after immune stimulation. It helps build a response to infection, but abnormal or uncontrolled proliferation can occur in lymphoid cancers.

name: lymphocytic leukemia
clinical_significance: Lymphocytic leukemia is a blood cancer in which abnormal lymphoid cells multiply in the bone marrow, blood, lymph nodes, or other tissues.

name: lymphocytoma cutis
clinical_significance: Lymphocytoma cutis is a benign skin lymphoid proliferation presenting as red or violaceous plaques or nodules and sometimes associated with infection or immune stimulation.

name: lymphocytosis
clinical_significance: An abnormally increased number or proportion of lymphocytes in the blood, often associated with viral infection, some bacterial infections, or lymphoproliferative disorders.

name: lymphogranuloma venereum
clinical_significance: A sexually transmitted infection caused by certain types of Chlamydia. It may begin with a small painless sore, followed by painful groin swelling or inflammation of the rectum, sometimes with bleeding or discharge.

name: lymphokine
clinical_significance: Cytokines are immune signaling proteins that coordinate inflammation and host defense; excess or blocked cytokine activity can contribute to severe inflammation or immunodeficiency.

name: lymphoma
clinical_significance: A cancer of lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma include many subtypes that may grow slowly or quickly and can cause swollen lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, weight loss, or organ symptoms.

name: lymphomatoid papulosis
clinical_significance: Lymphomatoid papulosis is a chronic, recurring skin disorder with cancer-like immune cells. The bumps often heal on their own, but some people later develop lymphoma.

name: lymphopenia
clinical_significance: Lymphopenia is an abnormally low number of lymphocytes, caused by infection, medicines, immune disease, malnutrition, marrow disorders, or other conditions.

name: lymphopoiesis
clinical_significance: The production and development of lymphocytes, a group of white blood cells that help fight infection and abnormal cells. These cells develop mainly in the bone marrow and thymus.

name: lymphoproliferative disorder
clinical_significance: A condition in which lymphocytes multiply excessively or abnormally. It may be temporary after infection or immune stimulation, or may represent a cancer such as leukemia or lymphoma.

name: Lynch syndrome
clinical_significance: An inherited condition that greatly increases the risk of colorectal, womb, ovarian, stomach, urinary-tract, and several other cancers. Regular screening can detect some cancers early, and relatives may need genetic counseling or testing.

name: lysine
clinical_significance: Lysine is an essential amino acid needed for protein production, growth, and tissue repair; it must be obtained from food.

name: lysinibacillus
clinical_significance: Lysinibacillus is a genus of spore-forming bacteria found mainly in soil and the environment. Rare human infections have been reported, so its recovery from a clinical sample requires confirmation and interpretation with symptoms and other findings.

name: lysogeny
clinical_significance: Lysogeny is a state in which a bacteriophage's genetic material is maintained inside a bacterial cell and replicated with the host genome.

name: lysophagy
clinical_significance: A form of selective autophagy that removes damaged lysosomes, the cell compartments that digest waste. It helps maintain cell health; failure of lysophagy can allow damaged lysosomes to accumulate and promote inflammation or cell injury.

name: lysophosphatidylcholine
clinical_significance: A fat-like molecule found in cell membranes and blood. It helps transport fats and can influence inflammation and cell communication; abnormal levels may occur in metabolic or inflammatory diseases.

name: lysophospholipids
clinical_significance: Lipids related to phospholipids but containing one fewer fatty-acid chain. They are parts of cell membranes and can act as signaling molecules, influencing inflammation, blood vessels, immune responses, and cell movement.

name: lysosome
clinical_significance: A small compartment inside a cell containing substances that break down waste, worn-out cell parts, and material brought into the cell. Lysosome disorders can cause harmful material to accumulate in tissues.

name: lysozyme test
clinical_significance: A lysozyme test measures the enzyme lysozyme in a sample and may support evaluation of selected blood, inflammatory, or infectious disorders.

name: lyssavirus
clinical_significance: A group of viruses that includes rabies virus and related viruses. They mainly spread through the bite or saliva of an infected mammal and can cause a severe brain infection. Prompt wound cleaning and exposure-appropriate vaccination can prevent disease before symptoms begin.

name: lytic lesion
clinical_significance: A lytic lesion is an area of bone destruction caused by processes such as cancer, infection, or some metabolic bone disorders.

name: M phase
clinical_significance: M phase is the part of the cell cycle when a cell divides its chromosomes and then splits into two cells. Abnormal control of this phase can contribute to cancer, and many chemotherapy drugs target dividing cells.

name: machine learning
clinical_significance: Machine learning uses computer algorithms to identify patterns in data. In healthcare it is studied for imaging, diagnosis, and risk prediction, but clinical tools require validation and do not replace clinical judgment.

name: macroautophagy
clinical_significance: A cell-cleaning process in which a cell encloses damaged parts or unwanted proteins, breaks them down, and reuses some of their materials. It helps maintain cell health during stress and normal turnover.

name: macrocephaly
clinical_significance: An unusually large head for a person's age and sex. It may run in a family or be linked to fluid buildup, increased brain growth, or another condition.

name: macrococcus
clinical_significance: Macrococcus is a genus of bacteria found mainly on animals and in the environment. Rare human wound and bloodstream infections have been reported, so identification from a clinical specimen should be interpreted with the patient’s condition and culture findings.

name: macrococcus caseolyticus
clinical_significance: Macrococcus caseolyticus is a bacterium associated mainly with animals and food products. Rare human wound or bloodstream infections have been reported, particularly in vulnerable patients; a positive culture requires clinical correlation.

name: macrocytic anemia
clinical_significance: Anemia in which red blood cells are larger than usual. Common causes include vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use, liver disease, underactive thyroid, some bone-marrow disorders, and recovery from blood loss. It may cause tiredness, pale skin, shortness of breath, or tingling.

name: macroglobulin
clinical_significance: A large protein in the blood, often made of several protein units joined together. Immunoglobulin M is a major example; abnormal amounts can occur in some immune or blood disorders.

name: macroglossia
clinical_significance: Macroglossia is an abnormally enlarged tongue that can affect feeding, speech, airway, or dental development and may be congenital or acquired.

name: macrolide
clinical_significance: A class of antibiotics that stops bacteria from making proteins. Examples include azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin; side effects and medicine interactions vary.

name: macrolide antibiotic
clinical_significance: A macrolide antibiotic blocks bacterial protein production and is used for selected respiratory, skin, and other infections. Resistance, heart-rhythm effects, and drug interactions vary among medicines in this class.

name: macronucleus
clinical_significance: A macronucleus is the larger, gene-expressing nucleus in certain single-celled organisms such as ciliates. It is relevant to microbiology and cell biology and is not a structure found in human cells.

name: macrophage
clinical_significance: A large immune cell that surrounds and removes germs, dead cells, and debris. It also helps coordinate inflammation and tissue repair.

name: macrophage activation
clinical_significance: The process by which macrophages, a type of immune cell, respond to infection or tissue injury. They may destroy germs and damaged cells, alert other immune cells, and release substances that promote inflammation or repair.

name: macrophage count
clinical_significance: The number or percentage of macrophages found in a tissue, body fluid, or laboratory sample. The result may help assess infection, inflammation, tissue repair, or a blood disorder, but its meaning depends on the sample and other findings.

name: macropsia
clinical_significance: A visual disturbance in which objects appear larger than they really are. It may occur with migraine, seizures, retinal problems, medicines, or brain disorders and can temporarily affect depth and distance judgment.

name: macroscopic hematuria
clinical_significance: Visible blood in the urine, also called gross hematuria; it may arise from the kidneys, ureters, bladder, prostate, or urethra and requires evaluation for causes such as infection, stones, trauma, or malignancy.

name: macrostomia
clinical_significance: An abnormally wide mouth or oral opening, usually a congenital facial cleft caused by incomplete fusion of the embryonic facial processes.

name: macular degeneration
clinical_significance: A general term for disorders that damage the macula, the central part of the retina responsible for detailed straight-ahead vision. Age-related macular degeneration is a common form and has dry (atrophic) and wet (neovascular) types; inherited and other disorders can also cause macular degeneration.

name: macular drusen
clinical_significance: Small yellow deposits beneath the retina in the macula, the area responsible for sharp central vision. A few small deposits may occur with aging, while many large deposits can signal increased risk of macular degeneration.

name: macular hole
clinical_significance: A full-thickness opening in the fovea, the center of the macula, often caused by traction between the vitreous gel and retina. It may cause blurred or distorted central vision or a central blind spot.

name: macule
clinical_significance: A flat, clearly defined change in skin color that cannot be felt as a raised or depressed area. Macules may be lighter, darker, red, or brown and can have many causes.

name: maculopapular lesion
clinical_significance: A skin lesion combining flat areas of altered color (macules) with small raised solid lesions (papules); it can occur in infections, drug eruptions, inflammatory diseases, and other conditions.

name: madurella
clinical_significance: Madurella is a genus of fungi that can cause mycetoma, a chronic infection of skin and deeper tissue after implantation through the skin.

name: madurella mycetomatis
clinical_significance: A fungus that commonly causes eumycetoma, a chronic infection producing nodules, draining sinuses, and grains, usually after traumatic implantation in the foot or limb.

name: maf protein
clinical_significance: MAF proteins are a family of transcription factors that regulate cell development and gene activity. Altered MAF genes can contribute to some cancers and inherited eye or bone disorders, depending on the specific gene and variant.

name: Maffucci syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare condition causing multiple benign cartilage growths and abnormal blood-vessel growths, usually beginning in childhood. It can deform bones, cause fractures, and increase the risk of certain cancers.

name: mafosfamide
clinical_significance: Mafosfamide is an investigational chemotherapy related to cyclophosphamide that can act without liver activation. It has been studied for cancer, including treatment delivered into the cerebrospinal fluid, but is not a routine standard medicine.

name: magnesium
clinical_significance: A mineral needed for healthy nerves, muscles, bones, heart rhythm, and many body processes. Too little can cause weakness, tremor, muscle cramps, or abnormal heart rhythms.

name: magnesium chloride
clinical_significance: A magnesium salt used in some oral supplements and medical preparations to provide magnesium or, in concentrated solutions, to help correct magnesium deficiency; dosing depends on the elemental magnesium content.

name: magnesium deficiency
clinical_significance: Magnesium deficiency is a low body magnesium level, often caused by poor intake, gastrointestinal loss, alcohol use, or certain medicines. It can cause weakness, cramps, tremor, seizures, or abnormal heart rhythms and may require blood testing and replacement.

name: magnesium hydroxide
clinical_significance: An osmotic laxative and antacid that neutralizes gastric acid and draws water into the bowel.

name: magnesium oxide
clinical_significance: An inorganic magnesium compound used in some supplements and antacids; it can also have a laxative effect, and excessive use may cause hypermagnesemia, especially with kidney impairment.

name: magnesium sulfate
clinical_significance: A magnesium salt used intravenously or intramuscularly to treat selected magnesium deficiencies and conditions such as eclampsia, and used orally as an osmotic laxative; it is also known as Epsom salt in its hydrated form.

name: magnet
clinical_significance: A magnet produces a magnetic field and is used in some medical devices and imaging systems. Strong magnets can interfere with implanted devices or attract metal objects, so MRI screening and safety procedures are important.

name: magnetic field
clinical_significance: A magnetic field is the region in which magnetic forces act. Strong fields used in MRI can affect some implants and draw ferromagnetic objects, so patients and equipment must be screened before scanning.

name: magnetic resonance imaging
clinical_significance: A scan that uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves to make detailed pictures inside the body without X-rays. It is especially useful for the brain, spinal cord, joints, muscles, and many organs; some scans require injected contrast.

name: magnetoencephalography
clinical_significance: A noninvasive technique that records the weak magnetic fields produced by neuronal electrical activity, using sensors outside the head to localize and study brain function and some epileptic discharges.

name: magnetosomes
clinical_significance: Magnetosomes are membrane-bound magnetic particles made by certain bacteria to help them orient along magnetic fields. They are studied as biological nanoparticles for imaging and targeted delivery, but are not established clinical products.

name: magnusiomyces capitatus
clinical_significance: An opportunistic yeast formerly known as \textit{Geotrichum capitatum} or \textit{Saprochaete capitata}; it can cause invasive infections, especially in people with severe immunosuppression or hematologic malignancy.

name: mahvash disease
clinical_significance: A rare inherited disorder in which the body’s cells do not respond normally to glucagon, a hormone that helps raise blood sugar. It can enlarge the pancreas, increase glucagon levels, and disturb blood-sugar control.

name: maintenance
clinical_significance: Ongoing care or treatment intended to preserve health, prevent relapse or deterioration, or sustain a therapeutic result; maintenance therapy is continued after initial control of a condition.

name: maintenance therapy
clinical_significance: Treatment continued after a disease has improved or been controlled to maintain that benefit, prevent return or worsening, or delay progression. The treatment may be a medicine, procedure, or other care, and its duration depends on the condition, response, risks, and treatment goals.

name: Majeed syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare autoinflammatory disorder caused by LPIN2 variants, characterized by chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, congenital dyserythropoietic anemia, and inflammatory skin disease.

name: Majewski syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited skeletal disorder involving abnormal bone growth and distinctive craniofacial or limb findings; the exact features depend on the genetic subtype.

name: malabsorption
clinical_significance: A condition in which the body cannot properly digest or absorb nutrients from food. It may cause chronic diarrhea, greasy stools, weight loss, anemia, or vitamin and mineral deficiencies.

name: malabsorption syndrome
clinical_significance: Impaired absorption of nutrients from the small intestine, causing diarrhea, weight loss, anemia, vitamin deficiencies, or other nutritional complications.

name: malacoplakia
clinical_significance: A rare long-term inflammation in which immune cells collect mineral deposits. It most often affects the bladder or digestive tract and can form a mass that looks like cancer.

name: malaise
clinical_significance: Malaise is a general feeling of illness, discomfort, or lack of well-being that commonly accompanies infection, inflammation, chronic disease, medication effects, or other systemic conditions.

name: malar rash
clinical_significance: A red or violaceous rash across the cheeks and bridge of the nose, often sparing the folds beside the nose.

name: malaria
clinical_significance: A serious infection caused by \textit{Plasmodium} parasites and spread by infected \textit{Anopheles} mosquitoes. The parasites first multiply in the liver and then enter red blood cells, causing fever, chills, sweating, headache, and weakness. Severe malaria can cause seizures, coma, severe anemia, kidney failure, or breathing problems. Some species can remain in the liver and cause later recurrences.

name: malaria vaccine
clinical_significance: Malaria vaccines RTS,S and R21 are recommended by WHO for preventing Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children living in malaria-endemic areas, particularly where transmission is moderate or high. They provide partial protection and are used alongside other malaria-prevention measures.

name: malassezia
clinical_significance: Malassezia is a yeast normally found on skin that can contribute to dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, pityriasis versicolor, and some folliculitis.

name: malassezia furfur
clinical_significance: Malassezia furfur is a yeast that normally lives on skin but can multiply excessively. It is linked with dandruff, oily skin inflammation, and pityriasis versicolor, which causes lighter or darker patches.

name: malassezia pachydermatis
clinical_significance: Malassezia pachydermatis is a yeast associated mainly with animals and is an uncommon cause of human disease. Rare bloodstream or other infections have occurred, especially in premature infants or immunocompromised people.

name: malate dehydrogenase
clinical_significance: An enzyme in energy-producing pathways that changes malate into oxaloacetate. It helps cells process nutrients and is involved in transferring chemical energy within mitochondria and other cellular compartments.

name: malathion
clinical_significance: An organophosphate insecticide that inhibits acetylcholinesterase; topical formulations have also been used to treat head lice, but exposure or ingestion can cause cholinergic toxicity.

name: male
clinical_significance: Describing a sex associated with reproductive anatomy that produces or is organized around small gametes (sperm); chromosomes, hormones, anatomy, and gender identity do not always fit a simple binary pattern.

name: male condom
clinical_significance: A thin sheath placed over the penis before sexual contact to reduce the risk of pregnancy and transmission of many sexually transmitted infections by acting as a physical barrier.

name: male hypogonadism
clinical_significance: Male hypogonadism is inadequate testosterone production, impaired sperm production, or both due to testicular or pituitary-hypothalamic problems. It can affect sexual function, fertility, muscle and bone health, and development; causes and treatment are assessed with symptoms and hormone testing.

name: male infertility
clinical_significance: Male infertility is difficulty achieving pregnancy due to problems with sperm production, sperm movement, ejaculation, or reproductive anatomy. Evaluation may include semen analysis and assessment of hormonal, genetic, medical, and lifestyle factors.

name: male phenotype
clinical_significance: The observable reproductive anatomy, secondary sex characteristics, and other traits associated with male sex development, produced by interacting genetic, hormonal, and developmental factors and showing natural variation.

name: malignant ameloblastoma
clinical_significance: A rare cancer arising from ameloblastoma-forming tissue, usually in the jaw, with potential to invade locally or spread to distant organs.

name: malignant ascites
clinical_significance: Buildup of fluid in the abdomen caused by cancer involving the abdominal lining or nearby organs. It can cause swelling, discomfort, early fullness, nausea, or breathlessness and may require drainage and cancer-directed treatment.

name: malignant bone neoplasm
clinical_significance: A cancer that begins in bone or nearby supporting tissue. It may cause persistent bone pain, swelling, or a fracture; scans and a biopsy identify the type and extent before treatment.

name: malignant glioma
clinical_significance: An aggressive primary tumor arising from glial or glial-like cells of the central nervous system; high-grade examples include anaplastic astrocytoma and glioblastoma.

name: malignant histiocytosis
clinical_significance: Malignant histiocytosis is an obsolete and imprecise term formerly applied to several distinct lymphoid or histiocytic disorders. Modern pathology uses a specific diagnosis, such as histiocytic sarcoma or lymphoma, because the classification determines treatment.

name: malignant hypertension
clinical_significance: A medical emergency in which very high blood pressure is causing new injury to organs such as the brain, heart, kidneys, or eyes. It can cause headache, confusion, chest pain, breathlessness, vision changes, seizures, or kidney failure.

name: malignant hyperthermia
clinical_significance: A rare, life-threatening reaction to certain anesthetic medicines that causes rapidly rising body temperature, severe muscle stiffness, fast heart rate, and dangerous chemical changes. It affects people with certain inherited susceptibilities.

name: malignant mastocytosis
clinical_significance: An older name for a severe disorder in which abnormal mast cells multiply and collect in organs. It can damage the bone marrow, liver, spleen, or other tissues and may cause flushing, faintness, bleeding, or organ failure.

name: malignant mesothelioma
clinical_significance: A cancer of the thin lining around the lungs, abdomen, or heart. It is strongly linked to asbestos exposure and may cause chest or abdominal pain, fluid buildup, cough, or breathlessness.

name: malignant myoepithelioma
clinical_significance: A rare cancer arising from supportive contractile cells in a gland, most often a salivary gland. It can grow into nearby tissue and spread elsewhere, causing a slowly enlarging or painful mass.

name: malignant thymoma
clinical_significance: An older term for an invasive thymic epithelial tumor; modern usage distinguishes invasive thymoma from thymic carcinoma, which is a separate, more aggressive thymic malignancy.

name: malingering
clinical_significance: Deliberately pretending to have, or exaggerating, symptoms to obtain an outside benefit such as money, medicines, shelter, or avoiding an obligation. It is not itself a mental illness and should not be diagnosed without reliable evidence.

name: malleus
clinical_significance: The largest of the three small bones in the middle ear, also called the hammer. It is attached to the eardrum and passes sound vibrations to the incus and then the inner ear.

name: mallory body
clinical_significance: A clump of damaged proteins inside a liver cell, seen most often in alcohol-related liver disease but also in other liver conditions. It is a laboratory finding, not a diagnosis by itself.

name: malnutrition
clinical_significance: Poor health caused by too little, too much, or an imbalance of nutrients. It can impair growth, immunity, wound healing, muscle function, and organ function and may involve undernutrition, nutrient deficiencies, or excess weight.

name: malocclusion
clinical_significance: A mismatch in the position of the upper and lower teeth or jaws that affects how the teeth meet. It may cause crowding, an overbite, an underbite, difficulty chewing, speech problems, jaw discomfort, or trouble cleaning the teeth.

name: malondialdehyde
clinical_significance: A chemical formed when fats are damaged by oxidation. Laboratory researchers may measure it as an indirect sign of oxidative stress, but the result alone does not diagnose a disease.

name: malposition
clinical_significance: An abnormal position of an organ, body part, implanted device, or fetus; in obstetrics, fetal malposition refers to an abnormal orientation of the presenting part during labor.

name: maltodextrin
clinical_significance: A mixture of short glucose polymers produced by partial hydrolysis of starch, used as a rapidly digestible carbohydrate and as a thickener, filler, or carrier in foods and medicines.

name: maltose
clinical_significance: A reducing disaccharide composed of two glucose molecules joined by an alpha-1,4 glycosidic bond, produced during starch digestion and hydrolyzed by maltase.

name: mammaglobin A
clinical_significance: A secretory protein expressed predominantly in mammary tissue and used as an immunohistochemical marker that can help identify breast origin in some metastatic carcinomas.

name: mammals
clinical_significance: Mammals are a class of animals that includes humans and other species. In medicine, mammalian biology informs anatomy, physiology, and research models, while animal exposure can be relevant to zoonotic disease.

name: mammaplasty
clinical_significance: Surgery to change the size or shape of the breast or to rebuild it after breast removal. It may enlarge, reduce, lift, or reconstruct the breast; possible risks include bleeding, infection, altered sensation, scarring, and problems with healing.

name: mammary disease
clinical_significance: Mammary disease refers broadly to disorders of breast tissue, including benign lumps, inflammation, cysts, and cancer. Evaluation depends on age, symptoms, examination, and imaging; persistent or changing breast findings need assessment.

name: mammary epithelium
clinical_significance: The epithelial lining of the mammary ducts and secretory alveoli; these cells help produce, secrete, and transport milk and can give rise to many breast carcinomas.

name: mammary gland
clinical_significance: The milk-producing gland in the breast. It contains small milk-making lobules connected to ducts that carry milk to the nipple, and its growth and activity are controlled by hormones.

name: mammillary body
clinical_significance: One of a pair of rounded nuclei on the underside of the hypothalamus that participate in memory circuits connecting the hippocampus with the thalamus; injury can contribute to memory impairment.

name: mammography
clinical_significance: Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to screen for breast cancer or evaluate a breast symptom. It can detect cancer before it can be felt, but may also produce false-positive findings or require additional imaging or biopsy.

name: managed care
clinical_significance: Managed care is a system for organizing and paying for healthcare, often using provider networks and rules for referrals or coverage. These rules can affect access, choice, and out-of-pocket costs but do not determine which care is clinically appropriate.

name: mandatory reporting
clinical_significance: A legal or regulatory duty to report specified findings or circumstances—such as suspected child or elder abuse, certain communicable diseases, or some injuries—to designated authorities; requirements vary by jurisdiction.

name: mandible
clinical_significance: The large movable bone forming the lower face and holding the lower teeth. It supports chewing and speech and contains nerves and blood vessels that supply the teeth, gums, and lip.

name: mandibular condyle
clinical_significance: The rounded superior end of each mandibular ramus that articulates with the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint and permits jaw movement.

name: mandibular fracture
clinical_significance: A mandibular fracture is a break in the lower jaw, usually after facial trauma. It can cause pain, swelling, a changed bite, loose teeth, numbness, or trouble opening the mouth; airway and dental or nerve injuries need assessment.

name: mandibular prosthesis
clinical_significance: An artificial implant or device used to replace, reconstruct, stabilize, or restore part of the mandible after trauma, tumor removal, congenital deformity, or other loss of jaw structure.

name: mandibulofacial dysostosis
clinical_significance: A congenital craniofacial disorder, classically Treacher Collins syndrome, involving underdevelopment of the mandible and cheekbones with variable abnormalities of the ears, eyes, and palate.

name: manganese
clinical_significance: An essential trace element required in small amounts. Excessive exposure, especially by inhalation, can injure the nervous system and cause manganism, a movement disorder resembling parkinsonism.

name: manic
clinical_significance: Relating to mania, a pathological episode of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy or activity and associated changes in thought, speech, sleep, or judgment.

name: manic disorder
clinical_significance: Bipolar disorder involves episodes of mania or hypomania and depression; treatment can reduce relapse, impaired function, and suicide risk, with attention to sleep and medication safety.

name: manic mood
clinical_significance: An abnormally elevated, expansive, or persistently irritable mood accompanied by increased energy or activity, reduced need for sleep, rapid speech, racing thoughts, inflated self-esteem, or risky behavior; it is characteristic of a manic episode.

name: manipulation procedure
clinical_significance: Deliberate movement of a body part by a trained clinician to restore motion, alignment, or function. It may be performed with or without anesthesia; soreness, bleeding, nerve injury, fracture, or worsening symptoms are possible depending on the procedure.

name: mannan
clinical_significance: A polysaccharide composed primarily of mannose units, found in the cell walls or capsules of many fungi and in some plants; fungal mannans can be recognized by the immune system and used in laboratory testing.

name: mannheimia
clinical_significance: A genus of gram-negative bacteria that mainly infects livestock, especially the respiratory tract of cattle and sheep.

name: mannheimia haemolytica
clinical_significance: Mannheimia haemolytica is a bacterium that commonly causes severe respiratory disease in cattle and sheep. It is not a common human pathogen, but occupational or animal-exposure context may matter when it is isolated from a patient.

name: mannitol
clinical_significance: A medicine that pulls water into the urine. It is given by injection in selected emergencies to reduce swelling or pressure around the brain or inside the eye and in some kidney-related situations; it can worsen dehydration or heart failure.

name: mannomustine
clinical_significance: Mannomustine is an older alkylating chemotherapy drug that damages DNA and was studied for cancer. It is not a current standard treatment; like related drugs it can suppress bone marrow and increase infection or bleeding risk.

name: mannose
clinical_significance: A six-carbon monosaccharide related to glucose that forms part of glycoproteins and glycolipids and is important in protein glycosylation and cell recognition.

name: mannosidosis
clinical_significance: An inherited lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-mannosidase activity, leading to accumulation of mannose-rich oligosaccharides and variable intellectual, skeletal, immune, hearing, and neurologic abnormalities.

name: manometry
clinical_significance: A test that measures pressure and muscle coordination inside an organ or passage, such as the esophagus, stomach, rectum, or urinary tract. It helps identify movement and sphincter disorders.

name: mansonella perstans
clinical_significance: A filarial worm that causes mansonellosis, usually acquired through bites of infected midges and often producing mild or no symptoms.

name: mansonella streptocerca
clinical_significance: A filarial worm transmitted by biting midges that lives mainly in the skin and can cause itchy skin disease or small nodules.

name: mansonelliasis
clinical_significance: Infection with filarial nematodes of the genus \textit{Mansonella}, transmitted by biting midges or blackflies; many infections are asymptomatic, but some cause itching, skin lesions, fever, or eosinophilia.

name: mantle field
clinical_significance: A historical radiation-treatment field encompassing lymph-node regions in the neck, mediastinum, and upper chest, formerly used for Hodgkin lymphoma; modern treatment generally uses more limited involved-site fields.

name: Mantoux test
clinical_significance: A skin test for immune sensitization to tuberculosis. A small amount of purified protein derivative is injected into the forearm, and the raised area is measured 48 to 72 hours later; a positive result does not by itself prove active disease.

name: manufactured form
clinical_significance: A manufactured form is a prepared version of a substance or medicine, such as a tablet, liquid, or injectable solution. The formulation can affect dose, absorption, storage, and how it is given.

name: MAO inhibitor
clinical_significance: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) are medicines used for selected mood disorders and other conditions. They can interact dangerously with some medicines or tyramine-rich foods, causing serotonin toxicity or severe blood-pressure elevation; restrictions depend on the specific drug.

name: mapatumumab
clinical_significance: Mapatumumab is an investigational antibody that activates the TRAIL-R1 death receptor on cells and was studied as a cancer treatment. Clinical trials did not establish it as standard therapy.

name: maraviroc
clinical_significance: A CCR5 antagonist (entry inhibitor) used in combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1

name: marburgvirus
clinical_significance: A group of filoviruses that includes Marburg virus and Ravn virus, the viruses that cause Marburg virus disease. The disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic fever that can spread from fruit bats to people and between people through direct contact with infected body fluids.

name: Marek's disease
clinical_significance: A contagious herpesvirus disease of chickens that can cause nerve paralysis, tumors, weight loss, or death.

name: Marfan syndrome
clinical_significance: An autosomal dominant connective-tissue disorder usually caused by a disease-causing variant in the \textit{FBN1} gene, which encodes fibrillin-1. It may affect the aortic root and heart valves, eyes, skeleton, joints, lungs, and dura. Features can include aortic-root enlargement, lens dislocation, tall or long-limbed stature, long fingers, scoliosis, chest-wall differences, and joint laxity; the severity varies among individuals.

name: margaric acid
clinical_significance: Margaric acid, also called heptadecanoic acid, is a saturated fatty acid present in small amounts in foods and body lipids. It is studied in nutrition research but is not a diagnostic marker or treatment by itself.

name: marginal ulcer
clinical_significance: An ulcer occurring at or near a gastrojejunal anastomosis, often after gastric bypass or other gastric surgery, where acid, ischemia, smoking, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or other factors may contribute.

name: maribavir
clinical_significance: Maribavir is an antiviral medicine used to treat certain cytomegalovirus infections that are resistant or refractory to other treatment after transplantation.

name: marijuana
clinical_significance: Cannabis preparations containing cannabinoids such as THC; medical effects and risks depend on dose, formulation, route, and patient factors.

name: marijuana abuse
clinical_significance: Marijuana abuse is an outdated term for cannabis use disorder: a pattern of cannabis use that causes impaired control, continued use despite harm, or problems in daily life. Assessment considers symptoms and functioning rather than cannabis use alone.

name: marimastat
clinical_significance: Marimastat is an investigational inhibitor of matrix metalloproteinases studied as a cancer treatment. Trials did not establish a routine clinical benefit, and joint and muscle pain limited its use.

name: marine biology
clinical_significance: Marine biology studies ocean organisms and ecosystems. It can inform public health through research on seafood toxins, marine pathogens, and environmental exposures but has no direct clinical use by itself.

name: marine toxin
clinical_significance: A poisonous substance produced or accumulated by marine organisms, such as some fish, shellfish, algae, or bacteria, that can cause neurologic, gastrointestinal, or other poisoning.

name: marital status
clinical_significance: A demographic or social-status variable describing whether a person is unmarried, married or partnered, separated, divorced, widowed, or in another legally or culturally recognized relationship; it may be relevant to social and health assessments.

name: marital therapy
clinical_significance: Counseling for couples that addresses communication, conflict, emotional distress, intimacy, and relationship problems. It may help partners improve interaction and make informed decisions about their relationship.

name: marked
clinical_significance: Pronounced, conspicuous, or substantially greater than usual; in a clinical report, the exact meaning depends on the finding and the comparison standard.

name: married
clinical_significance: Marital status is a social and demographic characteristic that may be relevant to support systems or social-health research. It does not establish a person’s health, family support, or decision-making authority.

name: Marshall syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare periodic-fever syndrome, usually associated with PFAPA features, including recurrent fever, aphthous ulcers, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis, often beginning in childhood.

name: mask
clinical_significance: A device placed over the face to deliver oxygen, anesthesia, ventilation, or protection; the meaning depends on clinical context.

name: masked data
clinical_significance: Data altered, obscured, or replaced so that identifying values or sensitive details are hidden while selected analytical properties may be retained; masking is used to protect privacy and can be reversible or irreversible.

name: masoprocol
clinical_significance: A synthetic derivative of nordihydroguaiaretic acid that inhibits lipoxygenase pathways and has been investigated for topical treatment of actinic keratoses and for antineoplastic activity.

name: mass screening
clinical_significance: Testing a large group of people who do not yet have symptoms to find disease or risk early. A useful screening program has a suitable test, an effective follow-up pathway, and benefits that outweigh harms.

name: mass spectrometer
clinical_significance: A laboratory instrument that identifies chemicals by giving their particles an electrical charge and separating them according to size and charge. It can measure medicines, toxins, proteins, and other substances.

name: mass spectrometry
clinical_significance: An analytical method that identifies and measures molecules by their mass-to-charge ratios; coupled with chromatography, it is widely used in clinical chemistry, toxicology, pharmacology, and proteomics.

name: massage
clinical_significance: Manual manipulation of soft tissues using techniques such as stroking, kneading, or pressure, used for relaxation or symptom relief; it is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment of an underlying disease.

name: massage therapy
clinical_significance: Massage therapy uses hands-on manipulation of soft tissues to promote relaxation or help manage selected pain and movement problems.

name: masseter muscle
clinical_significance: A strong chewing muscle running from the cheekbone to the lower jaw. It raises the jaw to close the mouth and may become painful or enlarged with teeth grinding.

name: mast cell
clinical_significance: An immune cell found in tissues that releases substances involved in allergy, inflammation, and defense against some germs. Its products can cause itching, swelling, mucus production, and changes in blood pressure.

name: mast-cell sarcoma
clinical_significance: An extremely rare cancer made of abnormal mast cells, immune cells involved in allergic and inflammatory reactions.

name: mastectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove breast tissue from one or both breasts, usually to treat or prevent selected breast cancers. Most mastectomies remove nearly all breast tissue; whether the nipple, areola, skin, or nearby lymph nodes are removed depends on the type. A lumpectomy removes a tumor or abnormal area while leaving most of the breast in place.

name: masticate
clinical_significance: To chew food, using the teeth, tongue, and muscles of mastication to mechanically break it down and mix it with saliva before swallowing.

name: masticatory muscle
clinical_significance: One of the muscles that moves the mandible during chewing, chiefly the masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid, and lateral pterygoid muscles.

name: mastitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of breast tissue, often occurring during lactation but also possible outside lactation. It may cause localized pain, warmth, swelling, redness, or fever. It may be infectious or noninfectious.

name: mastocytoma
clinical_significance: A localized collection or tumor of mast cells, usually presenting in the skin as a solitary cutaneous mastocytoma; rubbing the lesion can cause itching, redness, or swelling from mediator release.

name: mastocytosis
clinical_significance: A disorder in which too many mast cells, immune cells involved in allergic reactions, collect in the skin or internal organs. It may cause itchy spots, flushing, abdominal symptoms, wheezing, or low blood pressure.

name: mastodynia
clinical_significance: Pain or tenderness in one or both breasts, also called mastalgia. It may follow the menstrual cycle or result from injury, infection, medicines, cysts, or other breast conditions; a new persistent lump, skin change, or bloody discharge may indicate another breast problem.

name: mastoid process
clinical_significance: The conical bony projection of the temporal bone behind the ear, containing air cells and providing attachment for several neck muscles; infection of its air cells is mastoiditis.

name: mastoidectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove infected or diseased air cells in the bone behind the ear. It may treat chronic middle-ear infection, cholesteatoma, mastoiditis, or complications that have spread beyond the ear.

name: mastoiditis
clinical_significance: Mastoiditis is infection and inflammation of the mastoid air cells behind the ear, usually following middle-ear infection and potentially causing serious spread.

name: mastopexy
clinical_significance: Breast-lift surgery that removes extra skin and reshapes breast tissue to raise the breasts and nipples. It can improve shape but does not necessarily reduce breast size; scars, altered sensation, asymmetry, and changes in breastfeeding ability are possible risks.

name: masturbation
clinical_significance: Masturbation is common sexual behavior and is generally not harmful. It may merit clinical discussion if it causes injury, distress, interferes with daily life, or occurs in a way that raises safety concerns.

name: material
clinical_significance: A material is a substance or matter used in a product, device, implant, or laboratory sample. In healthcare, its properties can affect biocompatibility, durability, sterilization, test results, or risk of allergy.

name: maternal
clinical_significance: Maternal means relating to a mother or the pregnant person, especially in connection with pregnancy, childbirth, or postpartum health.

name: maternal age
clinical_significance: Maternal age is the age of the pregnant person and can influence fertility, pregnancy risks, screening choices, and obstetric care.

name: maternal mortality
clinical_significance: Maternal mortality is death during pregnancy or within the defined postpartum period from a pregnancy-related cause, measured as a population health indicator.

name: maternal obesity
clinical_significance: Obesity present before or during pregnancy. It can increase the risk of high blood pressure, diabetes, cesarean birth, and health problems for the pregnant person or baby.

name: maternal sepsis
clinical_significance: Maternal sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by infection during pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period. It can progress quickly and requires urgent recognition, antibiotics, and supportive treatment.

name: mathematics
clinical_significance: Mathematics supports clinical measurement, statistics, dose calculation, and analysis of health data. Errors in calculations can affect medicine dosing and interpretation of test results.

name: mating
clinical_significance: Sexual pairing or reproduction between organisms that permits exchange or transfer of gametes and may lead to fertilization.

name: matrix band
clinical_significance: A thin dental strip placed around a prepared tooth to temporarily replace a missing wall and contain restorative material while a filling or crown buildup is formed.

name: matrix metalloproteinase
clinical_significance: An enzyme that cuts proteins in the extracellular matrix surrounding cells. It helps with normal tissue repair and remodeling, but excessive or poorly controlled activity can promote inflammation, tissue destruction, or cancer spread.

name: mature teratoma
clinical_significance: A germ-cell tumor composed of well-differentiated tissues from one or more embryonic germ layers; many are benign, but behavior depends on the site, age, and tumor type, and some can undergo malignant transformation.

name: matuzumab
clinical_significance: Matuzumab is an investigational antibody that blocks the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and was studied for solid tumors. It is not an established cancer treatment.

name: maxilla
clinical_significance: The paired bones forming the upper jaw and supporting the upper teeth. They also form parts of the cheeks, nose, eye sockets, hard palate, and the air-filled sinuses behind the cheeks.

name: maxillary sinus
clinical_significance: The maxillary sinus is a paired, air-filled cavity in the maxilla beneath each orbit. It drains into the nasal cavity and may become inflamed or infected in sinusitis.

name: maxillary sinusitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation or infection of the air-filled spaces behind the cheekbones. It may cause cheek or tooth pain, blocked nose, thick nasal discharge, reduced smell, cough, or fever and can follow a cold, allergy, or dental infection.

name: maximum
clinical_significance: The maximum is the greatest value in a set of measurements or the highest level reached by a variable, such as a recorded temperature, blood pressure, or drug concentration.

name: maximum thickness
clinical_significance: Maximum thickness is the greatest measured thickness of a structure or specimen. It may be reported in imaging, pathology, or assessment of a lesion, organ, or tissue layer.

name: maytansine
clinical_significance: Maytansine is a potent antimitotic compound that binds tubulin and inhibits microtubule assembly. Its derivatives are used as cytotoxic payloads in some antibody--drug conjugates.

name: mazindol
clinical_significance: Mazindol is a sympathomimetic appetite suppressant that affects central catecholamine signaling. It has been used for short-term obesity treatment in some countries and may cause stimulant-related adverse effects.

name: mcc gene
clinical_significance: A gene that helps regulate cell growth and is considered a tumour-suppressor gene. Loss or alteration of its function has been found in some colorectal and other cancers, but the finding alone does not diagnose cancer.

name: MCF-7 cell
clinical_significance: MCF-7 is a human breast-cancer cell line used in laboratory research on tumor biology, drug response, and hormone signaling. Results from this cell model do not by themselves predict an individual patient’s response.

name: mead acid
clinical_significance: An omega-9 fatty acid made when the body lacks enough essential omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids. Increased levels can support laboratory assessment of essential-fatty-acid deficiency, although results must be interpreted with nutrition and illness history.

name: mean
clinical_significance: The mean is the arithmetic average, calculated by adding all values and dividing by the number of values. It is commonly used to summarize clinical measurements but can be distorted by extreme values.

name: mean diameter
clinical_significance: Mean diameter is the average diameter of a structure or lesion, usually calculated from one or more measured dimensions. The method used should be specified when measurements are clinically compared.

name: mean thickness
clinical_significance: Mean thickness is the average thickness calculated from multiple measurements of a tissue, structure, or specimen. It is used in imaging, pathology, and physiologic measurements.

name: measles
clinical_significance: A highly contagious viral infection causing fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and a rash that spreads from the face downward. It can cause pneumonia, brain inflammation, or other serious complications.

name: measles vaccine
clinical_significance: The measles vaccine is given as part of the MMR vaccine, which protects against measles, mumps, and rubella. Vaccination is the main way to prevent measles; dose recommendations depend on age, immunity, and exposure risk.

name: measles virus
clinical_significance: A negative-sense RNA virus that causes measles, a highly contagious respiratory illness.

name: measurement
clinical_significance: Measurement is the quantitative determination of a physical, biologic, or clinical characteristic using a defined method and unit. Interpretation depends on accuracy, precision, and the clinical context.

name: mebendazole
clinical_significance: A medicine used to treat several intestinal worm infections. It disrupts structures the worms need to absorb nutrients and survive; treatment choices and dosing depend on the parasite, age, pregnancy, and local guidance.

name: mecamylamine
clinical_significance: Mecamylamine is an orally active ganglionic nicotinic-receptor blocker that reduces sympathetic nerve transmission and lowers blood pressure. It has been used for severe hypertension and may cause postural hypotension, dizziness, constipation, and dry mouth.

name: mecarzole
clinical_significance: Mecarzole is a synonym for carbendazim, a benzimidazole fungicide that interferes with fungal microtubule formation. It is an agricultural chemical rather than a routine human medicine and may be toxic if exposure occurs.

name: mechanical ventilation
clinical_significance: Breathing support from a machine that pushes air and oxygen into the lungs and helps remove carbon dioxide. It may be delivered through a mask or a breathing tube when illness or injury prevents adequate breathing.

name: mechanical ventilator
clinical_significance: A mechanical ventilator is a machine that supports or replaces spontaneous breathing by delivering controlled or assisted breaths, usually through a mask or an endotracheal tube. Settings are adjusted to oxygenation, ventilation, mechanics, and patient needs.

name: mechanoreceptor
clinical_significance: A sensory receptor that detects physical forces such as touch, pressure, stretch, vibration, sound, or movement. It converts mechanical stimulation into electrical signals carried by nerves to the brain or spinal cord.

name: mechlorethamine
clinical_significance: Mechlorethamine is an alkylating antineoplastic agent that cross-links DNA and inhibits cell division. Topical gel is used for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; systemic use is limited by toxicities such as myelosuppression and tissue injury.

name: meckel diverticulum
clinical_significance: A small pouch present from birth on the lower small intestine, caused by a leftover connection from early development. It often causes no symptoms, but it can bleed, become inflamed, or cause blockage or twisting of the bowel. A Meckel scan may help find it when bleeding is suspected; treatment depends on symptoms and complications.

name: meclizine
clinical_significance: Meclizine is a first-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic and vestibular-suppressant effects. It is used to prevent or treat motion sickness and vertigo and may cause drowsiness, dry mouth, and blurred vision.

name: meconium ileus
clinical_significance: A blockage of a newborn’s small intestine by unusually thick first stool. It is strongly associated with cystic fibrosis and may cause a swollen abdomen, green vomiting, and failure to pass stool soon after birth.

name: meconium peritonitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the tissue lining a fetus’s abdomen after a hole in the intestine allows first stool to escape before birth. It can cause abdominal fluid or calcium deposits and may be linked to bowel blockage or cystic fibrosis.

name: medial
clinical_significance: Medial means toward or situated nearer the body's midline; it contrasts with lateral and is used to describe anatomical position, movement, or imaging findings.

name: medial meniscus
clinical_significance: The medial meniscus is a crescent-shaped fibrocartilage pad between the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. It distributes load and contributes to knee stability; tears may cause joint-line pain, swelling, or locking.

name: median
clinical_significance: Located in or relating to the middle plane or midpoint of a structure. In medicine, it describes anatomy, measurements, statistical values, nerve positions, or locations between two sides.

name: median nerve
clinical_significance: A major nerve running from the neck through the arm and forearm to the hand. It helps bend the wrist and fingers, moves the thumb, and provides feeling to the thumb, index, middle, and part of the ring finger; compression can cause carpal-tunnel symptoms.

name: mediastinal cyst
clinical_significance: A mediastinal cyst is a fluid- or tissue-filled cystic lesion in the mediastinum. Common types include bronchogenic, thymic, and pericardial cysts; symptoms depend on size and compression, and imaging guides evaluation.

name: mediastinal disease
clinical_significance: A disorder affecting structures in the mediastinum, including the heart, great vessels, thymus, lymph nodes, nerves, and tumors or cysts within the central chest.

name: Mediastinal Emphysema
clinical_significance: Mediastinal emphysema, or pneumomediastinum, is the presence of free air in the mediastinum. It can follow alveolar rupture, trauma, surgery, or esophageal injury and may cause chest pain, neck crepitus, or respiratory compromise.

name: mediastinal hemorrhage
clinical_significance: Bleeding into the mediastinum, commonly caused by trauma, vascular rupture, surgery, or invasive procedures, and potentially causing airway or cardiovascular compression.

name: mediastinal mass
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth or collection of tissue in the mediastinum, the central compartment of the chest. Causes include tumors, enlarged lymph nodes, cysts, and vascular abnormalities.

name: mediastinal neoplasm
clinical_significance: A mediastinal neoplasm is an abnormal growth in the central space of the chest between the lungs; it may arise from lymph nodes, thymus, nerves, or other tissues.

name: mediastinal pleura
clinical_significance: The mediastinal pleura is the portion of parietal pleura lining the lateral surfaces of the mediastinum. It separates the mediastinal contents from the pleural cavity and reflects around the lung root.

name: mediastinal shift
clinical_significance: Mediastinal shift is displacement of the mediastinal structures away from their usual position. It may result from increased pressure on one side, such as a tension pneumothorax, or loss of volume on the other, such as lung collapse.

name: mediastinitis
clinical_significance: Mediastinitis is inflammation or infection of the central chest compartment, often after esophageal rupture, surgery, trauma, or spread of infection.

name: mediastinoscopes
clinical_significance: Mediastinoscopes are slender endoscopic instruments used during mediastinoscopy to inspect the mediastinum and obtain tissue samples, especially from mediastinal lymph nodes. The procedure is performed through a small incision near the sternum.

name: mediastinoscopy
clinical_significance: Mediastinoscopy is a procedure that uses a scope inserted through a small incision above the breastbone to examine the mediastinum and sample lymph nodes or masses. It can help diagnose or stage cancer and investigate infection; bleeding, infection, or injury to nearby structures can occur.

name: mediastinum
clinical_significance: The central part of the chest between the lungs. It contains the heart, major blood vessels, windpipe, food pipe, thymus, nerves, and lymph nodes.

name: medicaid
clinical_significance: Medicaid is a U.S. public health-coverage program for people who meet applicable income and other eligibility rules. Coverage can affect access to preventive, diagnostic, and treatment services; eligibility and benefits vary by state.

name: medical device
clinical_significance: An instrument, implant, machine, software program, or other product used to diagnose, prevent, monitor, or treat disease or injury. Examples include pacemakers, syringes, imaging equipment, and blood-glucose meters.

name: medical economics
clinical_significance: Medical economics studies the costs, financing, and distribution of healthcare. It informs decisions about access, resource use, and coverage but does not determine the best clinical choice for an individual by itself.

name: medical history
clinical_significance: A medical history is a structured account of a person’s current concerns, past illnesses and operations, medications, allergies, family history, social history, and relevant exposures. It helps guide examination, diagnosis, and treatment.

name: medical indigency
clinical_significance: Medical indigency refers to inability to afford necessary healthcare. Financial barriers can delay diagnosis or treatment and are considered in care planning and social-service support.

name: medical pin
clinical_significance: A medical pin is a slender metal fixation device inserted into bone or across a joint to stabilize a fracture or support orthopedic treatment. Pins may be temporary or permanent and require monitoring for infection and displacement.

name: medical record
