name: microsphere
clinical_significance: A microsphere is a small spherical particle, often made of polymer, glass, or another material, used in drug delivery, imaging, embolization, or laboratory assays. Its size, composition, and surface properties determine its biologic behavior.

name: microspherophakia
clinical_significance: Microspherophakia is an abnormally small, spherical crystalline lens. It can occur in inherited disorders such as Weill--Marchesani syndrome and may cause lens displacement, pupillary block, angle-closure glaucoma, or reduced vision.

name: microsporidia
clinical_significance: A group of microscopic spore-forming organisms related to fungi. They can cause prolonged diarrhea, eye disease, muscle disease, or widespread infection, especially in people with weakened immune systems.

name: microsporidiosis
clinical_significance: An infection caused by microsporidia, microscopic organisms related to fungi that produce resistant spores. It most often affects the intestine and may cause long-lasting diarrhea and weight loss. It can also affect the eyes, muscles, kidneys, brain, or several organs, especially in people with weakened immune systems.

name: microsporum
clinical_significance: Microsporum is a genus of dermatophyte fungi that can cause ringworm of the skin, scalp, or hair.

name: microsporum audouinii
clinical_significance: Microsporum audouinii is a dermatophyte that mainly infects the scalp and can cause tinea capitis, especially in children.

name: microsporum distortum
clinical_significance: Microsporum distortum is a rare dermatophyte related to M. canis that can cause skin or scalp infection.

name: microsporum equinum
clinical_significance: Microsporum equinum is a dermatophyte mainly associated with ringworm in horses. Human infection is uncommon; a compatible rash or hair/scalp infection is confirmed by appropriate fungal testing.

name: microsporum ferrugineum
clinical_significance: A fungus that can cause ringworm of the scalp or skin, particularly in children. Laboratory examination can help confirm the infection and distinguish it from other causes of rash or hair loss.

name: microsporum gypseum
clinical_significance: Microsporum gypseum is a soil-associated dermatophyte that can cause ringworm of the skin or scalp.

name: microstomia
clinical_significance: Microstomia is abnormal narrowing or smallness of the mouth opening. It may be congenital or result from scarring, burns, surgery, trauma, or connective-tissue disease and can impair eating, speech, oral hygiene, and dental treatment.

name: microsurgery
clinical_significance: Microsurgery uses magnification and very small instruments to operate on delicate structures such as blood vessels, nerves, the eye, or lymphatic vessels. It can restore function in selected conditions, but success and risks depend on the site and procedure.

name: microtechnology
clinical_significance: Microtechnology is the design and manufacture of devices or structures with micrometer-scale features. Medical applications include microfluidic diagnostics, sensors, drug-delivery systems, and minimally invasive instruments.

name: microtubule
clinical_significance: A tiny hollow protein tube inside a cell. Microtubules help maintain cell shape, move materials within the cell, support cell division, and form part of cilia and other moving structures.

name: microtubule bundle
clinical_significance: A microtubule bundle is an organized group of parallel or otherwise coordinated microtubules within a cell. Bundles provide structural support and guide transport or movement, including in axons, cilia, and dividing cells.

name: microvillus
clinical_significance: A microvillus is a microscopic, actin-supported projection of a cell membrane that increases surface area. Microvilli are abundant on intestinal epithelial cells, where they support nutrient absorption, and on renal tubular cells.

name: microvolt
clinical_significance: A microvolt ($\mu$V) is one-millionth of a volt. It is used to express small bioelectric signals, such as those recorded by electroencephalography, electromyography, electrocardiography, or evoked-potential testing.

name: microwave therapy
clinical_significance: Treatment that uses microwave energy to heat or destroy selected tissue. It has specialized uses, such as treating some tumors or controlling bleeding, and the risks depend on the body area and device used.

name: microwell plate
clinical_significance: A microwell plate is a small-well tray used to run multiple laboratory assays at once. It supports diagnostic and research testing, but results depend on validated reagents, controls, and interpretation.

name: midazolam
clinical_significance: Midazolam is a short-acting benzodiazepine used for procedural sedation, anesthesia, and treatment of acute seizures in appropriate settings. It enhances GABA-A receptor activity and can cause profound sedation and respiratory depression, especially with opioids or other depressants.

name: midazolam hydrochloride
clinical_significance: Midazolam hydrochloride is the hydrochloride salt of the short-acting benzodiazepine midazolam. It is used for procedural sedation, anesthesia, and selected seizure emergencies and can cause dose-related sedation, hypotension, and respiratory depression.

name: middle ear
clinical_significance: The middle ear is an air-filled space behind the eardrum that contains three small bones transmitting sound to the inner ear. Infection or fluid buildup can cause pain, temporary hearing loss, and, rarely, complications beyond the ear.

name: middle insomnia
clinical_significance: Middle insomnia is repeated or prolonged awakening during the middle portion of the sleep period, often with difficulty returning to sleep. It may occur with stress, mood disorders, sleep apnea, pain, substances, medications, or other sleep disorders.

name: midodrine
clinical_significance: Midodrine is a medicine that tightens blood vessels and raises blood pressure when standing in selected cases of symptomatic orthostatic hypotension. It can cause high blood pressure while lying down, so dosing and monitoring require care.

name: midomafetamine
clinical_significance: Midomafetamine is another name for 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, a psychoactive amphetamine derivative. It is being studied in controlled psychotherapy-assisted research but can cause hyperthermia, hyponatremia, cardiovascular toxicity, serotonin toxicity, and misuse.

name: midostaurin
clinical_significance: Midostaurin is a multikinase inhibitor used with chemotherapy for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia with a susceptible FLT3 mutation and for advanced systemic mastocytosis. It can cause nausea, cytopenias, infection, and other treatment-related toxicities.

name: mifepristone
clinical_significance: Mifepristone is a progesterone-receptor antagonist and, at higher doses, a glucocorticoid-receptor antagonist. It is used with misoprostol for medication abortion under applicable protocols and for selected cases of hyperglycemia associated with Cushing syndrome.

name: migraine
clinical_significance: Migraine is a recurrent neurologic disorder causing attacks of moderate-to-severe headache, often with nausea and sensitivity to light or sound. Some people have a temporary aura. Effective acute and preventive treatments are available, and a sudden severe or unusual headache needs urgent assessment.

name: Mikulicz disease
clinical_significance: Mikulicz disease is a historically inconsistent term for persistent, often painless enlargement of the tear and salivary glands. It is now often described as IgG4-related dacryoadenitis and sialadenitis, but similar swelling can have other causes, including Sjögren disease or lymphoma, so diagnosis requires evaluation.

name: milatuzumab
clinical_significance: Milatuzumab is an investigational antibody targeting CD74, a protein expressed on some B cells and blood cancers. It has been studied for lymphoma and multiple myeloma but is not an established treatment.

name: mild
clinical_significance: Mild describes relatively low intensity, severity, or extent of a symptom, sign, disease, or abnormality. The meaning depends on the condition and the clinical scale used and does not by itself indicate that no treatment or evaluation is needed.

name: mile
clinical_significance: A mile is a unit of distance equal to 1,609.344 meters. It may be used in descriptions of walking or running distance, although scientific and clinical measurements generally use SI units.

name: milia
clinical_significance: Milia are tiny, firm, white or yellow bumps caused by small cysts containing keratin, a protein in the skin. They are common in newborns and may appear on the face in adults; they are harmless and usually go away on their own.

name: miliaria
clinical_significance: A sweat-retention disorder caused by blockage of eccrine ducts, producing small itchy or prickly papules.

name: milieu therapy
clinical_significance: Milieu therapy uses the structured social environment of a treatment setting as part of care, especially in some psychiatric and rehabilitation programs.

name: military personnel
clinical_significance: Military personnel may face occupational health risks such as combat injury, noise exposure, infectious disease, toxic exposures, sleep disruption, and psychological trauma. These are population-health concerns and do not imply a diagnosis for an individual.

name: milk
clinical_significance: Milk provides fluid, protein, fat, and micronutrients and may be an important food, especially during infancy. Cow’s-milk protein allergy and lactose intolerance are distinct conditions; infant feeding choices should account for age and nutritional needs.

name: millicurie
clinical_significance: A millicurie (mCi) is one-thousandth of a curie, equal to approximately 37 megabecquerels. It is used to express the activity of radioactive sources and some radiopharmaceutical doses.

name: milligram
clinical_significance: A metric unit of mass equal to one-thousandth of a gram. Its abbreviation is mg, and it is commonly used for medicine doses and small quantities of substances.

name: milliliter
clinical_significance: A unit of volume equal to one-thousandth of a liter and one cubic centimeter. It is commonly used to measure liquid medicines, blood, urine, laboratory samples, and other small amounts of fluid.

name: millimeter
clinical_significance: A millimeter is used in imaging, pathology, and physical examination to document lesion size; small measurement differences can affect growth assessment and treatment decisions.

name: millimole
clinical_significance: A unit measuring the amount of a chemical substance equal to one-thousandth of a mole. Laboratory tests use millimoles to report substances such as glucose, sodium, potassium, and other electrolytes.

name: milliosmole
clinical_significance: A milliosmole (mOsm) is one-thousandth of an osmole, a unit reflecting the number of osmotically active particles in a solution. Osmolality and osmolarity are commonly reported in mOsm/kg or mOsm/L.

name: millisecond
clinical_significance: A millisecond (ms) is one-thousandth of a second. It is used to measure brief physiologic events, reaction times, nerve conduction intervals, and timing of electrical or imaging signals.

name: milliunit
clinical_significance: A milliunit (mU) is one-thousandth of a unit of biologic or enzymatic activity. Because a unit is defined according to the substance or assay, the clinical meaning of a milliunit depends on the specific test or medication.

name: millivolt
clinical_significance: A unit of electrical voltage equal to one-thousandth of a volt. Small voltages are measured in millivolts in tests of the heart, brain, nerves, muscles, and other electrical activity in the body.

name: Milroy disease
clinical_significance: Milroy disease is an inherited primary lymphedema that usually causes swelling of one or both feet and lower legs from birth or early childhood. It is often associated with FLT4 variants; swelling can persist and may lead to skin changes or infection.

name: mindfulness
clinical_significance: Mindfulness is a practice of paying attention to present experience with openness and without immediate judgment. It may support stress management and wellbeing, but effects vary and it does not replace needed mental-health or medical care.

name: mineral
clinical_significance: An inorganic element or compound required for body structure, fluid balance, enzyme activity, or other physiological functions.

name: mineral oil
clinical_significance: Mineral oil is a purified mixture of liquid hydrocarbons derived from petroleum. It is used in some topical products, cosmetics, and laxatives; aspiration of liquid mineral oil can cause lipoid pneumonia.

name: mineralocorticoid
clinical_significance: A steroid hormone, mainly aldosterone, that helps the kidneys retain sodium and water while removing potassium. Too much can raise blood pressure and lower potassium; too little can cause dehydration and weakness.

name: minisatellite repeat
clinical_significance: A minisatellite repeat is a tandemly repeated DNA sequence with repeat units commonly ranging from about 10 to 100 base pairs. Variation in repeat number can serve as a genetic marker and, in some loci, influence gene regulation or disease risk.

name: minor response
clinical_significance: A minor response is a limited improvement after treatment that does not meet the predefined criteria for a partial or complete response. The exact threshold depends on the disease, study protocol, and outcome being measured.

name: minority health
clinical_significance: The health status and healthcare experiences of populations affected by social, economic, cultural, or structural disadvantage. Differences in exposure, income, environment, discrimination, and access to care can contribute to health disparities.

name: minoxidil
clinical_significance: A vasodilator used topically for pattern hair loss and orally in selected cases of resistant hypertension.

name: minretumomab
clinical_significance: Minretumomab is an investigational antibody directed against the tumor-associated antigen TAG-72 and was studied for cancer imaging or radioimmunotherapy. It did not become a standard cancer treatment.

name: miosis disorder
clinical_significance: Abnormally small pupils or an abnormal pupillary constriction response, caused by medications, neurologic disease, ocular disease, or exposure to certain toxins.

name: miotic
clinical_significance: A medicine or substance that makes the pupil smaller. Miotics may be used in glaucoma or during some eye procedures and can affect vision in dim light.

name: mirage syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare genetic disorder, usually related to SAMD9 variants, that can cause growth restriction, adrenal insufficiency, recurrent infections, and distinctive developmental findings.

name: mirex
clinical_significance: Mirex is a persistent organochlorine pesticide that can accumulate in soil, water, and body fat. Exposure is mainly an environmental or occupational concern; toxicology studies raise health concerns, while data on effects in people are limited.

name: mirtazapine
clinical_significance: Mirtazapine is a noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant used for major depressive disorder. It commonly causes sedation and increased appetite or weight and can rarely cause neutropenia or other serious adverse effects.

name: misalignment
clinical_significance: Misalignment is abnormal positioning or orientation of two or more structures relative to their intended relationship. It may affect bones, joints, teeth, eyes, implants, or medical devices and can impair function or healing.

name: miscarriage
clinical_significance: Spontaneous loss of a pregnancy before fetal viability, commonly caused by chromosomal abnormalities but requiring clinical assessment.

name: misdiagnosis
clinical_significance: Misdiagnosis is assignment of an incorrect diagnosis or failure to recognize the correct condition. It can lead to inappropriate treatment, delayed care, avoidable harm, or unnecessary testing and may result from atypical presentation, incomplete information, or system factors.

name: mismatch repair
clinical_significance: A system that checks newly copied DNA and corrects small errors. When it fails, genetic changes can accumulate and increase the risk of cancers such as colorectal and womb cancer.

name: misonidazole
clinical_significance: Misonidazole is an experimental radiosensitizer that was studied to make oxygen-poor tumor cells more responsive to radiation. Peripheral nerve toxicity and other adverse effects limited its clinical use, and it is not a standard cancer treatment.

name: misoprostol
clinical_significance: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin medicine used for several purposes, including prevention of NSAID-related stomach ulcers and, under clinical protocols, cervical ripening, labor care, miscarriage management, or abortion. It can cause uterine contractions, bleeding, fever, and diarrhea; the correct use depends on the indication and pregnancy status.

name: missed dose
clinical_significance: A missed dose is a scheduled dose of a medicine that was not taken or administered. The appropriate response depends on the drug and timing; doubling a dose can be dangerous, so the product instructions or a clinician or pharmacist should guide the next dose.

name: missense mutation
clinical_significance: A missense mutation is a DNA sequence change that substitutes one amino acid for another in a protein. Its effect may be harmful, beneficial, or neutral depending on the affected residue, protein function, and genetic context.

name: mite
clinical_significance: A tiny arachnid; some mites cause dermatitis or transmit disease, and house-dust mites can trigger allergy.

name: mithramycin
clinical_significance: An older antineoplastic antibiotic, also called plicamycin, whose use is limited by substantial toxicity.

name: mitigate
clinical_significance: To mitigate a risk or effect is to reduce its likelihood or severity. In healthcare, mitigation may include prevention, monitoring, dose adjustment, or other steps tailored to the specific risk.

name: mitobronitol
clinical_significance: Mitobronitol is an alkylating antineoplastic compound formerly investigated or used in selected hematologic malignancies. Its cytotoxic effects can damage DNA and cause myelosuppression and other treatment-related toxicities.

name: mitochondrial cristae
clinical_significance: Folds of the inner membrane of mitochondria, the energy-producing parts of cells. The folds provide space for the machinery that turns nutrients into usable cellular energy.

name: mitochondrial disease
clinical_significance: Mitochondrial disease is a group of disorders in which impaired mitochondrial energy production affects one or more organs. Symptoms can include muscle weakness, fatigue, seizures, vision or hearing loss, and heart or digestive problems; severity and inheritance vary widely.

name: mitochondrial DNA
clinical_significance: Small circular DNA molecules located primarily in mitochondria that encode some components of oxidative phosphorylation and are inherited predominantly through the maternal line.

name: mitochondrial fission
clinical_significance: Mitochondrial fission is division of one mitochondrion into two or more mitochondria. It helps distribute mitochondria, remove damaged portions through mitophagy, and respond to cell-cycle or metabolic signals; excessive fission may contribute to disease.

name: mitochondrial fusion
clinical_significance: Mitochondrial fusion is joining of mitochondria into a connected network. It permits exchange of mitochondrial contents and helps maintain bioenergetic function and genome integrity; fusion and fission are normally balanced dynamically.

name: mitochondrial inheritance
clinical_significance: Mitochondrial inheritance usually refers to transmission of mitochondrial DNA through the egg, so affected mothers may pass a variant to their children while affected fathers generally do not transmit it. Heteroplasmy can make severity and risk vary among relatives.

name: mitochondrial matrix
clinical_significance: The mitochondrial matrix is the protein-rich compartment enclosed by the inner mitochondrial membrane. It contains mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, and enzymes for the citric-acid cycle, fatty-acid oxidation, and other metabolic processes.

name: mitochondrial membrane
clinical_significance: The mitochondrial membrane system consists of an outer membrane and a highly folded inner membrane separated by an intermembrane space. It controls transport and houses the respiratory chain and ATP-producing machinery.

name: mitochondrial myopathy
clinical_significance: A muscle disorder caused by faulty mitochondria, the cell structures that make energy. It may cause weakness, exercise intolerance, drooping eyelids, hearing loss, seizures, or problems in other organs.

name: mitochondrial ribosome
clinical_significance: A mitochondrial ribosome is a ribosome within mitochondria that translates proteins encoded by mitochondrial DNA. Its structure differs from cytosolic ribosomes and defects in mitochondrial translation can cause energy-production disorders.

name: mitochondrial swelling
clinical_significance: Enlargement of mitochondria caused by disruption of ion and water balance, often indicating cellular injury, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, or permeability-transition changes.

name: mitochondrion
clinical_significance: A mitochondrion is a membrane-bound organelle that generates much of a cell’s ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. It also participates in apoptosis, calcium handling, metabolism, and production or regulation of reactive oxygen species.

name: mitogen
clinical_significance: A mitogen is a substance that stimulates a cell, especially a lymphocyte, to enter the cell cycle and proliferate. Mitogens include growth factors, lectins, and other signals that activate proliferative pathways.

name: mitoguazone
clinical_significance: Mitoguazone is an investigational anticancer drug that inhibits polyamine production, a pathway needed for cell growth. It was studied for lymphoma and other cancers but is not an established standard treatment.

name: mitolactol
clinical_significance: Mitolactol is an alkylating antineoplastic compound formerly used or investigated in cancer treatment. It damages DNA and can cause cytotoxic effects such as myelosuppression and gastrointestinal toxicity.

name: mitomycin
clinical_significance: Mitomycin is a chemotherapy medicine that damages DNA and is used for selected cancers; it can suppress bone marrow and injure the kidneys or bladder.

name: mitomycins
clinical_significance: Mitomycins are antitumor antibiotics that become activated in cells and cross-link DNA, inhibiting replication and transcription. Mitomycin C is the best-known member and is used in selected cancers and ophthalmic or surgical applications.

name: mitophagy
clinical_significance: The process by which a cell identifies and breaks down damaged or unnecessary mitochondria, the cell's energy-producing structures. This helps maintain healthy cells; abnormal mitophagy may contribute to some diseases.

name: mitosis
clinical_significance: Cell division that produces two genetically similar daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent

name: mitosporic fungi
clinical_significance: Fungi that reproduce by asexual spores; the term is mainly used for fungi whose sexual stage is unknown or not observed.

name: mitotane
clinical_significance: Mitotane is an adrenolytic drug used for selected adrenocortical carcinomas and to suppress excess adrenal steroid production. It can cause gastrointestinal and neurologic effects, adrenal insufficiency, and numerous drug interactions.

name: mitotic anaphase
clinical_significance: Mitotic anaphase is the stage of mitosis in which sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell. Accurate spindle attachment and chromosome segregation are required for formation of genetically similar daughter cells.

name: mitotic metaphase
clinical_significance: Mitotic metaphase is the stage of mitosis in which duplicated chromosomes align at the cell equator with sister kinetochores attached to opposite spindle poles. A checkpoint helps prevent premature chromosome separation.

name: mitotic prophase
clinical_significance: Mitotic prophase is the early stage of mitosis in which chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, the nucleolus disappears, and the mitotic spindle begins to form. In late prophase or prometaphase, the nuclear envelope breaks down.

name: mitotic recombination
clinical_significance: Mitotic recombination is exchange or rearrangement of DNA between homologous chromosomes during or around mitotic cell division. It can repair DNA or generate loss of heterozygosity and is relevant to tumor evolution and genetic disease.

name: mitotic telophase
clinical_significance: Mitotic telophase is the stage after chromosome separation when chromosomes reach opposite poles, decondense, and become enclosed in newly forming nuclear envelopes. Cytokinesis usually follows or overlaps with telophase.

name: mitoxantrone
clinical_significance: A chemotherapy and immunosuppressive medicine that interferes with DNA and is used for selected cancers and some forms of multiple sclerosis.

name: mitral atresia
clinical_significance: A serious heart defect present from birth in which the opening of the mitral valve is absent or completely closed. Blood cannot flow normally into the heart’s main pumping chamber, so newborns need urgent specialist care.

name: mitral valve
clinical_significance: The two-flap valve between the heart’s left upper and lower chambers. It opens to let blood pass forward and closes to prevent backward flow; it may become narrowed, leaky, infected, or weakened.

name: mitral valve insufficiency
clinical_significance: Leakage of the mitral valve that allows blood to flow backward into the left atrium when the heart contracts. It may cause breathlessness, fatigue, palpitations, swelling, or heart failure.

name: mitral valve prolapse
clinical_significance: Displacement of one or both mitral-valve leaflets backward into the left atrium during ventricular systole, often because of myxomatous or other degenerative valve changes. It may be harmless, but can cause mitral regurgitation, palpitations, arrhythmias, or rarely infective endocarditis or sudden cardiac death.

name: mitral valve stenosis
clinical_significance: Mitral stenosis obstructs flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle, raising left-atrial and pulmonary pressures and potentially causing atrial fibrillation, pulmonary hypertension, or heart failure. Rheumatic heart disease remains an important cause worldwide; severity and symptoms guide monitoring and intervention.

name: mitral valvuloplasty
clinical_significance: Mitral valvuloplasty is a procedure that widens a narrowed mitral valve, often with a balloon catheter or surgical repair.

name: mitsuokella
clinical_significance: Mitsuokella is a genus of anaerobic bacteria found mainly in the mouth and digestive tract; human infection is uncommon.

name: mitsuokella multacida
clinical_significance: Mitsuokella multacida is an anaerobic bacterium reported in human clinical specimens, including occasional invasive infections. A positive culture must be interpreted with the specimen site and clinical findings because related anaerobes may also be part of normal oral or intestinal flora.

name: mittelschmerz
clinical_significance: Recurrent one-sided lower-abdominal or pelvic pain occurring around ovulation. It is usually brief or lasts up to a day or two, but severe, persistent, or atypical pain requires assessment for other causes.

name: mixed glioma
clinical_significance: Mixed glioma is a historical term for a glioma with features of more than one glial cell type. Modern brain-tumor classification relies on histology and molecular markers, so the older label alone is insufficient for prognosis or treatment planning.

name: mobile health unit
clinical_significance: A mobile health unit is a vehicle or transportable facility equipped to provide health services at changing locations. It may deliver screening, vaccination, primary care, diagnostic testing, emergency support, or outreach to underserved communities.

name: mobiluncus
clinical_significance: A genus of curved anaerobic bacteria associated with bacterial vaginosis and occasionally isolated from other clinical specimens.

name: mobiluncus curtisii
clinical_significance: A curved bacterium that grows without oxygen and may be present with bacterial vaginosis. Its detection can support assessment, but symptoms, examination, and other test results are needed to interpret vaginal findings.

name: mobiluncus mulieris
clinical_significance: A curved bacterium that grows without oxygen and may be associated with bacterial vaginosis. Finding it can support a diagnosis, but symptoms, examination, and other laboratory results are also important.

name: Mobius syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare condition present from birth that affects certain facial and eye-moving nerves. It can cause facial weakness or paralysis, trouble closing the eyes, limited outward eye movement, and feeding or speech difficulties.

name: mocetinostat
clinical_significance: Mocetinostat is an investigational histone deacetylase inhibitor studied as an anticancer drug. Its use is limited to clinical research; trial eligibility and monitoring account for potential drug toxicities.

name: modafinil
clinical_significance: A prescription medicine that promotes wakefulness in narcolepsy, shift-work sleep disorder, and persistent sleepiness from obstructive sleep apnea when airway treatment is adequate. It can cause headache, anxiety, insomnia, serious rash, or dependence and is not a substitute for sleep or airway treatment.

name: modality
clinical_significance: A particular method used for treatment, diagnosis, imaging, or sensory stimulation. Examples include surgery, medicines, ultrasound, MRI, physiotherapy, and forms of counseling; the best modality depends on the health problem and the person's needs.

name: moderation
clinical_significance: Moderation is reduction or control of the intensity, amount, or severity of a process, symptom, behavior, or treatment effect. In clinical research, a moderator is a factor that changes the strength or direction of an association.

name: moellerella
clinical_significance: A rare group of bacteria that can occasionally cause urinary, bloodstream, or other infection, mainly in people who are seriously ill or have weakened defenses. Laboratory identification is needed to determine whether a specimen represents true infection.

name: moellerella wisconsensis
clinical_significance: A rare type of bacterium that can occasionally cause urinary, bloodstream, wound, or other infections, especially in people with serious illness or weakened immunity. Laboratory testing identifies it and guides antibiotic choice.

name: mogibacterium
clinical_significance: A genus of anaerobic bacteria found in the mouth and intestine and occasionally associated with dental or other infection.

name: mohs surgery
clinical_significance: Mohs surgery removes a skin cancer layer by layer while each layer is examined microscopically, allowing tissue-sparing removal with margin control. It is commonly selected for certain skin cancers in cosmetically or functionally important sites or when recurrence risk is high.

name: molar
clinical_significance: Molar teeth are important for chewing and can be affected by decay, gum disease, fracture, or impaction. In laboratory medicine, molar concentration expresses the amount of a substance per liter and is used to prepare and interpret solutions.

name: molecular biology
clinical_significance: Molecular biology underpins many clinical tests, including assays for pathogens, inherited variants, and tumor biomarkers. Results can guide diagnosis or treatment, but depend on validated methods and interpretation alongside the patient’s clinical findings.

name: molecular chaperone
clinical_significance: A molecular chaperone is a protein that assists other proteins with folding, assembly, transport, or refolding without becoming part of the final structure. Chaperones can also help prevent or resolve protein aggregation.

name: molecular diagnosis
clinical_significance: Molecular diagnosis uses analysis of DNA, RNA, proteins, or other molecular markers to identify a disease, pathogen, inherited variant, tumor subtype, or treatment-relevant characteristic. Results require appropriate assay validation and clinical interpretation.

name: molecular dynamic
clinical_significance: Molecular-dynamics methods simulate how molecules move and interact over time. In medicine and drug development, they can help study protein function, disease mechanisms, and candidate drug binding, but computational predictions require experimental validation.

name: molecular imaging
clinical_significance: Imaging that shows biological molecules, cell activity, or biochemical processes in the body, often using a targeted radioactive or fluorescent tracer. It can help characterize tumors, inflammation, infection, or organ function.

name: molecular medicine
clinical_significance: Molecular medicine applies molecular and genetic findings to diagnosis, risk assessment, and treatment selection. Examples include identifying actionable tumor alterations and selecting therapies for inherited or molecularly defined diseases.

name: molecular pathology
clinical_significance: The study of disease-related changes in genes, gene activity, or proteins within cells and tissues. It can help identify a disease, classify a tumor, estimate likely outcome, detect inherited risk, or select a treatment.

name: molecular probe
clinical_significance: A molecular probe is a labeled or otherwise detectable molecule designed to bind a particular nucleic-acid sequence, protein, metabolite, or other target. Probes are used in imaging, assays, microscopy, and molecular diagnostics.

name: molecular response
clinical_significance: A molecular response is a measurable change in a molecular marker, such as a pathogen load, oncogenic transcript, mutation burden, or biomarker, after disease progression or treatment. Its definition and clinical significance depend on the disease and assay.

name: molecular weight
clinical_significance: The mass of one molecule, usually expressed in atomic mass units; for a substance used in chemistry, its numerical value corresponds to molar mass in grams per mole. It helps calculate concentrations and doses.

name: molecule
clinical_significance: A group of chemically bonded atoms forming the smallest unit of a substance that retains its chemical properties.

name: mollusca
clinical_significance: The animal group containing snails, slugs, clams, and related species. Some mollusks can cause illness through venom, contaminated food, or parasites they carry; medical risk depends on the species and exposure.

name: molluscipoxvirus
clinical_significance: A group of poxviruses that includes the virus causing molluscum contagiosum. Infection produces small, firm, usually painless skin bumps with a central dimple and spreads through close skin contact or shared items.

name: molt
clinical_significance: Molt is the periodic shedding and replacement of an animal’s outer covering, such as feathers or hair. It is relevant to veterinary assessment when abnormal shedding reflects parasites, infection, nutritional problems, or systemic illness.

name: molybdenum
clinical_significance: An essential trace element required in small amounts for enzymes; excessive exposure can affect copper balance.

name: mometasone
clinical_significance: Mometasone is a potent synthetic glucocorticoid used topically or by inhalation for inflammatory skin or airway disease. It reduces local inflammation but may cause skin atrophy, oral candidiasis, adrenal effects, or other corticosteroid adverse effects.

name: mometasone furoate
clinical_significance: Mometasone furoate is the furoate ester of the corticosteroid mometasone. Depending on formulation, it is used for inflammatory skin disease, allergic rhinitis, or asthma; local and systemic corticosteroid precautions apply.

name: monascus
clinical_significance: Monascus is a genus of fungi used in some fermented foods; some species produce pigments, while contamination can produce harmful mycotoxins.

name: monascus ruber
clinical_significance: Monascus ruber is a mold used in some fermented foods and may produce red pigments. Contamination or poorly controlled fermentation can introduce fungal metabolites, so food safety depends on the strain and production conditions.

name: monensin
clinical_significance: Monensin is an ionophore antibiotic used mainly in veterinary practice and animal feed. Accidental ingestion or dosing errors can cause serious poisoning, including muscle and heart injury; it is not a human treatment.

name: mongolian spot
clinical_significance: A Mongolian spot, now preferably called congenital dermal melanocytosis, is a flat blue-gray patch caused by melanocytes in the dermis, usually present at birth. It is benign and often fades during childhood but should be documented to distinguish it from bruising.

name: monilethrix
clinical_significance: Monilethrix is an inherited hair-shaft disorder in which hair has regularly spaced narrow segments and breaks easily, producing a beaded appearance. It commonly causes short, brittle scalp hair and may involve follicles elsewhere.

name: monitoring device
clinical_significance: A monitoring device measures and displays or records a physiologic variable, such as heart rhythm, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, or respiratory rate. Accuracy, calibration, and clinical context determine how results should be interpreted.

name: monkeypox
clinical_significance: Mpox can cause painful skin lesions, fever, and lymph-node swelling and spreads through close contact; early recognition, isolation guidance, and care for complications reduce transmission and harm.

name: monobactams
clinical_significance: A class of antibiotics used mainly for certain infections caused by oxygen-using Gram-negative bacteria. Aztreonam is the main example; laboratory testing and allergy history help guide its use.

name: monoblast count
clinical_significance: A monoblast count is the number or proportion of monoblasts, immature precursors of monocytes, in a blood or bone-marrow sample. Increased blasts may support evaluation for acute myeloid leukemia or another marrow disorder and require expert morphologic or immunophenotypic interpretation.

name: monoclonal antibody
clinical_significance: A laboratory-made immune protein designed to recognize one specific target. Monoclonal antibodies are used in tests and treatments for cancer, inflammatory disease, infection, and other conditions.

name: monocrotophos
clinical_significance: Monocrotophos is a highly toxic organophosphorus insecticide that inhibits acetylcholinesterase. Exposure can cause acute cholinergic poisoning with secretions, bronchospasm, vomiting, bradycardia, weakness, seizures, and respiratory failure.

name: monocyte
clinical_significance: A type of white blood cell that travels in the blood and can enter tissues, where it becomes a macrophage or another immune cell. It helps remove germs and damaged material and coordinates inflammation and repair.

name: monocytopenia
clinical_significance: An abnormally low number of monocytes, a type of white blood cell, in the blood. It may occur with bone-marrow disorders, medicines, infections, or severe illness and is interpreted with the full blood count.

name: monocytosis
clinical_significance: Monocytosis is an increased absolute number of circulating monocytes. It may be reactive to infection or inflammation or associated with a hematologic neoplasm; persistent or marked monocytosis requires appropriate evaluation.

name: monogenic obesity
clinical_significance: Severe or early-onset obesity caused mainly by a disease-causing change in one gene. The affected gene may alter appetite or the body's control of energy use.

name: monograph
clinical_significance: A monograph is a detailed, authoritative document devoted to one subject. In health care it may describe a drug’s identity, quality, pharmacology, indications, dosing, safety, or regulatory standards.

name: monoiodotyrosine
clinical_significance: Monoiodotyrosine is an iodinated tyrosine residue formed during thyroid-hormone synthesis. Coupling of iodinated tyrosine residues within thyroglobulin contributes to production of thyroxine and triiodothyronine.

name: monokines
clinical_significance: Monokines are cytokines produced chiefly by monocytes and macrophages, including mediators such as tumor necrosis factor and interleukin-1. They regulate inflammation, immune responses, fever, and communication among cells.

name: monomer
clinical_significance: A monomer is a relatively small molecule that can chemically bond with other monomers to form a polymer. Biological examples include amino acids and nucleotides; some industrial monomers can irritate tissues or be toxic.

name: monomethylhydrazine
clinical_significance: Monomethylhydrazine is a volatile, corrosive, highly toxic chemical used as a rocket propellant. Exposure can injure the eyes, skin, lungs, liver, and nervous system and may cause seizures or systemic poisoning.

name: mononegavirales
clinical_significance: An order of viruses with nonsegmented, negative-sense RNA genomes, including rabies, measles, Ebola, and respiratory syncytial viruses.

name: mononeuropathy
clinical_significance: Mononeuropathy is dysfunction or injury of a single peripheral nerve. Common causes include compression, trauma, ischemia, inflammation, and metabolic disease; symptoms follow the nerve’s distribution and may include pain, numbness, weakness, or autonomic changes.

name: mononuclear leukocyte
clinical_significance: A white blood cell with one main, unsegmented nucleus. Monocytes and lymphocytes are examples; they help remove damaged material, recognize germs, and coordinate immune responses.

name: mononucleosis
clinical_significance: Infectious mononucleosis can cause fever, sore throat, swollen lymph nodes, and prolonged fatigue; splenic enlargement makes contact sports risky until recovery.

name: monosaccharide
clinical_significance: The simplest form of sugar, which cannot be split into a smaller carbohydrate. Glucose and fructose are examples; cells use these sugars mainly for energy.

name: monosomy
clinical_significance: A genetic condition in which a cell has one copy of a chromosome instead of the usual two. Effects depend on the chromosome and whether all cells or only some cells are affected.

name: monoterpenes
clinical_significance: Monoterpenes are compounds found in plants and essential oils, some of which are studied for pharmacologic effects or used as fragrance and flavor ingredients. Concentrated products can irritate skin or airways and may be toxic if swallowed, so exposure and formulation matter.

name: monozygotic twin
clinical_significance: A monozygotic twin develops when one fertilized egg divides into two embryos. The twins share nearly identical nuclear genomes but can differ through developmental, epigenetic, mitochondrial, and environmental factors.

name: montelukast
clinical_significance: Montelukast is a leukotriene CysLT1-receptor antagonist used for asthma prevention and allergic rhinitis; it is not a rescue bronchodilator, and neuropsychiatric adverse effects require attention.

name: montelukast sodium
clinical_significance: Montelukast sodium is the sodium salt of montelukast, a leukotriene-receptor antagonist used for asthma prevention and allergic rhinitis. It is not a rescue bronchodilator and carries an important warning for possible neuropsychiatric adverse effects.

name: mood disorder
clinical_significance: Mood disorders can impair energy, sleep, judgment, and daily function and may carry suicide risk; screening and timely treatment are important.

name: mood swing
clinical_significance: A mood swing is a noticeable change in emotional state or affect over time. Occasional changes can be normal, while frequent, severe, or impairing swings may occur with mood disorders, substance use, medical illness, medications, or sleep disruption.

name: mopidamol
clinical_significance: Mopidamol is an investigational dipyridamole-related phosphodiesterase inhibitor with antiplatelet activity. It is not a routine contemporary treatment; its relevance is mainly pharmacologic and historical.

name: mopp protocol
clinical_significance: The MOPP protocol combines mechlorethamine, vincristine, procarbazine, and prednisone and was used to treat Hodgkin lymphoma. It is now largely of historical relevance because other regimens are generally preferred and MOPP can cause substantial gonadal and other toxicities.

name: moral
clinical_significance: The word “moral” has no standalone diagnostic meaning, but moral distress can affect patients and health professionals when they feel unable to act according to their ethical responsibilities. In care settings, it may contribute to emotional strain and burnout.

name: morale
clinical_significance: Morale is the confidence, motivation, and sense of shared purpose within a person or group. It can affect teamwork and occupational well-being but is not itself a specific medical diagnosis.

name: moraxella
clinical_significance: Moraxella is a genus of bacteria that can colonize the respiratory tract and cause ear, sinus, eye, or respiratory infections.

name: moraxella atlantae
clinical_significance: Moraxella atlantae is a rare Moraxella species; its recovery from a clinical sample should be interpreted with the site and evidence of infection.

name: moraxella bovis
clinical_significance: Moraxella bovis is a major cause of infectious bovine keratoconjunctivitis (“pinkeye”), a contagious eye disease in cattle that can ulcerate the cornea and threaten vision. It is chiefly a veterinary pathogen.

name: moraxella canis
clinical_significance: Moraxella canis is associated mainly with dogs and can occasionally be recovered from human clinical specimens. Its significance depends on the infected site and supporting evidence, since a culture alone may represent colonization or contamination.

name: moraxella lacunata
clinical_significance: Moraxella lacunata can cause bacterial conjunctivitis and, less commonly, corneal infection in humans. Identification may guide evaluation of persistent or severe eye disease and targeted antimicrobial treatment.

name: moraxella lincolnii
clinical_significance: Moraxella lincolnii is a rare respiratory-tract bacterium; clinical importance depends on the specimen and evidence of infection.

name: moraxella nonliquefaciens
clinical_significance: Moraxella nonliquefaciens may colonize the upper respiratory tract and has occasionally been implicated in invasive infection. A laboratory finding should be interpreted with the specimen source, symptoms, and other evidence of infection.

name: moraxella oblonga
clinical_significance: Moraxella oblonga is a rare Moraxella species found in respiratory or oral specimens; significance depends on clinical evidence of infection.

name: moraxella osloensis
clinical_significance: An uncommon bacterium that can occasionally cause bloodstream, respiratory, wound, or other opportunistic infections, usually in people with serious illness or weakened immunity.

name: moraxellaceae
clinical_significance: A family of bacteria that includes Moraxella and related organisms. Some normally live on the skin or in the airways, while others can cause ear, sinus, lung, wound, or bloodstream infections.

name: morbid obesity
clinical_significance: Morbid obesity is an older term for very severe obesity, often corresponding to class III obesity or a body-mass index of at least 40 kg/m². Severe obesity raises the risk of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, sleep apnea, joint disease, and other complications; assessment should consider overall health rather than weight alone.

name: morbidity
clinical_significance: Morbidity describes illness, complications, or disability in an individual or population. It is used to measure disease burden and treatment outcomes and is distinct from mortality, which refers to death.

name: morbillivirus
clinical_significance: A genus of paramyxoviruses that includes measles virus and related animal viruses causing fever, respiratory illness, rash, or neurologic disease.

name: morcellation
clinical_significance: The division of tissue into smaller fragments, often during minimally invasive surgery; it may spread an unrecognized cancer and requires appropriate case selection.

name: morganella
clinical_significance: Morganella is a genus of gram-negative bacteria that can cause urinary, wound, bloodstream, and other opportunistic infections.

name: morganella morganii
clinical_significance: A gram-negative bacterium that can cause urinary, wound, bloodstream, or postoperative infections, especially in hospitalized or medically vulnerable people. Antibiotic choice requires susceptibility testing because resistance is common.

name: morning
clinical_significance: The time of morning can matter clinically because hormone levels, body temperature, symptoms, and test results follow daily rhythms. Some medicines and laboratory tests therefore have recommended timing; interpretation should use the collection time when relevant.

name: morning sickness
clinical_significance: Nausea, with or without vomiting, during pregnancy. It often begins early and improves by the middle of pregnancy, but severe or persistent vomiting can cause dehydration, weight loss, and nutrient problems and may need medical treatment.

name: moro reflex
clinical_significance: A normal newborn startle response that causes the baby to spread out the arms, open the hands, and then draw the arms inward. It usually fades by about 3 to 6 months; an absent or unequal response may indicate a nerve or developmental problem.

name: morphinans
clinical_significance: Morphinans are a group of chemical compounds with a fused-ring structure related to morphine. The class includes opioid analgesics and other compounds with varying receptor activity, potency, and clinical effects.

name: morphine
clinical_significance: Morphine is a potent opioid analgesic used for selected moderate-to-severe pain and palliative-care indications. It activates opioid receptors and can cause respiratory depression, sedation, constipation, nausea, tolerance, dependence, and overdose.

name: morphine sulfate
clinical_significance: Morphine sulfate is a salt formulation of the opioid analgesic morphine. It is available in immediate- and extended-release preparations for selected pain indications and carries risks of respiratory depression, misuse, dependence, and fatal overdose.

name: morphogenesis
clinical_significance: The biological process by which cells and tissues change shape, move, and organize to form organs and body structures during development or tissue repair.

name: morpholino
clinical_significance: Morpholino oligonucleotides are synthetic molecules designed to bind selected RNA sequences and block gene expression or alter RNA processing. They are used mainly in research and some specialized therapies; effects depend on the target sequence and delivery to the relevant tissue.

name: morphologic response
clinical_significance: A morphologic response is a treatment-related change in the visible or microscopic structure of a lesion, tumor, tissue, or cell population. It may include shrinkage, necrosis, differentiation, or altered cellular features and is interpreted using disease-specific criteria.

name: mortality
clinical_significance: Death, or the number of deaths in a particular group during a stated period. A mortality measure may describe all causes of death or deaths from a specific disease and population.

name: morton neuroma
clinical_significance: Thickening and irritation of a nerve in the ball of the foot, usually between the third and fourth toes. It can cause burning pain, numbness, or the feeling of a pebble under the foot, often worsened by tight shoes or walking.

name: morula
clinical_significance: A morula is an early embryo consisting of a compact ball of blastomeres formed after several cleavage divisions. It develops into a blastocyst before implantation in the uterine lining.

name: motexafin gadolinium
clinical_significance: Motexafin gadolinium is an investigational redox-active compound studied as a cancer radiosensitizer and imaging agent. It is not a routine clinical treatment; its significance is mainly in research on enhancing tumor response to radiation or chemotherapy.

name: motexafin lutetium
clinical_significance: Motexafin lutetium is an investigational photosensitizer studied for photodynamic therapy, in which light activation can damage targeted tissue. It has not become a routine approved cancer treatment, so its clinical relevance remains investigational.

name: motilin
clinical_significance: A hormone made mainly in the small intestine that helps trigger waves of movement through the stomach and small intestine, especially between meals. Its activity contributes to the pattern that clears leftover food and secretions from the upper digestive tract.

name: motion perception
clinical_significance: Motion perception is the ability of the visual, vestibular, and proprioceptive systems to detect and interpret movement of the body or surrounding objects. Disturbance may cause vertigo, oscillopsia, imbalance, or visual-motion sensitivity.

name: motion sickness
clinical_significance: Motion sickness causes nausea, dizziness, sweating, or vomiting when visual, vestibular, and other motion signals conflict. It is usually transient; persistent symptoms outside motion exposure or severe vomiting warrant evaluation for other causes.

name: motivation
clinical_significance: Motivation is the set of processes that initiate, direct, and sustain goal-directed behavior. Reduced or excessive motivation may occur with mood disorders, neurologic disease, substance use, medication effects, or other conditions.

name: motor aphasia
clinical_significance: Difficulty speaking or writing caused by damage to language areas of the brain, often after a stroke. A person may know what they want to say but struggle to find words, form sentences, or produce speech.

name: motor cortex
clinical_significance: Areas at the front of the brain that plan and control voluntary movement. Each side mainly controls the opposite side of the body. Injury can cause weakness, loss of fine movement, or difficulty planning purposeful actions.

name: motor delay
clinical_significance: Motor delay is slower-than-expected acquisition of gross- or fine-motor skills in a child. It may reflect neuromuscular, developmental, genetic, sensory, environmental, or systemic causes and warrants age-appropriate developmental assessment.

name: motor neuron
clinical_significance: A nerve cell that carries signals from the brain or spinal cord to skeletal muscle, allowing movement. Damage can cause weakness, muscle wasting, stiffness, cramps, or loss of voluntary control.

name: motor stereotypy
clinical_significance: A repeated, predictable movement such as hand flapping, rocking, or body waving. It may occur during normal development or with autism, intellectual disability, neurologic disease, stress, or other conditions.

name: motor tic
clinical_significance: A motor tic is a sudden, brief, repetitive movement such as blinking, facial grimacing, or shoulder shrugging. Tics are often temporarily suppressible and may occur in transient tic disorder, persistent tic disorder, or Tourette syndrome.

name: mouth diseases
clinical_significance: Disorders affecting the oral cavity, including infections, ulcers, inflammatory disease, dental disease, mucosal lesions, and tumors.

name: mouth neoplasm
clinical_significance: A mouth neoplasm is an abnormal growth in the oral cavity that may be benign or malignant; persistent sores, lumps, or patches need assessment.

name: mouthwash
clinical_significance: A liquid rinsed around the mouth and then expelled to freshen breath, deliver an active ingredient, or reduce selected oral microorganisms.

name: Movement
clinical_significance: Movement is a change in position of the body or a body part produced by coordinated activity of the nervous system, muscles, and joints. Abnormal movement may be excessive, reduced, involuntary, poorly coordinated, or restricted.

name: movement disorders
clinical_significance: Movement disorders affect voluntary movement and may cause tremor, slowness, stiffness, or involuntary motions; medication effects and neurologic causes guide management.

name: moxalactam
clinical_significance: Moxalactam is a beta-lactam antibiotic of the oxacephem group with activity against many gram-negative bacteria and some gram-positive organisms. It is rarely used today and may cause allergic reactions, diarrhea, or bleeding related to impaired coagulation.

name: moxibustion
clinical_significance: A traditional treatment that warms selected skin areas with burning mugwort or another heated material. Evidence of benefit varies by condition, and burns, smoke exposure, allergic reactions, or infection can occur.

name: moxifloxacin
clinical_significance: An antibiotic used for selected bacterial infections. It interferes with bacterial reproduction but can cause serious side effects, including tendon injury, nerve symptoms, blood-sugar changes, or dangerous heart rhythms, so use is selective.

name: Moyamoya disease
clinical_significance: A rare condition in which major arteries supplying the brain gradually narrow or close. Small fragile blood vessels form to compensate, but the condition can cause transient attacks, strokes, headaches, seizures, or thinking problems.

name: mrna precursor
clinical_significance: An initial RNA transcript that is processed by capping, splicing, and polyadenylation to form mature messenger RNA.

name: mu-Chain disease
clinical_significance: A rare B-cell disorder in which abnormal immunoglobulin heavy chains are produced, sometimes causing anemia, enlarged lymph nodes, or other features of lymphoproliferative disease.

name: mucin
clinical_significance: Mucin is a high-molecular-weight glycoprotein that forms mucus and helps lubricate and protect epithelial surfaces. Abnormal mucin production or accumulation occurs in some respiratory, gastrointestinal, and neoplastic diseases.

name: mucinous
clinical_significance: Mucinous means containing, producing, or resembling mucin. In pathology, the term describes lesions or tumors with extracellular or intracellular mucin and must be interpreted with the organ, architecture, and other histologic features.

name: mucinous adenocarcinoma
clinical_significance: Mucinous adenocarcinoma is a gland-forming cancer that produces abundant mucus and can arise in organs such as the colon, pancreas, lung, or breast.

name: mucinous cystadenoma
clinical_significance: A mucinous cystadenoma is a usually benign cystic epithelial tumor that produces mucin, commonly arising in the ovary or pancreas. Large lesions may cause pain or pressure, and pathology is needed to distinguish benign from borderline or malignant mucinous tumors.

name: mucocele
clinical_significance: A soft, mucus-filled swelling caused by leakage or blockage of a small salivary gland, most often on the inner lower lip after minor injury. It may come and go, but a persistent or recurrent swelling should be examined and may need removal.

name: mucoepidermoid carcinoma
clinical_significance: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is a cancer containing mucus-producing and squamous-like cells, most often arising in salivary glands or the lungs.

name: mucolipidoses
clinical_significance: A group of inherited lysosomal storage disorders in which cells cannot properly process certain lipids and carbohydrate-containing substances. Material accumulates in tissues and may cause developmental delay, skeletal changes, vision problems, and organ disease.

name: mucopolysaccharidosis
clinical_significance: The singular name for any of a group of inherited lysosomal storage disorders in which glycosaminoglycans accumulate because of deficient enzyme activity. Types differ in their genetic cause, age of onset, and effects on the skeleton, organs, airways, eyes, heart, and nervous system.

name: mucopolysaccharidosis vii
clinical_significance: Mucopolysaccharidosis VII, or Sly syndrome, is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient beta-glucuronidase activity. Accumulation of glycosaminoglycans can cause skeletal, connective-tissue, visceral, developmental, and sometimes neurologic abnormalities.

name: mucor
clinical_significance: Mucor is a genus of molds; related Mucorales fungi can cause mucormycosis, a serious invasive infection mainly in people with severe immune or metabolic problems.

name: mucor ramosissimus
clinical_significance: A type of mold found in the environment that rarely causes infection in people. When infection occurs, it is usually in someone with severely weakened immune defenses and requires identification of the fungus and specialist treatment.

name: mucorales
clinical_significance: Mucorales is an order of molds that includes fungi capable of causing mucormycosis, a rapidly invasive infection of the sinuses, lungs, skin, or other tissues.

name: mucosal immunity
clinical_significance: Mucosal immunity is immune defense at surfaces lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, and other tracts. It includes epithelial barriers, mucus, secretory IgA, antimicrobial molecules, innate cells, and locally regulated adaptive responses.

name: mucosal infection
clinical_significance: An infection involving a moist epithelial lining such as the mouth, eye, nose, airway, gastrointestinal tract, or genital tract.

name: mucous membrane
clinical_significance: A moist tissue lining body cavities that open to the outside, including the nose, mouth, and lungs.

name: mucus
clinical_significance: Mucus is a viscoelastic secretion containing water, mucin glycoproteins, salts, antimicrobial factors, and cellular material. It lubricates and protects epithelial surfaces and traps particles and microorganisms for clearance.

name: Muenke syndrome
clinical_significance: Muenke syndrome is an FGFR3-related craniosynostosis disorder, usually involving premature fusion of one or both coronal sutures. It can affect skull shape and facial development and may be associated with hearing loss, developmental or learning differences, and limb findings; care may involve craniofacial, hearing, and developmental monitoring.

name: mulibrey nanism
clinical_significance: Mulibrey nanism is a rare inherited multisystem disorder, usually caused by biallelic variants in \textit{TRIM37}. It may cause severe growth restriction, characteristic facial features, pericardial or hepatic disease, insulin resistance, and other organ involvement.

name: muller cells
clinical_significance: Supporting glial cells of the retina that help nourish retinal nerve cells and maintain the retina's structure and chemical environment.

name: multicenter study
clinical_significance: A multicenter study is a clinical or research investigation conducted at two or more sites under a coordinated protocol. It can improve enrollment and generalizability but requires harmonized methods, quality control, and site-specific oversight.

name: multi-drug resistance
clinical_significance: Multidrug resistance is the ability of a microorganism, cancer cell, or other target to withstand several drugs. It can make infections or cancers harder to treat and may require susceptibility testing, molecular profiling, or use of alternative therapies.

name: multienzyme complexes
clinical_significance: Groups of enzymes organized together so that several steps in a chemical pathway occur efficiently. This arrangement can speed reactions, limit loss of intermediates, and coordinate metabolism inside cells.

name: multi-infarct dementia
clinical_significance: A decline in memory and thinking caused by several strokes that damage different parts of the brain. Problems may include slowed thinking, poor planning, mood changes, walking difficulty, or memory loss; the term is now often included under vascular cognitive impairment.

name: multimodal imaging
clinical_significance: Use of two or more imaging methods, such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, or nuclear imaging, to examine the same disease or body region. Combining methods can provide complementary structural, functional, or molecular information.

name: multinodular goiter
clinical_significance: An enlarged thyroid containing multiple nodules. Thyroid function may be normal, underactive, or overactive; evaluation commonly includes thyroid-function tests and ultrasound, with further assessment of suspicious nodules or compressive symptoms.

name: multinucleated hepatocyte
clinical_significance: A multinucleated hepatocyte is a liver cell containing two or more nuclei, usually from nuclear division without complete cytokinesis. It may be a normal or reactive finding, but its significance depends on the number, morphology, and associated liver abnormalities.

name: multiple endocrine neoplasia
clinical_significance: A group of inherited, usually autosomal dominant cancer-predisposition syndromes causing tumors or overactivity in two or more hormone-making glands during a person's lifetime. Types include MEN1, MEN2, and related subtypes with different gene associations and tumor risks.

name: multiple exostoses
clinical_significance: Multiple exostoses, or hereditary multiple osteochondromas, is an inherited disorder causing multiple cartilage-capped bony projections near growth plates. Lesions can deform bones, restrict motion, compress nerves or vessels, and rarely undergo malignant transformation.

name: multiple fibrofolliculomas
clinical_significance: Numerous harmless small skin-colored growths arising from hair follicles, usually on the face and trunk. They can be a sign of Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome, which also increases the risk of kidney tumors and collapsed lung.

name: multiple myeloma
clinical_significance: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells that usually develops in bone marrow and often produces a monoclonal immunoglobulin. It can cause bone lesions, anemia, kidney injury, infections, and high blood calcium; diagnosis and treatment depend on laboratory, imaging, and marrow findings.

name: multiple organ failure
clinical_significance: A life-threatening condition in which two or more organs stop working properly, usually during severe infection, shock, injury, or widespread inflammation. Intensive care supports the organs while doctors treat the underlying cause.

name: multiple pregnancy
clinical_significance: A pregnancy involving two or more fetuses. Twins may develop from two separate eggs or from one fertilized egg that divides; triplets and higher-order pregnancies are less common. Multiple pregnancies have higher risks of premature birth, growth problems, and pregnancy complications and require closer monitoring.

name: multiple sclerosis
clinical_significance: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic immune-mediated disease of the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves that damages myelin and sometimes nerve fibers. It can cause episodes or progression of visual, sensory, motor, balance, bladder, bowel, or cognitive symptoms. Disease-modifying therapies can reduce relapses or slow activity, so diagnosis and monitoring are important.

name: multiplicity
clinical_significance: Multiplicity is the state of having more than one occurrence, copy, lesion, tumor, or pregnancy component. Its interpretation depends on context, such as multiple gestation, multifocal disease, or copy number in genetics.

name: multipolar neuron
clinical_significance: A nerve cell with one long output branch and several receiving branches. This common type of neuron includes many cells that control movement or pass signals within the brain and spinal cord.

name: multivesicular body
clinical_significance: A multivesicular body is an endosomal compartment containing many small intraluminal vesicles. It can fuse with the plasma membrane to release exosomes or with a lysosome to degrade its cargo.

name: mumps
clinical_significance: Mumps is a contagious viral infection spread through saliva and respiratory droplets. It commonly causes fever and painful swelling of the salivary glands; complications include meningitis, orchitis, pancreatitis, and hearing loss. Vaccination greatly reduces risk, and suspected cases require infection-control precautions.

name: mumps virus
clinical_significance: The virus that causes mumps, a contagious infection spread through saliva and respiratory droplets. It commonly causes fever and painful swelling near the jaw, and can sometimes inflame the brain, pancreas, or reproductive organs; vaccination reduces risk.

name: muparfostat
clinical_significance: Muparfostat (PI-88) is an investigational sulfated oligosaccharide studied for antitumor and antithrombotic effects, including as adjuvant therapy for liver cancer. It is not a routine approved treatment; its relevance is limited to research.

name: mupirocin
clinical_significance: Mupirocin is a topical antibiotic that inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase. It is used for selected skin infections and nasal eradication of certain staphylococci; resistance can develop with inappropriate or prolonged use.

name: muramidase
clinical_significance: Muramidase, or lysozyme, is an enzyme that cleaves the peptidoglycan backbone of bacterial cell walls. It is present in secretions and innate immune cells and contributes to defense against susceptible bacteria.

name: muromonab-CD3
clinical_significance: Muromonab-CD3 (OKT3) is an older mouse monoclonal antibody that was used to treat acute transplant rejection by depleting or altering T cells. It was withdrawn from clinical use; its history is relevant to transplant immunology and the development of biologic immunosuppressants.

name: muscarine
clinical_significance: Muscarine is a mushroom-derived agonist of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors. Ingestion of muscarine-containing mushrooms can cause a cholinergic syndrome with salivation, sweating, tearing, abdominal cramps, vomiting, diarrhea, bronchospasm, and bradycardia.

name: muscarinic antagonist
clinical_significance: A muscarinic antagonist blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in smooth muscle, glands, the heart, and the central nervous system. Examples include atropine, ipratropium, and oxybutynin; effects can include dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, tachycardia, and confusion.

name: muscidae
clinical_significance: Muscidae is a family of flies that includes the housefly. Some species can mechanically carry pathogens to food or wounds, and their larvae may occasionally cause myiasis.

name: muscimol
clinical_significance: Muscimol is a psychoactive compound found in some Amanita mushrooms and an agonist at GABA-A receptors. Ingestion can cause altered perception, sedation, agitation, incoordination, or seizures and may require toxicologic evaluation.

name: muscle
clinical_significance: Body tissue that shortens to create force and movement. Skeletal muscle moves the bones and supports posture, heart muscle pumps blood, and smooth muscle moves substances through organs such as the bowel and blood vessels.

name: muscle atrophy
clinical_significance: Muscle atrophy is loss of muscle mass that can reduce strength and function. It may follow disuse, nerve injury, inflammatory or genetic muscle disease, malnutrition, or systemic illness; evaluation focuses on the underlying cause and prevention of further loss.

name: muscle cell
clinical_significance: A cell specialized to contract; skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle cells perform different movement and organ functions.

name: muscle contraction
clinical_significance: The tightening of a muscle, allowing it to produce force or movement. Muscle fibers use calcium and energy from ATP to make their protein filaments slide against each other.

name: muscle cramp
clinical_significance: A muscle cramp is a sudden, involuntary, painful contraction of a muscle. It may follow exertion, dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, pregnancy, medication use, nerve disease, or vascular disease; recurrent cramps need assessment of the cause.

name: muscle development
clinical_significance: Muscle development is the formation, growth, differentiation, and maturation of muscle tissue. It depends on genetic programs, neural input, hormones, nutrition, mechanical loading, and repair processes.

name: muscle fatigue
clinical_significance: A reduced ability of a muscle to produce force after prolonged or repeated activity. It may result from exertion, poor sleep, illness, medicines, nerve problems, or muscle disease, and improves when the cause is treated.

name: muscle fiber
clinical_significance: A muscle fiber is an individual muscle cell containing contractile myofibrils. Skeletal muscle fibers vary in size and metabolic properties, while cardiac and smooth muscle cells have distinct structures and functions.

name: muscle hypertrophy
clinical_significance: Muscle hypertrophy is enlargement of individual muscle fibers, usually in response to resistance, hormonal stimulation, or compensatory workload. It can be physiologic or associated with disease, depending on the muscle and cause.

name: muscle neoplasm
clinical_significance: A muscle neoplasm is an abnormal growth in skeletal or smooth muscle or nearby soft tissue and may be benign or malignant.

name: muscle protein
clinical_significance: A protein found in muscle that provides structure, produces contraction, stores or transports substances, or regulates muscle activity. Important examples include actin, myosin, troponin, dystrophin, and myoglobin.

name: muscle relaxant
clinical_significance: A medicine that reduces skeletal-muscle spasms or tightness. Some act in the brain or spinal cord and may cause sleepiness or weakness. Neuromuscular-blocking medicines are a distinct group that temporarily paralyzes muscles and requires breathing support and close monitoring.

name: muscle rigidity
clinical_significance: Muscle rigidity is abnormal resistance to passive movement caused by sustained muscle contraction or altered tone. It occurs in conditions such as Parkinson disease, dystonia, meningitis, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and tetanus.

name: muscle spindle
clinical_significance: A small sensor inside skeletal muscle that detects how much the muscle is stretched and how quickly it changes length. It helps maintain posture, muscle tone, balance, and coordinated movement.

name: muscle strength
clinical_significance: Muscle strength is the maximal force a muscle or muscle group can generate under specified conditions. It is assessed by functional or resisted testing and may be reduced by muscle, nerve, neuromuscular-junction, central, or systemic disorders.

name: muscle tonus
clinical_significance: The slight, continuous activity present in resting muscles, which gives them resistance to being stretched. Too much or too little tone can occur with disorders of the brain, spinal cord, nerves, or muscles.

name: muscle weakness
clinical_significance: Muscle weakness is reduced ability to generate force. Causes range from pain, inactivity, and medication effects to nerve, muscle, neuromuscular-junction, or brain disorders; sudden weakness, especially with facial or speech changes, can signal an emergency such as stroke.

name: muscular dystrophy
clinical_significance: Muscular dystrophy refers to inherited disorders that cause progressive skeletal-muscle weakness and degeneration. The specific gene and subtype determine age of onset and progression; some forms also affect heart or breathing muscles, making cardiac and respiratory surveillance important.

name: musculoskeletal
clinical_significance: Musculoskeletal problems can affect movement, function, and independence and may arise from injury, inflammation, degeneration, infection, or systemic disease. Assessment distinguishes the affected tissue and cause to guide rehabilitation, medication, or procedural care.

name: musculoskeletal deformity
clinical_significance: A musculoskeletal deformity is an abnormal shape, alignment, or structure of bone, joint, muscle, or related tissue. It may be congenital, developmental, traumatic, degenerative, neuromuscular, or caused by disease.

name: musculoskeletal disease
clinical_significance: A disorder affecting bones, joints, muscles, tendons, ligaments, cartilage, or other supporting tissues, causing pain or limited movement.

name: musculoskeletal injury
clinical_significance: Trauma to muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, cartilage, or related soft tissues, ranging from strains and sprains to fractures and dislocations.

name: musculoskeletal pain
clinical_significance: Musculoskeletal pain may follow injury or arise from degenerative, inflammatory, infectious, or systemic disease. Persistent pain, impaired function, fever, major trauma, new neurologic deficits, or a hot swollen joint may require prompt assessment to identify serious causes.

name: musculoskeletal system
clinical_significance: The musculoskeletal system consists of bones, joints, cartilage, ligaments, tendons, muscles, and associated connective tissues. It provides support, protects organs, enables movement, and contributes to mineral storage and blood-cell production.

name: music therapy
clinical_significance: The planned use of music by a trained therapist to support health and wellbeing. It may help with pain, stress, communication, movement, memory, emotional expression, or coping during illness and rehabilitation.

name: mustard compounds
clinical_significance: Mustard compounds are chemical agents containing reactive sulfur or nitrogen mustard groups that can alkylate DNA and other molecules. Some are chemotherapy drugs; others are highly toxic chemical-warfare agents.

name: mustard gas
clinical_significance: Mustard gas, or sulfur mustard, is a vesicant chemical-warfare agent that damages skin, eyes, and respiratory tissues and can cause blistering, airway injury, and delayed complications. It is not a true gas at ordinary temperatures and has no specific widely available antidote.

name: mutagen
clinical_significance: A chemical, physical agent, or biological factor capable of causing a genetic mutation. Mutagenicity does not by itself prove that an agent causes cancer.

name: mutagenicity test
clinical_significance: A mutagenicity test checks whether a chemical or other exposure can damage genetic material or cause mutations. It supports hazard assessment and drug development, but a positive laboratory result alone does not establish the level of risk to people.

name: mutant
clinical_significance: A mutant is a cell, organism, or genetic sequence carrying a mutation relative to a reference or parental form. The change may have no effect, alter a trait, or cause disease, depending on its location and functional consequence.

name: mutant proteins
