clinical_significance: Causing the womb to contract. Oxytocic medicines, such as oxytocin, may start or strengthen labor or help control heavy bleeding after birth; they require monitoring because overly strong or frequent contractions can harm the pregnant person or baby.

name: oxytocin
clinical_significance: A hormone made in the brain and released by the pituitary gland. It helps the uterus contract during labor and causes milk to flow during breastfeeding; a manufactured form is used under monitoring to induce labor or control bleeding after birth.

name: ozone
clinical_significance: Ozone is a reactive form of oxygen that can irritate and injure the airways and lungs when inhaled, despite useful atmospheric and disinfecting roles.

name: ozone sterilization
clinical_significance: Ozone sterilization uses ozone gas to disinfect or sterilize selected equipment and environments. Residual ozone is toxic to the lungs and must be controlled with validated processes and adequate aeration before exposure.

name: pachygyria
clinical_significance: A birth-related brain-development abnormality in which the brain’s outer surface has fewer, broader folds than usual. It can cause developmental delay, learning difficulties, seizures, movement problems, or other neurologic effects of varying severity.

name: pachyonychia congenita
clinical_significance: An inherited skin disorder causing very thick, abnormal nails and painful thick skin on the palms and soles. Some people also develop blisters, cysts, excess sweating, or white patches in the mouth.

name: pacifier
clinical_significance: A pacifier can soothe an infant and may lower sudden infant death risk when offered during sleep, but it should not be forced or attached with a cord around the neck. Breastfeeding and dental considerations guide timing and use.

name: pacinian corpuscle
clinical_significance: A specialized nerve ending deep in the skin and connective tissue that detects deep pressure and vibration. It helps the nervous system sense contact, movement, and the handling of objects.

name: packaging tube
clinical_significance: A packaging tube is a container for medicines or health products; material compatibility, sterility, closure integrity, and labeling affect product quality and safe use.

name: paclitaxel
clinical_significance: Paclitaxel is a taxane chemotherapy drug that stabilizes microtubules and prevents cell division; it treats several cancers and can cause myelosuppression, neuropathy, alopecia, myalgia, and hypersensitivity reactions.

name: paclitaxel liposome
clinical_significance: A liposomal formulation of paclitaxel designed to alter drug distribution and delivery; paclitaxel disrupts microtubules and is used as chemotherapy in selected cancers.

name: paclitaxel poliglumex
clinical_significance: Paclitaxel poliglumex is an investigational polymer-linked formulation of paclitaxel designed to alter drug delivery to tumors. It is not a routine approved chemotherapy and remains of research significance.

name: paecilomyces
clinical_significance: Paecilomyces is a genus of environmental molds that can cause rare opportunistic infection, including eye, skin, lung, or disseminated disease. Species identification is important because some isolates resist commonly used antifungals.

name: paenibacillus
clinical_significance: Paenibacillus is a genus of environmental and soil bacteria that rarely causes human infection. When isolated from a clinical sample, the result must be interpreted with the specimen source and evidence of illness.

name: paenibacillus alvei
clinical_significance: Paenibacillus alvei is mainly an environmental and insect-associated bacterium and only rarely causes human infection. A culture finding may represent contamination unless supported by clinical evidence.

name: paenibacillus phoenicis
clinical_significance: Paenibacillus phoenicis is a rare environmental bacterium with limited evidence as a human pathogen. Its significance depends on isolation from a sterile site and compatible signs of infection.

name: paenibacillus polymyxa
clinical_significance: Paenibacillus polymyxa is an environmental bacterium studied for antimicrobial compounds and agricultural uses; human infection is uncommon. Clinical isolates require correlation with the patient and specimen.

name: pagetoid reticulosis
clinical_significance: A rare localized variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with solitary slowly enlarging scaly plaques containing atypical pagetoid lymphocytes.

name: pain
clinical_significance: An unpleasant physical and emotional experience linked to actual or possible tissue injury. Pain can be short-lived or persistent and is influenced by nerves, inflammation, health, emotions, past experiences, and social circumstances.

name: pain management
clinical_significance: Care that identifies the cause of pain and reduces pain while improving function and quality of life. It may combine medicines, physical treatment, psychological support, procedures, and treatment of the underlying condition, with risks reviewed regularly.

name: pain perception
clinical_significance: The process by which the nervous system notices possible or actual tissue injury and the brain interprets it as pain. Attention, emotions, past experiences, inflammation, and medicines can change how pain feels.

name: pain threshold
clinical_significance: The minimum intensity of a stimulus that a person perceives as painful; it varies with tissue, context, attention, inflammation, medications, and neurologic state.

name: palatal muscle
clinical_significance: Muscle of the soft palate that elevates or tenses the palate and helps separate the nasal and oral cavities during swallowing and speech.

name: palate
clinical_significance: Palate abnormalities such as cleft palate can impair feeding, speech, hearing, and dental development. Painful lesions, persistent white or red patches, or a mass may require oral examination and biopsy.

name: palate neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in the roof of the mouth. It may be noncancerous or cancerous and can cause a lump, pain, bleeding, loose teeth, difficulty swallowing, or speech changes.

name: palatine tonsil
clinical_significance: The palatine tonsils can become infected or enlarged and may contribute to sore throat, sleep-disordered breathing, or swallowing difficulty. Recurrent or severe disease may prompt testing or consideration of tonsillectomy.

name: palatorrhaphy
clinical_significance: Palatorrhaphy is surgical repair of a cleft or defect of the palate to restore separation between the oral and nasal cavities and improve feeding and speech.

name: palifermin
clinical_significance: Palifermin is a keratinocyte growth factor used to reduce severe oral mucositis in selected patients receiving intensive cancer therapy and stem-cell transplantation. It is given under specialist protocols and can cause skin, oral, and taste-related effects.

name: palivizumab
clinical_significance: A monoclonal antibody against respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein, used prophylactically in selected high-risk infants and young children during RSV season.

name: palladium
clinical_significance: Palladium is a metal used in dental and medical materials and can cause allergic contact dermatitis in sensitized people. Implant or device reactions require assessment of the specific material and other possible causes.

name: palliative care
clinical_significance: Medical care for serious illness that relieves pain and other symptoms and supports daily life, emotional health, and family needs. It can begin at any stage and can be provided alongside treatment intended to control or cure disease.

name: pallister-hall syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited condition that may cause an extra finger or toe, a noncancerous growth near the brain’s hormone-control center, and abnormalities of the anus, kidneys, airway, or pituitary hormones.

name: pallor
clinical_significance: Unusual paleness of skin or mucous membranes, often due to reduced blood flow, anemia, or other illness.

name: palm oil
clinical_significance: Palm oil contains substantial saturated fat; replacing unsaturated fats with it may adversely affect blood lipids. Dietary effects depend on the overall pattern and what fats it replaces.

name: palmar reflex
clinical_significance: The palmar reflex is an infant response in which stroking the palm causes finger flexion; persistence or asymmetry beyond the expected age may indicate neurologic dysfunction.

name: palmitic acid
clinical_significance: A 16-carbon saturated fatty acid common in dietary and stored fats; excess saturated-fat intake can contribute to adverse lipid profiles, although the body also synthesizes it normally.

name: palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
clinical_significance: Excessive thickening of the skin on the palms and soles, inherited or acquired, causing calluses, fissures, pain, impaired walking, and sometimes infection.

name: palonosetron
clinical_significance: Palonosetron is a long-acting serotonin 5-HT3 receptor blocker used to prevent chemotherapy-related nausea and vomiting and in some perioperative settings. Headache and constipation can occur; it is often combined with other antiemetics for highly emetogenic regimens.

name: palonosetron hydrochloride
clinical_significance: A long-acting 5-HT3 serotonin-receptor antagonist used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, surgery, or selected other treatments.

name: palpable
clinical_significance: Palpable means detectable by touch during physical examination, such as a mass, enlarged organ, lymph node, pulse, tenderness, or abnormal surface.

name: palpation
clinical_significance: Examination by touching the body to assess tenderness, temperature, texture, masses, pulses, organ size, and movement.

name: palpebral conjunctiva
clinical_significance: The thin, moist membrane lining the inner surfaces of the eyelids. It joins the membrane covering the front of the eye and helps protect, lubricate, and move tears across the eye’s surface.

name: palpitation
clinical_significance: Awareness of the heart beating fast, forcefully, irregularly, or as if it skipped a beat. Causes include stress, stimulants, anemia, thyroid disease, medicines, and abnormal rhythms.

name: palsy
clinical_significance: Weakness or loss of movement in a body part, often affecting muscles supplied by a particular nerve. It may be temporary or lasting and can result from nerve injury, infection, stroke, inflammation, or a problem present from birth.

name: pamidronic acid
clinical_significance: An intravenous bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and is used for selected hypercalcemia, bone complications of cancer, and Paget disease.

name: pan troglodyte
clinical_significance: Pan troglodytes is the scientific name for the common chimpanzee, an important biomedical research species and a natural host of simian immunodeficiency viruses related to HIV. Animal research requires strict ethical and biosafety oversight.

name: panax
clinical_significance: Panax refers to ginseng plants used in traditional products and dietary supplements. Evidence for benefit varies, and products may interact with anticoagulants, diabetes medicines, or other drugs and can differ in composition.

name: pancoast syndrome
clinical_significance: Symptoms caused by a cancer at the top of the lung growing into nearby nerves or other tissues. It may cause severe shoulder or arm pain, hand weakness, numbness, and drooping of one eyelid with a smaller pupil.

name: pancoast tumor
clinical_significance: A lung cancer at the top of the lung that can grow into nearby nerves, blood vessels, or the spine. It may cause severe shoulder or arm pain, hand weakness, or drooping of one eyelid.

name: pancreas
clinical_significance: An organ behind the stomach that makes digestive juices and hormones. Its digestive enzymes enter the small intestine, while insulin and other hormones help control blood sugar and digestion.

name: pancreas enzyme
clinical_significance: An enzyme produced by the pancreas, such as amylase, lipase, or proteases, that helps digest carbohydrate, fat, or protein in the small intestine.

name: pancreas infection
clinical_significance: Infection involving the pancreas or a pancreatic collection, usually occurring with pancreatitis, surgery, trauma, or spread from nearby infection.

name: pancreas neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in the pancreas that may be noncancerous, precancerous, or cancerous. Its effects depend on its location and may include pain, jaundice, digestive problems, or diabetes.

name: pancreas transplantation
clinical_significance: Pancreas transplantation can restore insulin production for selected people with severe diabetes, often alongside kidney transplantation. It requires lifelong immunosuppression and monitoring for rejection, infection, and graft complications.

name: pancreatectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part or all of the pancreas. It may treat a pancreatic tumor, severe injury, or another serious disease; removal of pancreatic tissue can affect digestion and blood-sugar control.

name: pancreatic adenocarcinoma
clinical_significance: The most common cancer of the pancreas, arising from cells in its digestive-juice ducts. It may cause jaundice, abdominal or back pain, weight loss, or no early symptoms; smoking, chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, obesity, and inherited risks can contribute.

name: pancreatic carcinoma
clinical_significance: Pancreatic carcinoma is cancer arising in the pancreas, most often from duct cells, and may cause jaundice, pain, weight loss, or digestive problems.

name: pancreatic cysts
clinical_significance: Fluid-filled sacs in or around the pancreas. Some follow inflammation or injury, while others are growths that can become cancerous; imaging and sometimes fluid or tissue testing guide follow-up or treatment.

name: pancreatic diseases
clinical_significance: Disorders affecting the pancreas’s digestive or hormone-producing functions, including inflammation, cysts, tumors, duct blockage, and diabetes-related damage. They may cause abdominal pain, vomiting, weight loss, jaundice, abnormal blood sugar, or poor digestion.

name: pancreatic duct
clinical_significance: The main tube carrying digestive fluid from the pancreas into the first part of the small intestine. It often joins the bile duct before opening into the intestine; blockage can cause pain, jaundice, or pancreatitis.

name: pancreatic fistula
clinical_significance: A pancreatic fistula is an abnormal passage through which pancreatic juice leaks from the pancreas, often after trauma or surgery, causing fluid collections, ascites, or skin drainage.

name: pancreatic hormones
clinical_significance: Hormones produced by pancreatic islet cells, including insulin, glucagon, somatostatin, and pancreatic polypeptide, which regulate glucose, digestion, and energy metabolism.

name: pancreatic islet
clinical_significance: A pancreatic islet is a cluster of endocrine cells that releases hormones such as insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin to regulate blood glucose and digestion.

name: pancreatic juice
clinical_significance: Pancreatic juice is an alkaline digestive secretion containing bicarbonate and enzymes such as amylase, lipase, and proteases, delivered into the duodenum.

name: pancreatic pseudocyst
clinical_significance: A walled-off collection of pancreatic fluid that usually develops after acute or chronic pancreatitis. It has no true cell lining and may cause abdominal pain, vomiting, early fullness, infection, bleeding, or blockage of nearby organs.

name: pancreaticoduodenectomy
clinical_significance: Pancreaticoduodenectomy, or the Whipple procedure, removes the head of the pancreas and nearby parts of the digestive tract to treat selected tumors and other serious disease.

name: pancreatitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the pancreas that may be acute or chronic. Causes include gallstones, alcohol, medicines, metabolic disorders, and other conditions. Acute disease may cause severe upper-abdominal pain, vomiting, fluid loss, infection, tissue death, or organ failure; chronic disease can permanently scar the pancreas and cause poor digestion, weight loss, or diabetes.

name: pancreatoblastoma
clinical_significance: A rare cancer of the pancreas that occurs mainly in children. It may cause an abdominal lump, pain, vomiting, weight loss, or hormone-related symptoms and requires specialist imaging, biopsy, staging, and treatment.

name: pancrelipase
clinical_significance: Pancrelipase is a mixture of pancreatic digestive enzymes used as replacement therapy for exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, including that caused by cystic fibrosis or pancreatic disease.

name: pancuronium
clinical_significance: A long-acting medicine that temporarily prevents skeletal muscles from contracting during anesthesia or assisted breathing. It causes paralysis but does not relieve pain or cause unconsciousness and must be given with reliable airway and breathing support.

name: pancytopenia
clinical_significance: A reduction in red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets at the same time. It can cause tiredness, infections, and bleeding and may result from medicines, infection, immune disease, or a problem in the bone marrow.

name: pandemic
clinical_significance: An epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or continents and affects many people. It may occur when an infectious agent spreads widely among populations with limited previous immunity.

name: pandoraea
clinical_significance: Pandoraea is a genus of bacteria associated with environmental sources and chronic lung colonization or infection in some people with cystic fibrosis. Species can be highly drug-resistant, so identification and susceptibility testing matter when infection is suspected.

name: pandoraea apista
clinical_significance: Pandoraea apista has been isolated from respiratory samples, particularly in people with cystic fibrosis, and may be associated with chronic lung infection. Its role can be difficult to distinguish from colonization, and antimicrobial resistance may limit treatment options.

name: pandoraea pnomenusa
clinical_significance: Pandoraea pnomenusa is an uncommon bacterium reported in respiratory infection in people with cystic fibrosis and in occasional other infections. Culture results require clinical correlation and susceptibility testing because resistance is common.

name: pandoraea sputorum
clinical_significance: Pandoraea sputorum is a rare opportunistic bacterium reported in respiratory and bloodstream infections. Its clinical importance depends on specimen source and evidence of disease; laboratory susceptibility results guide therapy.

name: paneth cells
clinical_significance: Paneth cells are intestinal epithelial cells that release antimicrobial peptides and help maintain gut-barrier defenses. Their dysfunction is studied in Crohn disease and other intestinal inflammation.

name: panhypopituitarism
clinical_significance: Failure of the pituitary gland to make most or all of its important hormones. It can cause tiredness, low blood pressure, infertility, growth or thyroid problems, and inability to respond normally to illness; lifelong hormone replacement may be needed.

name: panic
clinical_significance: Panic is sudden intense fear or distress with autonomic symptoms such as racing heart, sweating, trembling, breathlessness, or a sense of impending danger.

name: panic attack
clinical_significance: A sudden surge of intense fear or discomfort that usually reaches peak intensity within minutes. Symptoms may include a racing or pounding heart, sweating, trembling, breathlessness, chest pain, nausea, dizziness, tingling, a sense of losing control, or fear of dying. A first or atypical episode—especially with chest pain or breathing difficulty—should not be assumed to be panic until urgent medical causes are considered.

name: panic disorder
clinical_significance: Repeated unexpected panic attacks followed by ongoing worry about more attacks or major changes in behavior to avoid them. Attacks peak within minutes and may cause a racing heart, breathlessness, trembling, dizziness, or fear of dying.

name: panitumumab
clinical_significance: Panitumumab is an EGFR-targeting antibody used for selected metastatic colorectal cancers, with treatment choice guided by tumor RAS status and other molecular features. Skin toxicity, diarrhea, infusion reactions, and low magnesium can occur.

name: panniculitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the layer of fat beneath the skin, usually causing tender red or purple lumps, often on the legs. Causes include infection, immune disease, medicines, injury, and pancreatic disease; treatment depends on the cause.

name: panobinostat
clinical_significance: Panobinostat is a histone-deacetylase inhibitor used with other medicines for selected multiple myeloma after prior treatment. It can cause severe diarrhea, low blood counts, infection, and QT prolongation, requiring close monitoring.

name: pantoea
clinical_significance: Pantoea is a genus of environmental and plant-associated bacteria that can occasionally cause wound, bloodstream, or device-related infection. A positive culture should be assessed for contamination and confirmed with clinical context.

name: pantoea agglomerans
clinical_significance: Pantoea agglomerans can cause infection after plant-thorn injury and occasionally causes bloodstream or device-associated disease. It may be mistaken for a contaminant; specimen source and susceptibility testing inform treatment.

name: pantoprazole
clinical_significance: Pantoprazole is a proton-pump inhibitor used for reflux, ulcers, and prevention of selected acid-related injury. Long-term use should be periodically reviewed because it may be associated with nutrient deficiencies, enteric infection, kidney effects, or fractures in some patients.

name: pantothenic acid
clinical_significance: Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is required for coenzyme A and normal energy metabolism. Deficiency is rare, but severe malnutrition can affect multiple metabolic pathways; supplementation is not generally beneficial when intake is adequate.

name: panuveitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation affecting all the main internal layers around the eye, including the iris, the gel inside the eye, and the tissues near the retina. It can cause pain, redness, light sensitivity, floaters, and vision loss.

name: pap smear
clinical_significance: A screening test in which cells are collected from the cervix and examined for early changes that could become cervical cancer or for cancer itself. It may be done alone or with a test for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV).

name: papain
clinical_significance: A protein-breaking enzyme found in papaya latex. It is used in some foods and products, but evidence for many medicinal claims is limited; it can irritate tissues or cause allergic reactions.

name: papaverine
clinical_significance: Papaverine is a smooth-muscle relaxant used in selected settings, including vasospasm and certain vascular procedures. It can lower blood pressure and may cause heart-rhythm or liver complications, so route and monitoring matter.

name: papiliotrema laurentii
clinical_significance: Papiliotrema laurentii, formerly Cryptococcus laurentii, is an environmental yeast that rarely causes opportunistic infection, including fungemia or meningitis in vulnerable patients. Identification and antifungal susceptibility help guide care.

name: papillary adenocarcinoma
clinical_significance: Papillary adenocarcinoma is a malignant gland-forming tumor with papillary architecture; behavior and treatment depend on the organ of origin and tumor subtype. Pathology and molecular findings establish the diagnosis.

name: papillary adenoma
clinical_significance: A papillary adenoma is a usually benign glandular tumor with finger-like projections, but risk and management depend on the organ and histologic features. Tissue diagnosis may be needed to exclude carcinoma.

name: papillary cystadenocarcinoma
clinical_significance: Papillary cystadenocarcinoma is a malignant cystic glandular tumor with papillary structures. The primary organ, extent, and pathologic subtype determine prognosis and treatment.

name: papillary cystadenoma
clinical_significance: Papillary cystadenoma is a usually benign cystic tumor with papillary projections. Its clinical significance depends on the organ, size, symptoms, and pathology, since some lesions have borderline or malignant counterparts.

name: papillary dermis
clinical_significance: The papillary dermis is the superficial layer of skin beneath the epidermis and contains capillaries and sensory structures. Inflammation or injury here may affect skin healing, sensation, and visible rash patterns.

name: papillary muscle
clinical_significance: Muscles inside the lower chambers of the heart that connect by thin cords to the heart valves. They tighten when the heart contracts to keep the valves from turning inside out and prevent blood from flowing backward.

name: papilledema
clinical_significance: Swelling of the area where the optic nerve enters the eye because pressure inside the skull is raised. It can threaten vision and may result from bleeding, a mass, infection, or other serious illness.

name: papilloma
clinical_significance: A usually noncancerous growth from a surface lining, often appearing as a wart, skin tag, or small finger-like projection. Some are linked to human papillomavirus; the site, appearance, and tissue examination determine whether further treatment is needed.

name: papillomavirus
clinical_significance: A papillomavirus, especially human papillomavirus, which can cause warts and some anogenital, oropharyngeal, and other cancers.

name: papio
clinical_significance: Papio is a genus of baboons used in comparative biology and some biomedical research. Contact can involve zoonotic risks, so animal handling and research require appropriate biosafety and ethical oversight.

name: papio papio
clinical_significance: Papio papio, the Guinea baboon, is a nonhuman primate used in some biological research. Its clinical relevance is primarily comparative and veterinary, with biosafety precautions for zoonotic exposures.

name: papovavirus
clinical_significance: Papovavirus is an obsolete grouping that included viruses now classified as papillomaviruses and polyomaviruses. Correct modern virus identification matters because these families cause different diseases and have different clinical implications.

name: papulopustular rash
clinical_significance: A papulopustular rash consists of raised bumps and pus-filled lesions and can result from acne, rosacea, infection, medicines, or inflammatory disease. Rapid spread, fever, mucosal involvement, or severe pain requires prompt evaluation.

name: para-aortic node
clinical_significance: A para-aortic lymph node lies beside the aorta in the abdomen. Enlargement may reflect infection, inflammation, lymphoma, or metastatic cancer; size, imaging features, and clinical history determine whether further testing is needed.

name: parabacteroides
clinical_significance: Parabacteroides are anaerobic gut bacteria that are usually part of intestinal microbiota but can cause abdominal or bloodstream infection if they enter normally sterile sites. Culture and susceptibility results guide treatment.

name: parabacteroides johnsonii
clinical_significance: Parabacteroides johnsonii is an intestinal anaerobe with limited evidence as a human pathogen. Isolation from a sterile site may be clinically important, while detection in stool generally reflects gut microbiota.

name: parabacteroides merdae
clinical_significance: Parabacteroides merdae is a gut anaerobe that may cause opportunistic infection when intestinal barriers are disrupted. Its significance depends on the source and evidence of invasive disease.

name: parabrachial nucleus
clinical_significance: The parabrachial nucleus relays visceral, respiratory, pain, and taste signals and helps regulate breathing, arousal, and autonomic responses. Injury or abnormal activity can affect these functions.

name: paracentesis
clinical_significance: A procedure in which a clinician uses a needle to remove fluid from the abdomen. The fluid may be tested to find its cause or removed to relieve pressure and discomfort.

name: paracoccidioidomycosis
clinical_significance: Paracoccidioidomycosis is a systemic fungal infection acquired by inhaling Paracoccidioides from the environment, mainly in Latin America. It can cause chronic lung disease, mouth or skin lesions, lymph-node enlargement, and disseminated illness.

name: paracoccus bacteria
clinical_significance: Paracoccus bacteria are widespread environmental organisms and rarely cause human infection. A clinical isolate requires correlation with the specimen and symptoms to distinguish true infection from contamination.

name: paracoccus yeei
clinical_significance: Paracoccus yeei is a rare environmental bacterium reported in occasional bloodstream, peritoneal, or device-associated infection. Because it may contaminate samples, diagnosis depends on repeat or sterile-site isolation and clinical evidence.

name: paracrine communication
clinical_significance: Paracrine communication occurs when cells signal nearby cells through locally released molecules. It is important in immune responses, tissue repair, hormone regulation, and cancer biology.

name: paraffin
clinical_significance: A mixture of hydrocarbons used in laboratory tissue processing, topical preparations, and other applications; some forms are flammable.

name: paraganglia
clinical_significance: Paraganglia are clusters of neuroendocrine cells that help sense oxygen and regulate autonomic responses. Tumors arising from them can secrete catecholamines and cause hypertension, palpitations, or other symptoms.

name: paraganglioma
clinical_significance: A rare tumor arising from specialized nerve-related cells outside the adrenal glands. Some release hormones that cause high blood pressure, sweating, headaches, or a fast heartbeat; inherited risk may require genetic assessment.

name: paragonimiasis
clinical_significance: A parasitic infection caused by lung flukes, usually acquired by eating raw or undercooked freshwater crab or crayfish. It commonly affects the lungs and may cause a long-lasting cough, chest pain, fever, or blood-stained sputum.

name: paragonimus westermani
clinical_significance: Paragonimus westermani is a lung fluke acquired by eating raw or undercooked freshwater crab or crayfish. It can cause chronic cough, chest pain, or blood-stained sputum and may rarely migrate to the brain.

name: parahippocampal gyrus
clinical_significance: The parahippocampal gyrus supports memory and spatial processing and connects with the hippocampus. Injury or disease in this region can contribute to memory impairment or altered recognition of places.

name: parakeratosis
clinical_significance: Parakeratosis is retention of nuclei in the outer skin layer and occurs in disorders such as psoriasis, eczema, and some infections. In biopsy reports it is interpreted with the tissue pattern and other findings.

name: parallel lesion
clinical_significance: A parallel lesion is a separate lesion occurring alongside a primary lesion, often considered in imaging or pathology. The number, location, and relationship between lesions can affect staging, diagnosis, or treatment.

name: parallel study
clinical_significance: A parallel study compares groups or interventions over the same period, commonly in clinical trials. Randomization and appropriate controls help distinguish treatment effects from bias and natural disease progression.

name: paralysis
clinical_significance: Paralysis is loss of voluntary movement that may result from stroke, spinal-cord injury, nerve or muscle disease, or toxins. Sudden paralysis is an emergency; chronic paralysis may require respiratory, skin, bladder, mobility, and rehabilitation support.

name: paralytic ileus
clinical_significance: Failure of intestinal peristalsis without a mechanical blockage, causing abdominal distension, pain, vomiting, and absent or reduced bowel sounds.

name: paramecium
clinical_significance: Paramecium is a single-celled freshwater organism commonly used in biology education and research. It is not a human parasite or usual cause of disease.

name: parametrium
clinical_significance: The parametrium is connective tissue beside the uterus that contains blood vessels, lymphatics, and nerves. Cervical or uterine cancer staging considers parametrium involvement because it can alter treatment options.

name: paramyxoviridae
clinical_significance: Paramyxoviridae is a virus family that includes measles, mumps, parainfluenza, and respiratory syncytial viruses. Members cause respiratory or systemic infections, and prevention and treatment depend on the specific virus.

name: paramyxovirinae
clinical_significance: Paramyxovirinae is a former subfamily grouping of viruses such as measles, mumps, and parainfluenza viruses. Current classification may differ, but identifying the virus remains important for diagnosis and infection control.

name: paramyxovirus
clinical_significance: Paramyxoviruses include agents that cause measles, mumps, and respiratory infections. Some are highly contagious, so vaccination, isolation, and supportive or specific management depend on the virus.

name: paraneoplastic syndromes
clinical_significance: Paraneoplastic syndromes are symptoms caused by a cancer’s immune or hormone effects rather than direct tumor spread. They can precede cancer diagnosis and may affect the nervous system, skin, blood, kidneys, or endocrine function.

name: paranoia
clinical_significance: Paranoia involves persistent, excessive suspiciousness or beliefs of threat that may occur with psychosis, mood disorders, trauma, substance use, medicines, or neurologic illness. New or severe paranoia needs assessment for safety and underlying causes.

name: paranoid schizophrenia
clinical_significance: “Paranoid schizophrenia” is an older subtype label no longer used in current diagnostic classifications. Psychotic symptoms such as delusions or hallucinations are now assessed within the broader schizophrenia diagnosis and differential.

name: paraoxon
clinical_significance: Paraoxon is a highly toxic organophosphate formed from parathion and inhibits acetylcholinesterase. Exposure can cause cholinergic poisoning with secretions, breathing difficulty, weakness, seizures, or death and requires emergency treatment.

name: paraparesis
clinical_significance: Paraparesis is weakness in both legs from spinal-cord, nerve, brain, or muscle disease. New or worsening weakness, especially with back pain, numbness, or bladder or bowel changes, needs urgent assessment for cord compression or other serious causes.

name: paraphimosis
clinical_significance: Paraphimosis occurs when a retracted foreskin cannot be returned over the glans, causing painful swelling and possible loss of blood flow. Treatment involves promptly returning the foreskin to its normal position.

name: paraplegia
clinical_significance: Paralysis of both legs and usually part of the lower trunk. Paralysis of both legs and often part of the trunk, usually from spinal-cord or neurologic disease.

name: parapoxvirus
clinical_significance: Parapoxviruses cause animal diseases such as orf and can spread to people through contact with infected sheep, goats, or cattle. Human infection usually causes a localized skin nodule on the hand or arm.

name: paraproteinemia
clinical_significance: Paraproteinemia is the presence of an abnormal monoclonal immunoglobulin in blood or urine. It can be a precursor state or indicate myeloma, lymphoma, or another plasma-cell disorder and is interpreted with blood counts, kidney function, calcium, and symptoms.

name: parapsoriasis
clinical_significance: A group of chronic scaly patches or thin plaques that resemble psoriasis but have different causes and risks. Some forms remain stable, while large-plaque disease can rarely evolve into cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and needs follow-up.

name: paraquat
clinical_significance: A highly toxic herbicide. Ingestion can cause injury to the mouth and gastrointestinal tract, kidney failure, and delayed lung injury; severe poisoning has a high risk of death.

name: parasite
clinical_significance: An organism that lives on or inside another organism, called the host, and obtains food or shelter from it. Parasites may cause disease in the skin, intestine, blood, or organs.

name: parasite present
clinical_significance: “Parasite present” indicates detection of a parasite in a specimen or examination. Species identification, burden, and sample type determine whether treatment is needed and whether the finding represents active disease.

name: parasitic disease
clinical_significance: Parasitic diseases range from mild intestinal illness to severe malaria, tissue infection, or neurologic disease. Diagnosis depends on exposure history, organism-specific testing, and geography; effective treatment is often available.

name: parasitic infection
clinical_significance: Parasitic infections can involve the intestine, blood, skin, or internal organs and may cause anemia, inflammation, malnutrition, or organ damage. The specific parasite determines testing, treatment, and prevention; this entry replaces the truncated text with clinical context.

name: parasomnia
clinical_significance: A parasomnia is an undesirable movement, behavior, emotion, or experience occurring during sleep or transitions between sleep and wakefulness.

name: paraspeckles
clinical_significance: Paraspeckles are nuclear structures involved in RNA retention and gene regulation. They are studied in cell stress and cancer biology but have no routine diagnostic role.

name: paraspinal region
clinical_significance: The paraspinal region contains muscles, joints, nerves, and other tissues alongside the spine. Pain or swelling there may reflect strain, spinal infection, tumor, or nerve compression, so fever or neurologic deficits require prompt assessment.

name: parathion
clinical_significance: Parathion is a highly toxic organophosphate pesticide that inhibits acetylcholinesterase. Exposure can cause life-threatening cholinergic poisoning and requires immediate emergency and toxicology care.

name: parathyroid adenoma
clinical_significance: A parathyroid adenoma is a usually benign tumor of a parathyroid gland that can secrete excess parathyroid hormone and cause primary hyperparathyroidism with high calcium.

name: parathyroid disorder
clinical_significance: Parathyroid disorders alter calcium and phosphate balance and can affect bones, kidneys, muscles, and nerves. Blood calcium and parathyroid hormone measurements help distinguish overactivity, underactivity, and secondary causes.

name: parathyroid gland
clinical_significance: Parathyroid glands maintain calcium balance through parathyroid hormone. Excess or deficient hormone can cause kidney stones, bone loss, muscle symptoms, or abnormal blood calcium.

name: parathyroid hormone
clinical_significance: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) regulates blood calcium and phosphate. PTH is measured with calcium and kidney-function tests to evaluate hyperparathyroidism, hypoparathyroidism, and metabolic bone disease.

name: parathyroid hyperplasia
clinical_significance: Enlargement of one or more small glands behind the thyroid, causing them to release too much parathyroid hormone. This can raise blood calcium and may occur with kidney disease or inherited multiple-gland disorders.

name: parathyroid neoplasm
clinical_significance: A parathyroid neoplasm may be benign or malignant and can produce excess parathyroid hormone, leading to high calcium, kidney stones, bone disease, or neurocognitive symptoms. Biochemical testing and imaging guide evaluation and surgery.

name: parathyroidectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove one or more overactive parathyroid glands. It may treat primary or kidney-related hyperparathyroidism when hormone excess causes high calcium, kidney stones, bone disease, or other complications; calcium levels must be monitored afterward.

name: paratyphoid fever
clinical_significance: An infection caused by Salmonella Paratyphi bacteria, usually spread through contaminated food or water. It can cause prolonged fever, headache, weakness, abdominal symptoms, and sometimes serious complications without antibiotic treatment.

name: paraxial mesoderm
clinical_significance: Paraxial mesoderm forms structures including vertebrae, skeletal muscle, and dermis during embryonic development. Disruption can contribute to congenital abnormalities of the spine, ribs, or musculature.

name: parenchyma
clinical_significance: The working tissue of an organ, distinguished from its supporting framework, blood vessels, and connective tissue. For example, lung parenchyma performs gas exchange, while liver parenchyma processes nutrients and harmful substances.

name: parent
clinical_significance: Parent information can be clinically relevant to family history, consent, caregiving, and inherited-risk assessment. Records should distinguish biological, adoptive, and legal relationships when that distinction matters to care.

name: parenteral nutrition
clinical_significance: Nutrition given through a vein when the digestive tract cannot safely absorb enough nutrients. The solution can contain water, glucose, amino acids, fats, vitamins, and minerals. It can cause bloodstream infection, liver problems, or abnormal blood sugar and salts, so it requires monitoring.

name: parenting behavior
clinical_significance: Parenting behavior can influence child development, attachment, safety, and mental health, while also being affected by caregiver stress or illness. Clinical assessment should consider family context without treating a single behavior as a diagnosis.

name: paresis
clinical_significance: Partial weakness or incomplete paralysis of voluntary muscles. It may affect one limb, one side of the body, both legs, or all four limbs, depending on the nerves, brain, or spinal cord involved.

name: paresthesia
clinical_significance: An unusual sensation such as tingling, prickling, burning, pins and needles, or numbness. Brief symptoms often follow pressure on a nerve, while persistent or spreading symptoms need assessment for nerve or circulation problems.

name: pargyline
clinical_significance: Pargyline is an older monoamine-oxidase inhibitor once used for hypertension and studied in neurologic disease. It is not a routine current medicine; interactions with foods and other drugs can cause dangerous blood-pressure or neurologic effects.

name: paricalcitol
clinical_significance: Paricalcitol is a vitamin-D receptor activator used to reduce secondary hyperparathyroidism in selected chronic kidney disease, with monitoring for calcium and phosphate changes.

name: parietal bone
clinical_significance: One of two broad bones forming much of the skull's sides and roof. They protect the brain, meet along the top midline, and connect with several neighboring skull bones.

name: parietal lobe
clinical_significance: A part of the brain that processes touch, pain, temperature, body position, and spatial awareness. Damage may cause numbness, difficulty recognizing objects by touch, poor coordination, or trouble understanding where parts of the body are.

name: parietal pleura
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the parietal pleura causes sharp pain with breathing or coughing because this lining is sensitive to pain. Pleuritic pain may arise from pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, or other chest disease and needs assessment in context.

name: parinaric acid
clinical_significance: Parinaric acid is a polyunsaturated fatty acid used mainly as a fluorescent probe in studies of lipid oxidation and membranes. It has no routine diagnostic or therapeutic use.

name: parity
clinical_significance: Parity is the number of pregnancies that reached a viable gestational age, regardless of whether the infants were born alive or stillborn; it differs from gravidity.

name: parkinsonism
clinical_significance: A group of movement problems involving slowness, stiffness, shaking, or balance difficulty. Parkinson disease is one cause, but medicines, other brain disorders, and several less common conditions can produce similar symptoms.

name: Parkinson's disease
clinical_significance: A progressive disorder of the nervous system that mainly affects movement. It develops when nerve cells in a part of the brain called the substantia nigra become damaged or die. These cells normally make dopamine, a chemical messenger that helps produce smooth, purposeful movement. Reduced dopamine can cause tremor, slowness of movement, muscle stiffness, balance or walking problems, a softer voice, and smaller handwriting. Non-movement symptoms may include constipation, loss of smell, tiredness

name: paromomycin
clinical_significance: Paromomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used mainly in the intestine for selected parasitic infections and sometimes for other infections under specialist care.

name: paronychia
clinical_significance: Infection or inflammation of the skin around a fingernail or toenail, causing pain, redness, swelling, and sometimes pus. It may follow nail biting, injury, a hangnail, or repeated water exposure.

name: parosteal osteosarcoma
clinical_significance: Parosteal osteosarcoma is a usually lower-grade bone cancer that grows on the outer surface of a bone, often near the back of the thigh.

name: parotid gland
clinical_significance: The largest major saliva-producing gland, located in front of and below each ear. It releases saliva into the mouth near the upper back teeth and can become swollen from infection, blockage, inflammation, or a tumor.

name: parotid neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in a parotid salivary gland in front of or below the ear. Most are noncancerous, but some are cancerous; a painless lump, facial weakness, pain, or rapid growth may occur.

name: parotidectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part or all of a parotid salivary gland, usually because of a tumor. Possible complications include facial-nerve weakness, bleeding, infection, saliva leakage, numbness, or sweating while eating.

name: parotitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation or infection of one or both parotid salivary glands, which lie in front of and below the ears. It can cause painful swelling, fever, dry mouth, or pus near the upper back teeth. Causes include viruses such as mumps, bacteria, blocked ducts, dehydration, and autoimmune disease.

name: paroxetine
clinical_significance: Paroxetine is an SSRI used for depression and anxiety disorders. It can cause sexual dysfunction, weight change, and discontinuation symptoms if stopped abruptly and may interact with other serotonergic medicines.

name: paroxetine hydrochloride
clinical_significance: Paroxetine hydrochloride is an SSRI antidepressant used for depression and several anxiety-related disorders; it can cause sexual side effects and withdrawal symptoms if stopped abruptly.

name: paroxysmal hemicrania
clinical_significance: Paroxysmal hemicrania causes frequent, short attacks of severe one-sided orbital or temporal pain with autonomic symptoms such as tearing or nasal congestion. A complete response to indomethacin supports diagnosis, but treatment requires monitoring for gastrointestinal and kidney harms.

name: pars compacta
clinical_significance: A dopamine-producing part of the substantia nigra, a movement-control area deep in the brain. Loss of these nerve cells contributes to the slowness, stiffness, and tremor of Parkinson disease.

name: pars planitis
clinical_significance: A form of inflammation inside the eye, near the edge of the retina. It may cause floaters, blurred vision, and swelling or other retinal complications and is treated according to its severity and cause.

name: parthenogenesis
clinical_significance: Parthenogenesis is reproduction from an unfertilized egg in some species and has no natural role in human reproduction. It is relevant to developmental biology and reproductive research.

name: partial
clinical_significance: Partial means incomplete or involving only a portion, such as partial loss, partial response, partial thickness, or partial seizure; the specific meaning depends on context.

name: partial cystectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part of the urinary bladder, usually for a tumor or localized disease while leaving the rest of the bladder in place. The remaining bladder may need monitoring, and urinary or surgical complications can occur.

name: partial hysterectomy
clinical_significance: A common but imprecise term usually referring to supracervical or subtotal hysterectomy, in which the uterine body is removed while the cervix remains. The fallopian tubes and ovaries may or may not be removed separately.

name: partial nephrectomy
clinical_significance: Partial nephrectomy removes a kidney tumor while preserving functioning kidney tissue, often for localized renal cancer or selected benign lesions. Preserving kidney function is especially valuable when both kidneys are affected or baseline function is reduced.

name: partial remission
clinical_significance: A reduction in signs, symptoms, or measurable disease burden that does not meet criteria for complete remission; the definition depends on the disease and response criteria used.

name: participation
clinical_significance: A person’s involvement in life situations and activities, a central concept in rehabilitation and the International Classification of Functioning that extends beyond impairment alone.

name: particle size
clinical_significance: Particle size is the diameter or size distribution of particles in a powder, suspension, aerosol, or formulation, influencing dissolution, absorption, stability, and delivery.

name: parvimonas micra
clinical_significance: An anaerobic gram-positive bacterium found in the mouth and gastrointestinal tract that can cause dental, bone, joint, or bloodstream infections.

name: parvoviridae
clinical_significance: Parvoviridae includes parvovirus B19, which can cause fifth disease, transient aplastic crisis in people with hemolytic disorders, fetal anemia or hydrops, and arthralgia. Exposure matters during pregnancy and in patients with chronic anemia or immunosuppression.

name: parvovirus
clinical_significance: A small DNA virus; parvovirus B19 is the main human pathogen and can cause rash, joint symptoms, or red-cell aplasia.

name: passive immunization
clinical_significance: Protection produced by giving preformed antibodies, such as immunoglobulin or antivenom, which acts quickly but is temporary because the recipient does not generate durable immune memory.

name: paste
clinical_significance: A paste is a thick semisolid preparation that may be applied to skin or mucosa or used as a medicine vehicle. Formulation and route determine absorption, effectiveness, and safety.

name: pasteurella
clinical_significance: Pasteurella species commonly live in animal mouths and can cause rapidly developing wound infection after bites or scratches; they may also cause respiratory or invasive disease. Animal exposure and early wound care are important clinical clues.

name: pasteurella aerogenes
clinical_significance: Pasteurella aerogenes is a rare Pasteurella species; its recovery from a clinical sample should be interpreted with the source and evidence of infection.

name: pasteurella bettyae
clinical_significance: Pasteurella bettyae is a rare bacterium associated with the female genital tract and occasional urinary or bloodstream infection. Its significance depends on the site, symptoms, and evidence of invasive disease.

name: pasteurella canis
clinical_significance: Pasteurella canis is a bacterium found in dogs and cats that can cause wound or soft-tissue infection after an animal bite.

name: pasteurella multocida
clinical_significance: Pasteurella multocida is carried by cats and dogs and commonly causes cellulitis after bites or scratches, sometimes progressing rapidly. It can also cause respiratory or invasive infection in vulnerable people; prompt wound assessment and appropriate antibiotics reduce complications.

name: pasteurella pneumotropica
clinical_significance: Pasteurella pneumotropica is associated mainly with rodents and other animals and can rarely cause human wound or opportunistic infection. Animal exposure and laboratory susceptibility help guide interpretation and treatment.

name: pasteurellaceae
clinical_significance: Pasteurellaceae is a family of bacteria that includes Pasteurella and related animal-associated organisms capable of causing bite-wound and respiratory infections.

name: Patau syndrome
clinical_significance: A genetic condition caused by an extra copy of chromosome 13. It can cause severe problems involving brain development, growth, the eyes, heart, kidneys, hands or feet, and the lip or palate. Many affected pregnancies end before birth, and surviving infants need complex specialist care.

name: patch
clinical_significance: A skin patch is a flat area of altered color; its pattern, size, and change over time help distinguish pigment disorders, inflammation, infection, bruising, or malignancy. A new or changing pigmented lesion should be examined.

name: patch test
clinical_significance: Patch testing identifies delayed allergic contact dermatitis by exposing skin to suspected allergens and checking for a delayed reaction. It can help guide avoidance of substances causing persistent eczema.

name: patella
clinical_significance: The patella protects the knee and improves quadriceps leverage. Fracture, dislocation, or cartilage injury can impair knee extension and walking and may require imaging and orthopedic care.

name: patellar dislocation
clinical_significance: Complete displacement of the kneecap from the femoral groove, usually laterally, causing acute pain, deformity, swelling, and difficulty extending the knee.

name: patent ductus arteriosus
clinical_significance: A blood-vessel connection between the heart’s main lung artery and the aorta that remains open after birth instead of closing. It can send extra blood to the lungs and strain the heart; effects range from none to heart failure.

name: patent urachus
clinical_significance: A patent urachus is persistence of the fetal channel between the bladder and umbilicus after birth, allowing urine to drain from the umbilicus and predisposing to infection.

name: paternal behavior
clinical_significance: Paternal behavior can influence caregiving, attachment, and child development, while caregiver health and stress can affect family wellbeing. In clinical settings, assessment should focus on safety, support, and the child’s needs rather than assumptions about family roles.

name: pathogen
clinical_significance: An organism or infectious agent that can enter the body and cause disease. Examples include viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites.

name: pathogenesis
clinical_significance: The way a disease begins and develops, including its causes, changes in cells or tissues, and progression over time. Understanding pathogenesis helps explain symptoms, complications, and possible treatment targets.

name: pathogenicity
clinical_significance: Pathogenicity describes how likely and how severely a microorganism causes disease in a host. It depends on microbial traits, exposure, and host defenses and informs infection risk, diagnosis, and prevention.

name: pathologic dilatation
clinical_significance: Abnormal widening of a hollow organ, duct, blood vessel, or other structure beyond its expected size because of obstruction, weakness, pressure, or disease.

name: pathologic ossification
clinical_significance: Abnormal formation of bone in soft tissue or in a location where bone should not develop, as in heterotopic ossification after trauma, neurologic injury, or surgery.

name: pathologic process
clinical_significance: A pathologic process is an abnormal biological change that produces disease, such as infection, inflammation, ischemia, degeneration, abnormal growth, or immune injury.

name: pathologic response
clinical_significance: A pathologic response is an abnormal reaction of cells, tissues, or organs to injury, infection, immune activation, toxins, or other stressors that contributes to disease.

name: pathological fracture
clinical_significance: A pathologic fracture occurs in bone weakened by cancer, osteoporosis, infection, or another disorder and may follow minimal force. It can be the first sign of underlying disease and usually requires evaluation of the bone and cause.

name: pathologist
clinical_significance: A pathologist is a physician who diagnoses disease by examining tissues, cells, blood, or body fluids and may guide laboratory testing, cancer classification, and treatment decisions.

name: pathology
clinical_significance: Study of disease. Includes general pathology (cell injury, inflammation, neoplasia) and systemic pathology (organ-specific diseases).

name: patient
clinical_significance: A person receiving medical care, advice, examination, or treatment. Good care includes listening to the patient's concerns, explaining choices clearly, respecting informed decisions, protecting privacy, and reducing avoidable harm.

name: patient care
clinical_significance: Patient care includes assessment, treatment, prevention, communication, and support tailored to a person’s needs and goals. Coordination and clear handoffs help reduce errors and improve outcomes.

name: patient discharge
clinical_significance: Patient discharge marks transition from a care setting to home or another facility. Medication reconciliation, follow-up plans, warning signs, equipment, and caregiver instructions reduce preventable complications and readmission.

name: patient observation
clinical_significance: Systematic monitoring of a patient’s symptoms, vital signs, examination findings, behavior, and response to treatment to detect deterioration or guide management.

name: patient rights
clinical_significance: Ethical and legal protections for people receiving care, including informed consent, privacy, access to information, respectful treatment, participation in decisions, and refusal of treatment where lawful.

name: patient safety
clinical_significance: Preventing avoidable harm during healthcare. It includes accurate identification, safe prescribing and medicine use, infection prevention, clear communication, fall prevention, and checking procedures and results.

name: patient-controlled analgesia
clinical_significance: Patient-controlled analgesia lets a patient self-administer clinician-programmed doses, commonly through an intravenous pump. Only the patient should press the control; sedation and breathing are monitored because opioid overdose can occur.

name: paxillin
clinical_significance: Paxillin is a focal-adhesion adaptor protein that links integrin signaling to the actin cytoskeleton and helps regulate cell adhesion, migration, and mechanical sensing.

name: pazopanib
clinical_significance: An oral tyrosine-kinase inhibitor targeting vascular endothelial growth factor and other receptors, used for selected advanced renal-cell carcinoma and soft-tissue sarcoma.

name: peanut oil
clinical_significance: Peanut oil is oil extracted from peanuts; refined oil usually contains little allergenic protein, whereas unrefined products may trigger reactions in susceptible people.

name: peau d'orange
clinical_significance: Peau d’orange is dimpled skin resembling an orange peel, caused by edema tethered around hair follicles; it can occur with breast cancer, infection, or lymphatic obstruction.

name: pectin
clinical_significance: Pectin is a soluble plant fiber used as a food ingredient and thickener. Dietary pectin can affect stool consistency, while some medicines or supplements may alter absorption when taken together.

name: pectinate line
clinical_significance: A boundary inside the anal canal where the lining, nerve supply, blood vessels, and lymph drainage change. Conditions above and below this line may cause different symptoms and may be treated differently.

name: pectoral girdle
clinical_significance: The pectoral girdle consists of the clavicles and scapulae, attaching the upper limbs to the trunk and providing broad surfaces for shoulder and arm movement.

name: pectoralis muscles
clinical_significance: The pectoralis major and minor muscles of the chest, which move and stabilize the shoulder and assist with movements such as pushing, adduction, and breathing.

name: pectus excavatum
clinical_significance: A chest-wall shape present from childhood in which the breastbone is pushed inward, sometimes called funnel chest. It may cause no symptoms, but severe cases can affect exercise, breathing, posture, or emotional wellbeing.

name: pediatric AIDS
clinical_significance: Pediatric AIDS is advanced HIV infection in a child, with severe immune suppression or AIDS-defining illness; antiretroviral therapy and prevention of opportunistic infection are essential.

name: pediatric nursing
clinical_significance: Pediatric nursing provides age-appropriate care to infants, children, and adolescents, accounting for growth, development, family involvement, communication, safety, and medication differences.

name: pediatric obesity
clinical_significance: Excess body fat in a child or adolescent, assessed by comparing weight and height with other children of the same age and sex. It can affect breathing, joints, blood sugar, sleep, and emotional wellbeing; assessment should be supportive and non-stigmatizing.

name: pediatrician
clinical_significance: Pediatricians provide preventive care, vaccination, developmental screening, and treatment for infants, children, and adolescents. Age-specific dosing and recognition of developmental or safeguarding concerns are central to pediatric care.

name: pediatrics
clinical_significance: Pediatrics addresses health from infancy through adolescence, including growth, development, vaccination, acute illness, chronic disease, and family support. Treatment and communication must be appropriate to the child’s age and capacity.

name: pedigree
clinical_significance: A family diagram that shows relationships and who has a particular trait or disease. Doctors and genetic counselors use it to look for inheritance patterns and estimate the chance that relatives may be affected.

name: pediococcus
clinical_significance: Pediococcus is a genus of lactic-acid bacteria used in food fermentation and rarely implicated in opportunistic human infection. A blood or sterile-site isolate should be assessed carefully, especially in a medically vulnerable patient.

name: pediococcus pentosaceus
clinical_significance: Pediococcus pentosaceus is mainly used in fermented foods and is rarely a human pathogen. It can occasionally cause opportunistic bloodstream infection, so recovery from a sterile site requires clinical assessment.

name: pedophilia
clinical_significance: A continuing sexual interest in children who have not reached puberty. The term describes an interest and is not synonymous with pedophilic disorder; sexual contact with a child is abuse and cannot be consensual.

name: pedunculate
clinical_significance: Pedunculate describes a structure, lesion, or polyp attached by a narrow stalk rather than a broad base.

name: peer review
clinical_significance: Peer review evaluates research or clinical work by independent experts before publication or adoption. It can improve quality but does not guarantee that findings are correct, unbiased, or applicable to every patient.

name: pefloxacin
clinical_significance: Pefloxacin is an older fluoroquinolone antibiotic used in some countries for selected infections. Serious class risks include tendon injury, nerve effects, central nervous system reactions, and resistance, limiting its use.

name: pegargiminase
clinical_significance: Pegargiminase is an investigational pegylated enzyme that depletes arginine and has been studied in cancers that cannot synthesize enough of this amino acid. It remains a clinical-trial therapy, with toxicity and tumor biology guiding study.

name: pegaspargase
clinical_significance: Pegaspargase is a long-acting asparaginase used in combination chemotherapy for acute lymphoblastic leukemia. It can cause allergic reactions, pancreatitis, liver injury, blood clots, or bleeding and requires laboratory monitoring.

name: pegdinetanib
clinical_significance: An investigational targeted anticancer agent studied for inhibition of platelet-derived growth factor receptors and tumor-associated vasculature. It is not an established routine treatment, and its clinical role depends on trial evidence.

name: pegfilgrastim
clinical_significance: Pegfilgrastim stimulates neutrophil production to reduce infection risk from chemotherapy-related neutropenia. Bone pain is common, and rare complications include splenic rupture, serious allergy, and lung injury.

name: peldesine
clinical_significance: Peldesine is an investigational purine nucleoside phosphorylase inhibitor studied for immune and infectious diseases. It has no established routine clinical role.

name: pelitrexol
clinical_significance: Pelitrexol is an investigational antifolate chemotherapy drug studied for cancer. It is not a standard current treatment and remains of research significance.

name: pellagra
clinical_significance: Pellagra is severe niacin deficiency, classically causing dermatitis, diarrhea, and cognitive or neurologic changes. It can progress to life-threatening illness but is treatable with niacin and correction of the underlying nutritional or absorption problem.

name: pellet
clinical_significance: A pellet is a small compacted mass of medication, material, or tissue; drug pellets may be formulated for implantation or controlled release.

name: pelvic bone
clinical_significance: The ring of bones formed by the paired hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx that supports the trunk, protects pelvic organs, and transmits weight to the lower limbs.

name: pelvic cavity
clinical_significance: The space inside the lower part of the body enclosed by the pelvic bones. It contains the bladder, rectum, reproductive organs, blood vessels, nerves, and supporting muscles.

name: pelvic diaphragm
clinical_significance: The group of muscles and supporting tissue forming the floor of the pelvis. It supports the bladder, bowel, and reproductive organs and helps control urine and stool.

name: pelvic examination
clinical_significance: Clinical inspection and palpation of the external genitalia, vagina, cervix, uterus, and adnexa to evaluate bleeding, pain, discharge, lesions, pregnancy-related findings, or infection.

name: pelvic exenteration
clinical_significance: Very extensive surgery removing some pelvic organs and nearby tissues, usually for selected cancers that have returned or grown locally when less extensive treatment cannot control them. Recovery is prolonged and reconstruction may be needed.

name: pelvic girdle
clinical_significance: The pelvic girdle transfers body weight between the spine and legs and protects pelvic organs. Fracture or congenital variation can affect mobility, childbirth planning, and nearby nerves or blood vessels.

name: pelvic infection
clinical_significance: An infection involving pelvic organs or tissues, including pelvic inflammatory disease, urinary infection, abscess, or postoperative infection.

name: pelvic inflammatory disease
clinical_significance: Infection and inflammation of the upper reproductive tract, including the uterus, fallopian tubes, and nearby tissues. It often follows an ascending infection: chlamydia and gonorrhea are important causes, but other genital-tract bacteria can also be involved. Symptoms vary and may include lower-abdominal pain, unusual discharge or bleeding, pain during sex, or tenderness on examination; fever may occur, but some cases cause mild symptoms or none.

name: pelvic kidney
clinical_significance: A kidney that remains in the pelvis rather than ascending to its usual lumbar position during development; it may be asymptomatic or associated with abnormal drainage, stones, infection, or vascular anatomy.

name: pelvic lymphadenectomy
clinical_significance: Pelvic lymphadenectomy removes pelvic lymph nodes for cancer staging or treatment. The number of involved nodes can alter prognosis and adjuvant therapy; complications include lymphocele, lymphedema, and vascular or nerve injury.

name: pelvic mass
clinical_significance: A lump or abnormal enlargement in the pelvis arising from reproductive, urinary, gastrointestinal, lymphatic, or other tissues.

name: pelvic neoplasm
clinical_significance: A pelvic neoplasm is an abnormal growth in the pelvis, arising from organs, bones, soft tissues, or lymph nodes; it may be benign or malignant.

name: pelvic pain
clinical_significance: Pain in the lower abdomen, pelvis, or area between the genitals and anus. Causes include reproductive, urinary, bowel, muscle, nerve, and other conditions. Sudden severe pain, pregnancy, fever, fainting, vomiting, or heavy bleeding needs urgent assessment.

name: pelvic viscus
clinical_significance: An organ located in the pelvic cavity, such as the bladder, rectum, uterus, ovaries, prostate, or related structures.

name: pelvis
clinical_significance: Pelvic structure and anatomy affect walking, childbirth, urinary and reproductive function, and access for surgery. Pelvic injury can damage major vessels or organs and may require urgent evaluation.

name: pemetrexed
clinical_significance: Pemetrexed is a folate-antimetabolite chemotherapy drug that inhibits several enzymes involved in nucleotide synthesis, used especially for mesothelioma and nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer; folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce toxicity.

name: pemetrexed disodium
clinical_significance: The disodium salt of pemetrexed, an antifolate chemotherapy medicine used with other treatment for selected non-small-cell lung cancer and mesothelioma.

name: pemoline
clinical_significance: Pemoline is a stimulant formerly used for attention-deficit disorders; serious liver toxicity led to withdrawal or severe restriction in many countries.

name: pemphigoid gestationis
clinical_significance: Pemphigoid gestationis is an autoimmune blistering disorder that usually arises during pregnancy or shortly after birth, often beginning with intense itch around the navel. It can flare around delivery and may affect fetal growth or cause transient newborn rash, so obstetric and dermatologic care is needed.

name: pemphigus
clinical_significance: Pemphigus causes fragile skin or mucosal blisters and erosions that can lead to pain, dehydration, infection, and difficulty eating. Diagnosis and treatment require specialist care; systemic immunosuppression carries infection and other risks.

name: penbutolol
clinical_significance: Penbutolol is a beta-blocker formerly used for high blood pressure; it can slow the heart rate and worsen asthma in susceptible people.

name: penclomedine
clinical_significance: Penclomedine is an investigational anticancer compound studied for solid tumors. It has no established routine clinical use and is mainly of research significance.

name: pendulous
clinical_significance: Pendulous means hanging loosely from a supporting structure, as in a pedunculated lesion, drooping tissue, or an organ suspended by a stalk.

name: penetrance
clinical_significance: The proportion of people with a particular gene change who develop the related trait or condition. Penetrance may be complete, incomplete, or influenced by other factors.

name: penicillamine
clinical_significance: Penicillamine is a chelating and immunomodulatory medicine used for Wilson disease and selected other conditions. It can cause severe kidney, blood, skin, or autoimmune complications, so blood and urine monitoring are essential.

name: penicillin
clinical_significance: A family of antibiotics that kill bacteria by stopping them from making cell walls. Different types treat different bacterial infections; they do not work against viruses. Allergy, resistance, and kidney problems can affect the choice of medicine.

name: penicillin G
clinical_significance: Penicillin G is an injectable penicillin antibiotic used for infections such as syphilis and selected streptococcal or other susceptible bacterial infections.

name: penicillin V
clinical_significance: Penicillin V is an oral penicillin antibiotic used for selected susceptible infections, including some throat and dental infections.

name: penicillium
clinical_significance: A genus of molds that includes species used to make medicines and foods and species that can cause allergy or opportunistic infection.

name: penile disease
clinical_significance: A disorder affecting the penis, including infection, inflammation, erectile or structural disease, trauma, skin disease, or malignancy.

name: penile erection
clinical_significance: Stiffening and enlargement of the penis when blood fills erectile tissue and is temporarily held there. It can occur with sexual or other stimulation; persistent difficulty getting or keeping an erection may be erectile dysfunction.

name: penile infection
clinical_significance: Infection of the penis or foreskin caused by bacteria, fungi, viruses, or parasites, producing pain, redness, discharge, sores, or swelling.

name: penile leukoplakia
clinical_significance: A persistent white patch on penile skin or mucosa that may reflect irritation, inflammation, or a precancerous disorder and requires assessment.

name: penile prosthesis
clinical_significance: An implanted device used to produce an erection when erectile dysfunction has not improved with other treatments. It may be inflatable or bendable. Surgery can cause infection, bleeding, pain, device failure, or erosion into nearby tissue.

name: penis
clinical_significance: An external genital organ that contains the outlet for urine and can deliver sperm during sexual activity. It becomes firm when filled with blood during an erection and contains sensitive tissue, skin, blood vessels, and nerves.

name: penis carcinoma
clinical_significance: Penis carcinoma is cancer of the penis, most often arising from skin or squamous cells and sometimes linked to HPV infection.

name: penoscrotal transposition
clinical_significance: A congenital difference in which the penis and scrotum are positioned abnormally relative to each other, often associated with hypospadias or other genital and urinary anomalies.

name: pentadecanoic acid
clinical_significance: Pentadecanoic acid is a saturated odd-chain fatty acid found in dairy and some foods. Blood levels are studied as dietary and metabolic biomarkers, but they are not a standalone clinical test.

name: pentamidine
clinical_significance: An antimicrobial medicine used for certain parasitic infections and Pneumocystis pneumonia, with potentially serious side effects.

name: pentamidine isethionate
clinical_significance: An antiprotozoal and antimicrobial drug used in selected cases of Pneumocystis pneumonia, leishmaniasis, trypanosomiasis, and other infections; toxicity includes hypoglycemia, kidney injury, and arrhythmia.

name: pentatrichomonas hominis
clinical_significance: Pentatrichomonas hominis is a flagellated intestinal protozoan generally regarded as nonpathogenic; finding it in stool usually indicates exposure to fecal contamination.

name: pentetic acid
clinical_significance: A chelating compound that binds metal ions and is used in selected radiopharmaceuticals, contrast agents, or laboratory applications.

name: pentobarbital
clinical_significance: Pentobarbital is a barbiturate sedative used in limited settings, including selected seizure emergencies or medically controlled sedation. It can suppress breathing and blood pressure and is dangerous with opioids or alcohol.

name: pentosan polysulfate
clinical_significance: A semi-synthetic sulfated polysaccharide used for selected bladder pain syndrome and historically as an anticoagulant; prolonged use can cause pigmentary maculopathy and bleeding.

name: pentose
clinical_significance: A pentose is a five-carbon sugar, including ribose in RNA and deoxyribose in DNA, and participates in nucleotide and carbohydrate metabolism.

name: pentoxifylline
clinical_significance: A methylxanthine derivative that improves red-cell flexibility and is used in some countries for peripheral vascular disease; benefit varies by condition.

name: pentylenetetrazole
clinical_significance: Pentylenetetrazole is a convulsant chemical historically used to provoke seizures in laboratory research and formerly in obsolete seizure therapy. It is not a human treatment and exposure can cause life-threatening seizures.

name: peplomycin
clinical_significance: Peplomycin is a bleomycin-related chemotherapy medicine used in some countries for selected cancers; lung toxicity is an important risk.

name: pepsin A
clinical_significance: Pepsin A is a stomach enzyme that digests protein; pepsin in throat samples is sometimes studied as a marker of reflux, but the test is not definitive on its own.

name: pepsinogen
clinical_significance: Pepsinogen is a precursor of the stomach enzyme pepsin. Blood pepsinogen levels may be used with other tests to assess gastric mucosal changes or atrophy, but they do not diagnose stomach cancer by themselves.

name: peptic esophagitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation and injury of the esophageal lining caused mainly by repeated gastroesophageal reflux of acid or bile, producing heartburn, chest discomfort, swallowing pain, or strictures.

name: peptic ulcer
clinical_significance: An open sore in the lining of the stomach or duodenum, most commonly caused by \textit{Helicobacter pylori} infection or NSAID use.

name: peptichemio
clinical_significance: Peptichemio is an investigational chemotherapy compound studied for cancer and is not a routine approved treatment.

name: peptide
clinical_significance: A short chain of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. Peptides can form parts of proteins or act independently as hormones, neurotransmitters, immune signals, or medicines.

name: peptide biosynthesis
clinical_significance: The process by which cells make peptides, short chains of amino acids, by linking amino acids according to genetic instructions. Some peptides act as hormones, neurotransmitters, or signals between cells.

name: peptide hormone
clinical_significance: A hormone made of amino acids that binds a cell-surface receptor and regulates processes such as metabolism, growth, reproduction, stress, and fluid balance.

name: peptide library
clinical_significance: A peptide library is a collection of peptides used to identify antibody binding, enzyme activity, or candidate drug targets. It supports research and assay development rather than direct patient diagnosis unless incorporated into a validated test.

name: peptide metabolism
clinical_significance: The body's production, breakdown, and use of peptides. These processes regulate signaling molecules, hormones, digestion, and protein turnover.

name: peptide transport
