clinical_significance: Abnormally rapid breathing. It may occur with exercise or anxiety, but can also signal fever, low oxygen, pneumonia, blood clot in the lung, heart failure, severe infection, pain, or acid buildup.

name: tacrine
clinical_significance: Tacrine is an older acetylcholinesterase inhibitor formerly used for Alzheimer disease; liver toxicity and frequent dosing led to its replacement by safer alternatives.

name: tacrolimus
clinical_significance: A medicine that suppresses immune activity. It is used to prevent rejection after an organ transplant and, in different preparations, to treat eczema and some other inflammatory skin conditions; infection risk and other side effects require monitoring.

name: tactile agnosia
clinical_significance: Inability to recognize a familiar object by touch even though basic sensation is intact. It usually results from a problem in areas of the brain that interpret sensory information.

name: tadalafil
clinical_significance: Tadalafil is a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor used for erectile dysfunction, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and pulmonary hypertension; headache, flushing, hypotension, priapism, and dangerous nitrate interactions are important risks.

name: taenia
clinical_significance: A group of tapeworms that includes Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, and Taenia saginata, the beef tapeworm. Adult worms can live in the intestine; T. solium eggs can also cause cysts in body tissues.

name: taenia saginata
clinical_significance: Taenia saginata is the beef tapeworm acquired from undercooked infected beef; intestinal infection may cause abdominal symptoms or passage of motile segments but does not usually cause human cysticercosis.

name: taenia solium
clinical_significance: A pork tapeworm that infects people who eat undercooked pork or swallow its eggs. Adult worms live in the intestine, while eggs can cause cysticercosis, including dangerous infection of the brain.

name: taeniasis
clinical_significance: Intestinal infection caused by adult \textit{Taenia} tapeworms. It is usually acquired by eating undercooked beef or pork containing larval cysts. It may cause abdominal discomfort, nausea, diarrhea, or passage of worm segments. Swallowing \textit{Taenia solium} eggs causes cysticercosis in tissues, which is a different infection.

name: tail
clinical_significance: Tail may describe the end portion of an organ, cell, or molecule; precise anatomical context matters because symptoms and procedures depend on the structure involved.

name: takayasu arteritis
clinical_significance: An immune-mediated large-vessel vasculitis affecting the aorta and its major branches. Inflammation can narrow, block, or weaken these arteries, causing limb pain with use, weak or unequal pulses, blood-pressure differences, bruits, fever, fatigue, vision or neurological symptoms, or organ ischemia.

name: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
clinical_significance: A temporary weakening of the heart muscle, often after intense emotional or physical stress. It can resemble a heart attack with chest pain and ECG changes, but the heart arteries are usually not blocked; most people recover with appropriate care.

name: talabostat
clinical_significance: Talabostat is an investigational enzyme inhibitor studied for cancer and immune effects; it is not standard therapy, and clinical-trial evidence guides any potential use.

name: talactoferrin alfa
clinical_significance: Talactoferrin alfa is a recombinant lactoferrin-related immunomodulatory protein studied as a treatment or adjunct in cancer and infectious disease.

name: talaporfin sodium
clinical_significance: Talaporfin sodium is a photosensitizer used or studied in photodynamic therapy, where light activation produces local cytotoxic effects.

name: talc
clinical_significance: A soft mineral; inhalation of talc dust can cause talcosis, and contaminated injected talc can injure vessels and lungs.

name: talipes
clinical_significance: A deformity of the foot and ankle present at birth or acquired later. It may affect position, flexibility, walking, and shoe fit, and treatment depends on severity, cause, age, and function.

name: talipes calcaneovalgus
clinical_significance: A foot deformity in which the heel is turned outward and the ankle is dorsiflexed so the foot points upward; flexible newborn cases often improve, while rigid cases need evaluation.

name: tall stature
clinical_significance: Tall stature means height substantially above the expected range for age and sex and may be familial, endocrine, genetic, or associated with another condition.

name: talotrexin
clinical_significance: Talotrexin is an investigational antifolate anticancer drug; it is not routine treatment, and clinical studies evaluate its effectiveness and adverse effects.

name: talus
clinical_significance: The ankle bone between the shinbones and the heel and foot bones. It transfers body weight through the ankle and has a limited blood supply, so some fractures can damage the bone and cause delayed healing or bone death.

name: tamoxifen
clinical_significance: A medicine that blocks or changes oestrogen effects in breast tissue. It treats and helps prevent some breast cancers, but can increase the risk of blood clots and, rarely, cancer of the uterine lining.

name: tamoxifen citrate
clinical_significance: The citrate salt of tamoxifen, a selective estrogen-receptor modulator used to treat or prevent some breast cancers; blood clots and endometrial cancer are important uncommon risks.

name: tamsulosin
clinical_significance: Tamsulosin relaxes smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder outlet to improve urinary symptoms from benign prostate enlargement; dizziness and low blood pressure can occur.

name: tamsulosin hydrochloride
clinical_significance: The hydrochloride salt of tamsulosin, an alpha-1 blocker that relaxes prostate and bladder-neck muscle to improve urinary symptoms from benign prostatic enlargement.

name: tandutinib
clinical_significance: Tandutinib is an investigational kinase inhibitor studied for cancer; it is not an established treatment and may affect heart rhythm, liver function, and blood counts.

name: tanespimycin
clinical_significance: Tanespimycin is an investigational Hsp90 inhibitor studied in cancer; it is not routine therapy, and trial use requires monitoring for gastrointestinal, hepatic, and other toxicities.

name: Tangier disease
clinical_significance: A rare inherited disorder causing extremely low HDL cholesterol and buildup of cholesterol in tissues. It may cause enlarged yellow-orange tonsils, enlarged liver or spleen, nerve symptoms, or clouding of the cornea; cardiovascular risk varies and specialist testing is needed.

name: tannic acid
clinical_significance: Tannic acid is a plant polyphenol used in some topical and laboratory products; ingestion or excessive exposure can irritate tissue and interfere with nutrient or medicine absorption.

name: tanomastat
clinical_significance: Tanomastat is an investigational matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor studied as an anticancer drug; it is not an established therapy, and clinical trials did not establish routine benefit.

name: tantalum
clinical_significance: A corrosion-resistant metal used in some surgical implants and medical devices; exposure risk depends on the form, dose, and route.

name: tapentadol
clinical_significance: A prescription pain medicine with opioid-like and nerve-signal effects, used for selected moderate or severe pain. It can cause sleepiness, constipation, dependence, seizures, and dangerously slow breathing, especially with alcohol or other sedatives.

name: taq polymerase
clinical_significance: Taq polymerase amplifies DNA in PCR testing; enzyme performance and contamination control affect the accuracy of molecular diagnostic results.

name: tardive dyskinesia
clinical_significance: Repeated, involuntary movements that may develop after long-term use of some antipsychotic medicines. They often affect the mouth, tongue, face, arms, or legs and may continue after the medicine is reduced or stopped.

name: tarenflurbil
clinical_significance: Tarenflurbil is an investigational anti-amyloid drug studied for Alzheimer disease; clinical studies did not establish it as an effective treatment, and it is not routine care.

name: target population
clinical_significance: A target population is the group a study or intervention is intended to address; clear definition affects screening, eligibility, and whether findings generalize to patients.

name: targeted therapy
clinical_significance: Treatment that acts on a specific change or feature helping cancer cells grow, survive, or spread. Testing the tumor may identify a target and predict benefit. These treatments can be more selective than traditional chemotherapy but may still cause serious side effects and resistance.

name: tariquidar
clinical_significance: Tariquidar is an investigational inhibitor of drug-efflux transporters studied to alter cancer-drug resistance; it is not an established treatment and may change exposure to other medicines.

name: Tarlov cyst
clinical_significance: A fluid-filled sac around a nerve near the lower spine. Many cause no symptoms and are found by chance, but a larger cyst can cause lower-back or buttock pain, numbness, weakness, or bladder, bowel, or sexual problems.

name: tarsal bones
clinical_significance: The seven bones of the hindfoot and midfoot that connect the ankle to the metatarsals and form the arches and load-bearing framework of the foot.

name: tarsal coalition
clinical_significance: An abnormal connection between two foot bones, usually present from birth. It can make the foot stiff or flat and cause pain, repeated ankle sprains, or difficulty walking, often becoming noticeable during adolescence.

name: tarsal joints
clinical_significance: The articulations among the tarsal bones and between the tarsals and metatarsals, providing stability and controlled movement for walking and adapting the foot to surfaces.

name: taste
clinical_significance: The sensation produced by the interaction of chemical substances with taste receptor

name: taste bud
clinical_significance: A taste bud is a cluster of specialized sensory cells in papillae of the tongue and some oral tissues that detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami stimuli and transmits signals through cranial nerves.

name: taste disorder
clinical_significance: Abnormal reduction, loss, distortion, or unpleasant alteration of taste, caused by infection, medications, oral disease, nerve injury, neurologic disease, or other factors.

name: tat genes
clinical_significance: Tat genes encode HIV regulatory proteins that control viral gene expression and replication; they are research targets but not routine clinical tests.

name: tat protein
clinical_significance: The HIV Tat protein promotes viral gene expression and replication and is studied as a target for vaccines and antivirals; it is not a routine diagnostic marker.

name: tata box
clinical_significance: The TATA box is a DNA promoter sequence that helps initiate gene transcription; mutations can alter gene expression and are relevant to molecular genetics research.

name: tatlockia micdadei
clinical_significance: Tatlockia micdadei is a Legionella species that can cause pneumonia, particularly in immunocompromised patients; it is detected by specialized laboratory methods and requires appropriate antimicrobial treatment.

name: tattoo site
clinical_significance: A tattoo site can develop infection, allergic reaction, or scarring; redness that spreads, increasing pain, pus, or fever warrants medical evaluation.

name: tatumella
clinical_significance: Tatumella is a genus of environmental bacteria that rarely causes human infection; positive cultures require species confirmation and clinical correlation.

name: tatumella ptyseos
clinical_significance: Tatumella ptyseos is an uncommon environmental bacterium reported in rare human infections; isolate significance depends on the source, symptoms, and immune status.

name: tau protein
clinical_significance: Tau protein stabilizes neuronal microtubules; abnormal tau accumulation is a feature of Alzheimer disease and several other neurodegenerative disorders and is studied in biomarkers and imaging.

name: taurine
clinical_significance: Taurine is a sulfur-containing compound involved in normal cell, nerve, muscle, and bile-acid function. It is present in foods and added to some energy drinks; high caffeine intake in such drinks can be harmful.

name: taurolidine
clinical_significance: Taurolidine is an antimicrobial compound used in some catheter-lock solutions to reduce catheter-related bloodstream infection; local protocols and device compatibility guide use.

name: tausonia pullulans
clinical_significance: Tausonia pullulans is an environmental yeast rarely associated with human infection; culture findings should be evaluated for contamination versus opportunistic disease.

name: taxis response
clinical_significance: Taxis response is directed movement of a cell or organism toward or away from a stimulus; in medicine, related responses explain immune-cell migration, infection behavior, and tissue signaling.

name: Tay-Sachs disease
clinical_significance: A rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder usually caused by disease-causing variants in the \textit{HEXA} gene. Reduced or absent beta-hexosaminidase A activity prevents normal breakdown of GM2 ganglioside, which accumulates mainly in neurons. The infantile form causes progressive loss of previously acquired skills, weakness, an exaggerated startle response, seizures, and vision changes; juvenile and late-onset forms may progress more slowly and have variable movement, speech, psychi

name: tazarotene
clinical_significance: A topical retinoid used for acne, plaque psoriasis, and some sun-damaged skin. It can irritate skin and increases sun sensitivity; pregnancy precautions are important.

name: tazobactam
clinical_significance: Tazobactam inhibits many bacterial beta-lactamases and is combined with antibiotics such as piperacillin to treat susceptible serious infections; cultures and susceptibility guide use.

name: T-cell activation
clinical_significance: T-cell activation initiates immune responses against infection and cancer; excessive or misdirected activation contributes to autoimmune disease, while immunosuppressive drugs can blunt protective responses.

name: T-cell lymphoma
clinical_significance: A cancer of T lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. It includes several different diseases that may affect lymph nodes, skin, blood, or organs and can cause swollen nodes, fever, weight loss, rash, or other symptoms.

name: T-cell receptor
clinical_significance: A protein on a T cell that recognizes a particular piece of a germ or abnormal cell when another cell displays it. This recognition helps start or direct a targeted immune response.

name: teacher
clinical_significance: Teachers can help recognize learning, behavior, or health changes in children and coordinate school supports; sharing health information requires appropriate consent and privacy safeguards.

name: teaching rounds
clinical_significance: Teaching rounds provide supervised discussion of patient cases and clinical decisions; structured participation supports trainee learning while protecting patient privacy and safety.

name: teat
clinical_significance: The teat is the terminal part of a mammary gland through which milk exits; injury or infection can impair nursing and is an important veterinary and lactation-related finding.

name: technetium
clinical_significance: Technetium-99m is a widely used radionuclide for diagnostic imaging; the tracer and scan are selected to evaluate specific organs while limiting radiation exposure.

name: technician
clinical_significance: Healthcare technicians perform technical tasks such as laboratory testing, imaging, or patient monitoring; training and quality controls support accurate results and safe care.

name: tegafur
clinical_significance: Tegafur is a prodrug converted to the anticancer medicine fluorouracil; toxicity can include diarrhea, mouth sores, cytopenias, and rare severe reactions in patients with impaired drug metabolism.

name: tegafur-uracil
clinical_significance: Tegafur-uracil is an oral fluoropyrimidine combination used for selected cancers in some countries; marrow, gastrointestinal, and liver toxicity and drug-metabolism differences require monitoring.

name: tegmentum
clinical_significance: The tegmentum is a brainstem region containing pathways and nuclei involved in movement, arousal, and autonomic control; lesions can produce complex neurologic signs.

name: teicoplanin
clinical_significance: A glycopeptide antibiotic used for selected serious infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive bacteria, including some resistant staphylococci. Kidney function and blood levels may need monitoring.

name: telangiectasia
clinical_significance: A visible, permanently dilated small blood vessel near the skin or mucosal surface, occurring alone or with conditions such as rosacea, liver disease, or inherited vascular syndromes.

name: telbivudine
clinical_significance: Telbivudine is an older antiviral for hepatitis B that is generally avoided because resistance and muscle toxicity can occur; current antiviral selection follows updated hepatitis guidance.

name: telemedicine
clinical_significance: Delivery of medical care at a distance using information and communication technology. It may include video or telephone consultations, secure messages, remote diagnosis, treatment, and review of clinical information.

name: telemetry
clinical_significance: Telemetry continuously transmits physiologic data such as heart rhythm to a monitoring station; it can detect dangerous changes but requires appropriate indication and response protocols.

name: telencephalon
clinical_significance: The telencephalon develops into the cerebral hemispheres and includes regions for cognition, movement, sensation, and behavior; developmental abnormalities can cause neurologic symptoms.

name: teleradiology
clinical_significance: The remote review of medical images, such as X-rays, CT scans, or MRI scans, by a qualified radiologist who is not at the imaging site. It can provide urgent or specialist interpretation when local expertise is unavailable and must protect patient information.

name: tellurium
clinical_significance: Tellurium and some tellurium compounds can cause toxic exposure with gastrointestinal, neurologic, or garlic-like breath and sweat odor; occupational exposure assessment may be needed.

name: telmisartan
clinical_significance: Telmisartan is an angiotensin-receptor blocker used for hypertension and cardiovascular risk reduction; potassium, kidney function, blood pressure, and pregnancy exposure require consideration.

name: telogen effluvium
clinical_significance: A common, non-scarring form of diffuse hair shedding that occurs when more hairs than usual enter the resting (telogen) phase. Shedding often begins 2--4 months after illness, fever, surgery, childbirth, major stress, rapid weight loss, nutritional deficiency, or certain medicines. It is usually temporary, with regrowth after the trigger is corrected, although recovery may take several months.

name: telomerase
clinical_significance: Telomerase maintains chromosome ends in stem and cancer cells; abnormal activity can contribute to tumor growth, while telomerase disorders can cause marrow, lung, liver, and immune problems.

name: telomere
clinical_significance: A protective DNA region at the end of each chromosome. It helps keep genetic material stable during cell division and usually becomes shorter as cells divide and age.

name: telomere capping
clinical_significance: Telomere capping protects chromosome ends from being mistaken for DNA breaks; defective capping can cause genomic instability, cell senescence, or inherited telomere disorders.

name: telomere maintenance
clinical_significance: Telomere maintenance preserves chromosome stability in dividing cells; defects can cause inherited bone-marrow failure and organ disease, while increased maintenance helps many cancers proliferate.

name: telomere shortening
clinical_significance: Telomere shortening occurs with cell division and can accelerate in telomere biology disorders; very short telomeres may cause marrow failure, pulmonary fibrosis, liver disease, or immune dysfunction.

name: telophase
clinical_significance: Telophase is the final stage of cell division when daughter nuclei form; abnormal chromosome segregation during mitosis can contribute to developmental disorders and cancer.

name: temazepam
clinical_significance: A sedative medicine sometimes used for short-term insomnia. It can cause drowsiness, poor coordination, memory problems, dependence, and dangerously slow breathing, especially when combined with alcohol, opioids, or other sedatives.

name: temoporfin
clinical_significance: Temoporfin is a photosensitizing drug used in selected photodynamic cancer treatments; light exposure can cause prolonged photosensitivity and treatment requires controlled illumination.

name: temozolomide
clinical_significance: Temozolomide is chemotherapy used for selected brain tumors; it can suppress blood counts and increase infection risk, and blood monitoring and infection precautions are important.

name: temperament
clinical_significance: Temperament describes a person’s usual emotional and behavioral style; understanding it can help tailor communication and support but is not itself a psychiatric diagnosis.

name: temperature
clinical_significance: A measurement of body heat. The result varies with the measurement site, time, activity, age, and illness.

name: temple syndrome
clinical_significance: A genomic-imprinting disorder involving chromosome 14q32 that causes prenatal and

name: temporal arteri
clinical_significance: The temporal artery supplies blood to the scalp and face; tenderness, thickening, or reduced pulse in an older adult with headache or visual symptoms can indicate giant-cell arteritis, a vision-threatening emergency.

name: temporal arteritis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of arteries, especially those at the temples, usually in adults over 50. It may cause a new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain while chewing, fever, or vision problems and can threaten sight.

name: temporal bone
clinical_significance: The temporal bone houses structures for hearing and balance and protects important nerves; fractures or infection can cause hearing loss, vertigo, facial weakness, or cerebrospinal-fluid leak.

name: temporal lobe
clinical_significance: One of the main areas on each side of the brain, near the ears. It helps process sounds, understand language, form memories, and process emotions.

name: temporomandibular joint
clinical_significance: The jaw joint in front of each ear, where the lower jaw meets the skull. It allows the mouth to open, close, and move side to side; problems can cause pain, clicking, stiffness, or limited movement.

name: temsirolimus
clinical_significance: Temsirolimus is an mTOR inhibitor used for selected kidney cancers; infection risk, mouth sores, elevated glucose and lipids, lung inflammation, and wound-healing effects may require monitoring.

name: tenascin
clinical_significance: A group of proteins in the tissue surrounding cells that help organize tissue structure and influence growth, healing, and inflammation. Levels may change in wounds, developing tissues, and some tumors.

name: tendinitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of a tendon, often associated with repetitive loading, overuse, or injury. It can cause localized tenderness, stiffness, swelling, or pain with movement. Tendinitis is distinct from tendinopathy, a broader term that includes tendon pain and structural change without necessarily involving active inflammation.

name: tendon
clinical_significance: A strong band of tissue that connects a muscle to a bone and transfers the muscle’s pull to move a joint. Tendons have a limited blood supply, so some injuries heal slowly.

name: tendon injury
clinical_significance: Damage to a tendon ranging from microscopic overuse injury to partial or complete rupture, causing localized pain, weakness, swelling, or loss of function.

name: tendon sheath
clinical_significance: A thin lubricated covering around some tendons that reduces friction as the tendon moves; inflammation is called tenosynovitis.

name: tenecteplase
clinical_significance: A clot-dissolving medicine that helps restore blood flow during selected ischemic strokes and heart attacks. It is given through a vein, usually as one dose, but can cause serious bleeding, including bleeding in the brain.

name: tenericutes
clinical_significance: A former classification group for bacteria that lack a rigid cell wall, including Mycoplasma. The name is mainly used in older biological classifications; it is not a diagnosis or a routine clinical test result.

name: teniposide
clinical_significance: Teniposide is a podophyllotoxin-derived antineoplastic drug that inhibits topoisomerase II and is used in selected leukemia or lymphoma regimens.

name: tennis elbow
clinical_significance: Lateral epicondylitis causes pain over the outer elbow, usually worsened by gripping or wrist extension; load modification and rehabilitation often support recovery.

name: tenofovir
clinical_significance: An antiviral medicine used with other drugs to treat HIV and, in some forms, to treat or prevent hepatitis B. It stops viruses copying their genetic material; kidney and bone effects require appropriate monitoring.

name: tenosynovitis
clinical_significance: Tenosynovitis is inflammation of the sheath surrounding a tendon, producing pain, swelling, and restricted gliding, commonly in the hand or wrist.

name: tensile strength
clinical_significance: The ability of a tissue or material to resist being pulled apart; it is important in wound healing and the integrity of sutures, tendons, and other connective tissues.

name: tension-type headache
clinical_significance: A usually bilateral, pressing or tightening headache of mild-to-moderate intensity without prominent nausea, often associated with stress, muscle tenderness, or poor sleep.

name: tenuazonic acid
clinical_significance: Tenuazonic acid is a toxin produced by some molds and plants that can contaminate food; exposure may cause gastrointestinal or systemic toxicity, so food safety and mycotoxin testing matter.

name: teprotumumab
clinical_significance: A monoclonal antibody targeting the insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor and used to treat thyroid eye disease in selected patients.

name: terameprocol
clinical_significance: Terameprocol is an investigational anticancer compound studied for cell-cycle effects; it is not established treatment, and clinical-trial data determine its potential value.

name: teratocarcinoma
clinical_significance: A teratocarcinoma is a malignant germ-cell tumor containing tissues from more than one embryonic layer, often arising in the testis or ovary.

name: teratogen
clinical_significance: A medicine, chemical, infection, radiation exposure, or other influence that can harm an embryo or fetus and cause birth defects, growth problems, abnormal development, or pregnancy loss. Risk depends on the exposure, amount, timing, and individual factors.

name: teratogenesis
clinical_significance: The development of a birth defect, impaired growth, abnormal function, or pregnancy loss after harmful exposure during pregnancy. Risk depends on the substance or infection, amount, timing, route, and genetic factors; exposure does not automatically mean that harm will occur.

name: teratoma
clinical_significance: A tumor made of several types of tissue, such as skin, muscle, bone, or nerve tissue, because it develops from cells capable of forming different body tissues. It may be noncancerous or cancerous and can occur in the ovary, testicle, or other sites.

name: teratozoospermia
clinical_significance: Teratozoospermia is a high proportion of abnormally shaped sperm and may contribute to reduced fertility, though semen results must be interpreted as a whole.

name: terazosin
clinical_significance: Terazosin relaxes smooth muscle in the prostate and blood vessels and is used for urinary symptoms and hypertension; dizziness and orthostatic low blood pressure can occur, especially after the first dose.

name: terazosin hydrochloride
clinical_significance: The hydrochloride salt of terazosin, an alpha-1 blocker used for urinary symptoms from benign prostatic enlargement and sometimes for hypertension; dizziness and first-dose fainting can occur.

name: terbinafine
clinical_significance: An antifungal medicine that damages the outer covering of fungi, stopping their growth or killing them. It is used on the skin or taken by mouth for selected fungal infections; liver problems and taste changes are possible.

name: terbufos
clinical_significance: Terbufos is a highly toxic organophosphate pesticide that inhibits acetylcholinesterase and can cause severe cholinergic poisoning.

name: terbutaline
clinical_significance: A beta-2 agonist used as a bronchodilator; it has limited and specialist use as a tocolytic.

name: terfenadine
clinical_significance: An older antihistamine withdrawn or restricted in many places because interactions and excessive blood levels can cause dangerous heart-rhythm abnormalities.

name: terlipressin
clinical_significance: A medicine similar to vasopressin that tightens certain blood vessels. It is used in selected hospital treatments for life-threatening bleeding from enlarged esophageal veins or kidney failure related to advanced liver disease; reduced blood flow and breathing problems are important risks.

name: term birth
clinical_significance: Birth at or after 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. Early term is 37 to 38 weeks, full term is 39 to 40 weeks, and late or post-term describes later births; gestational age helps guide newborn care.

name: terminal illness
clinical_significance: An advanced disease that is expected to lead to death, although the timing is uncertain and treatment may sometimes slow it. Care may focus on comfort, symptom relief, personal goals, and support for the patient and family.

name: terminal insomnia
clinical_significance: Waking too early and being unable to return to sleep, a pattern that can occur in depression, circadian-rhythm disorders, aging, or other insomnia conditions.

name: terpene
clinical_significance: Terpenes are plant-derived or synthesized compounds used in fragrances and products; some can irritate skin or airways or cause allergic reactions depending on exposure.

name: tertiary hyperparathyroidism
clinical_significance: Persistent overproduction of parathyroid hormone after long-standing kidney disease or another cause of parathyroid overactivity. It can raise the blood calcium level and damage bones or kidneys.

name: tertiary protein
clinical_significance: Tertiary protein structure is a protein’s three-dimensional shape; changes from genetic variants or misfolding can impair function and contribute to disease.

name: tesetaxel
clinical_significance: Tesetaxel is an investigational oral taxane studied for cancer treatment; it is not routine therapy, and evidence from clinical trials and risks such as neuropathy and cytopenias guide evaluation.

name: testicular atrophy
clinical_significance: Shrinkage of a testicle with loss of some functioning tissue. Causes include an undescended testicle, infection, twisting, injury, varicocele, hormone problems, aging, or other damage; it may reduce sperm or testosterone production.

name: testicular feminization
clinical_significance: Testicular feminization is an outdated term for complete androgen insensitivity syndrome, in which a person with a 46,XY chromosome pattern has typically female external anatomy; respectful terminology and individualized endocrine and gonadal care are important.

name: testicular gonadoblastoma
clinical_significance: A rare tumor made from developing reproductive cells and supporting cells in an abnormally developed or undescended testicle. It is often associated with Y-chromosome material and may increase the risk of another germ-cell cancer.

name: testicular hydrocele
clinical_significance: A buildup of clear fluid around a testicle, causing painless swelling of the scrotum. It may be present from birth or develop after injury, infection, inflammation, or another condition; examination helps exclude other causes of swelling.

name: testicular mass
clinical_significance: A lump or enlargement within or around a testicle caused by tumor, infection, inflammation, cyst, hematoma, or torsion. A solid mass within the testicle can be linked to cancer or another serious condition.

name: testicular torsion
clinical_significance: A medical emergency in which the cord supplying a testicle twists and cuts off its blood supply. It usually causes sudden, severe one-sided scrotal pain, swelling, nausea, or vomiting. Treatment usually involves immediate surgery.

name: testis
clinical_significance: One of the two male reproductive glands in the scrotum. It produces sperm and testosterone and is surrounded by protective tissue. Sudden pain, swelling, or a new lump needs prompt medical assessment.

name: testis disorder
clinical_significance: A condition affecting a testicle, including torsion, infection, tumor, trauma, infertility-related damage, hormonal dysfunction, or abnormal development.

name: testis neoplasm
clinical_significance: A tumor arising in testicular tissue, most commonly a germ-cell tumor in younger adults; painless enlargement, heaviness, or a solid mass requires prompt ultrasound and evaluation.

name: testolactone
clinical_significance: Testolactone is an older aromatase inhibitor used in selected hormone-sensitive conditions; it is not a common current treatment and may affect bone, liver, and hormone status.

name: testosterone
clinical_significance: A steroid sex hormone produced mainly by the testes and, in smaller amounts, by the ovaries and adrenal glands. It supports reproductive development, muscle and bone maintenance, red-blood-cell production, libido, and other physiologic functions; levels vary with age, sex, time of day, illness, and medicines.

name: testosterone propionate
clinical_significance: A short-acting injectable testosterone ester used in selected hormone-replacement or androgen-deficiency settings; risks include erythrocytosis, infertility, acne, mood effects, and prostate-related monitoring needs.

name: tetanus
clinical_significance: A serious infection caused by bacteria entering a wound and producing a toxin that causes severe muscle stiffness and painful spasms. It can cause lockjaw, breathing problems, and death.

name: tetanus toxin
clinical_significance: A toxin made by the bacterium Clostridium tetani. It blocks calming signals in the nervous system, causing painful muscle stiffness and spasms, including lockjaw. Vaccination and proper wound care reduce the risk of tetanus.

name: tetany
clinical_significance: Muscle cramps, spasms, or twitching caused by increased nerve and muscle excitability, most often from low calcium or magnesium. Tingling around the mouth or in the hands may occur; severe spasms or breathing difficulty may occur in serious cases.

name: tetracaine
clinical_significance: Tetracaine is a potent ester local anaesthetic used topically or for spinal anaesthesia; excessive dose can cause seizures, cardiovascular toxicity, and methemoglobinaemia.

name: tetrachloroethylene
clinical_significance: Tetrachloroethylene, or perchloroethylene, is an industrial solvent used in dry cleaning; substantial exposure can affect the nervous system, liver, and kidneys.

name: tetrachlorvinphos
clinical_significance: An organophosphate insecticide that can block acetylcholinesterase. Significant exposure may cause sweating, vomiting, pinpoint pupils, muscle twitching, slow breathing, seizures, or coma.

name: tetracosahexaenoic acid
clinical_significance: Tetracosahexaenoic acid is an omega-3 fatty acid studied in lipid and nutrition research; it is not a routine standalone diagnostic marker or therapy.

name: tetracosenoic acid
clinical_significance: Tetracosenoic acid is a very-long-chain fatty acid; elevated levels can occur in peroxisomal disorders such as X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy and may support diagnostic testing.

name: tetracycline
clinical_significance: An antibiotic that stops bacteria making proteins needed for growth. It treats selected infections but can cause stomach upset, sensitivity to sunlight, and permanent tooth discolouration if used during tooth development.

name: tetracycline antibiotic
clinical_significance: Tetracycline antibiotics inhibit bacterial protein synthesis and are used for selected infections; pregnancy, young-child tooth effects, photosensitivity, and drug interactions influence use.

name: tetradecanoylphorbol acetate
clinical_significance: Tetradecanoylphorbol acetate is a potent protein kinase C activator used in laboratory studies of inflammation, cell signaling, and tumor promotion; it is not a therapeutic agent.

name: tetragenococcus
clinical_significance: Tetragenococcus bacteria are used in fermented foods and are rarely implicated in human infection; a clinical isolate should be assessed in light of specimen source and patient condition.

name: tetrahydrouridine
clinical_significance: Tetrahydrouridine inhibits cytidine deaminase and is studied to increase exposure to certain nucleoside medicines; combination use remains specialized and requires protocol-specific safety monitoring.

name: tetrahymena
clinical_significance: Tetrahymena is a free-living ciliate used in biology and toxicology research; it is not a typical human pathogen, though unusual opportunistic infections have been reported.

name: tetralogy of fallot
clinical_significance: A heart defect present from birth with four features: a hole between the lower chambers, narrowing of the route from the right ventricle to the lungs (usually pulmonary stenosis), an aorta positioned over the hole, and thickening of the right ventricle. Reduced blood flow to the lungs can lower the oxygen level in the blood.

name: tetranitromethane
clinical_significance: Tetranitromethane is a highly reactive laboratory and industrial chemical that can cause severe inhalation, skin, and eye injury; exposure requires poison-control or occupational-health assessment.

name: tetraploidy
clinical_significance: Tetraploidy is a chromosome abnormality with four copies of each chromosome; it is usually incompatible with normal development, though mosaic forms can be associated with congenital abnormalities or pregnancy loss.

name: tetrapyrroles
clinical_significance: Tetrapyrroles include heme and related molecules needed for oxygen transport and metabolism; defects in their synthesis or breakdown can cause porphyrias and other metabolic disorders.

name: tetraspanins
clinical_significance: Tetraspanins organize cell-surface proteins involved in immune signaling, cell adhesion, and tumor biology; they are research markers and potential therapeutic targets rather than standalone clinical tests.

name: tetrodotoxin
clinical_significance: Tetrodotoxin blocks nerve sodium channels and can cause tingling, weakness, paralysis, and respiratory failure after contaminated seafood or animal exposure; there is no specific antidote, so urgent supportive care is essential.

name: tezacitabine
clinical_significance: Tezacitabine is an investigational nucleoside anticancer drug; it is not routine treatment, and trial evidence and marrow toxicity determine its potential role.

name: thalamic disease
clinical_significance: Thalamic disease can disrupt sensation, movement, alertness, or memory; stroke, tumor, infection, and degenerative disease are among causes requiring neurologic evaluation.

name: thalamic nuclei
clinical_significance: Thalamic nuclei relay sensory and motor signals and contribute to arousal and cognition; focal injury can produce characteristic neurologic deficits or altered consciousness.

name: thalamus
clinical_significance: A pair of structures deep within the brain that relay most sensory information, such as touch, vision, and hearing, to the outer brain. They also help regulate movement, alertness, and memory.

name: thalassemia
clinical_significance: A group of inherited blood disorders in which the body makes too little of one part of hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. This causes anemia, ranging from mild to severe, and may require regular treatment.

name: thalidomide
clinical_significance: A medicine that changes immune activity and is used for selected cancers and inflammatory conditions. It can cause severe birth defects, nerve damage, blood clots, sleepiness, and other harms, requiring strict safety controls.

name: thallium
clinical_significance: Thallium is a toxic heavy metal that can cause gastrointestinal illness followed by painful nerve damage, hair loss, skin changes, kidney or liver injury, seizures, and heart or brain problems.

name: thanatophoric dysplasia
clinical_significance: A severe inherited disorder of bone growth causing extremely short limbs, a narrow chest, a large head, and abnormal skull and spine development. The small chest can prevent adequate breathing after birth and is often life-threatening.

name: thapsigargin
clinical_significance: Thapsigargin is a potent inhibitor of cellular calcium pumps used in laboratory research and in experimental cancer-drug development; it is not a routine clinical treatment.

name: thaw
clinical_significance: Thawing frozen medicines, specimens, or tissues under controlled conditions preserves their integrity; repeated freeze-thaw cycles can reduce test accuracy or drug potency.

name: thebaine
clinical_significance: Thebaine is an opium poppy alkaloid used as a precursor in pharmaceutical manufacturing; it is not a routine medicine and can be toxic if ingested.

name: theca cell
clinical_significance: Theca cells in the ovary produce androgens that support estrogen synthesis; abnormal androgen production can contribute to hirsutism, menstrual irregularity, or ovarian disorders.

name: thecoma
clinical_significance: A usually benign ovarian sex-cord stromal tumor composed of theca-like cells, often producing estrogen and presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding or an incidental adnexal mass.

name: theobromine
clinical_significance: Theobromine is a stimulant found in cocoa and chocolate; large exposures, especially in pets, can cause vomiting, agitation, abnormal heart rhythm, or seizures.

name: theophylline
clinical_significance: A medicine that can relax airway muscles and improve breathing in selected lung diseases. Its safe and harmful doses are close together, so blood levels, medicine interactions, heart rhythm, and side effects need monitoring.

name: theophylline assay
clinical_significance: A theophylline assay measures blood drug concentration because the medicine has a narrow therapeutic range; testing helps avoid toxicity and assess inadequate exposure.

name: therapeutic
clinical_significance: Therapeutic describes an intervention intended to improve health; claims of therapeutic benefit should be supported by evidence of meaningful patient outcomes and acceptable harms.

name: therapeutic abortion
clinical_significance: Intentional termination of a pregnancy because of medical, fetal, or other legally recognized indications, according to applicable law and clinical guidance.

name: therapeutic embolization
clinical_significance: Therapeutic embolization intentionally blocks a blood vessel to control bleeding, shrink a tumor, or treat vascular disease; risks include ischemia, pain, and damage to nearby tissue.

name: therapeutic index
clinical_significance: A measure of how close a medicine’s effective dose is to a dose that causes harm. A narrow index means small dose changes may be risky and require careful monitoring.

name: therapeutic touch
clinical_significance: Therapeutic touch is a complementary practice involving movement of the hands near or on the body; evidence for disease treatment is limited, and it should not replace effective medical care.

name: therapy
clinical_significance: Treatment intended to prevent, relieve, or cure disease or to improve function and quality of life.

name: therapy compliance
clinical_significance: Therapy adherence describes how treatment is followed over time; barriers such as cost, side effects, or regimen complexity can be addressed through shared decision-making and practical support.

name: thermodynamics
clinical_significance: Thermodynamics governs heat and energy transfer in the body and in medical devices; it is relevant to temperature control, burns, hypothermia, and laboratory or equipment design.

name: thermogenesis
clinical_significance: The production of heat by the body. It comes mainly from normal metabolism, muscle activity such as shivering, digestion, and specialized fat tissue that releases stored energy as heat.

name: thermography
clinical_significance: Recording the pattern of heat released from the body surface with a special camera. It may show temperature differences, but these are not specific for one disease and usually require confirmation with standard examination or tests.

name: thermogravimetry
clinical_significance: Thermogravimetry measures mass changes as a sample is heated; it is used mainly in materials and pharmaceutical analysis to assess composition, moisture, or stability.

name: thermometry
clinical_significance: Thermometry measures body temperature; accurate technique and measurement site matter when assessing fever, hypothermia, or response to treatment.

name: thermoreceptor
clinical_significance: A nerve ending that senses warmth or cold in the skin and other tissues. Signals travel through the spinal cord to the brain, helping a person recognize temperature and helping the body control heat through sweating, shivering, and changes in skin blood flow. Damage to these nerves can reduce temperature sensation and increase the risk of burns or cold injury.

name: thermoregulation measures
clinical_significance: Thermoregulation measures help prevent heat illness and hypothermia in vulnerable patients; monitoring and environmental adjustments are important during anesthesia, neonatal care, and critical illness.

name: thermosensing
clinical_significance: Thermosensing detects temperature changes through specialized receptors and neural pathways; dysfunction can impair heat or cold perception and increase burn or cold-injury risk.

name: thiabendazole
clinical_significance: An antiparasitic medicine used for selected worm infections and, historically, some fungal infections. It can cause nausea, dizziness, liver problems, or nervous-system effects, so safer alternatives are often preferred.

name: thiamine
clinical_significance: Vitamin B1, a water-soluble vitamin required for carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function. Severe deficiency

name: thiamine assay
clinical_significance: A thiamine assay assesses vitamin B1 status in selected cases; results can support evaluation of malnutrition or metabolic disease but should be interpreted with symptoms and treatment urgency.

name: thiamine deficiency
clinical_significance: Thiamine deficiency can cause beriberi, heart failure, neuropathy, or Wernicke encephalopathy; give prompt replacement when strongly suspected, especially in malnutrition or alcohol dependence.

name: thiamine pyrophosphate
clinical_significance: Thiamine pyrophosphate is the active coenzyme form of vitamin B1; low availability impairs energy metabolism and can cause neurologic and cardiac disease.

name: thiazide
clinical_significance: Thiazides are a class of diuretics used for hypertension and fluid disorders; low sodium or potassium, gout, glucose changes, and kidney function require monitoring.

name: thiazide diuretic
clinical_significance: Thiazide diuretics lower blood pressure by increasing sodium excretion; they can cause electrolyte abnormalities, dehydration, gout, and changes in glucose or uric acid.

name: thiazole
clinical_significance: Thiazoles are chemical rings found in some medicines and biologically active compounds; clinical effects and toxicity depend on the specific drug, not the ring alone.

name: thiazolidinedione
clinical_significance: Thiazolidinediones improve insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes; fluid retention, heart-failure worsening, fractures, and weight gain affect patient selection and monitoring.

name: thick
clinical_significance: Thickening of tissue or fluid may indicate inflammation, scarring, edema, or tumor; the clinical meaning depends on the location and imaging or examination findings.

name: thienopyridines
clinical_significance: Thienopyridines are antiplatelet medicines that reduce clot formation after acute coronary syndromes or stenting; bleeding risk and interactions must be balanced against thrombosis prevention.

name: thiethylperazine
clinical_significance: Thiethylperazine is an older anti-nausea medicine with dopamine-blocking effects; sedation, low blood pressure, and movement disorders can occur, particularly in older adults.

name: thigh
clinical_significance: The part of the lower limb between the hip and knee. It contains the femur, large muscles, major blood vessels, and nerves that help move and support the leg.

name: thimerosal
clinical_significance: A preservative containing ethylmercury that is used in some multidose vaccines and medical products. Ethylmercury leaves the body faster than methylmercury; its safety depends on the product, amount, and applicable regulations.

name: thinking
clinical_significance: Thinking includes attention, memory, reasoning, and problem-solving; changes can signal delirium, dementia, mood disorder, medication effects, or acute illness.

name: thioacetamide
clinical_significance: Thioacetamide is a toxic industrial and laboratory chemical that can injure the liver; exposure history is relevant when evaluating unexplained hepatic injury.

name: thioacetazone
clinical_significance: Thioacetazone is an older tuberculosis drug with limited current use because of severe skin reactions, especially in people with HIV; resistance and safer regimens have largely displaced it.

name: thioamide
clinical_significance: Thioamides such as methimazole and propylthiouracil reduce thyroid-hormone synthesis; they can cause rash, liver injury, or rare agranulocytosis requiring urgent evaluation of fever or sore throat.

name: thiocarbamates
clinical_significance: Thiocarbamate pesticides can cause neurologic or respiratory toxicity depending on the compound and exposure; occupational or accidental exposure may require poison-control guidance.

name: thioctic acid
clinical_significance: Thioctic acid, also called alpha-lipoic acid, is marketed as a supplement and studied for neuropathy; evidence varies, and it can lower blood glucose or interact with treatment.

name: thiocyanate
clinical_significance: Thiocyanate is a metabolite of cyanide and can accumulate with exposure or impaired clearance; elevated levels may affect thyroid function and help assess chronic cyanide exposure.

name: thiofanox
clinical_significance: Thiofanox is a highly toxic carbamate pesticide that inhibits acetylcholinesterase; exposure can cause a cholinergic emergency with sweating, secretions, weakness, seizures, or respiratory failure.

name: thioguanine
clinical_significance: Thioguanine is an antimetabolite chemotherapy used for selected leukemias; bone-marrow suppression and liver vascular injury require blood-count and liver monitoring.

name: thioinosine
clinical_significance: Thioinosine is a purine analog studied in cancer therapy; it is not a routine medicine, and research use requires monitoring for marrow and metabolic toxicity.

name: thiones
clinical_significance: Thiones are sulfur-containing chemical compounds found in some drugs and laboratory reagents; toxicity and clinical relevance depend on the individual compound and exposure.

name: thiopental
clinical_significance: Thiopental is a short-acting barbiturate anesthetic used in selected settings; it can suppress breathing and circulation and requires airway and hemodynamic monitoring.

name: thioredoxins
clinical_significance: Thioredoxins help maintain cellular redox balance and protein function; abnormal activity is studied in cancer, inflammation, and oxidative stress but is not a routine diagnostic test.

name: thioridazine
clinical_significance: An older antipsychotic medicine used only in selected situations because it can cause severe sleepiness, movement problems, and dangerous changes in heart rhythm, especially at high doses or with interacting medicines.

name: thiosulfate
clinical_significance: Thiosulfate is used medically in selected poisoning and drug-toxicity protocols and also appears in laboratory testing; indication and dose depend on the specific clinical context.

name: thiotepa
clinical_significance: A chemotherapy medicine that damages DNA and stops cells from multiplying. It is used for selected cancers and sometimes before a stem-cell transplant; side effects may include low blood counts, infection, nausea, mouth sores, and organ injury.

name: thiothixene
clinical_significance: Thiothixene is an antipsychotic used for schizophrenia; movement disorders, sedation, low blood pressure, and rare neuroleptic malignant syndrome are important risks.

name: thiouracil
clinical_significance: Thiouracil is an older antithyroid medicine that can cause serious liver and blood disorders; it is generally not used in humans when safer alternatives are available.

name: thiourea
clinical_significance: Thiourea is an industrial and laboratory chemical with potential thyroid and toxic effects; exposure assessment matters in occupational or environmental illness.

name: third ventricle
clinical_significance: The third ventricle is a cerebrospinal-fluid space in the brain; obstruction or a mass can raise intracranial pressure and require urgent imaging and treatment.

name: third-degree burn
clinical_significance: A full-thickness burn that destroys the epidermis and dermis and may extend into subcutaneous tissue.

name: thirst
clinical_significance: The conscious desire to drink, regulated mainly by body-fluid concentration and circulating blood volume. Excessive thirst may occur with dehydration, diabetes, medicines, kidney problems, or other conditions and may need evaluation.

name: thoracentesis
clinical_significance: A medical procedure in which a thin needle or catheter is gently inserted through the back of the chest wall into the pleural space (the narrow gap between the lungs and the inner chest wall) to withdraw accumulated excess fluid (a pleural effusion). Thoracentesis is performed for two key reasons: diagnostic (collecting a small sample of fluid for laboratory analysis to find the underlying cause, such as pneumonia, heart failure, kidney disease, tuberculosis, or cancer) and therapeutic (removing

name: thoracic aorta
clinical_significance: The thoracic aorta carries blood from the heart through the chest; aneurysm or dissection can be life-threatening and may present with sudden chest or back pain.

name: thoracic artery
clinical_significance: Thoracic arteries supply the chest wall and organs; injury, aneurysm, or blockage can compromise blood flow and may require urgent imaging or intervention.

name: thoracic cavity
clinical_significance: The space inside the chest, enclosed by the ribs and breathing muscles. It contains the lungs, heart, esophagus, trachea, major blood vessels, and other structures protected by the chest wall.

name: thoracic disease
clinical_significance: Thoracic disease affects structures in the chest, including lungs, heart, pleura, and chest wall; shortness of breath or chest pain may require prompt evaluation.

name: thoracic duct
clinical_significance: The body’s largest lymph vessel. It collects excess fluid and immune cells from most of the body and returns them to the bloodstream near the neck; injury can cause lymph fluid to leak into the chest.

name: thoracic esophagus
clinical_significance: The thoracic esophagus carries swallowed food through the chest; obstruction, inflammation, or cancer can cause dysphagia, pain, or aspiration.

name: thoracic Injury
clinical_significance: Thoracic injury can damage the lungs, heart, great vessels, ribs, or spine; respiratory compromise or internal bleeding may develop even when external signs are limited.

name: thoracic radiography
clinical_significance: Thoracic radiography provides chest images to assess lungs, heart size, bones, and devices; it can detect pneumonia or pneumothorax but may not exclude disease when findings are normal.

name: thoracic surgery
clinical_significance: Thoracic surgery treats disease or injury in the chest, including lung, esophageal, and mediastinal conditions; pulmonary, cardiac, and infection risks affect perioperative care.

name: thoracic vertebrae
clinical_significance: The twelve vertebrae of the chest region, each articulating with ribs and protecting the thoracic spinal cord while supporting the trunk and rib cage.

name: thoracogastroschisis
clinical_significance: Thoracogastroschisis is a rare congenital body-wall defect involving the chest and stomach; associated abnormalities require neonatal surgical and multidisciplinary management.

name: thoracoplasty
clinical_significance: Thoracoplasty reshapes or removes part of the chest wall to treat selected lung or chest-wall conditions; postoperative breathing function and complications require monitoring.

name: thoracoschisis
clinical_significance: Thoracoschisis is a rare congenital chest-wall defect that may expose or displace thoracic organs; urgent neonatal evaluation and surgical planning are often needed.

name: thoracoscopes
clinical_significance: Thoracoscopes are cameras and instruments used for minimally invasive chest procedures; visualization allows biopsy or treatment while reducing the incision size compared with open surgery.

name: thoracoscopy
clinical_significance: A minimally invasive procedure using a camera inserted through the chest wall to examine or treat the pleura, lungs, or mediastinum.

name: thoracotomy
clinical_significance: A surgical incision into the chest wall to access the thoracic cavity (pleural space,

name: thorax
clinical_significance: The thorax is the chest region between the neck and abdomen, enclosed by ribs and containing the heart, lungs, major vessels, and mediastinal structures.

name: thorax neoplasm
clinical_significance: A thoracic neoplasm may arise in the lung, pleura, mediastinum, or chest wall; imaging and tissue diagnosis establish the site and guide staging and treatment.

name: thorium dioxide
clinical_significance: Thorium dioxide was formerly used as a radiographic contrast agent and can remain radioactive in tissues for decades; prior exposure is associated with increased cancer risk and is important in medical history.

name: threatened abortion
clinical_significance: Threatened abortion is an older term for bleeding in early pregnancy when the pregnancy may continue; evaluation assesses pregnancy location, viability, and causes of bleeding.

name: threonine
clinical_significance: An essential amino acid used to build proteins and other body molecules. The body cannot make enough of it, so it must come from food.

name: throat
clinical_significance: The passage behind the mouth and nose that connects them with the voice box and esophagus. It carries air toward the lungs and food toward the stomach and contains the tonsils and other protective tissues.

name: throat cancer
clinical_significance: Cancer arising in the pharynx or nearby structures of the throat. Persistent hoarseness, difficulty or pain

name: thrombasthenia
clinical_significance: Thrombasthenia is an inherited platelet-function disorder, usually due to defective platelet aggregation; it causes easy bruising, nosebleeds, heavy menstrual bleeding, or surgical bleeding despite a normal platelet count.

name: thrombectomy
clinical_significance: A procedure to remove a blood clot from a blood vessel and restore blood flow. A catheter may remove the clot from a blocked brain artery during some ischemic strokes; surgery is used in selected other situations.

name: thrombin
clinical_significance: A blood-clotting substance that changes fibrinogen into fibrin, the protein threads that form a clot, and also activates platelets. The body makes thrombin after a blood vessel is injured; too much or too little clotting can cause disease.

name: thrombin receptor
clinical_significance: Thrombin receptors activate platelets and other cells during clotting; receptor signaling is a target for antiplatelet drugs and may influence thrombosis and inflammation.

name: thrombocyte differentiation
clinical_significance: Thrombocyte differentiation produces platelets from bone-marrow megakaryocytes; impaired production can cause bleeding, while abnormal overproduction can increase clot risk.

name: thrombocytopathy
clinical_significance: A problem with how platelets work, even when the platelet count is normal or nearly normal. It may cause easy bruising, nosebleeds, heavy menstrual bleeding, or prolonged bleeding after an injury or procedure.

name: thrombocytopenia
clinical_significance: A low number of platelets, the blood cells that help stop bleeding. It may result from reduced production, increased destruction, trapping in an enlarged spleen, or dilution and can cause bruising, bleeding, or no symptoms.

name: thrombocytopenic purpura
clinical_significance: Thrombocytopenic purpura describes low platelets with skin or mucosal bleeding; immune thrombocytopenia is a common cause, but medication, infection, and other disorders must be considered.

name: thrombocytosis
clinical_significance: A higher-than-normal number of platelets in the blood. It may be a temporary response to infection, inflammation, bleeding, or iron deficiency, or result from a bone-marrow disorder. It can increase bleeding or clotting risk depending on the cause.

name: thromboembolism
clinical_significance: Obstruction of a blood vessel by a clot that formed elsewhere and traveled through the circulation.

name: thrombomodulin
clinical_significance: Thrombomodulin is an endothelial protein that helps regulate clotting and inflammation; reduced or abnormal function can contribute to thrombosis and vascular injury.

name: thrombophilia
clinical_significance: A tendency for blood to form clots too easily. It may be inherited or develop with cancer, pregnancy, some medicines, inflammation, or other conditions and can increase the risk of clots in veins.

name: thrombophlebitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of a vein associated with a blood clot. Superficial thrombophlebitis may cause a tender, warm, red, firm cord along a vein just beneath the skin. Thrombosis in a deep vein is deep-vein thrombosis and can break away and cause a life-threatening pulmonary embolism; sudden limb swelling, chest pain, or breathlessness requires urgent assessment.

name: thromboplastin
clinical_significance: Thromboplastin refers to tissue factor activity used in coagulation testing; the prothrombin time and INR help assess clotting and monitor selected anticoagulants.

name: thrombopoiesis
clinical_significance: The process by which the bone marrow makes platelets. Platelets develop from large marrow cells and enter the bloodstream, where they help stop bleeding.

name: thrombosis
clinical_significance: Formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel or the heart. The clot can block blood flow and damage tissue, causing problems such as deep-vein thrombosis, stroke, heart attack, or loss of blood supply to a limb.

name: thrombospondin
clinical_significance: Thrombospondins are proteins involved in platelet activity, blood-vessel growth, and tissue repair; abnormal signaling is studied in cancer, fibrosis, and cardiovascular disease.

name: thromboxane
clinical_significance: A chemical made mainly by activated platelets that makes platelets stick together and narrows blood vessels. These actions help stop bleeding but can also contribute to harmful clot formation.

name: thumb
clinical_significance: The thumb is essential for grip and fine motor function; injury, arthritis, or nerve damage can substantially limit daily activities.

name: thymalfasin
clinical_significance: Thymalfasin is an immune-modulating peptide used in some countries for selected conditions and studied in other diseases; availability and evidence vary, and it is not a substitute for established treatment.

name: thymectomy
clinical_significance: Thymectomy removes the thymus, most often to treat thymoma or selected myasthenia gravis; surgery may improve disease control but requires attention to operative and immune-related considerations.

name: thymic carcinoma
clinical_significance: A malignant epithelial tumor of the thymus that is generally more aggressive and biologically distinct from thymoma. It may invade nearby structures or spread to other sites.

name: thymic cord
clinical_significance: Thymic cords are epithelial structures involved in thymus development and organization; abnormal thymic development can affect T-cell maturation and immune function.

name: thymidine
clinical_significance: Thymidine is a DNA nucleoside used in cell growth and laboratory research; abnormal nucleoside metabolism can affect DNA synthesis and be relevant to rare genetic disorders.

name: thymidine kinase
clinical_significance: Thymidine kinase supports DNA synthesis and is measured in some cancers as a marker of cell proliferation; herpesvirus thymidine kinase is also a target for antiviral activation.

name: thymidine monophosphate
clinical_significance: Thymidine monophosphate is a DNA building block produced in nucleotide metabolism; impaired synthesis can disrupt cell division and contribute to marrow or developmental disease.

name: thymidine phosphorylase
clinical_significance: Thymidine phosphorylase breaks down thymidine and is deficient in mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy; testing can support diagnosis of this progressive disorder.

name: thymidylate synthase
clinical_significance: Thymidylate synthase is required for DNA synthesis and is a target of fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy; tumor expression can influence treatment response but is not interpreted alone.

name: thymine
clinical_significance: Thymine is one of the four main bases in DNA. It pairs with adenine through hydrogen bonds and helps store genetic information.

name: thymocyte
clinical_significance: An immature T lymphocyte developing in the thymus, where it undergoes selection before becoming a mature T cell.

name: thymol
clinical_significance: Thymol is an antiseptic and flavoring compound used in some products; concentrated exposure can irritate or poison, and it should not be ingested in medicinal amounts without guidance.

name: thymoma
clinical_significance: A tumor arising from the thymus, an immune-system organ behind the breastbone. It may cause chest pressure or no symptoms and is associated with conditions such as myasthenia gravis; behavior depends on whether it grows beyond the thymus.

name: thymopentin
clinical_significance: Thymopentin is a synthetic peptide studied for immune effects; it is not a routine treatment, and clinical evidence and availability vary by region.

name: thymopoietin
clinical_significance: Thymopoietin is a thymic peptide involved in immune-cell development; its clinical relevance is mainly research into T-cell maturation and immune disorders.

name: thymosin
clinical_significance: Thymosins are peptides involved in immune and tissue-repair pathways; specific thymosin products have different evidence and regulatory status, so supplement claims should be assessed cautiously.

name: thymus
clinical_significance: An immune-system organ behind the breastbone where immature T cells mature and learn not to attack the body’s own tissues. It is most active in childhood and becomes smaller after puberty.

name: thymus hyperplasia
clinical_significance: Thymic hyperplasia is enlargement of thymic tissue that may occur with autoimmune disease or after treatment; it can mimic a tumor on imaging and may regress when the underlying condition is treated.

name: thymus neoplasm
clinical_significance: Thymic neoplasms include thymoma and thymic carcinoma, which may cause chest symptoms or autoimmune disease such as myasthenia gravis; imaging, pathology, and staging guide care.

name: thyroglobulin
clinical_significance: Thyroglobulin is a protein made by thyroid tissue and used as a tumor marker after treatment for differentiated thyroid cancer; antibodies and residual tissue can affect interpretation.

name: thyroglossal cyst
clinical_significance: A thyroglossal cyst is a congenital midline neck cyst that can become infected or enlarge; persistent masses are evaluated and often removed to prevent recurrence and exclude malignancy.

name: thyroid agenesis
clinical_significance: Thyroid agenesis is congenital absence of the thyroid gland and causes permanent hypothyroidism; newborn screening and early hormone replacement prevent impaired growth and neurodevelopment.

name: thyroid carcinoma
clinical_significance: Thyroid carcinoma includes several cancers with different behavior and prognosis; a neck nodule, biopsy, and staging guide surgery, radioactive iodine, or other treatment.

name: thyroid cartilage
clinical_significance: The largest cartilage of the larynx, formed by two plates that meet in front and create the laryngeal prominence. It

name: thyroid crisis
clinical_significance: Thyroid crisis, or thyroid storm, is life-threatening severe thyrotoxicosis with fever, delirium, rapid heart rate, and organ dysfunction; it requires emergency intensive care.

name: thyroid disease
clinical_significance: Thyroid disease can alter metabolism, heart rate, mood, fertility, and growth; thyroid-function tests help identify underactivity, overactivity, or structural disease.

name: thyroid dysgenesis
clinical_significance: Thyroid dysgenesis is abnormal development or position of the thyroid and is a common cause of congenital hypothyroidism; newborn screening enables timely treatment.

name: thyroid follicular adenoma
clinical_significance: A thyroid follicular adenoma is usually a benign nodule, but cytology may not distinguish it from follicular carcinoma; surgical pathology may be needed for definitive classification.

name: thyroid gland
clinical_significance: A butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck. It makes hormones that help control energy use, temperature, heart rate, growth, and development.

name: thyroid hormone
clinical_significance: The hormones T3 and T4, made by the thyroid gland, that help control energy use, temperature, heart rate, growth, and brain development. Too little can slow body functions, while too much can make them overactive.

name: thyroid neoplasm
clinical_significance: A thyroid neoplasm may be benign or malignant; ultrasound features and biopsy risk category determine whether it needs surveillance or treatment.

name: thyroid nodule
clinical_significance: Thyroid nodules are common and mostly benign, but some produce excess hormone or represent cancer; ultrasound risk features and, when indicated, fine-needle biopsy guide management.

name: thyroid sarcoma
clinical_significance: Thyroid sarcoma is a rare aggressive cancer arising from supporting tissue rather than thyroid hormone-producing cells; specialist pathology and staging guide treatment.

name: thyroidectomy
clinical_significance: Surgery to remove part or all of the thyroid gland. It may treat thyroid cancer, an overactive thyroid, or a large goiter; possible complications include bleeding, voice-nerve injury, and low calcium.

name: thyroiditis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the thyroid gland. It may cause neck pain, fever, or temporary overactivity followed by underactivity; some forms are painless and autoimmune. Features vary according to the type and duration.

name: thyrotoxicosis
clinical_significance: A condition caused by too much thyroid hormone activity in the body, whatever the source. It may cause weight loss, fast heartbeat, tremor, sweating, anxiety, diarrhea, heat intolerance, or severe illness.

name: thyrotroph adenoma
clinical_significance: A usually noncancerous pituitary tumor arising from cells that make thyroid-stimulating hormone. It may produce too much hormone, causing an overactive thyroid, headaches, or vision problems if it presses on nearby structures.

name: thyrotropin
clinical_significance: Thyroid-stimulating hormone, a pituitary hormone that stimulates thyroid growth and thyroid-hormone production; it is also called TSH.

name: thyrotropin alfa
clinical_significance: A recombinant form of thyroid-stimulating hormone used to stimulate residual thyroid tissue or differentiated thyroid cancer cells during selected diagnostic or treatment protocols.

name: thyroxine
clinical_significance: The thyroid hormone T4, which contains four iodine atoms. The thyroid releases it into the blood, and much of it is converted to the more active hormone triiodothyronine (T3).

name: tiazofurin
clinical_significance: Tiazofurin is an investigational nucleoside anticancer agent that alters cellular nucleotide metabolism; it is not routine therapy and remains primarily a research compound.

name: tibia
clinical_significance: The larger, weight-bearing bone of the lower leg, extending from the knee to the ankle. It forms part of both joints and is commonly called the shinbone.

name: tibia vara
clinical_significance: Tibia vara is inward angulation of the upper shinbone causing bowing of the leg, classically associated with Blount disease or other growth disorders.

name: tibial artery
clinical_significance: An artery of the lower leg, chiefly the anterior and posterior tibial arteries, supplying the leg, ankle, and foot and contributing to pedal pulses.

name: tibial fracture
clinical_significance: A break in the tibia, the major weight-bearing bone of the lower leg, often caused by high-energy trauma, twisting injury, or repetitive stress.

name: tibial nerve
clinical_significance: A large nerve running from the back of the knee down the back of the leg and behind the inner ankle. It controls several leg and foot muscles and carries sensation from parts of the foot.

name: tibialcrural artery
clinical_significance: A term describing the arteries and branching vessels near the lower leg and ankle, especially connections between the tibial and fibular arteries. These vessels supply blood to the ankle and foot.

name: tibialis cranialis
clinical_significance: The tibialis cranialis is a muscle described mainly in veterinary anatomy; dysfunction of the corresponding human anterior-compartment muscles can impair ankle dorsiflexion.

name: tic disorder
clinical_significance: A neurologic condition causing repeated, sudden movements or sounds that are difficult to control, such as blinking, shrugging, throat clearing, or grunting. Tics may be briefly suppressed, often worsen with stress, and vary in severity.

name: ticarcillin
clinical_significance: A penicillin antibiotic with activity against many gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas; it is usually given with clavulanate and can cause allergy or electrolyte disturbances.

name: tick
clinical_significance: A small blood-feeding arachnid that can attach to people or animals and transmit infections such as Lyme disease, rickettsial diseases, and babesiosis.

name: ticlopidine
clinical_significance: An antiplatelet medicine that reduces the blood’s ability to form clots. It was used to prevent stroke or heart-related clots in selected people but is now less common because it can cause serious blood-count and bleeding problems.

name: tidal volume
clinical_significance: The amount of air breathed in or out with one normal breath. It varies with body size, activity, illness, and breathing support and can be measured during lung-function testing.

name: tigecycline
clinical_significance: An antibiotic used in selected serious infections when other treatments are unsuitable. It stops bacteria making proteins and commonly causes nausea and vomiting; it is not appropriate for every type of infection.

name: tight junction
clinical_significance: A seal between neighboring lining cells that controls what can pass between them. It helps keep separate the cell surfaces facing the body cavity and the underlying tissue.

name: tilorone
clinical_significance: Tilorone is a synthetic antiviral and immune-modulating compound used or studied in some countries; evidence and indications vary by setting.

name: time
clinical_significance: Time measurement is essential for symptom onset, drug dosing, monitoring, and emergency treatment; accurate timelines can change diagnosis and outcomes.

name: time perception
clinical_significance: Time perception can be altered by neurologic disease, psychiatric conditions, medication, or sleep loss; changes are interpreted with the person’s broader cognitive and health status.

name: timolol
clinical_significance: Timolol is a non-selective beta blocker used in glaucoma eye drops and for selected cardiovascular conditions; topical ocular use can still cause bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm, or fatigue.

name: Timothy syndrome
clinical_significance: A rare inherited disorder affecting the heart and several body systems. It can cause a dangerously prolonged heart rhythm, heart defects, webbed fingers or toes, and developmental or immune problems.

name: tincture
clinical_significance: A tincture is an alcohol-based liquid preparation of a substance; concentration varies, and alcohol content or unregulated ingredients can create safety concerns.

name: tinea
clinical_significance: A fungal infection of the skin, hair, or nails caused by fungi that feed on a protein called keratin. Common forms include ringworm, athlete’s foot, and jock itch.

name: tinea capitis
clinical_significance: A fungal infection of the scalp and hair, most common in children. It may cause scaling, itching, broken or falling hair, swollen tender areas, or pus-filled sores and usually needs prescription treatment.

name: tinea favosa
clinical_significance: A long-lasting fungal infection of the scalp or skin that causes yellow, cup-shaped crusts around hair follicles. It can lead to scarring and permanent hair loss if untreated and is now uncommon in many regions.

name: tinea pedis
clinical_significance: A fungal infection of the feet, also called athlete’s foot. It may cause itching, peeling or cracking between the toes, dry scaling on the soles, blisters, or sores and can spread to the nails.

name: tinea versicolor
clinical_significance: A common yeast-related skin condition causing lighter or darker patches with fine scaling, usually on the chest, back, or upper arms. The patches become more noticeable after surrounding skin tans.

name: tinidazole
clinical_significance: Tinidazole is a nitroimidazole antimicrobial effective against anaerobic bacteria and protozoa such as Giardia and Trichomonas; metallic taste, gastrointestinal effects, neuropathy, and an alcohol interaction may occur.

name: tinnitus
