clinical_significance: An ectopic pregnancy that implants in a fallopian tube instead of the uterus. It can rupture and cause internal bleeding; one-sided pain, vaginal bleeding, dizziness, or fainting may occur.

name: tube feeding
clinical_significance: Tube feeding delivers nutrition through a tube when swallowing is unsafe or intake is inadequate; tube position, aspiration risk, hydration, and formula tolerance require monitoring.

name: tuber cinereum
clinical_significance: The tuber cinereum is a hypothalamic region involved in endocrine and autonomic control; lesions can affect appetite, temperature, puberty, or pituitary function.

name: tubercidin
clinical_significance: Tubercidin is a toxic nucleoside antibiotic used mainly in research; it can interfere with RNA and DNA synthesis and is not a clinical treatment.

name: tuberculin
clinical_significance: Protein material from Mycobacterium tuberculosis used in a skin test for immune sensitization. A positive result suggests exposure or vaccination but does not by itself prove active tuberculosis or show when exposure occurred.

name: tuberculin test
clinical_significance: A skin test that checks whether the immune system has reacted to tuberculosis proteins. A positive result suggests infection or previous vaccination and does not by itself prove active disease.

name: tuberculosis
clinical_significance: An infection caused by \textit{Mycobacterium tuberculosis} bacteria. It usually affects the lungs but can affect other parts of the body. TB infection may remain inactive, causing no symptoms and not spreading to others, or develop into active TB disease. Active TB in the lungs or throat can spread through the air. Symptoms may include a lasting cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.

name: tuberculosis vaccine
clinical_significance: The BCG vaccine protects mainly against severe forms of tuberculosis in children and is used in many countries with high TB burden; it may complicate interpretation of tuberculin skin tests.

name: tuberous sclerosis
clinical_significance: A rare genetic disorder, also called tuberous sclerosis complex, that causes growths in the brain and

name: tubocurarine
clinical_significance: Tubocurarine is an older neuromuscular-blocking drug used to paralyze muscles during anesthesia; it can cause respiratory paralysis and requires controlled ventilation and monitoring.

name: tubular adenoma
clinical_significance: A benign glandular polyp, most often in the colon, that can develop dysplastic changes and is considered a precursor lesion for some colorectal cancers.

name: tubulin
clinical_significance: Tubulin forms microtubules needed for cell division and intracellular transport; many cancer drugs target tubulin, and defects can affect development and neurologic function.

name: tubulin binding
clinical_significance: Tubulin-binding compounds can disrupt cell division or nerve transport; this mechanism is used by several cancer drugs but can cause neuropathy and marrow suppression.

name: tubulostromal adenoma
clinical_significance: A tubulostromal adenoma is a rare ovarian stromal tumor that is usually benign; pathology and hormone-related symptoms guide follow-up.

name: tubulovillous adenoma
clinical_significance: A tubulovillous adenoma is a colorectal polyp with precancerous potential; complete removal and surveillance colonoscopy reduce the risk of progression to cancer.

name: tularemia
clinical_significance: Tularemia is infection with Francisella tularensis acquired from ticks, animals, contaminated water, or aerosols and causing ulcer-glandular, pulmonary, or other disease.

name: tumor angiogenesis
clinical_significance: Tumor angiogenesis is formation of blood vessels that supply a growing tumor; antiangiogenic drugs target this process but can cause hypertension, bleeding, clotting, or impaired wound healing.

name: tumor antigen
clinical_significance: Tumor antigens are molecules recognized by the immune system and can support cancer diagnosis, vaccine development, or targeted immunotherapy; expression varies between tumors.

name: tumor burden
clinical_significance: The total amount of cancer in the body, estimated from the number, size, and spread of tumor deposits. It can help doctors assess disease extent and treatment response but does not alone determine a person’s outlook.

name: tumor debulking
clinical_significance: Tumor debulking removes as much tumor as feasible when complete removal is not possible; it may relieve symptoms or improve response to other treatment, depending on cancer type.

name: tumor examination
clinical_significance: Tumor examination includes clinical assessment and imaging or pathology to define location, size, spread, and tissue type; biopsy often determines diagnosis and treatment.

name: tumor fragmentation
clinical_significance: Tumor fragmentation can occur during surgery or sample processing; it may affect margin assessment, staging, or risk of tumor-cell spread depending on the procedure and tumor type.

name: tumor identification
clinical_significance: Tumor identification determines whether a mass is benign or malignant and establishes its origin; pathology, imaging, and molecular tests guide staging and treatment selection.

name: tumor initiation
clinical_significance: Tumor initiation is the first step in cancer development after genetic or epigenetic changes; understanding initiating exposures supports prevention and early detection research.

name: tumor lysis syndrome
clinical_significance: A medical emergency caused by rapid cancer-cell breakdown, releasing substances that disturb blood chemistry. It can damage kidneys, trigger seizures or abnormal heart rhythms, and requires prevention, monitoring, and urgent treatment.

name: tumor marker
clinical_significance: A substance found in blood, urine, tissue, or another body fluid that may be produced by cancer or by the body’s response to it. Tumor markers can help monitor treatment or recurrence and sometimes guide diagnosis, but most are not specific enough to prove cancer alone.

name: tumor pain
clinical_significance: Tumor pain can result from pressure, invasion, inflammation, or treatment; assessment and timely symptom control improve function and quality of life.

name: tumor promotion
clinical_significance: Tumor promotion is the expansion of initiated cells through growth signals or exposures; it is studied in cancer prevention and does not alone establish an individual’s cancer risk.

name: tumor suppressor gene
clinical_significance: A gene that helps prevent uncontrolled cell growth by slowing cell division, repairing damaged DNA, or removing abnormal cells. Loss of its protective function can increase the chance of cancer.

name: tumor tissue
clinical_significance: Tumor tissue contains cancer cells and supporting cells; representative sampling is important for accurate pathology, biomarker testing, and treatment selection.

name: tumorigenicity
clinical_significance: Tumorigenicity is the ability of cells or tissue to form tumors; it is used in research and safety testing but is not a routine individual clinical measurement.

name: tumour necrosis
clinical_significance: Tumor necrosis is dead tissue within a tumor, often from inadequate blood supply or treatment; it can affect imaging, biopsy sampling, prognosis, and response assessment.

name: tungsten
clinical_significance: Tungsten is a metal used in medical devices and radiation shielding; occupational dust exposure can irritate lungs, and toxicity depends on compound and route.

name: tunica intima
clinical_significance: The tunica intima is the innermost blood-vessel layer; endothelial injury or plaque formation here contributes to atherosclerosis and thrombosis.

name: tunica media
clinical_significance: The middle layer of a blood-vessel wall, made mainly of muscle and elastic tissue. It can tighten or relax to change vessel width and help control blood pressure and blood flow.

name: tunica vaginalis
clinical_significance: A thin, slippery covering around most of the testis, formed from the abdominal lining during testicular descent. It allows the testis to move smoothly inside the scrotum.

name: tunicamycin
clinical_significance: Tunicamycin blocks protein glycosylation and is used to study cellular stress in research; it is toxic and not a therapeutic medicine.

name: turbinate
clinical_significance: Nasal turbinates warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air; enlargement or inflammation can obstruct breathing and contribute to congestion or sleep-disordered breathing.

name: turicella
clinical_significance: Turicella otitidis is a bacterium associated with ear infections, particularly otitis externa or media; culture results should be interpreted with examination and specimen source.

name: Turner's syndrome
clinical_significance: A chromosome condition affecting females in which one X chromosome is missing or altered. It commonly causes short stature and reduced ovarian function, with delayed or absent puberty and infertility. Heart, kidney, hearing, and thyroid problems may also occur, so lifelong medical follow-up is important.

name: turpentine
clinical_significance: Turpentine is a volatile solvent that can cause skin or airway irritation and severe poisoning if swallowed or aspirated; exposure needs prompt poison-control assessment.

name: T-wave alternans
clinical_significance: T-wave alternans is a beat-to-beat change in the size or shape of the heart's T wave and may indicate increased risk of dangerous ventricular rhythms.

name: twin
clinical_significance: A twin is one of two offspring from the same pregnancy, either identical from one fertilized egg or fraternal from two eggs and two sperm.

name: tympanic bulla
clinical_significance: The tympanic bulla is a hollow or expanded bony chamber surrounding the middle ear, especially prominent in many mammals.

name: tympanic membrane
clinical_significance: The thin eardrum separating the outer ear canal from the middle ear. Sound makes it vibrate, and those vibrations move the middle-ear bones; infection, injury, or pressure can tear it.

name: tympanometry
clinical_significance: An objective test that varies air pressure in the ear canal while measuring movement of the tympanic membrane and middle-ear pressure. It helps assess middle-ear fluid, eustachian-tube dysfunction, perforation, and ossicular or tympanic-membrane abnormalities.

name: tympanoplasty
clinical_significance: Surgical repair or reconstruction of the tympanic membrane and, when necessary, the middle-ear ossicles to close a perforation or improve hearing.

name: typhlitis
clinical_significance: A serious infection and inflammation of the first part of the large intestine, usually in someone with very low white-cell counts after cancer treatment. It can cause right-sided abdominal pain, fever, diarrhea, and bowel damage and needs urgent care.

name: typhoid
clinical_significance: Typhoid fever is a potentially severe systemic infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually spread through contaminated food or water; early diagnosis, antibiotics, and sanitation reduce complications and transmission.

name: tyramine
clinical_significance: A naturally occurring amine found in some aged or fermented foods. In people taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors, excessive tyramine can cause a dangerous rise in blood pressure.

name: tyrosinase peptide
clinical_significance: Tyrosinase peptides are studied as melanoma antigens for immune recognition and vaccine development; their clinical use depends on tumor expression and trial evidence.

name: tyrosine
clinical_significance: An amino acid used to build proteins and make thyroid hormones, melanin, and adrenaline-like chemicals. The body usually makes enough from phenylalanine, but inherited metabolic disorders can disrupt this pathway.

name: ubidecarenone
clinical_significance: Ubidecarenone is coenzyme Q10, a mitochondrial electron-transport component used as a supplement; evidence varies by condition and it can interact with warfarin and some cancer treatments.

name: ubiquitin
clinical_significance: Ubiquitin tags proteins for degradation or trafficking; disruption of ubiquitin pathways is linked to cancer and neurodegeneration and is targeted by some cancer therapies.

name: ubiquitination
clinical_significance: Ubiquitination regulates protein stability and signaling; altered ubiquitin pathways can contribute to cancer, immune disorders, and neurodegenerative disease.

name: uhl anomaly
clinical_significance: A rare heart defect present from birth in which much of the muscle of the right lower chamber is missing. The chamber may pump poorly, causing blue coloring, abnormal rhythms, or heart failure in infancy or childhood.

name: ulcer
clinical_significance: A crater-like open sore caused by loss of the surface layers of skin or a mucous membrane, sometimes extending into deeper tissue. Causes include poor blood flow, pressure, infection, nerve damage, inflammation, injury, and cancer; the appearance and cause determine treatment.

name: ulcerative colitis
clinical_significance: A long-term disease causing inflammation and open sores in the inner lining of the rectum and colon. It usually starts in the rectum and spreads continuously through part of the colon. It may cause repeated diarrhea, blood or mucus in the stool, urgent bowel movements, abdominal cramps, tiredness, weight loss, or a feeling that the bowel has not emptied. Symptoms often flare and then improve. Severe disease may cause heavy bleeding, anemia, dehydration, or a hole in the bowel; long-standing exte

name: ulna
clinical_significance: The forearm bone on the side of the little finger. Its upper end forms most of the hinge of the elbow, and its lower end helps form the wrist. Together with the radius, it supports rotation of the forearm and movement of the hand.

name: ulnar hypoplasia
clinical_significance: Underdevelopment or partial absence of the ulna, the forearm bone on the little-finger side. Present from birth in most cases, it may shorten or bend the forearm, limit elbow or wrist movement, and occur with finger or other body differences.

name: ulocladium
clinical_significance: Ulocladium is an environmental mold that rarely causes opportunistic infection; identification from a clinical specimen requires correlation with symptoms and immune status.

name: ultracentrifugation
clinical_significance: Ultracentrifugation separates particles such as viruses, proteins, and lipoproteins by density; it supports research and specialized diagnostic testing.

name: ultradian rhythm
clinical_significance: Ultradian rhythms are biological cycles shorter than a day, including hormone and sleep-stage patterns; disruption may affect sleep, endocrine function, or treatment timing.

name: ultrafiltration
clinical_significance: A process in which pressure pushes water and small dissolved substances through a very fine filter while larger particles remain behind. The kidneys use it to begin forming urine, and dialysis uses it to remove excess fluid.

name: ultralente insulin
clinical_significance: Ultralente insulin is a long-acting insulin formulation that is no longer commonly used; patients should not substitute insulin products without clinician guidance because action profiles differ.

name: ultrasonic therapy
clinical_significance: Treatment using high-frequency sound energy to heat, move, break up, or otherwise affect tissue. It is used in selected physical-therapy procedures and some operations; benefits and risks depend on the device, body site, and condition.

name: ultrasonography
clinical_significance: A scan using high-frequency sound waves to create images of organs, tissues, vessels, or a fetus without radiation.

name: ultrasound biomicroscopy
clinical_significance: Very high-frequency ultrasound that creates detailed images of the front part of the eye, including the cornea, iris, lens, and drainage angle when an ordinary eye examination is not enough.

name: ultraviolet microscopy
clinical_significance: Ultraviolet microscopy uses UV light to improve contrast or resolution in specialized laboratory imaging; controlled exposure protects specimens and operators.

name: ultraviolet rays
clinical_significance: Invisible electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible violet light. Excess exposure can cause sunburn, photoaging, eye injury, and skin cancers; controlled ultraviolet exposure has selected therapeutic uses.

name: ultraviolet therapy
clinical_significance: Ultraviolet therapy uses controlled UV exposure for selected skin disorders; cumulative exposure can increase skin aging and cancer risk, so dose and monitoring are important.

name: umbilical cord
clinical_significance: The connection between a fetus and the placenta. It contains blood vessels that carry oxygen, nutrients, and waste between them and is protected by a soft, cushioning tissue.

name: umbilical hernia
clinical_significance: A soft bulge caused when tissue pushes through the opening at the navel. Many infant hernias close as the child grows, while adult hernias may enlarge or become trapped and painful and sometimes need surgery.

name: umbilical vein
clinical_significance: The umbilical vein carries oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus during pregnancy.

name: uncertainty
clinical_significance: Uncertainty in diagnosis or treatment reflects incomplete evidence or prediction; communicating what is known, what remains uncertain, and the next steps supports informed decisions.

name: unconsciousness
clinical_significance: Loss of awareness and normal response to surroundings, ranging from brief fainting to prolonged coma. It can result from reduced brain blood flow, injury, seizures, low blood sugar, drugs, or serious illness.

name: underage drinking
clinical_significance: Underage drinking can impair brain development and judgment and increases risks of injury, poisoning, violence, and later substance-use disorder; screening and early support can reduce harm.

name: undetermined
clinical_significance: Undetermined means the cause or classification has not yet been established; further testing, observation, or expert review may be needed before choosing treatment.

name: undifferentiated
clinical_significance: Not showing the recognizable features of a specialized cell or tissue. An undifferentiated tumor has cells that look very unlike normal tissue, so its origin and behavior may be difficult to determine.

name: undifferentiated carcinoma
clinical_significance: A high-grade carcinoma whose cells lack recognizable features of a specific tissue or tumor subtype; diagnosis and treatment require pathology, immunostaining, and staging.

name: undulate ribs
clinical_significance: Undulate ribs are a descriptive morphologic term for wavy or irregular rib contours; clinical importance depends on imaging findings and symptoms, such as pain or respiratory compromise.

name: unencoded data
clinical_significance: Unencoded data are information not represented in a structured code; they may be missed by automated clinical systems, so accurate narrative documentation remains important.

name: unequivocal
clinical_significance: Unequivocal means clear and unambiguous; in clinical reporting it signals that a finding meets the stated diagnostic criteria without material doubt.

name: unerupted tooth
clinical_significance: A tooth that has not emerged into the oral cavity at the expected time. It may be normally developing, delayed, impacted, or prevented from erupting by obstruction or abnormal position.

name: unevaluable
clinical_significance: Unevaluable means there is not enough information or specimen quality to make a reliable assessment; repeat testing or a new sample may be needed.

name: unilaminar epithelium
clinical_significance: Unilaminar epithelium is a single layer of lining cells; damage or abnormal growth can affect barrier function, absorption, or secretion in the involved organ.

name: unilateral
clinical_significance: Affecting, occurring on, or involving one side of the body or one paired organ, such as unilateral weakness or unilateral eye disease.

name: unilateral microphthalmos
clinical_significance: A congenital condition in which one eye is abnormally small. It may be associated with other ocular malformations and can cause substantial visual impairment.

name: uninodular goiter
clinical_significance: An enlarged thyroid containing one main lump, or nodule. Blood tests and ultrasound help assess thyroid function and the chance of cancer; some nodules need follow-up or a needle sample.

name: uniparental disomy
clinical_significance: A chromosome difference in which both copies of a chromosome, or part of one, come from the same parent. It can cause disease by disrupting genes that depend on parental origin or by giving a child two copies of a harmful gene variant.

name: unipolar neuron
clinical_significance: A unipolar neuron has a single process and is mainly encountered in sensory pathways; sensory neuron injury can cause pain, numbness, or loss of protective sensation.

name: unknown
clinical_significance: Unknown status indicates that a health condition, exposure, or history has not been confirmed; it should prompt clarification when the information affects testing, treatment, or safety.

name: unresectable
clinical_significance: Describing a tumor or lesion that cannot be completely removed safely by surgery because of its location, extent, invasion of vital structures, or the patient’s operative risk.

name: unsaturated phytosterol
clinical_significance: Unsaturated phytosterols are plant-derived compounds that can reduce intestinal cholesterol absorption; people with sitosterolemia should avoid excess plant sterols because they can accumulate and cause vascular disease.

name: unstable angina
clinical_significance: Chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart that is new, worsening, lasts longer, or occurs at rest, without clear evidence of heart-muscle death. It is an emergency warning of possible heart attack.

name: untranslated region
clinical_significance: An untranslated region regulates messenger RNA stability, localization, and translation without encoding protein; variants can alter gene expression and contribute to disease.

name: upamostat
clinical_significance: Upamostat is an investigational protease inhibitor studied in cancer and inflammatory disease; it is not established routine treatment, and clinical-trial evidence determines its potential role.

name: upper arm
clinical_significance: The portion of the upper limb between the shoulder and elbow, containing the humerus and muscles, nerves, and vessels that serve the arm.

name: upper extremity
clinical_significance: The anatomic region extending from the shoulder through the arm, forearm, wrist, and hand. Disorders may involve its bones, joints, muscles, nerves, vessels, or skin.

name: urachal cyst
clinical_significance: A fluid-filled sac left from the temporary fetal connection between the bladder and navel. It may cause no symptoms, but infection can produce lower-abdominal pain, fever, navel discharge, or urinary symptoms.

name: urachus
clinical_significance: An embryologic connection between the fetal bladder and umbilicus that normally becomes the median umbilical ligament after birth. Persistent urachal remnants can form cysts, sinuses, or other complications.

name: uracil
clinical_significance: Uracil is a nucleic-acid base found in RNA; altered uracil handling can cause DNA damage and is relevant to rare metabolic disorders and cancer-drug mechanisms.

name: uracil mustard
clinical_significance: Uracil mustard is an older alkylating chemotherapy drug that damages DNA; use is largely historical because of marrow suppression and other toxicities.

name: uracil nucleotides
clinical_significance: Uracil nucleotides are RNA building blocks and metabolic intermediates; abnormal nucleotide synthesis can impair cell growth and cause inherited metabolic disease.

name: uranium
clinical_significance: A naturally occurring radioactive heavy metal. Internal exposure can damage the kidneys, while inhaled or retained radioactive material can also expose tissues to ionizing radiation.

name: urea
clinical_significance: The principal nitrogen-containing waste product of protein metabolism, formed in the liver and excreted mainly by the kidneys.

name: urea cycle
clinical_significance: A series of chemical reactions in the liver that changes toxic ammonia, produced when the body breaks down protein, into urea. The kidneys then remove urea in urine.

name: ureaplasma
clinical_significance: A genus of very small bacteria without a cell wall that can colonize the genital or urinary tract and is sometimes associated with urethritis or pregnancy complications.

name: ureaplasma urealyticum
clinical_significance: A cell-wall-free bacterium that can colonize the genital or urinary tract and is sometimes associated with nongonococcal urethritis, pregnancy complications, or infection in vulnerable newborns.

name: uremia
clinical_significance: A clinical syndrome caused by advanced kidney failure and accumulation of waste products and other biologically active

name: ureter
clinical_significance: One of two muscular tubes that carry urine from a kidney to the bladder. A stone or narrowing can block a ureter and cause severe side pain, swelling of the kidney, infection, or kidney damage.

name: ureter duplex
clinical_significance: A birth variation in which one kidney has two urine tubes instead of one. It may cause no problems but can lead to urine flowing backward, blockage, repeated infections, or poor drainage.

name: ureter fissus
clinical_significance: A birth difference in which a ureter is divided lengthwise or partly duplicated. It may cause no symptoms, but abnormal urine flow can lead to urine reflux, blockage, repeated infection, or poor kidney drainage.

name: ureter obstruction
clinical_significance: Blockage of urine flow from a kidney to the bladder, commonly caused by a stone, stricture, tumor, or external compression and potentially leading to hydronephrosis, infection, or kidney injury.

name: ureteral calculi
clinical_significance: Stones that form in or pass through a ureter, the tube carrying urine from a kidney to the bladder.

name: ureteral catheters
clinical_significance: Thin tubes passed into a ureter to drain urine, inject contrast, measure pressure, or guide a procedure. Possible complications include infection, bleeding, a tear, movement of the tube, or blockage.

name: ureteral polyp
clinical_significance: Usually a benign fibroepithelial growth arising from the ureter. It may cause hematuria, flank pain, or obstruction and must be distinguished from urothelial malignancy when evaluated.

name: ureteral stenosis
clinical_significance: Narrowing of the ureter caused by scar tissue, prior surgery, radiation, stones, inflammation, or congenital disease, impairing urine drainage and possibly causing hydronephrosis or recurrent infection.

name: ureteric perforation
clinical_significance: A tear or hole in the ureter that can allow urine to leak into surrounding tissue, usually after instrumentation, surgery, trauma, or a stone; it needs prompt urologic assessment.

name: ureteritis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the ureter, usually related to infection, obstruction, stone passage,

name: ureterocele
clinical_significance: A balloon-like dilation of the lower ureter where it enters the bladder, usually congenital; it can obstruct urine flow and cause infection, hydronephrosis, reflux, stones, or impaired renal function.

name: ureterolithiasis
clinical_significance: A kidney stone located in the ureter, the tube from the kidney to the bladder. It can block urine and cause severe wave-like side pain, blood in the urine, nausea, infection, or kidney damage.

name: ureteroscopes
clinical_significance: Small endoscopes used to inspect the ureter and renal collecting system and to perform procedures such as stone removal, biopsy, or stent placement.

name: ureterostomy procedure
clinical_significance: Surgery that creates an opening from a ureter to the skin or another urinary conduit to divert urine when normal drainage to the bladder is impossible or must be bypassed.

name: urethan
clinical_significance: Urethane (ethyl carbamate) is a carcinogenic chemical historically used in research and some industrial processes; exposure should be minimized and assessed by occupational health.

name: urethra
clinical_significance: The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body. In people with male reproductive anatomy it also carries semen; the shorter urethra in people with female reproductive anatomy makes bladder infections more likely.

name: urethra disorder
clinical_significance: A condition affecting the urethra, such as infection, inflammation, stricture, trauma, congenital abnormality, or tumor, that may cause pain, discharge, weak stream, or retention.

name: urethral carcinoma
clinical_significance: A rare cancer arising from the urethra that may cause bleeding, a lump, discharge, pain, or difficult urination; diagnosis requires examination, imaging, and biopsy.

name: urethral catheter
clinical_significance: A tube inserted through the urethra into the bladder to drain urine, obtain a specimen, instill medication, or monitor output. Urinary infection and urethral trauma are important risks.

name: urethral diverticulum
clinical_significance: A pocket beside the urethra that connects with the urine tube, often developing after infection or blockage of nearby glands. It may cause burning urination, urine dribbling after voiding, repeated infections, pain during sex, or a vaginal-wall lump.

name: urethral fistula
clinical_significance: An abnormal channel between the urethra and another epithelial surface, often the vagina or skin. It can cause continuous urine leakage, recurrent infection, and local irritation.

name: urethral infection
clinical_significance: Infection involving the urethra, commonly caused by bacteria, including sexually transmitted organisms.

name: urethral obstruction
clinical_significance: Partial or complete blockage of urine leaving the bladder, often from stricture, stone, prostate disease, tumor, or a congenital valve. Acute retention can damage the bladder or kidneys.

name: urethral sphincter
clinical_significance: Muscles around the urine tube that help keep urine from leaking and relax when a person urinates. Nerve or muscle damage can weaken control and cause leakage or difficulty emptying the bladder.

name: urethral stenosis
clinical_significance: Scar-related narrowing of the urethral channel that restricts urinary flow and can cause spraying, weak stream, recurrent infection, retention, or bladder damage.

name: urethritis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the urethra, often caused by infection, including sexually transmitted infections, but sometimes by irritation or injury. It can cause burning urination, itching, pelvic discomfort, or discharge.

name: uric acid
clinical_significance: A waste product formed when the body breaks down purines. High blood levels can cause gout or kidney stones, although many people with high levels have no symptoms.

name: uricosuric agent
clinical_significance: Uricosuric agents increase urinary uric-acid excretion to lower blood levels in gout; kidney stones, drug interactions, and kidney function affect their suitability.

name: uridine
clinical_significance: Uridine is a nucleoside used to make RNA and support metabolism; uridine triacetate is used for specific severe fluoropyrimidine toxicity and hereditary orotic aciduria.

name: uridine diphosphate
clinical_significance: Uridine diphosphate participates in carbohydrate metabolism and synthesis of glycogen and complex sugars; pathway defects can affect energy balance and development.

name: uridine monophosphate
clinical_significance: Uridine monophosphate is a nucleotide involved in RNA synthesis and pyrimidine metabolism; abnormal pathways can be relevant to rare metabolic disorders.

name: uridine triacetate
clinical_significance: An oral prodrug that supplies uridine and is used as an emergency antidote for severe or life-threatening toxicity from fluorouracil or related fluoropyrimidines, under specialist direction.

name: uridine triphosphate
clinical_significance: Uridine triphosphate is used in RNA synthesis and cellular signaling; its conversion products also regulate airway surface hydration and mucus clearance.

name: urinal
clinical_significance: A portable container used to collect urine from someone who cannot easily reach a toilet. It should be emptied, cleaned, and stored safely to reduce spills, odor, and infection risk.

name: urinalysis
clinical_significance: Laboratory examination of urine for its appearance, acidity, blood, cells, protein, sugar, ketones, bacteria, and other substances. It can provide clues to infection, kidney disease, bleeding, diabetes, dehydration, and other illness.

name: urinary
clinical_significance: Relating to urine or to the organs and processes involved in making, storing, and passing urine, including the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.

name: urinary bladder
clinical_significance: A hollow muscular organ in the lower abdomen that stores urine until it is released through the urethra.

name: urinary bladder disorder
clinical_significance: A disease affecting bladder storage or emptying, including infection, overactivity, pain syndrome, stones, tumor, neurologic dysfunction, or outlet obstruction.

name: urinary calculi
clinical_significance: Stones formed from crystallized minerals in the urinary tract. They may cause colicky pain, hematuria, obstruction, infection, or kidney injury depending on their size and location.

name: urinary catheter
clinical_significance: A hollow, flexible tube inserted through the urethra into the bladder to drain urine; it may be used intermittently or left in place.

name: urinary catheterization
clinical_significance: Insertion of a tube into the bladder to drain urine, measure output, obtain a specimen, or deliver treatment; infection, trauma, and blockage are possible complications.

name: urinary diversion
clinical_significance: Surgical or catheter-based rerouting of urine when the normal passage from the kidneys to the urethra cannot be used, often to a stoma or bowel reservoir.

name: urinary fistula
clinical_significance: An abnormal connection between part of the urinary tract and another organ or the skin, allowing urine to leak outside its normal pathway. Causes include surgery, childbirth injury, inflammation, and cancer.

name: urinary hesitation
clinical_significance: Difficulty starting or maintaining urination, which may result from prostate enlargement, urethral narrowing, medications, nerve disorders, pain, or impaired bladder contraction.

name: urinary incontinence
clinical_significance: Unwanted leakage of urine. It may happen with coughing or exercise, a sudden strong urge, an overfull bladder, difficulty reaching the toilet, or nerve and muscle problems. More than one pattern may occur in the same person.

name: urinary retention
clinical_significance: Inability to empty the bladder fully. It may be sudden and painful or develop gradually with a weak stream, frequent small amounts of urine, or leakage from an overfull bladder. Blockage, medicines, nerve problems, or weak bladder muscles can cause it.

name: urinary system
clinical_significance: The kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra. Together they filter blood, make and transport urine, store and remove it, and help regulate fluid volume, electrolytes, acid-base balance, blood pressure, and hormone-related functions such as red-cell production.

name: urinary tract
clinical_significance: The kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra. Together these organs make urine, carry it to the bladder, store it, and remove it from the body.

name: urinary tract disorder
clinical_significance: Any disease of the kidneys, ureters, bladder, or urethra, including infection, stones, obstruction, congenital abnormalities, cancer, and functional or neurologic disorders.

name: urinary tract infection
clinical_significance: Infection of the urinary tract, classified as lower infection such as cystitis or urethritis,

name: urinary tract neoplasm
clinical_significance: A benign or malignant growth in the kidneys, ureters, bladder, or urethra; evaluation depends on its site, symptoms, tissue type, and extent of spread.

name: urinary urgency
clinical_significance: A sudden, difficult-to-delay need to urinate. It may occur with urinary infection, bladder irritation,

name: urination
clinical_significance: The process of releasing urine from the bladder through the urethra and out of the body.

name: urination disorder
clinical_significance: Abnormal storage or emptying of urine causing frequency, urgency, dysuria, incontinence, hesitancy, weak stream, retention, or excessive or reduced urine output.

name: urine
clinical_significance: The liquid waste produced by the kidneys, containing water and dissolved substances eliminated from the blood.

name: urine conductivity
clinical_significance: Urine conductivity measures how readily urine carries electrical current and reflects its dissolved electrolyte and solute concentration.

name: urine cytology
clinical_significance: Microscopic examination of cells shed into urine, mainly used to help detect high-grade urothelial carcinoma and some other abnormalities. A negative result does not exclude all urinary-tract cancers.

name: urochordata
clinical_significance: Urochordates are marine animals used in developmental and evolutionary research; they are not a human pathogen or clinical diagnosis.

name: urogenital fistula
clinical_significance: An abnormal connection between the urinary and genital tracts, such as a vesicovaginal or ureterovaginal fistula. It commonly causes continuous urinary leakage and requires specialist evaluation.

name: urogenital system
clinical_significance: The related urinary and reproductive organs and their associated ducts, vessels, and supporting tissues. The systems share developmental origins and anatomic relationships.

name: urolithiasis
clinical_significance: Formation of stones in the urinary tract, including the kidneys, ureters, bladder, or urethra. Stone composition

name: urologist
clinical_significance: A doctor who specializes in the urinary system and, in many practices, the male reproductive system. Urologists diagnose and treat kidney stones, infections, urine leakage, prostate problems, cancers, infertility, and conditions requiring procedures or surgery.

name: urology
clinical_significance: The medical specialty that diagnoses and treats diseases of the kidneys, urine tubes, bladder, and urethra, as well as the male reproductive organs. Treatment may include medicines, procedures, or surgery.

name: urostomy leak
clinical_significance: Escape of urine beneath or around a urostomy appliance or from a surgical connection. Persistent leakage can irritate the skin and may signal poor appliance fit, obstruction, infection, or a surgical complication.

name: urostomy procedure
clinical_significance: Surgery that diverts urine through a stoma into an external pouch or conduit, commonly after bladder removal or when the lower urinary tract cannot safely transport urine.

name: urostomy prolapse
clinical_significance: Protrusion of a segment of bowel used as a urostomy stoma beyond its usual level. It may cause bleeding, swelling, appliance problems, or impaired urine drainage and should be assessed clinically.

name: urostomy stenosis
clinical_significance: Narrowing of a urinary stoma or conduit that impedes drainage, causing reduced urine output, leakage, infection, or kidney-pressure changes and sometimes requiring revision.

name: urothelium
clinical_significance: A specialized stretchable lining of the renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, and part of the urethra. It forms a protective barrier between urine and underlying tissues and allows the bladder to expand.

name: ursodeoxycholic acid
clinical_significance: A hydrophilic bile acid used for primary biliary cholangitis and selected cholestatic liver diseases; it may also dissolve certain small cholesterol gallstones when bile flow is preserved.

name: urticaria
clinical_significance: A skin reaction causing transient, itchy raised welts that change location and usually resolve within 24 hours.

name: urticaria pigmentosa
clinical_significance: A skin condition in which too many mast cells collect in the skin, causing tan or brown spots or bumps that swell and itch when rubbed. Flushing or other body-wide symptoms can occur.

name: Usher syndrome
clinical_significance: An inherited condition causing hearing loss together with gradually worsening vision from retinal disease. The age and severity vary by type; hearing, vision, balance, communication, and genetic support may all be needed.

name: ustekinumab
clinical_significance: A biologic medicine that blocks immune signals involved in inflammation. It is used for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, and other approved conditions; infections and allergic reactions are important risks.

name: ustilago
clinical_significance: Ustilago is a genus of smut fungi that mainly infect plants and grain; human infection is rare, and food or occupational exposure may be relevant when illness is suspected.

name: uterine adnexae
clinical_significance: The structures beside and connected to the uterus, mainly the fallopian tubes, ovaries, and supporting tissues. Problems in these structures can cause pelvic pain, abnormal bleeding, infertility, or an ectopic pregnancy.

name: uterine cancer
clinical_significance: Cancer arising in the uterus, most commonly from the endometrium. Abnormal vaginal bleeding,

name: uterine cavity
clinical_significance: The hollow space inside the uterus, lined by the endometrium. A fertilized egg normally implants in this lining, which thickens during the menstrual cycle and supports pregnancy; polyps, fibroids, scar tissue, or abnormal shape may affect it.

name: uterine fibroids
clinical_significance: Benign tumors arising from the smooth muscle of the uterus, commonly called uterine leiomyomas or uterine myomas. They may be single or multiple and may be submucosal, intramural, or subserosal. Many cause no symptoms, while others may cause heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pressure, pain, urinary or bowel symptoms, infertility, or pregnancy-related complications. Degeneration within a fibroid can cause localized or acute pain; rare malignant uterine smooth-muscle tumors must be distinguished wh

name: uterine fistula
clinical_significance: A uterine fistula is an abnormal passage connecting the uterus with another organ or the skin, often after surgery, childbirth injury, infection, or cancer.

name: uterine gland
clinical_significance: A small gland in the lining of the uterus that produces fluid and helps support the early embryo. Its activity changes during the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.

name: uterine hemorrhage
clinical_significance: Heavy or abnormal bleeding from the uterus, occurring during pregnancy, after childbirth, or at other

name: uterine leiomyosarcoma
clinical_significance: A rare malignant tumor of uterine smooth muscle that may cause abnormal bleeding, pelvic pain, or an enlarging mass; diagnosis is based on tissue examination and staging.

name: uterine monitoring
clinical_significance: Recording how often, how long, and how strongly the uterus contracts. During labor it helps assess progress, response to induction medicines, and excessive contractions that could affect the baby.

name: uterine myomectomy
clinical_significance: Surgical removal of uterine fibroids while preserving the uterus; it may be performed through hysteroscopy, laparoscopy, or open surgery depending on fibroid size and location.

name: uterine obstruction
clinical_significance: Blockage that prevents normal passage through the uterus or cervix, which may cause menstrual outflow obstruction, infertility, pregnancy complications, or retained blood or tissue.

name: uterine perforation
clinical_significance: A hole through the wall of the uterus, most often caused by an instrument used during a procedure such as hysteroscopy or removal of uterine tissue. It can cause internal bleeding or injury to nearby organs and may need repair.

name: uterine prolapse
clinical_significance: Descent of the uterus toward or through the vaginal opening because pelvic-floor muscles and supporting tissues have weakened. It may cause pelvic pressure, a bulge, backache, urinary or bowel problems, or discomfort during sex; childbirth and aging increase risk.

name: uterine rupture
clinical_significance: A complete tear through the wall of the uterus, usually during pregnancy or labor. It can cause severe internal bleeding and reduce the baby’s oxygen supply; previous cesarean surgery is an important risk factor.

name: uterus
clinical_significance: A hollow muscular organ in the pelvis between the bladder and rectum. Its inner lining thickens to prepare for pregnancy and is shed during menstruation. A fertilized egg normally implants in this lining, and a fetus develops in the uterus during pregnancy.

name: uterus disorder
clinical_significance: A condition affecting the uterus, including fibroids, adenomyosis, endometriosis, infection, abnormal bleeding, congenital anomalies, prolapse, and cancer.

name: uterus neoplasm
clinical_significance: A benign or malignant growth arising in the uterus, including fibroids, endometrial cancer, and sarcomas; diagnosis depends on examination, imaging, and tissue sampling.

name: uvea
clinical_significance: The middle layer of the eye, made up of the iris, ciliary body, and choroid. It controls the amount of light entering the eye, helps focus vision, and supplies blood to eye tissues.

name: uveal disease
clinical_significance: A disorder of the iris, ciliary body, or choroid, including uveitis, tumors, vascular disease, and inflammation that may cause eye pain, photophobia, floaters, or visual loss.

name: uveal melanoma
clinical_significance: The most common primary cancer inside the adult eye. It begins in pigment-producing cells of the iris, ciliary body, or choroid and may cause visual changes or be found during an eye examination; it can spread to other organs.

name: uveal neoplasm
clinical_significance: A tumor arising in the uveal tract of the eye—the iris, ciliary body, or choroid; malignant melanoma may threaten vision and spread to distant organs.

name: uveitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of the uvea, the middle layer of the eye containing the iris, ciliary body, and choroid. It may also affect nearby eye tissues and may result from infection, immune-mediated disease, injury, or an unknown cause. Symptoms vary with the affected area and may include pain, redness, light sensitivity, floaters, or blurred vision.

name: uvula
clinical_significance: A small, soft flap hanging from the back of the roof of the mouth. It helps with swallowing and speech; swelling can cause gagging, pain, snoring, or difficulty breathing.

name: vaccination
clinical_significance: Giving a vaccine to train the immune system to recognize a specific infection. Vaccination lowers the risk of illness, severe complications, and sometimes transmission; the recommended schedule depends on age, health, and local guidance.

name: vaccine
clinical_significance: A vaccine trains the immune system to recognize a specific infection or toxin and respond more effectively. Vaccination lowers the risk of severe disease and helps protect communities.

name: vaccine adjuvant
clinical_significance: Vaccine adjuvants enhance or shape immune responses to vaccine antigens; they can improve protection or reduce antigen dose, while local reactions and rare adverse events are monitored.

name: vaccine development
clinical_significance: Vaccine development evaluates safety, immune response, efficacy, and manufacturing quality before a vaccine is approved; clinical trials and ongoing safety surveillance are essential.

name: vaccine therapy
clinical_significance: Vaccine therapy uses a vaccine to prevent or treat disease, including some cancer immunotherapies; effects depend on the target and evidence for patient benefit.

name: vaccinia virus
clinical_significance: Vaccinia virus is a poxvirus used to make smallpox vaccines and studied in some experimental cancer treatments; accidental infection is uncommon but possible.

name: vacuole
clinical_significance: Vacuoles store or process materials within cells; abnormal vacuolar function can contribute to lysosomal, kidney, or other cellular disorders.

name: vacuum curettage
clinical_significance: A procedure that removes tissue from the uterus using suction, commonly for uterine evacuation or endometrial sampling. Risks include bleeding, infection, retained tissue, and rarely uterine injury.

name: vadimezan
clinical_significance: Vadimezan is an investigational vascular-disrupting anticancer agent studied in clinical trials; it is not routine therapy, and clinical evidence determines its potential role.

name: vagal paraganglioma
clinical_significance: A usually slow-growing tumor arising from nerve-related cells near the vagus nerve in the neck. It may cause a neck mass, hoarseness, swallowing difficulty, or nerve symptoms and can be identified with imaging and specialist assessment.

name: vagina
clinical_significance: A muscular, elastic canal connecting the cervix to the vaginal opening. It allows menstrual blood to leave the body, receives a penis or other objects during vaginal sex, and serves as the birth canal.

name: vagina carcinoma
clinical_significance: Cancer arising from the vagina. It may cause unusual bleeding, discharge, pain, or a visible sore, although early cancer may cause no symptoms; examination and tissue testing are needed for diagnosis.

name: vagina neoplasm
clinical_significance: An abnormal growth in the vagina that may be benign, precancerous, or cancerous. It can cause bleeding, discharge, pain, or a lump, although early growths may cause no symptoms.

name: vaginal
clinical_significance: Vaginal refers to the vagina or its route of medication delivery; symptoms such as pain, bleeding, or discharge should be assessed in context of infection, trauma, hormones, and pregnancy.

name: vaginal adenosis
clinical_significance: Vaginal adenosis is the presence of glandular tissue in the vaginal lining, sometimes associated with prenatal diethylstilbestrol exposure; surveillance may be advised because rare clear-cell cancer risk is increased.

name: vaginal diaphragm
clinical_significance: A vaginal diaphragm is a barrier contraceptive placed over the cervix; effectiveness depends on correct fit and use, and it does not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

name: vaginal dilator
clinical_significance: A smooth device used to gently stretch or keep open the vaginal canal when it has become narrow or short because of scarring, surgery, radiation, or a difference present from birth.

name: vaginal discharge
clinical_significance: Vaginal discharge may be normal or may indicate infection, inflammation, hormonal change, or another condition. Normal discharge is usually clear to whitish and odourless and varies with the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, sexual arousal, and some contraceptives.

name: vaginal disease
clinical_significance: Vaginal disease includes infection, inflammation, structural change, and neoplasia; diagnosis depends on symptoms, examination, and targeted testing rather than discharge alone.

name: vaginal douching
clinical_significance: Vaginal douching can disrupt normal vaginal flora, irritate tissue, and increase infection risk; it is not recommended for routine hygiene or treatment.

name: vaginal dryness
clinical_significance: Reduced vaginal lubrication, commonly associated with menopause, breastfeeding, hormonal

name: vaginal fistula
clinical_significance: An abnormal passage between the vagina and another organ, commonly the bladder or rectum. It may cause continuous urine or stool leakage, infection, skin irritation, and emotional distress.

name: vaginal hemorrhage
clinical_significance: Heavy or clinically significant bleeding from the vagina. Causes include childbirth, pregnancy complications, trauma, infection, structural disease, hormonal disorders, and gynecologic cancer; severe or pregnancy-related bleeding can be life-threatening.

name: vaginal hysterectomy
clinical_significance: Surgical removal of the uterus through the vagina. It may be used for selected benign uterine conditions and usually avoids an abdominal incision, although suitability depends on anatomy and disease.

name: vaginal obstruction
clinical_significance: Vaginal obstruction can result from congenital anomalies, scarring, tumors, or foreign bodies and may cause pain, retained menstrual blood, or difficulty with intercourse or childbirth.

name: vaginal perforation
clinical_significance: Vaginal perforation is a full-thickness injury that can damage adjacent organs or cause bleeding and infection; symptoms after procedures or trauma need prompt evaluation.

name: vaginal polyp
clinical_significance: A vaginal polyp is often benign but may bleed or resemble a more serious lesion; examination and pathology are considered when growth is symptomatic or atypical.

name: vaginal pruritus
clinical_significance: Vaginal itching can result from yeast, bacterial vaginosis, sexually transmitted infection, dermatitis, or hormonal dryness; testing helps avoid inappropriate treatment.

name: vaginal stricture
clinical_significance: Vaginal stricture is narrowing from scarring, radiation, surgery, or inflammation; it can cause pain, difficulty with examination or intercourse, and may require dilation or reconstructive care.

name: vaginal system
clinical_significance: A vaginal delivery system releases medication locally over time; correct placement and product-specific dosing reduce treatment failure and adverse effects.

name: vaginectomy
clinical_significance: Surgical removal of part or all of the vagina, usually to treat selected cancers or severe disease; effects may include changes in sexual function, fertility, urination, and bowel function.

name: vaginitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation or irritation of the vagina that may cause discharge, itching, burning, odor, pain, or discomfort with urination or sex. Causes include infections, hormones, chemicals, allergies, and tissue dryness.

name: vaginospasm
clinical_significance: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder involves persistent pain, fear, or difficulty with vaginal penetration; trauma-informed assessment and individualized pelvic-floor, medical, and psychological care can help.

name: vagococcus
clinical_significance: Vagococcus is a genus of bacteria found in animals and the environment that rarely causes human infection; identification from a patient sample requires clinical correlation.

name: vagotomy
clinical_significance: Surgery that cuts selected branches of the vagus nerve to reduce signals that stimulate stomach acid and movement. It was once used for difficult stomach ulcers but is now uncommon because medicines and less invasive treatments are available.

name: vagus nerve
clinical_significance: The tenth cranial nerve, carrying signals between the brain and the heart, lungs, throat, voice box, and digestive tract. It helps regulate heart rate, breathing, swallowing, voice, and digestion.

name: valacyclovir
clinical_significance: An antiviral medicine that the body changes into acyclovir to stop herpes viruses from multiplying. It treats cold sores, genital herpes, and shingles; the dose may need adjustment in kidney disease, and excessive levels can affect the nervous system.

name: valdecoxib
clinical_significance: Valdecoxib is a COX-2 inhibitor withdrawn or restricted in many countries because of cardiovascular and serious skin-reaction risks; prior use may be relevant in medication history.

name: valganciclovir
clinical_significance: An antiviral medicine used mainly to prevent or treat cytomegalovirus infection after transplantation. The body changes it into ganciclovir, which blocks viral multiplication; it can lower blood counts, injure the kidneys, affect fertility, and harm a fetus.

name: valid
clinical_significance: Valid means meeting accepted criteria or accurately measuring the intended finding; validated tests and instruments reduce false results and support sound clinical decisions.

name: validation
clinical_significance: Validation confirms that a test, device, or process performs reliably for its intended use; clinical validation should include accuracy, reproducibility, and relevant patient populations.

name: valine
clinical_significance: Valine is an essential amino acid needed for protein synthesis; markedly abnormal metabolism can cause rare inherited disorders and neurologic illness.

name: valinemia
clinical_significance: A rare inherited condition in which the body cannot process the amino acid valine normally. High valine levels may cause feeding problems, low muscle tone, developmental delay, or other nervous-system symptoms.

name: valinomycin
clinical_significance: Valinomycin is a toxic ionophore used in laboratory research; it disrupts potassium transport across cell membranes and is not a therapeutic drug.

name: valproic acid
clinical_significance: A medicine used for certain seizures, bipolar disorder, and migraine prevention. It can cause liver injury, pancreatitis, birth defects, and developmental harm during pregnancy.

name: valrubicin
clinical_significance: A chemotherapy medicine placed directly into the bladder for selected bladder cancers that have not responded adequately to other treatment. It can cause bladder irritation, blood in the urine, infection, and, rarely, effects throughout the body.

name: valsartan
clinical_significance: Valsartan is an angiotensin-II receptor blocker used for hypertension, heart failure, and selected cardiovascular indications; hyperkalaemia, renal-function changes, hypotension, and fetal toxicity are important risks.

name: valspodar
clinical_significance: Valspodar is an investigational inhibitor of drug-efflux pumps studied to overcome chemotherapy resistance; it is not routine treatment and can alter levels of other medicines.

name: valvular stenosis
clinical_significance: Valvular stenosis narrows a heart valve and obstructs blood flow; severity and symptoms determine the need for monitoring, medication, or valve intervention.

name: vanadium
clinical_significance: Vanadium is a trace element with no established need for routine supplementation; high exposure can irritate the lungs and digestive tract and affect kidney or blood function.

name: vancomycin
clinical_significance: An antibiotic used for selected serious bacterial infections and, by mouth, for certain infections of the large intestine. It can cause infusion reactions, kidney injury, hearing problems, or low blood counts and requires medical monitoring.

name: vandetanib
clinical_significance: A targeted cancer medicine used for selected medullary thyroid cancers. It blocks signals that help cancer cells grow and blood vessels form; diarrhea, high blood pressure, skin effects, and dangerous heart-rhythm changes require monitoring.

name: vanrija humicola
clinical_significance: Vanrija humicola is an environmental yeast that can rarely cause opportunistic infection; its isolation should be assessed against symptoms, immune status, and sample quality.

name: vaping
clinical_significance: Vaping uses an electronic device to heat a liquid and produce an aerosol for inhalation. Aerosols may contain nicotine and other substances that can harm the lungs and cause dependence.

name: vapor
clinical_significance: Vapor exposure can irritate or injure the eyes and airways or cause systemic poisoning, depending on the substance; identify the agent and route when evaluating exposure.

name: vapreotide
clinical_significance: Vapreotide is a somatostatin analog studied for endocrine tumors and acute bleeding; it is not widely used, and treatment choice depends on indication and local availability.

name: varenicline
clinical_significance: Varenicline is a medicine that reduces nicotine cravings and the rewarding effects of smoking; nausea, vivid dreams, and mood changes may occur, and it works best with behavioral support.

name: variant
clinical_significance: A variant is a genetic change, pathogen strain, or altered form of a condition; its clinical meaning depends on evidence, classification, and the patient’s context.

name: varibaculum
clinical_significance: Varibaculum is a genus of anaerobic bacteria from human mucosal sites that can occasionally cause infection; specimen source and reliable species identification inform interpretation.

name: varibaculum cambriense
clinical_significance: A bacterial species in the genus Varibaculum reported from human clinical specimens. Its role may be opportunistic and requires identification with the clinical context and susceptibility data.

name: varicellovirus
clinical_significance: Varicellovirus is a genus of herpesviruses that includes varicella-zoster virus, the cause of chickenpox and shingles.

name: varicocele
clinical_significance: Enlargement of veins in the scrotum, often on the left. It may cause aching, a soft “bag of worms” feeling, testicular growth differences, or reduced fertility, but many cause no symptoms.

name: varicose vein
clinical_significance: An abnormally enlarged and twisted superficial vein, usually in the leg, caused by venous-wall weakness or valve dysfunction that permits blood pooling.

name: variegate porphyria
clinical_significance: An inherited disorder of heme production that can cause attacks of abdominal pain, vomiting, nerve symptoms, confusion, or dark urine and can also cause fragile, blistering skin after sunlight exposure.

name: vas deferens
clinical_significance: A muscular tube that carries sperm from the epididymis toward the urethra during ejaculation.

name: vasa previa
clinical_significance: A pregnancy complication in which fetal blood vessels run across or near the cervix without the usual protection of the placenta or umbilical cord. If the membranes break, the vessels can tear and cause rapid fetal blood loss, so specialist planning is essential.

name: vascular
clinical_significance: Relating to blood vessels or, sometimes, lymphatic vessels. Vascular conditions include narrowed or blocked arteries, aneurysms, blood clots, abnormal vessel connections, and problems with veins; the term may also describe tests, surgery, or medicines involving these vessels.

name: vascular calcification
clinical_significance: Vascular calcification is calcium deposition in blood-vessel walls and is common in chronic kidney disease and diabetes; it is associated with arterial stiffness and cardiovascular risk.

name: vascular dementia
clinical_significance: Problems with thinking, memory, mood, or walking caused by strokes or long-term damage to the brain’s small blood vessels. Symptoms may appear suddenly or gradually, and treatment focuses on preventing further vessel damage and supporting daily function.

name: vascular diseases
clinical_significance: Vascular diseases affect arteries, veins, or lymphatic vessels and can reduce blood flow or cause bleeding, clotting, or swelling; symptoms and location determine urgency and testing.

name: vascular endothelium
clinical_significance: The vascular endothelium regulates vessel tone, clotting, and inflammation; endothelial injury contributes to atherosclerosis, thrombosis, and organ damage.

name: vascular headache
clinical_significance: Vascular headache is an older, nonspecific term for headache associated with blood-vessel changes; current diagnosis classifies specific disorders such as migraine and cluster headache.

name: vascular neoplasm
clinical_significance: A vascular neoplasm arises from blood or lymphatic vessel cells and may be benign or malignant; growth, bleeding, and location guide imaging and pathology assessment.

name: vascular resistance
clinical_significance: Vascular resistance is the opposition to blood flow and influences blood pressure and organ perfusion; abnormal resistance can reflect vasoconstriction, vessel disease, or shock.

name: vascular ring
clinical_significance: A birth defect in which blood vessels around the heart form a ring that can press on the windpipe or food pipe. It may cause noisy breathing, cough, repeated chest infections, swallowing difficulty, or feeding problems. Some people need no treatment; symptomatic rings may require surgery.

name: vasculitis
clinical_significance: Inflammation of blood vessels that can narrow them, reduce blood flow, or cause bleeding and tissue damage. It may affect large, medium, or small vessels and can involve the skin, nerves, kidneys, lungs, or other organs.

name: vasculostatin
clinical_significance: Vasculostatin is an experimental protein that inhibits new blood-vessel growth; it is studied as a potential cancer therapy but is not an established clinical treatment.

name: vasectomy
clinical_significance: A permanent contraceptive procedure in which the vas deferens are divided or occluded to prevent sperm from entering the ejaculate. It does not immediately provide sterility and does not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

name: vasoactive
clinical_significance: Vasoactive substances alter blood-vessel tone and may affect blood pressure and organ perfusion; medication effects are important in shock, anesthesia, and cardiovascular care.

name: vasoconstriction
clinical_significance: Narrowing of blood vessels caused by contraction of vascular smooth muscle, which can raise blood pressure or reduce blood flow to affected tissues.

name: vasoconstrictor agent
clinical_significance: Vasoconstrictor agents narrow blood vessels to raise blood pressure or control bleeding; excessive vasoconstriction can reduce blood flow and injure tissues.

name: vasodilation
clinical_significance: Widening of blood vessels when their muscular walls relax. It can increase blood flow and lower blood pressure and occurs with exercise, heat, medicines, and inflammation.

name: vasodilator agent
clinical_significance: Vasodilator agents widen blood vessels and are used for conditions such as hypertension, angina, or pulmonary hypertension; hypotension, headache, and reflex heart-rate changes may occur.

name: vasomotion
clinical_significance: Vasomotion is rhythmic change in small-vessel diameter that helps regulate tissue blood flow; impaired microvascular control is studied in diabetes and vascular disease.

name: vasopressin antagonist
clinical_significance: Vasopressin antagonists block water-retaining hormone effects and are used in selected cases of low blood sodium or polycystic kidney disease; sodium correction, liver toxicity, and dehydration require monitoring.

name: vasopressin receptor
clinical_significance: A cell sensor that responds to the hormone vasopressin. Different types help the kidneys retain water and help blood vessels narrow, influencing body-fluid balance and blood pressure.

name: vasospasm
clinical_significance: Sudden narrowing of a blood vessel caused by contraction of its muscular wall. It can temporarily reduce blood flow and cause chest pain, headache, stroke-like symptoms, or tissue injury, depending on the vessel affected.

name: vasotocin
clinical_significance: Vasotocin is a hormone in nonmammalian vertebrates related to vasopressin and oxytocin; it is primarily relevant to comparative physiology, not routine human care.

name: vasovagal reaction
clinical_significance: A reflex that slows the heart and widens blood vessels, briefly lowering blood pressure and sometimes causing fainting; triggers include pain, fear, prolonged standing, heat, or blood exposure.

name: vasovagal syncope
clinical_significance: A common faint caused by a reflex that briefly slows the heart or widens blood vessels, lowering blood pressure and brain blood flow. Triggers include standing still, heat, pain, fear, or seeing blood; warning symptoms often occur first.

name: vasovasostomy
clinical_significance: Vasovasostomy reconnects the vas deferens after vasectomy to restore the possibility of natural conception; success depends on time since vasectomy, surgical factors, and fertility of both partners.

name: vatalanib
clinical_significance: Vatalanib is an investigational angiogenesis inhibitor studied in cancer; it is not routine therapy, and trial evidence and vascular adverse effects determine its potential role.

name: vecuronium bromide
clinical_significance: Vecuronium bromide is a neuromuscular-blocking medicine used during anesthesia or ventilation; it paralyzes breathing muscles and requires controlled ventilation and monitoring.

name: vegan
clinical_significance: A vegan diet excludes animal-derived foods; a well-planned diet can be adequate, but vitamin B12 supplementation is essential and iron, calcium, iodine, vitamin D, and omega-3 intake may need attention.

name: vegan diet
clinical_significance: A vegan diet can support health when planned for adequate energy, protein, vitamin B12, iron, calcium, iodine, and vitamin D; nutritional planning is especially important during pregnancy and childhood.

name: vegetarian diet
clinical_significance: A vegetarian diet excludes some or all meat, and nutritional adequacy depends on food choices; iron, vitamin B12, protein, and omega-3 intake may need review.

name: veillonella
clinical_significance: Veillonella are anaerobic bacteria found in the mouth and gut; they may be normal flora but can rarely contribute to bloodstream, joint, or other infection.

name: veillonella atypica
clinical_significance: Veillonella atypica is an oral and intestinal commensal that can rarely cause invasive infection; its recovery from blood or a sterile site should be interpreted with clinical findings.

name: veillonella dispar
clinical_significance: Veillonella dispar is part of normal oral flora and may be involved in periodontal disease; it can rarely cause invasive infection, so specimen source matters.

name: veillonella parvula
clinical_significance: Veillonella parvula is an anaerobic commensal that can cause rare bloodstream, bone, or joint infections; identification from a sterile specimen may warrant targeted evaluation.

name: veillonellaceae
clinical_significance: Veillonellaceae are anaerobic bacteria commonly found in the mouth and gut; members can participate in mixed infections, and clinical significance depends on specimen and symptoms.

name: vein
clinical_significance: A blood vessel that carries blood toward the heart. Most veins carry oxygen-poor blood, but veins from the lungs and placenta carry oxygen-rich blood. Veins often contain valves that help prevent backward flow.

name: VeIP regimen
clinical_significance: A cancer-treatment combination of vinblastine, ifosfamide, and cisplatin, used mainly for selected germ-cell tumors. It can lower blood counts and damage the kidneys, nerves, or bladder, so specialist monitoring is required.

name: velafermin
clinical_significance: Velafermin is an investigational fibroblast growth factor studied to protect or repair mucosal tissue after cancer treatment; it is not standard care, and trial evidence guides use.

name: veliparib
clinical_significance: Veliparib is a PARP inhibitor studied in cancer treatment; it is not widely established for routine use, and marrow suppression and combination-treatment toxicity are important in trials.

name: veltuzumab
clinical_significance: Veltuzumab is an investigational anti-CD20 antibody studied for B-cell cancers and autoimmune disease; it is not standard therapy and may cause infusion reactions and infection risk.

name: vemurafenib
clinical_significance: A targeted cancer medicine for tumors with a specific BRAF V600 gene change, including some melanomas. It can cause joint pain, sun sensitivity, abnormal heart rhythm, new skin cancers, or treatment resistance.

name: venae cava
clinical_significance: The venae cavae are the major veins returning blood from the body to the right atrium; obstruction or injury can impair circulation and cause swelling, low blood pressure, or bleeding.

name: venipuncture
clinical_significance: Puncture of a vein with a needle to obtain blood, administer fluids or medicines, or establish intravenous access. Bruising, infection, bleeding, and nerve or artery injury are uncommon complications.

name: venlafaxine
clinical_significance: Venlafaxine is an SNRI antidepressant used for depression and anxiety; blood pressure changes, nausea, sexual effects, withdrawal symptoms, and serotonin toxicity are potential concerns.

name: venlafaxine hydrochloride
clinical_significance: Venlafaxine hydrochloride is the salt form of venlafaxine used for depression and anxiety; abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal symptoms, so dose changes are usually tapered.

name: venom
clinical_significance: A poisonous substance delivered by an animal through a bite, sting, or similar structure. Its effects vary by species and may include pain, swelling, nerve problems, bleeding, or dangerous changes in breathing or blood pressure.

name: venous
clinical_significance: Relating to veins, which usually carry blood back toward the heart. Vein problems include blood clots, varicose veins, poor return of blood, and ulcers; pulmonary veins are an exception because they carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the heart.

name: venous injury
clinical_significance: Venous injury can cause bleeding, clot formation, or impaired blood return; severity depends on the vessel and may require compression, imaging, or surgery.

name: venous insufficiency
clinical_significance: Impaired return of blood through the veins, usually in the legs, because valves allow backward flow, veins are blocked, or the calf-muscle pump is ineffective. Blood may pool and cause aching, heaviness, swelling, varicose veins, itching, darkened or hardened skin, stasis dermatitis, and difficult-to-heal ulcers near the ankle.

name: venous plasma
clinical_significance: Venous plasma is the liquid portion of blood collected from a vein; proper processing and anticoagulant choice are necessary for accurate laboratory results.

name: venous stenosis
clinical_significance: Venous stenosis narrows a vein and can obstruct drainage, impair dialysis access, or cause swelling and collateral veins; imaging can guide treatment.

name: venous thromboembolism
clinical_significance: A blood clot that forms in a vein, usually deep in the leg, and may travel to the lungs. A clot in the lungs can cause sudden breathlessness, chest pain, collapse, or death.

name: venous thrombosis
clinical_significance: The formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a vein, most commonly in the deep veins

name: ventilator
clinical_significance: A machine that supports or replaces spontaneous breathing by delivering air, oxygen, or an air-oxygen mixture under positive pressure. Noninvasive ventilators deliver support through a mask, while invasive ventilators connect through an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube. Ventilators can provide different patterns and levels of pressure or volume according to the device and clinical purpose.

name: ventral
clinical_significance: Relating to the belly or front side of the body; synonym for anterior in human anatomy.

name: ventral hernia
clinical_significance: Protrusion of abdominal tissue through a weakness in the front abdominal wall, including incisional and umbilical hernias. It may cause a bulge or pain and requires urgent assessment if incarceration or strangulation is suspected.

name: ventral roots
clinical_significance: Ventral roots carry motor signals from the spinal cord to muscles; damage can cause weakness or paralysis in the muscles supplied by the affected spinal level.

name: ventricle
clinical_significance: One of the two lower chambers of the heart that pump blood out of it. The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs to receive oxygen; the left ventricle sends oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body.

name: ventricular ablation
clinical_significance: Ventricular ablation destroys a small area of heart tissue responsible for a dangerous rhythm; it can reduce recurrent arrhythmias but carries risks of bleeding, heart block, or cardiac injury.

name: ventricular arrhythmia
clinical_significance: An abnormal heart rhythm arising from the ventricles. It may cause palpitations, dizziness, fainting,

name: ventricular dysfunction
clinical_significance: Ventricular dysfunction impairs the heart’s ability to pump or fill; it can cause heart failure, breathlessness, fluid retention, and reduced exercise tolerance.

name: ventricular fibrillation
clinical_significance: A chaotic, disorganized ventricular rhythm in which the ventricles quiver rather than contract, producing no effective cardiac output and cardiac arrest. It is a shockable rhythm; immediate CPR and unsynchronized defibrillation are required, with treatment of the underlying cause.

name: ventricular flutter
clinical_significance: Ventricular flutter is an extremely rapid ventricular rhythm that can deteriorate into ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest; it requires immediate emergency treatment.

name: ventricular hypertrophy
clinical_significance: Thickening of the wall of one of the heart’s lower chambers. It may develop from long-term high blood pressure, valve disease, inherited heart muscle disease, or intense training and can lead to stiffness, abnormal rhythms, or heart failure.

name: ventriculostomy
clinical_significance: Ventriculostomy creates or accesses a pathway to drain cerebrospinal fluid, often to relieve dangerous intracranial pressure; infection, bleeding, and over-drainage are risks.

name: ventrolateral
clinical_significance: Ventrolateral describes a position toward the front and side; precise localization helps interpret neurologic findings, imaging, and surgical targets.

name: venule
clinical_significance: A small blood vessel that collects blood from capillaries and carries it into larger veins. Venules also allow white blood cells and fluid to leave the bloodstream during inflammation.

name: verapamil
clinical_significance: A non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker used for selected hypertension, angina, and supraventricular tachyarrhythmias; it can cause bradycardia and constipation.

name: veratrum alkaloids
clinical_significance: Veratrum alkaloids are toxic plant compounds that can cause vomiting, low blood pressure, and dangerous slow or abnormal heart rhythms; suspected ingestion needs urgent toxicology care.

name: verbal behavior
clinical_significance: Verbal behavior includes speaking and other language responses; changes can signal neurologic, developmental, or psychiatric conditions and affect communication and consent.

name: verbal learning
clinical_significance: Verbal learning is the ability to acquire and recall spoken or written information; deficits can occur in brain injury, dementia, or learning disorders and are assessed in neuropsychology.

name: vernier caliper
clinical_significance: A vernier caliper measures small dimensions accurately in laboratories and device manufacturing; calibration helps ensure the quality of medical instruments and implants.
